phases.label: Evaluate evidence

playbooks.label: Test competing explanations
playbooks.description: Generate, compare, challenge, and monitor serious competing hypotheses.

steps.name: Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH)
steps.role: Compare hypotheses against diagnostic evidence.

steps.name: Discriminating Evidence Matrix
steps.role: Focus attention on evidence that separates explanations.

steps.name: Null Hypothesis Challenge
steps.role: Test whether the favored explanation is actually necessary.

steps.name: Process Tracing
steps.role: Examine whether the proposed causal mechanism appears in the case evidence.

playbooks.label: Build a warning assessment
playbooks.description: Move from broad change signals to alternative futures and explicit monitoring logic.

steps.name: Environmental Scanning
steps.role: Collect weak signals, emerging issues, and peripheral developments.

steps.name: Scenario Discovery
steps.role: Identify combinations of uncertainties associated with important outcomes.

steps.name: Signpost-to-Scenario Mapping
steps.role: Connect observable developments to movement among scenarios.

steps.name: Backcasting
steps.role: Work backward from consequential futures to milestones and present requirements.

playbooks.label: Produce and calibrate a forecast
playbooks.description: Frame uncertainty, estimate outcomes, explore alternative futures, and score performance.

steps.name: Structured Expert Judgment
steps.role: Elicit explicit estimates and uncertainty from informed judgments.

steps.name: Scenario Discovery
steps.role: Identify combinations of uncertainties that drive materially different outcomes.

steps.name: Environmental Scanning
steps.role: Maintain awareness of developments that should update the forecast.

steps.name: Brier Score Review
steps.role: Score and calibrate resolved probabilistic forecasts.

playbooks.label: Investigate a cyber incident
playbooks.description: Reconstruct activity, map behaviors, test explanations, and identify next collection steps.

steps.name: Incident Reconstruction
steps.role: Build the best-supported timeline and causal sequence.

steps.name: MITRE ATT&CK Mapping
steps.role: Map supported adversary behaviors to tactics and techniques.

steps.name: Diamond Model Analysis
steps.role: Pivot among adversary, capability, infrastructure, and victim evidence.

steps.name: Hypothesis-Driven Investigation
steps.role: Test competing explanations and prioritize evidence collection.

playbooks.label: Assess system safety risk
playbooks.description: Identify system hazards, controls, organizational causes, and residual risk.

steps.name: Systems-Theoretic Process Analysis
steps.role: Identify unsafe control actions and loss scenarios.

steps.name: Risk Matrix Analysis
steps.role: Prioritize hazards using explicit severity and likelihood criteria.

steps.name: AcciMap
steps.role: Trace causal influences across technical and organizational levels.

steps.name: Tripod Beta
steps.role: Distinguish immediate failures from latent organizational conditions.

playbooks.label: Compare and stress-test options
playbooks.description: Rank alternatives, model uncertainty, and test robustness before commitment.

steps.name: TOPSIS
steps.role: Rank alternatives by distance from ideal and anti-ideal outcomes.

steps.name: ELECTRE
steps.role: Test outranking where tradeoffs are not fully compensatory.

steps.name: Expected Utility Analysis
steps.role: Compare options under uncertain outcomes and explicit values.

steps.name: Sensitivity Analysis
steps.role: Test whether the preferred option survives plausible changes.

playbooks.label: Synthesize a research base
playbooks.description: Map, review, synthesize, and explain a body of evidence.

steps.name: Scoping Review
steps.role: Map concepts, study types, and evidence gaps.

steps.name: Systematic Review
steps.role: Apply reproducible eligibility, search, appraisal, and synthesis.

steps.name: Meta-Analysis
steps.role: Pool compatible quantitative effects when appropriate.

steps.name: Narrative Synthesis
steps.role: Integrate findings that cannot be validly pooled.

playbooks.label: Investigate an actor network
playbooks.description: Define relationships, identify brokers, and locate structural vulnerabilities.

steps.name: Link Analysis
steps.role: Establish entities and observed relationships.

steps.name: Betweenness Centrality Review
steps.role: Identify nodes positioned on many shortest paths.

steps.name: Broker and Gatekeeper Analysis
steps.role: Assess actors controlling flows between groups.

steps.name: Structural Hole Analysis
steps.role: Find brokerage positions created by disconnected network regions.

playbooks.label: Make a rapid operational decision
playbooks.description: Orient quickly, exploit expert recognition, challenge the first plausible action, and preserve learning under time pressure.

steps.name: OODA Decision-Cycle Analysis
steps.role: Diagnose observation, orientation, tempo, and feedback before acting under pressure.

steps.name: Recognition-Primed Decision Audit
steps.role: Test whether an experienced decision-maker's first plausible action survives mental simulation.

steps.name: Premortem Analysis
steps.role: Expose failure mechanisms that rapid recognition may have overlooked before commitment.

steps.name: After-Action Review
steps.role: Capture what actually happened and feed the result back into future recognition and orientation.

playbooks.label: Assess complex-system failure risk
playbooks.description: Diagnose structural accident susceptibility, control limits, hazards, and resilience rather than stopping at component failure.

steps.name: Interactive Complexity / Tight-Coupling Audit
steps.role: Determine whether unexpected interactions and limited slack make failure intrinsically hard to control.

steps.name: Requisite Variety Analysis
steps.role: Test whether sensing and response capacity can match the range of disturbances the system can generate.

steps.name: Systems-Theoretic Process Analysis
steps.role: Trace unsafe control actions and system-level loss scenarios across the control structure.

steps.name: Resilience Engineering Review
steps.role: Assess adaptive capacity, graceful degradation, recovery resources, and resilience under disturbed conditions.

playbooks.label: Audit metrics and incentives
playbooks.description: Check whether measurement and accountability systems are driving gaming, displaced goals, or asymmetric risk-taking.

steps.name: Goodhart–Campbell Metric Gaming Audit
steps.role: Identify how target pressure can corrupt a proxy and displace the substantive objective.

steps.name: Skin-in-the-Game Incentive Audit
steps.role: Map who receives upside, who bears downside, and where decision influence is detached from consequences.

steps.name: Measurement System Analysis
steps.role: Test whether the measurement process itself is stable, repeatable, and capable of supporting the decisions placed on it.

steps.name: Exit–Voice–Loyalty Analysis
steps.role: Examine whether participants can surface metric failures through voice or instead respond through exit, silence, or loyalty.

playbooks.label: Design governance under complexity
playbooks.description: Preserve local knowledge, test institutional feedback, and design governance that works across multiple centers and scales.

steps.name: Legibility / Local-Knowledge Audit
steps.role: Identify what administrative simplification hides or destroys before redesigning the system.

steps.name: Commons Governance Design Audit
steps.role: Test boundaries, participation, monitoring, sanctions, conflict resolution, and local rule fit.

steps.name: Polycentric Governance Analysis
steps.role: Map overlapping decision centers and assess scale fit, redundancy, coordination, and autonomy.

steps.name: Exit–Voice–Loyalty Analysis
steps.role: Check whether participants have credible feedback and correction channels when governance performance declines.

definition.name: Key Assumptions Check
definition.summary: Make the assumptions supporting a judgment explicit and test how much the analysis depends on them.

steps.title: Current analytic line
steps.prompt: State the judgment, assessment, or working explanation you are testing.

steps.title: Assumptions
steps.prompt: List the stated and unstated premises that must be true for that analytic line to hold.

steps.title: Challenge the assumptions
steps.prompt: For each important assumption, ask why it must be true and what evidence or circumstances could make it fail.

steps.title: Confidence and sensitivity
steps.prompt: Which assumptions are least secure? If one proved false, how much would your conclusion change?

steps.title: What would change your mind?
steps.prompt: List information, events, or indicators that should trigger a reassessment.

prerequisites: A current judgment or line of reasoning
Explicit and implicit assumptions that can be challenged
A decision about which assumptions are load-bearing

definition.name: Quality of Information Check
definition.summary: Review the reliability, completeness, corroboration, and limitations of the information supporting an assessment.

steps.title: Critical information
steps.prompt: Identify the sources or pieces of information that carry the most weight in the assessment.
steps.placeholder: One source or item per line

steps.title: Reliability and access
steps.prompt: What is known about each source's reliability, access, collection conditions, processing, translation, or interpretation?

steps.title: Corroboration
steps.prompt: Which important claims are independently corroborated, and which depend on a single or ambiguous source?

steps.title: Gaps and ambiguity
steps.prompt: What important information is missing, recalled, disputed, stale, or open to multiple interpretations?
steps.placeholder: One gap or ambiguity per line

steps.title: Resulting confidence
steps.prompt: Given the quality of the information base, what confidence is justified and why?

definition.name: Indicators or Signposts of Change
definition.summary: Define observable events that would provide warning that a hypothesis, scenario, or trend is emerging or failing.

steps.title: Hypotheses or scenarios
steps.prompt: List the competing hypotheses, scenarios, or states you want to monitor.
steps.placeholder: One hypothesis or scenario per line

steps.title: Positive indicators
steps.prompt: What observable events or trends would you expect if the development were occurring?

steps.title: Negative indicators
steps.prompt: What would you expect to observe if the development were not occurring?

steps.title: Triggers
steps.prompt: Identify events that could abruptly accelerate, reverse, or transform the situation.

steps.title: Review plan
steps.prompt: How often should the indicators be revisited, and what threshold would justify changing the assessment?

definition.name: Analysis of Competing Hypotheses (ACH)
definition.summary: Compare multiple explanations against the full body of evidence, emphasizing disconfirmation rather than confirmation.

steps.title: Competing hypotheses
steps.prompt: Generate the reasonable alternative explanations that deserve consideration.

steps.title: Evidence and arguments
steps.prompt: List significant evidence and arguments relevant to any of the hypotheses.

steps.title: Disconfirming evidence
steps.prompt: Which evidence is inconsistent with each hypothesis? Focus on evidence that discriminates among alternatives.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Which conclusions depend on a small number of critical or potentially unreliable evidence items?

steps.title: Expected but missing evidence
steps.prompt: What should be observable if each hypothesis were true but is not currently seen? Could denial or deception explain the absence?

steps.title: Relative likelihood and monitoring
steps.prompt: Which hypotheses are strongest or weakest now, and what indicators should be monitored going forward?

prerequisites: Analyst willingness to retain disconfirming evidence

definition.name: Devil's Advocacy
definition.summary: Build the strongest plausible case against a dominant judgment, consensus, or key assumption.

steps.title: Mainline judgment
steps.prompt: State the prevailing judgment and the key assumptions supporting it.

steps.title: Vulnerable assumptions
steps.prompt: Which assumptions, logic, or evidence are most susceptible to challenge?

steps.title: Best contrary case
steps.prompt: Construct the strongest alternative explanation or conclusion you can support.

steps.title: Contrary evidence
steps.prompt: What evidence supports the alternative or contradicts the prevailing view?

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: Does the exercise reinforce the mainline judgment, reveal caveats, or justify revising it?

definition.name: Team A / Team B
definition.summary: Develop and compare two or more strongly held competing views with equal analytical discipline.

steps.title: Competing positions
steps.prompt: Define the competing hypotheses or viewpoints as fairly and precisely as possible.

steps.title: Best case for Position A
steps.prompt: Present its assumptions, strongest evidence, logic, and missing information.

steps.title: Best case for Position B
steps.prompt: Present its assumptions, strongest evidence, logic, and missing information.

steps.title: Challenge and rebuttal
steps.prompt: What are the strongest criticisms each side can make of the other?

steps.title: Areas of agreement and disagreement
steps.prompt: What differences remain, what evidence could resolve them, and what should be collected or researched next?

definition.name: High-Impact / Low-Probability Analysis
definition.summary: Examine a seemingly unlikely event whose consequences would be large enough to merit preparation and warning.

steps.title: High-impact outcome
steps.prompt: Define the low-probability outcome clearly and explain why its consequences matter.

steps.title: Plausible pathways
steps.prompt: Describe one or more credible ways the outcome could occur.

steps.title: Triggers and accelerants
steps.prompt: What shocks, decisions, accidents, or changes in momentum could make the outcome more plausible?

steps.title: Early indicators
steps.prompt: What observable signposts would suggest that a pathway is beginning to unfold?

steps.title: Deflectors and mitigations
steps.prompt: What factors or actions could prevent, delay, or reduce the impact of the outcome?

definition.name: What If? Analysis
definition.summary: Assume an important event has already happened, then reason backward to explain how it could have occurred and what would follow.

steps.title: Assumed event
steps.prompt: State the event as if it has already happened. Be concrete about timing and scope.

steps.title: How did we get here?
steps.prompt: Work backward through the decisions, conditions, surprises, and interactions that could plausibly have produced the event.

steps.title: Critical drivers
steps.prompt: Which assumptions, actors, forces, or uncertainties were necessary for the pathway?

steps.title: Signposts
steps.prompt: What observable indicators would have appeared before the event?

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: If the event occurred, what consequences, opportunities, or policy choices would follow?

definition.name: Brainstorming
definition.summary: Generate a broad set of possibilities before evaluating or narrowing them.

steps.title: Question
steps.prompt: Frame the problem or question narrowly enough to focus ideas but broadly enough to allow surprise.

steps.title: Generate ideas
steps.prompt: List possibilities without evaluating them while generating.

steps.title: Patterns and clusters
steps.prompt: Group related ideas, combine duplicates, and identify themes or surprising connections.

steps.title: Promising directions
steps.prompt: Which ideas deserve deeper investigation, testing, or collection?

definition.name: Outside-In Thinking
definition.summary: Examine broad external forces first, then trace how they could shape the narrower issue being analyzed.

steps.title: Focal issue
steps.prompt: Define the issue, organization, country, market, or problem you are trying to understand.

steps.title: External forces
steps.prompt: Identify broad political, economic, social, technological, security, environmental, or other forces outside the immediate issue.

steps.title: Interactions
steps.prompt: How might those external forces interact with the focal issue or with one another?

steps.title: Potential surprises
steps.prompt: What developments would be easy to miss if analysis stayed focused only on the immediate problem?

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: Which external changes deserve monitoring or should alter the current assessment?

definition.name: Red Team Analysis
definition.summary: Adopt the perspective of another actor to test how their goals, culture, constraints, and perceptions could produce different choices.

steps.title: Actor and decision
steps.prompt: Whose perspective are you adopting, and what decision or problem are they facing?

steps.title: Objectives and constraints
steps.prompt: What do they want, fear, value, and need to protect? What limits their choices?

steps.title: Worldview and assumptions
steps.prompt: How might history, culture, doctrine, incentives, biases, or incomplete information shape their perception?

steps.title: Options from their perspective
steps.prompt: What actions might look rational or attractive to them even if they look unattractive to us?

steps.title: Observable implications
steps.prompt: What behavior or indicators would you expect if this perspective is approximately correct?

prerequisites: A sufficiently developed baseline judgment or plan
An independent challenger or deliberately separated perspective
Access to the evidence and assumptions supporting the baseline

definition.name: Alternative Futures Analysis
definition.summary: Construct several plausible, causally distinct futures to expose implications, robust actions, vulnerabilities, and signposts without treating any scenario as the forecast.

steps.title: Focal question
steps.prompt: Define the strategic issue, decision context, and time horizon without assuming a preferred or most likely future.

steps.title: Drivers, constraints, and uncertainties
steps.prompt: Identify structural drivers, constraints, critical uncertainties, and plausible discontinuities grounded in evidence and scanning.
steps.placeholder: One driver or uncertainty per line

steps.title: Distinct plausible futures
steps.prompt: Construct several internally coherent futures that differ in causal structure, actor behavior, and important conditions—not merely in whether outcomes are good or bad.

steps.title: Implications and robust actions
steps.prompt: For each future, identify consequences, vulnerabilities, opportunities, assumptions under stress, and actions that remain useful across multiple futures.

steps.title: Indicators and signposts
steps.prompt: Define observable events, trends, behaviors, thresholds, or absences that would shift attention toward or away from each future.

steps.title: Monitoring and update
steps.prompt: Specify how accumulating signposts should change scenario attention while preserving viable alternatives and avoiding premature collapse to a single forecast.

definition.name: Issue Redefinition
definition.summary: Reframe a question several ways to expose hidden assumptions, boundaries, and alternative problem statements.

steps.title: Current question
steps.prompt: State the question exactly as it is currently framed.

steps.title: Embedded assumptions
steps.prompt: What does the wording assume about causes, actors, boundaries, timing, or available choices?

steps.title: Alternative frames
steps.prompt: Rewrite the issue from several different perspectives or levels of analysis.

steps.title: What changes?
steps.prompt: Which evidence, explanations, or options become visible under the alternative frames?

steps.title: Working frame
steps.prompt: Choose the most useful framing for the next analytic step and explain why.

definition.name: Chronologies and Timelines
definition.summary: Order events to reveal sequences, gaps, tempo changes, dependencies, and possible causal relationships.

steps.title: Events
steps.prompt: List the relevant events with the best available dates or time ranges.

steps.title: Sequence and phases
steps.prompt: Group events into meaningful phases and note changes in pace or direction.

steps.title: Gaps and anomalies
steps.prompt: Where are there unexplained intervals, missing events, contradictions, or sudden changes?
steps.placeholder: One gap or anomaly per line

steps.title: Possible relationships
steps.prompt: Which events may enable, trigger, constrain, or follow from others?

steps.title: Analytic implications
steps.prompt: What does the chronology suggest that was less visible before ordering the events?

definition.name: Sorting and Prioritizing
definition.summary: Organize a large set of items into meaningful groups and rank what deserves attention first.

steps.title: Items
steps.prompt: List the items, issues, actors, risks, or evidence to organize.

steps.title: Sorting criteria
steps.prompt: Define the dimensions or criteria that matter for grouping and comparison.

steps.title: Groups
steps.prompt: Cluster the items using the chosen criteria and name the resulting groups.

steps.title: Priority order
steps.prompt: Rank the most important items or groups and state the reason for the ordering.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Would a different reasonable criterion materially change the ranking?

definition.name: Matrix Analysis
definition.summary: Compare entities, hypotheses, options, or evidence across a consistent set of dimensions.

steps.title: Rows
steps.prompt: List the things being compared.

steps.title: Comparison dimensions
steps.prompt: List the dimensions, attributes, or questions to apply consistently.

steps.title: Cell observations
steps.prompt: Record the most important matches, differences, absences, and outliers across the matrix.

steps.title: Patterns
steps.prompt: What clusters, contrasts, or discriminating dimensions emerge?

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: What judgments or follow-up questions does the comparison support?

definition.name: Network Analysis
definition.summary: Examine actors or entities as a network to identify central nodes, brokers, clusters, dependencies, and vulnerabilities.

steps.title: Nodes
steps.prompt: List the relevant people, organizations, systems, places, or other entities.

steps.title: Links
steps.prompt: Describe the important relationships or flows among the nodes.

steps.title: Network structure
steps.prompt: Which nodes are central, isolated, bridging clusters, or dependent on a small number of links?

steps.title: Unknown or uncertain links
steps.prompt: Which suspected or missing relationships would most change the picture?

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: What opportunities, risks, collection needs, or hypotheses follow from the network structure?

definition.name: Argument Mapping
definition.summary: Make a judgment's reasoning explicit by separating claims, evidence, assumptions, objections, and dependencies.

steps.title: Main claim
steps.prompt: State the judgment or conclusion being evaluated.

steps.title: Supporting reasons
steps.prompt: List the reasons and evidence that support the claim.

steps.title: Bridging assumptions
steps.prompt: What must be true for the supporting reasons to justify the claim?

steps.title: Objections and counterevidence
steps.prompt: List the strongest reasons or evidence against the claim.

steps.title: Assessment
steps.prompt: Which parts of the argument are strongest, weakest, or most dependent on uncertain premises?

definition.name: Diagnostic Reasoning
definition.summary: Compare observable features against alternative explanations and emphasize the features that discriminate among them.

steps.title: Observed problem
steps.prompt: Define the event, condition, or pattern that requires explanation.

steps.title: Possible explanations
steps.prompt: List plausible explanations before choosing among them.

steps.title: Diagnostic features
steps.prompt: Which observations are expected under some explanations but not others?

steps.title: Mismatches
steps.prompt: For each explanation, identify important observations it fails to explain.

steps.title: Best current explanation
steps.prompt: Which explanation best fits the discriminating evidence, and what uncertainty remains?

definition.name: Indicators Validator
definition.summary: Test whether proposed indicators are observable, distinctive, timely, and useful enough to support monitoring.

steps.title: Outcome or hypothesis
steps.prompt: State what the indicator set is intended to detect.

steps.title: Candidate indicators
steps.prompt: List the proposed indicators.

steps.title: Indicator quality
steps.prompt: For each indicator, assess observability, timeliness, uniqueness, reliability, and susceptibility to manipulation.

steps.title: Coverage and blind spots
steps.prompt: What important pathways or failure modes are not covered by the current set?

steps.title: Validated set
steps.prompt: Keep, revise, or discard each indicator and identify the strongest monitoring set.

definition.name: Deception Detection
definition.summary: Evaluate whether observed information could be intentionally shaped to create a false or misleading picture.

steps.title: Current interpretation
steps.prompt: State the interpretation that could be vulnerable to deception.

steps.title: Incentive and capability
steps.prompt: Who could benefit from misleading observers, and do they have the access or capability to do so?

steps.title: Anomalies
steps.prompt: What inconsistencies, convenient patterns, missing data, or improbable coincidences deserve scrutiny?

steps.title: Deception hypotheses
steps.prompt: List plausible ways the information environment could have been manipulated.

steps.title: Discriminating tests
steps.prompt: What independent evidence or future observations could distinguish deception from benign explanations?

definition.name: Premortem Analysis
definition.summary: Assume the current judgment or plan later proved badly wrong, then identify plausible reasons for that failure.

steps.title: Judgment or plan
steps.prompt: State the assessment, forecast, or plan being stress-tested.

steps.title: Assume failure
steps.prompt: Imagine that it is now clear the judgment or plan failed badly. Describe the failure concretely.

steps.title: Why did it fail?
steps.prompt: Generate as many plausible reasons as possible without filtering them too early.

steps.title: Warning signs
steps.prompt: What indicators would have been visible before the failure?

steps.title: Changes now
steps.prompt: What should be revised, monitored, hedged, or investigated because of the exercise?

definition.name: Structured Self-Critique
definition.summary: Systematically challenge an analysis for weak assumptions, evidence problems, gaps, and overconfidence.

steps.title: Bottom line
steps.prompt: State the current analytic judgment and confidence.

steps.title: Weakest elements
steps.prompt: Which assumptions, evidence items, inferences, or definitions are most vulnerable?

steps.title: Neglected alternatives
steps.prompt: What plausible explanations or outcomes received too little attention?

steps.title: Information gaps
steps.prompt: What missing information could materially change the judgment?

steps.title: Revision
steps.prompt: What should change in the judgment, confidence, caveats, or collection priorities?

definition.name: Structured Debate
definition.summary: Force competing positions to state their strongest cases, rebuttals, and points of possible resolution.

steps.title: Debate question
steps.prompt: Frame the disagreement as a clear proposition or choice.

steps.title: Positions
steps.prompt: State the competing positions fairly and precisely.

steps.title: Strongest cases
steps.prompt: Give each position its strongest supporting evidence, assumptions, and logic.

steps.title: Rebuttals
steps.prompt: What are the strongest objections each position must answer?

steps.title: Resolution conditions
steps.prompt: What evidence, event, or test would most help resolve the disagreement?

definition.name: Adversarial Collaboration
definition.summary: Have analysts with differing views jointly define disagreements, tests, and evidence that could move either side.

steps.title: Core disagreement
steps.prompt: State exactly where the competing views diverge.

steps.title: Common ground
steps.prompt: List facts, definitions, and assumptions all sides accept.

steps.title: Cruxes
steps.prompt: Which factual or causal questions actually drive the disagreement?

steps.title: Joint tests
steps.prompt: Design observations, research, or indicators that both sides agree would be informative.

steps.title: Update conditions
steps.prompt: What result would cause each side to revise its view?

definition.name: Starbursting
definition.summary: Generate a disciplined set of questions around an issue before jumping to answers.

steps.title: Focus
steps.prompt: Name the event, proposal, actor, or problem to explore.

steps.title: Who?
steps.prompt: Generate important who questions about actors, stakeholders, beneficiaries, decision-makers, and affected groups.

steps.title: What?
steps.prompt: Generate important what questions about actions, resources, constraints, effects, and unknowns.

steps.title: When and where?
steps.prompt: Generate questions about timing, sequence, location, scope, and context.

steps.title: Why and how?
steps.prompt: Generate questions about motives, mechanisms, causes, pathways, and implementation.

definition.name: Cross-Impact Analysis
definition.summary: Explore how important developments could reinforce, inhibit, trigger, or reshape one another.

steps.title: Developments
steps.prompt: List the important events, trends, decisions, or uncertainties to compare.

steps.title: Pairwise impacts
steps.prompt: For each important pair, ask how one could increase, decrease, accelerate, delay, or transform the other.

steps.title: Feedback loops
steps.prompt: Identify reinforcing or balancing loops that could create nonlinear change.

steps.title: Cascades
steps.prompt: Which initial developments could trigger the largest chains of secondary effects?

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: What interactions deserve monitoring or make current forecasts fragile?

definition.name: Morphological Analysis
definition.summary: Break a complex possibility space into dimensions, then recombine them to discover plausible configurations that might be overlooked.

steps.title: Problem space
steps.prompt: Define the issue or future state being explored.

steps.title: Dimensions
steps.prompt: List the major dimensions that can vary independently.

steps.title: Possible states
steps.prompt: For each dimension, list materially different states or values.

steps.title: Interesting combinations
steps.prompt: Combine states across dimensions to generate distinct configurations, including unusual but coherent ones.

steps.title: Assessment
steps.prompt: Which configurations are plausible, consequential, or useful for further analysis?

definition.name: Multiple Hypotheses Generation
definition.summary: Deliberately widen the explanation set before evaluation so the first plausible answer does not become the only one considered.

steps.title: Observation
steps.prompt: State the event, behavior, or condition requiring explanation.

steps.title: Obvious explanations
steps.prompt: List the explanations that come to mind immediately.

steps.title: Expand the set
steps.prompt: Generate explanations from different actors, mechanisms, incentives, accidents, external forces, and combinations.

steps.title: Merge and split
steps.prompt: Combine duplicates and split hypotheses that hide materially different mechanisms.

steps.title: Shortlist
steps.prompt: Retain the distinct hypotheses that deserve evidence-based testing.

definition.name: Structured Analogies
definition.summary: Compare the current case with prior cases using explicit dimensions rather than relying on superficial resemblance.

steps.title: Target case
steps.prompt: Define the current problem and the feature you are trying to understand or forecast.

steps.title: Candidate analogs
steps.prompt: List potentially comparable historical or contemporary cases.

steps.title: Comparison dimensions
steps.prompt: Choose the dimensions that matter for causal similarity, not just surface resemblance.

steps.title: Similarities and differences
steps.prompt: Compare each analog to the target across the chosen dimensions.

steps.title: Transferable lessons
steps.prompt: Which lessons remain credible after accounting for the important differences?

definition.name: Role Playing
definition.summary: Simulate decisions from the perspectives of relevant actors to expose incentives, constraints, interactions, and unexpected responses.

steps.title: Decision environment
steps.prompt: Define the situation, actors, and decision to be simulated.

steps.title: Actor roles
steps.prompt: For each actor, state objectives, fears, constraints, information, and leverage.

steps.title: Likely moves
steps.prompt: What would each actor plausibly do first from their own perspective?

steps.title: Interaction
steps.prompt: How might other actors respond, adapt, bargain, escalate, or exploit those moves?

steps.title: Insights
steps.prompt: What assumptions, vulnerabilities, or indicators became visible through the simulation?

definition.name: Decision Matrix
definition.summary: Compare options against explicit criteria so tradeoffs and sensitivity are visible.

steps.title: Decision
steps.prompt: State the decision and the options under consideration.

steps.title: Criteria
steps.prompt: List the criteria that should determine the choice.

steps.title: Importance
steps.prompt: Identify which criteria matter most and why.

steps.title: Option comparison
steps.prompt: Assess each option consistently against each criterion.

steps.title: Sensitivity and choice
steps.prompt: Which option performs best, and would modest changes in assumptions or priorities change the result?

definition.name: Force Field Analysis
definition.summary: Identify forces pushing toward and resisting a change, outcome, or decision and assess where leverage exists.

steps.title: Proposed change or outcome
steps.prompt: State the change, outcome, or decision being analyzed.

steps.title: Driving forces
steps.prompt: List the forces pushing toward it.

steps.title: Restraining forces
steps.prompt: List the forces resisting or slowing it.

steps.title: Relative strength
steps.prompt: Which forces are strongest, most uncertain, or most changeable?

steps.title: Leverage
steps.prompt: Where could intervention strengthen drivers, reduce resistance, or reveal a hidden constraint?

definition.name: Pros, Cons, Faults, and Fixes
definition.summary: Evaluate an option by separating benefits, drawbacks, failure modes, and possible remedies.

steps.title: Option
steps.prompt: State the proposal, plan, explanation, or course of action being evaluated.

steps.title: Pros
steps.prompt: List the strongest benefits or advantages.

steps.title: Cons
steps.prompt: List the strongest costs or disadvantages.

steps.title: Faults
steps.prompt: Identify ways the option could fail, create second-order effects, or depend on fragile assumptions.

steps.title: Fixes
steps.prompt: For each important fault, identify a mitigation, redesign, hedge, or monitoring measure.

definition.name: Delphi Method
definition.summary: Elicit independent judgments from multiple experts, surface the reasons for disagreement, and iterate without forcing face-to-face consensus.

steps.title: Question
steps.prompt: Define the judgment or forecast to be elicited from the panel.

steps.title: Independent judgments
steps.prompt: Record the panel's initial estimates or judgments and their key reasons.

steps.title: Areas of dispersion
steps.prompt: Where do judgments differ most, and what assumptions or information explain the spread?

steps.title: Anonymous feedback
steps.prompt: Summarize the range of views and strongest reasons without attaching status or personality to them.

steps.title: Revised judgments
steps.prompt: Record revised judgments, remaining disagreement, and the information that would most reduce uncertainty.

definition.name: Red Hat Analysis
definition.summary: Adopt an actor's perspective with emphasis on how that actor may perceive the situation differently from the analyst.

steps.title: Actor
steps.prompt: Identify the actor whose perspective is being modeled.

steps.title: Perception
steps.prompt: How might the actor define the situation based on its information, history, culture, and incentives?

steps.title: Interests and fears
steps.prompt: What outcomes does the actor seek, tolerate, or fear most?

steps.title: Perceived choices
steps.prompt: Which actions might appear reasonable or necessary from that perspective?

steps.title: Observable signatures
steps.prompt: What behavior would support or weaken this perspective model?

definition.name: Complexity Manager
definition.summary: Decompose a complicated problem into interacting components so key dependencies and leverage points can be examined separately.

steps.title: Complex problem
steps.prompt: State the problem and why it is difficult to reason about as a whole.

steps.title: Components
steps.prompt: Break it into actors, processes, constraints, resources, uncertainties, or other meaningful parts.

steps.title: Dependencies
steps.prompt: Which components strongly affect or depend on one another?

steps.title: Critical components
steps.prompt: Which components are most influential, uncertain, or vulnerable?

steps.title: Next analytic moves
steps.prompt: Which parts should be analyzed, monitored, or modeled in greater depth first?

definition.name: Five Whys
definition.summary: Trace a problem through successive layers of causation instead of stopping at the first plausible explanation.

steps.title: Problem
steps.prompt: State the observable problem without embedding a cause.

steps.title: Why chain
steps.prompt: Ask why the problem occurred, then ask why each answer was possible until you reach actionable underlying causes.

steps.title: Alternative branches
steps.prompt: Where could the causal chain branch into multiple contributing causes?

steps.title: Verification
steps.prompt: What evidence would verify or falsify the proposed underlying causes?

steps.title: Actionable cause
steps.prompt: Which cause is both well-supported and useful to address?

prerequisites: Willingness to verify proposed causes rather than stop at plausible stories

definition.name: Fishbone / Ishikawa Analysis
definition.summary: Generate and organize possible causes of a problem across distinct causal families before narrowing them.

steps.title: Effect
steps.prompt: Define the problem or effect to explain.

steps.title: Cause categories
steps.prompt: Choose useful causal families such as people, process, equipment, environment, materials, policy, or information.

steps.title: Possible causes
steps.prompt: Generate candidate causes within each category without selecting a favorite too early.

steps.title: Priority causes
steps.prompt: Which candidate causes are most plausible, consequential, and testable?

steps.title: Verification plan
steps.prompt: What observations or tests could distinguish the leading causes?

definition.name: Is / Is Not Analysis
definition.summary: Define a problem by contrasting where, when, and how it appears with closely related cases where it does not.

steps.title: Problem
steps.prompt: State the deviation or failure precisely.

steps.title: Where it is
steps.prompt: Describe what, where, when, and to what extent the problem occurs.

steps.title: Where it is not
steps.prompt: Describe similar contexts where the problem could occur but does not.

steps.title: Meaningful differences
steps.prompt: What differences between the IS and IS NOT cases could explain the pattern?

steps.title: Cause tests
steps.prompt: Which differences can be tested as candidate causes?

definition.name: 5W2H Problem Definition
definition.summary: Clarify an ambiguous problem by forcing explicit answers to who, what, when, where, why, how, and how much.

steps.title: Who?
steps.prompt: Who is involved, affected, responsible, or observing?

steps.title: What?
steps.prompt: What exactly is happening or failing?

steps.title: When and where?
steps.prompt: When and where does it occur, and when or where does it not?

steps.title: Why and how?
steps.prompt: Why does it matter, and how does the process or event unfold?

steps.title: How much / how many?
steps.prompt: Quantify frequency, duration, magnitude, cost, scope, or affected population where possible.

definition.name: Pareto Prioritization
definition.summary: Rank recurring causes, issues, or losses by contribution so attention goes first to the few that drive most of the impact.

steps.title: Items
steps.prompt: List the recurring causes, defect types, incidents, requests, or losses being compared.

steps.title: Measure
steps.prompt: Choose a consistent impact measure such as frequency, cost, delay, harm, or effort.

steps.title: Rank contribution
steps.prompt: Order the items from largest to smallest contribution.

steps.title: Cumulative impact
steps.prompt: Which small set accounts for a large share of the total burden?

steps.title: Focus
steps.prompt: Which high-contribution items should be investigated or improved first?

definition.name: SIPOC Analysis
definition.summary: Map a process at high level through suppliers, inputs, process, outputs, and customers to clarify scope and dependencies.

steps.title: Process
steps.prompt: Define the process in a small number of major steps.

steps.title: Suppliers and inputs
steps.prompt: What inputs are required and who or what supplies them?

steps.title: Outputs
steps.prompt: What does the process produce, intentionally or unintentionally?

steps.title: Customers / recipients
steps.prompt: Who receives, depends on, or is affected by the outputs?

steps.title: Gaps and failure points
steps.prompt: Where are requirements unclear, handoffs fragile, or dependencies poorly controlled?

definition.name: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)
definition.summary: Anticipate how a system, process, or plan can fail and prioritize failure modes by consequence and detectability.

steps.title: Scope
steps.prompt: Define the system, process, plan, or component being analyzed.

steps.title: Failure modes
steps.prompt: List ways each important function could fail or degrade.

steps.title: Effects and causes
steps.prompt: For each failure mode, identify likely effects and plausible causes.

steps.title: Priority
steps.prompt: Which failures combine high consequence, plausible occurrence, and poor detectability?

steps.title: Controls and mitigations
steps.prompt: What prevention, detection, redundancy, or contingency measures would reduce risk?

prerequisites: Defined product, process, or service scope
A cross-functional team able to judge failure effects and controls

definition.name: Fault Tree Analysis
definition.summary: Reason backward from an unwanted top event through combinations of failures or conditions that could produce it.

steps.title: Top event
steps.prompt: State the specific unwanted event or failure.

steps.title: Immediate causes
steps.prompt: What directly necessary or sufficient conditions could produce the top event?

steps.title: Decompose
steps.prompt: For each cause, identify lower-level failures, dependencies, and combinations that could produce it.

steps.title: Common causes
steps.prompt: Are multiple branches vulnerable to the same dependency, environment, assumption, or control failure?

steps.title: Critical paths
steps.prompt: Which minimal combinations of failures deserve the most attention or mitigation?

definition.name: Event Tree Analysis
definition.summary: Reason forward from an initiating event through branching successes and failures to identify possible outcomes.

steps.title: Initiating event
steps.prompt: Define the event that starts the sequence.

steps.title: Key barriers or decisions
steps.prompt: List the safeguards, responses, decisions, or conditions that shape what happens next.

steps.title: Success / failure branches
steps.prompt: For each branch point, trace materially different paths depending on whether it succeeds, fails, or behaves unexpectedly.

steps.title: Outcomes
steps.prompt: Describe the important end states produced by the branching paths.

steps.title: Critical branches
steps.prompt: Which branches dominate risk, uncertainty, or opportunity?

definition.name: Bow-Tie Analysis
definition.summary: Connect threats and causes to a top event, then map preventive and mitigative barriers, degradation factors, and assurance needs around it.

steps.title: Top event
steps.prompt: Define the loss-of-control event that separates preventive from mitigative reasoning.

steps.title: Threats and preventive barriers
steps.prompt: List credible threats or causes leading to the top event and the preventive barriers intended to stop each path.
steps.placeholder: One threat / barrier path per line

steps.title: Consequences and mitigative barriers
steps.prompt: Identify material consequences after the top event and the barriers intended to detect, contain, recover, or reduce harm.
steps.placeholder: One consequence / barrier path per line

steps.title: Escalation factors and dependencies
steps.prompt: Identify conditions that degrade barriers, shared dependencies, common-cause failures, bypasses, and controls for those escalation factors.

steps.title: Barrier assurance
steps.prompt: Assign owners, performance standards, monitoring, verification, and follow-up for the barriers carrying the most risk reduction.

definition.name: HAZOP-Style Guideword Review
definition.summary: Systematically perturb intended behavior with guidewords to discover deviations, causes, consequences, and safeguards.

steps.title: Intended behavior
steps.prompt: Describe what the process, system, or plan is supposed to do.

steps.title: Guideword deviations
steps.prompt: Consider deviations such as none, more, less, reverse, other-than, early, late, or intermittent.

steps.title: Causes
steps.prompt: What could produce each meaningful deviation?

steps.title: Consequences
steps.prompt: What would follow if the deviation occurred?

steps.title: Safeguards and actions
steps.prompt: What existing controls address it, and what additional action is warranted?

definition.name: Plan–Do–Check–Act (PDCA)
definition.summary: Run a bounded improvement cycle that turns assumptions about a change into observable results and revision.

steps.title: Plan
steps.prompt: Define the problem, desired change, prediction, measures, and implementation plan.

steps.title: Do
steps.prompt: Describe the smallest practical test or implementation and what actually happened.

steps.title: Check
steps.prompt: Compare observed results with the prediction using the chosen measures.

steps.title: Act
steps.prompt: Adopt, adapt, abandon, or run another cycle based on what was learned.

steps.title: Learning
steps.prompt: What changed in your understanding of the system or problem?

definition.name: 8D Problem Solving
definition.summary: Use a disciplined sequence for team-based containment, root-cause verification, corrective action, and prevention of recurrence.

steps.title: Define the problem
steps.prompt: Specify the problem and its impact precisely.

steps.title: Containment
steps.prompt: What temporary actions prevent further impact while causes are investigated?

steps.title: Root cause
steps.prompt: Identify and verify the causes of occurrence and escape.

steps.title: Corrective action
steps.prompt: Choose, test, and implement actions that eliminate the verified causes.

steps.title: Prevent recurrence
steps.prompt: What system, process, standard, or control changes keep the problem from returning elsewhere?

definition.name: Causal Loop Mapping
definition.summary: Map reinforcing and balancing feedback loops, delays, evidence strength, and changing loop dominance to explain system behavior.

steps.title: System, behavior, and variables
steps.prompt: Define the system boundary, time horizon, behavior pattern to explain, and the quantities or conditions that materially change over time.

steps.title: Signed causal links
steps.prompt: For each important pair, state whether a rise in one tends to raise or lower the other, all else equal, and distinguish measured, inferred, and speculative links.

steps.title: Feedback loops
steps.prompt: Close causal chains into reinforcing and balancing loops and identify the delays that materially change their behavior.

steps.title: Evidence and weak links
steps.prompt: Identify loops that depend on fragile assumptions, missing observations, uncertain polarity, or poorly evidenced causal links.

steps.title: Behavior and loop dominance
steps.prompt: Explain which loops plausibly dominate under current conditions, what unintended consequences follow, and what observations would indicate a shift in dominance.

definition.name: Rich Picture
definition.summary: Represent a messy situation as interacting actors, concerns, structures, conflicts, flows, and uncertainties before imposing a narrow model.

steps.title: Situation
steps.prompt: Describe the messy situation without trying to simplify it yet.

steps.title: Elements
steps.prompt: List relevant people, organizations, processes, resources, constraints, emotions, conflicts, and environmental factors.

steps.title: Connections
steps.prompt: What relationships, flows, tensions, absences, or feedbacks connect the elements?

steps.title: Perspectives
steps.prompt: How do different participants understand the situation differently?

steps.title: Emerging insights
steps.prompt: What important features become visible before formal modeling begins?

definition.name: Boundary Critique
definition.summary: Challenge what an analysis includes, excludes, privileges, or treats as outside scope.

steps.title: Current boundary
steps.prompt: What is currently considered part of the problem or system?

steps.title: Excluded factors
steps.prompt: What actors, effects, time horizons, populations, or dependencies sit outside the current boundary?

steps.title: Who benefits?
steps.prompt: Whose goals, measures, and definitions of success dominate the framing?

steps.title: Who bears consequences?
steps.prompt: Who is affected but has little influence over the framing or decision?

steps.title: Boundary changes
steps.prompt: How would expanding or shrinking the boundary change the analysis or preferred action?

definition.name: Behavior-Over-Time Analysis
definition.summary: Examine how a variable changes over time so trends, oscillations, delays, thresholds, and regime shifts become visible.

steps.title: Variable
steps.prompt: Choose the quantity or condition whose behavior matters.

steps.title: Observed history
steps.prompt: Describe or record its behavior across a meaningful time window.

steps.title: Pattern
steps.prompt: Is the behavior growing, declining, oscillating, saturating, spiking, or shifting regimes?

steps.title: Events versus structure
steps.prompt: Which visible events may be symptoms rather than underlying causes of the pattern?

steps.title: Structural hypotheses
steps.prompt: What feedbacks, constraints, delays, or external drivers could generate this behavior?

definition.name: Reference Class Forecasting
definition.summary: Anchor a forecast in outcomes from comparable past cases before adjusting for the specifics of the current case.

steps.title: Target case
steps.prompt: Define exactly what is being forecast.

steps.title: Reference class
steps.prompt: Identify genuinely comparable past cases rather than only memorable examples.
steps.placeholder: One reference case or class per line

steps.title: Base rate
steps.prompt: What distribution of outcomes occurred in the reference class?

steps.title: Case-specific adjustments
steps.prompt: Which differences justify moving away from the base rate, and how strongly?

steps.title: Forecast
steps.prompt: State the resulting estimate, range, and main reasons it could still be wrong.

definition.name: Fermi Estimation
definition.summary: Decompose a difficult quantitative question into smaller estimable parts to produce an order-of-magnitude answer and expose uncertainty.

steps.title: Quantity to estimate
steps.prompt: State the quantity, unit, place, and time period.

steps.title: Decomposition
steps.prompt: Break the quantity into factors or subproblems that can be estimated independently.

steps.title: Component estimates
steps.prompt: Estimate each component using known anchors, bounds, or simple assumptions.

steps.title: Combine
steps.prompt: Calculate the implied total and keep track of units.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Which assumptions dominate the result, and what plausible range follows from varying them?

definition.name: Value of Information
definition.summary: Decide what to investigate next by comparing the cost of uncertainty with the expected value of reducing it.

steps.title: Decision
steps.prompt: State the decision that must eventually be made.

steps.title: Key uncertainties
steps.prompt: List uncertain facts or variables that could change the preferred decision.

steps.title: Decision impact
steps.prompt: How differently would you act under plausible values of each uncertainty?

steps.title: Possible information
steps.prompt: What research, collection, experiment, or observation could reduce each uncertainty?

steps.title: Information priority
steps.prompt: Which information has the highest expected decision value relative to its cost, delay, and feasibility?

definition.name: Decision Tree Analysis
definition.summary: Lay out sequential choices, uncertain events, and consequences so contingent decisions and tradeoffs are explicit.

steps.title: Initial decision
steps.prompt: State the choice and available options.

steps.title: Uncertain events
steps.prompt: For each option, list important uncertain events that could occur next.

steps.title: Subsequent choices
steps.prompt: What follow-on choices become available under each important outcome?

steps.title: Consequences
steps.prompt: Describe the costs, benefits, risks, or other outcomes at the end of each major path.

steps.title: Compare paths
steps.prompt: Which paths dominate, which depend on uncertain assumptions, and where would more information matter?

definition.name: Bayesian Update Worksheet
definition.summary: Revise a belief explicitly by separating the prior view from how strongly new evidence favors competing explanations.

steps.title: Hypotheses
steps.prompt: State the competing explanations or states being considered.

steps.title: Prior belief
steps.prompt: Before the new evidence, how plausible was each hypothesis and why?

steps.title: New evidence
steps.prompt: State the new observation as neutrally as possible.

steps.title: Expectedness
steps.prompt: How expected would this evidence be if each hypothesis were true?

steps.title: Updated belief
steps.prompt: How should the relative plausibility change after considering the evidence, and what remains uncertain?

definition.name: Confounder Check
definition.summary: Challenge a claimed causal relationship by searching for common causes, selection effects, reverse causality, and measurement artifacts.

steps.title: Causal claim
steps.prompt: State the proposed cause-and-effect relationship.

steps.title: Alternative causal structures
steps.prompt: Could a third factor drive both variables, could causality run backward, or could selection create the pattern?

steps.title: Measurement issues
steps.prompt: Could definitions, instrumentation, missing data, aggregation, or timing create the observed association?

steps.title: Discriminating tests
steps.prompt: What observations or designs would distinguish the claimed mechanism from these alternatives?

steps.title: Assessment
steps.prompt: How much causal confidence remains after the challenge?

definition.name: Falsification Test Design
definition.summary: Turn a favored explanation into risky predictions that could genuinely show it to be wrong.

steps.title: Hypothesis
steps.prompt: State the explanation precisely enough that it has observable implications.

steps.title: Risky predictions
steps.prompt: What should be observed if the hypothesis is true that would not be expected otherwise?

steps.title: Failure conditions
steps.prompt: What observation would seriously weaken or falsify the hypothesis?

steps.title: Tests
steps.prompt: What feasible observations, comparisons, or experiments could expose those failure conditions?

steps.title: Interpretation rules
steps.prompt: Define in advance how different results would change confidence.

definition.name: Robustness Check
definition.summary: Test whether a conclusion survives reasonable changes in assumptions, definitions, samples, thresholds, and model choices.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.prompt: State the result being stress-tested.

steps.title: Analytic choices
steps.prompt: List assumptions, definitions, thresholds, data subsets, and model choices that could reasonably differ.

steps.title: Reasonable variants
steps.prompt: For each choice, define plausible alternatives rather than extreme strawmen.

steps.title: Result stability
steps.prompt: Which variants preserve, weaken, reverse, or fragment the conclusion?

steps.title: Robust conclusion
steps.prompt: What can still be claimed confidently, and what depends on fragile analytic choices?

definition.name: Affinity Mapping
definition.summary: Cluster many observations or ideas by emergent similarity so themes arise from the material rather than a predetermined taxonomy.

steps.title: Items
steps.prompt: List the observations, quotes, issues, or ideas to organize.

steps.title: Emergent clusters
steps.prompt: Group items that seem meaningfully related without naming the groups too early.

steps.title: Theme labels
steps.prompt: Name each cluster in a way that captures why its items belong together.

steps.title: Outliers and tensions
steps.prompt: Which items resist clustering or connect multiple themes?
steps.placeholder: One outlier or tension per line

steps.title: Insights
steps.prompt: What themes, gaps, or relationships deserve deeper investigation?

definition.name: Journey Analysis
definition.summary: Trace an experience or process from the perspective of a participant to expose handoffs, friction, needs, and failure points.

steps.title: Actor
steps.prompt: Identify whose journey is being examined.

steps.title: Stages
steps.prompt: List the major stages from trigger through completion or abandonment.

steps.title: Actions and decisions
steps.prompt: What does the actor try to do at each stage, and what decisions arise?

steps.title: Friction and unmet needs
steps.prompt: Where do confusion, delay, workarounds, errors, or unmet needs appear?

steps.title: Improvement opportunities
steps.prompt: Which changes would remove the most important friction or uncertainty?

definition.name: Assumption Mapping
definition.summary: Separate assumptions by importance and uncertainty so the riskiest beliefs are tested first.

steps.title: Goal or proposal
steps.prompt: State the decision, product, plan, or strategy under consideration.

steps.title: Assumptions
steps.prompt: List the beliefs that must hold for it to succeed.

steps.title: Importance
steps.prompt: Which assumptions have the largest effect on success or failure?

steps.title: Uncertainty
steps.prompt: Which important assumptions are supported weakly or indirectly?

steps.title: Test order
steps.prompt: Prioritize cheap, fast tests for assumptions that are both important and uncertain.

definition.name: Stakeholder Analysis
definition.summary: Map who can affect or is affected by an issue, then compare interests, influence, incentives, and likely responses.

steps.title: Issue
steps.prompt: Define the decision, change, conflict, or system being analyzed.

steps.title: Stakeholders
steps.prompt: List affected and influential actors, including less visible groups.

steps.title: Interests and incentives
steps.prompt: What does each stakeholder want, fear, gain, or lose?

steps.title: Influence and dependencies
steps.prompt: Who can block, enable, shape, or absorb the consequences of action?

steps.title: Likely responses
steps.prompt: How might key stakeholders react under different choices or outcomes?

definition.name: Attack Tree Analysis
definition.summary: Reason backward from an adversary objective through alternative and combined paths that could achieve it.

steps.title: Adversary goal
steps.prompt: State the undesirable objective the attacker or competitor seeks.

steps.title: Primary paths
steps.prompt: List distinct high-level ways the goal could be achieved.

steps.title: Subgoals and prerequisites
steps.prompt: Break each path into required actions, access, capabilities, and conditions.

steps.title: Weak links
steps.prompt: Which prerequisites are easiest to disrupt, detect, or make costly?

steps.title: Coverage gaps
steps.prompt: What plausible attack paths remain outside current defenses or assumptions?

definition.name: STRIDE Threat Review
definition.summary: Prompt a systematic threat review across spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service, and privilege escalation.

steps.title: Asset or system
steps.prompt: Define the system, data, workflow, or trust boundary being reviewed.

steps.title: Threat categories
steps.prompt: For each STRIDE category, generate credible threats relevant to the system.

steps.title: Preconditions
steps.prompt: What access, weakness, dependency, or mistake would each threat require?

steps.title: Impact
steps.prompt: What confidentiality, integrity, availability, accountability, or control consequences could follow?

steps.title: Controls
steps.prompt: What prevention, detection, response, or recovery measures address the highest-priority threats?

definition.name: After-Action Review
definition.summary: Convert an event or project into learning by comparing intent, actual outcomes, causes, and changes for next time.

steps.title: What was intended?
steps.prompt: State the objective, plan, assumptions, and expected result.

steps.title: What actually happened?
steps.prompt: Describe outcomes and important deviations without assigning blame prematurely.

steps.title: Why was it different?
steps.prompt: Identify conditions, decisions, surprises, coordination issues, and assumptions that explain the gap.

steps.title: Keep / change
steps.prompt: What should be repeated, stopped, modified, or newly introduced?

steps.title: Transfer
steps.prompt: Where else should these lessons change practice, planning, or monitoring?

definition.name: Failure-Informed Redesign
definition.summary: Use identified failure mechanisms to redesign a plan around prevention, graceful degradation, recovery, and observability.

steps.title: Failure mechanisms
steps.prompt: List the most credible ways the plan or system could fail.

steps.title: Prevent
steps.prompt: What design changes reduce the chance of each failure?

steps.title: Graceful degradation
steps.prompt: If prevention fails, how can impact be limited rather than catastrophic?

steps.title: Recovery
steps.prompt: How can the system or team restore function quickly?

steps.title: Observability
steps.prompt: What indicators make emerging failure visible early enough to act?

definition.name: Close Reading
definition.summary: Analyze how precise choices in language, form, structure, imagery, and pattern create meaning within a passage and the work as a whole.

steps.title: Passage or scene
steps.prompt: Identify the bounded passage, scene, stanza, or sequence being examined.

steps.title: Salient details
steps.prompt: Mark striking diction, syntax, imagery, figurative language, sound, form, repetition, omissions, or disruptions.

steps.title: Patterns and contrasts
steps.prompt: Which details repeat, vary, oppose, or interrupt one another?

steps.title: Effects
steps.prompt: What interpretive, emotional, rhetorical, or structural effects do these choices produce?

steps.title: Relation to the whole
steps.prompt: How does the passage complicate or illuminate the larger work?

definition.name: Narratological Analysis
definition.summary: Examine how a narrative organizes story, discourse, sequence, duration, perspective, and information to shape interpretation.

steps.title: Story events
steps.prompt: Summarize what happens in chronological order.

steps.title: Presented order
steps.prompt: How does the text rearrange, omit, repeat, accelerate, or delay those events?

steps.title: Narrating voice
steps.prompt: Who tells the story, from what position, and with what degree of access or reliability?

steps.title: Time and pacing
steps.prompt: Where does narration linger, compress, loop backward, anticipate, or pause?

steps.title: Narrative effect
steps.prompt: How do these choices guide attention, sympathy, suspense, knowledge, or judgment?

definition.name: Focalization and Point-of-View Analysis
definition.summary: Separate who speaks from who perceives to track how perspective limits, filters, or distorts what readers can know.

steps.title: Narrator / speaker
steps.prompt: Who is speaking or narrating?

steps.title: Perceiving consciousness
steps.prompt: Through whose awareness are events, objects, or people filtered?

steps.title: Access and limits
steps.prompt: What can this perspective know, infer, misunderstand, or conceal?

steps.title: Perspective shifts
steps.prompt: Where does focalization change, widen, narrow, or become unstable?

steps.title: Interpretive effect
steps.prompt: How does perspective shape sympathy, irony, reliability, or uncertainty?

definition.name: Character and Agency Analysis
definition.summary: Examine characterization through action, speech, desire, conflict, relationships, constraints, and change rather than summary labels.

steps.title: Character evidence
steps.prompt: List actions, speech, descriptions, decisions, and reactions that materially characterize the figure.

steps.title: Desires and fears
steps.prompt: What does the character pursue, avoid, protect, or misunderstand?

steps.title: Constraints
steps.prompt: What social, material, psychological, narrative, or institutional forces shape available choices?

steps.title: Relationships
steps.prompt: How do other characters expose, reinforce, or challenge the figure's identity and agency?

steps.title: Change or persistence
steps.prompt: What changes, fails to change, or is revealed over the course of the work?

definition.name: Motif and Symbol Tracking
definition.summary: Track recurring images, objects, phrases, settings, or actions to test how their meanings accumulate and change.

steps.title: Recurring element
steps.prompt: Identify the image, object, phrase, setting, color, action, or symbol to track.

steps.title: Occurrences
steps.prompt: List significant appearances with surrounding context.

steps.title: Variation
steps.prompt: How does the element's form, context, speaker, or emotional valence change across occurrences?

steps.title: Associations
steps.prompt: What characters, themes, conflicts, or values become linked to it?

steps.title: Interpretive pattern
steps.prompt: What larger function or meaning is supported by the full pattern rather than a single instance?

definition.name: Theme and Tension Analysis
definition.summary: Develop thematic interpretations by tracing recurring questions, contradictions, competing values, and unresolved tensions across a work.

steps.title: Thematic question
steps.prompt: Frame the theme as an open problem or tension rather than a one-word topic.

steps.title: Textual evidence
steps.prompt: List passages or events that bear directly on the question.

steps.title: Competing positions
steps.prompt: What incompatible or partially compatible answers does the work stage?

steps.title: Complications
steps.prompt: Where does the text resist a simple thematic claim?

steps.title: Thematic interpretation
steps.prompt: State the strongest interpretation that preserves the work's important tensions.

definition.name: Intertextual Analysis
definition.summary: Trace allusion, quotation, adaptation, echo, genre memory, and other relationships between texts to see how meaning changes through reuse.

steps.title: Target text
steps.prompt: Identify the passage or work whose textual relationships are being examined.

steps.title: Possible intertexts
steps.prompt: List texts, traditions, genres, phrases, or cultural works that may be invoked.

steps.title: Evidence of connection
steps.prompt: What wording, structure, image, plot, convention, or historical relationship supports each connection?

steps.title: Transformation
steps.prompt: What is preserved, reversed, omitted, intensified, parodied, or reframed?

steps.title: Effect of the relationship
steps.prompt: How does recognizing the intertext alter interpretation of either work?

definition.name: Genre and Convention Analysis
definition.summary: Interpret a work by comparing what it does with the expectations, conventions, and hybrid possibilities of its genres.

steps.title: Candidate genres
steps.prompt: Identify genres or modes the work plausibly invokes.

steps.title: Expected conventions
steps.prompt: What formal, thematic, rhetorical, or plot conventions normally accompany those genres?

steps.title: Conformity
steps.prompt: Where does the work strongly follow those expectations?

steps.title: Departures
steps.prompt: Where does it violate, mix, parody, or transform conventions?

steps.title: Interpretive significance
steps.prompt: What does the handling of genre make possible or meaningful?

definition.name: Literary Rhetorical Analysis
definition.summary: Analyze how a text addresses audiences, constructs credibility, organizes appeals, and uses style to persuade or position readers.

steps.title: Rhetorical situation
steps.prompt: Who appears to speak, to whom, under what circumstances, and toward what apparent purpose?

steps.title: Appeals
steps.prompt: Identify appeals to authority, emotion, reason, values, identity, or shared assumptions.

steps.title: Rhetorical devices
steps.prompt: Track framing, repetition, questions, irony, analogy, juxtaposition, omission, or other persuasive devices.

steps.title: Audience positioning
steps.prompt: What roles, beliefs, emotions, or judgments does the text invite the audience to adopt?

steps.title: Rhetorical effect
steps.prompt: How do form and persuasion interact with the work's literary meaning?

definition.name: Structural and Semiotic Analysis
definition.summary: Examine systems of opposition, codes, signs, categories, and transformations that organize meaning beyond individual passages.

steps.title: Key signs and categories
steps.prompt: List recurrent signs, categories, roles, spaces, or concepts that structure the work.

steps.title: Binary or graded oppositions
steps.prompt: What contrasts organize the text: self/other, center/margin, nature/culture, order/disorder, sacred/profane, or others?

steps.title: Structural rules
steps.prompt: What combinations, substitutions, exclusions, or transformations recur?

steps.title: Instabilities
steps.prompt: Where do categories blur, reverse, or fail?

steps.title: System-level interpretation
steps.prompt: What does the pattern of signs and oppositions make thinkable or difficult within the work?

definition.name: Reader-Response Analysis
definition.summary: Examine how a text structures acts of reading and how different readers or interpretive communities may construct different meanings.

steps.title: Reader expectations
steps.prompt: What assumptions, genre knowledge, values, or prior information does the text appear to expect?

steps.title: Gaps and invitations
steps.prompt: Where must readers infer, imagine, judge, connect, or resolve ambiguity?

steps.title: Possible responses
steps.prompt: What emotions, judgments, identifications, or resistances might different readers experience?

steps.title: Interpretive communities
steps.prompt: How could historically or culturally different readerships read the same features differently?

steps.title: Textual constraints
steps.prompt: Which interpretations remain strongly constrained by the text despite reader variation?

definition.name: Historical-Contextual Literary Analysis
definition.summary: Relate a literary work to historical conditions, institutions, debates, genres, and audiences without reducing the text to background context.

steps.title: Relevant context
steps.prompt: Identify the historical circumstances most plausibly connected to the text's production or reception.

steps.title: Contextual evidence
steps.prompt: What external evidence establishes the relevance of those conditions?

steps.title: Text-context links
steps.prompt: Where does the work engage, reproduce, evade, or contest those conditions?

steps.title: Alternative contextualizations
steps.prompt: Could a different historical frame explain the same textual features better?

steps.title: Integrated interpretation
steps.prompt: How does context sharpen interpretation without substituting for close reading?

definition.name: Poetic Form and Prosody Analysis
definition.summary: Analyze meter, rhythm, lineation, rhyme, sound, stanza, syntax, and visual form as meaning-bearing structures.

steps.title: Formal structure
steps.prompt: Describe stanza, line, meter, rhythm, rhyme, typography, or other visible and audible organization.

steps.title: Sound patterning
steps.prompt: Track rhyme, alliteration, assonance, consonance, stress, pause, and sonic repetition.

steps.title: Syntax versus line
steps.prompt: Where do sentence structure, line breaks, caesura, and enjambment reinforce or resist one another?

steps.title: Variation and disruption
steps.prompt: Where does the poem depart from its established formal expectations?

steps.title: Formal meaning
steps.prompt: How do these formal choices shape emphasis, pace, tone, ambiguity, or theme?

definition.name: Textual Criticism
definition.summary: Compare textual witnesses and variants to assess transmission history and determine what readings are earlier, later, or otherwise significant.

steps.title: Passage and witnesses
steps.prompt: Identify the passage and the manuscripts, editions, translations, or textual witnesses being compared.

steps.title: Variants
steps.prompt: List meaningful differences in wording, order, omission, addition, or orthography.

steps.title: External evidence
steps.prompt: Assess date, provenance, textual family, independence, and transmission relationships of the witnesses.

steps.title: Internal evidence
steps.prompt: Which readings better explain how the alternatives could have arisen through copying, editing, harmonization, or correction?

steps.title: Textual assessment
steps.prompt: State the best-supported reading or preserve uncertainty where evidence remains balanced.

definition.name: Source Criticism
definition.summary: Investigate whether a text draws on distinguishable earlier sources, traditions, documents, or compositional layers.

steps.title: Textual unit
steps.prompt: Define the passage or corpus whose compositional sources are being investigated.

steps.title: Source signals
steps.prompt: Identify duplications, tensions, vocabulary shifts, seams, parallel accounts, or changes in viewpoint.

steps.title: Possible sources
steps.prompt: Propose the smallest useful set of sources or traditions that could explain the evidence.

steps.title: Competing explanations
steps.prompt: Could genre, rhetoric, development of argument, or later transmission explain the same features without separate sources?

steps.title: Source hypothesis
steps.prompt: State what source relationships are well-supported, tentative, or unsupported.

definition.name: Form Criticism
definition.summary: Identify a textual unit's genre or conventional form and infer how its shape relates to recurring social, ritual, pedagogical, or communal uses.

steps.title: Unit
steps.prompt: Delimit the smallest coherent textual or oral unit being studied.

steps.title: Form and genre
steps.prompt: Identify recurring structural features, formulas, motifs, speech forms, or conventional sequences.

steps.title: Comparable forms
steps.prompt: What other examples share enough structure or function to support a genre classification?

steps.title: Likely setting in use
steps.prompt: What social, ritual, legal, pedagogical, commemorative, or communal setting could make this form useful?

steps.title: Limits
steps.prompt: Which inferences about original use remain uncertain or overly dependent on reconstruction?

definition.name: Redaction Criticism
definition.summary: Study how an editor or compiler shapes inherited material through selection, arrangement, addition, omission, and modification.

steps.title: Parallel or source material
steps.prompt: Identify related versions or plausible source material for comparison.

steps.title: Editorial changes
steps.prompt: List additions, omissions, reorderings, substitutions, transitions, and framing changes.

steps.title: Editorial patterns
steps.prompt: Which changes recur consistently enough to suggest priorities or tendencies?

steps.title: Compositional purpose
steps.prompt: What concerns, audience needs, arguments, or theological emphases might the editing serve?

steps.title: Limits of inference
steps.prompt: What cannot be confidently attributed to editorial intention?

definition.name: Historical-Critical Analysis
definition.summary: Interpret a religious text in relation to its historical settings, languages, institutions, audiences, and processes of composition and transmission.

steps.title: Historical question
steps.prompt: Specify the historical problem rather than asking only what the text means now.

steps.title: Context
steps.prompt: Identify relevant political, social, economic, religious, linguistic, and material conditions.

steps.title: Historical evidence
steps.prompt: Separate evidence from the text, archaeology, inscriptions, comparative texts, and later tradition.

steps.title: Historical reconstruction
steps.prompt: What account best explains the evidence while minimizing unsupported assumptions?

steps.title: Text and reconstruction
steps.prompt: Clearly distinguish what the text claims, what historians infer, and what remains uncertain.

definition.name: Reception History
definition.summary: Trace how a text, figure, doctrine, image, or practice has been interpreted, used, contested, and transformed across communities and periods.

steps.title: Object of reception
steps.prompt: Identify the text, figure, doctrine, symbol, or practice being traced.

steps.title: Reception episodes
steps.prompt: List significant interpretations, adaptations, controversies, performances, artworks, institutions, or practices.

steps.title: Contexts
steps.prompt: What historical needs, institutions, power relations, media, or debates shaped each reception?

steps.title: Transformation
steps.prompt: What meanings are preserved, forgotten, amplified, reversed, or newly created?
