steps.title: Reception pattern
steps.prompt: What does the history of reception reveal that a single-period reading would miss?

definition.name: Comparative Religious Analysis
definition.summary: Compare traditions, practices, concepts, or institutions using explicit dimensions while resisting superficial equivalence and assumed universals.

steps.title: Objects of comparison
steps.prompt: Define exactly which traditions, practices, texts, communities, or concepts are being compared.

steps.title: Comparison dimensions
steps.prompt: Choose dimensions that are meaningful in both cases rather than forcing one tradition's categories onto another.

steps.title: Similarities
steps.prompt: Identify comparable structures or functions and specify the evidence.

steps.title: Differences and asymmetries
steps.prompt: Where do apparent similarities break down because histories, meanings, institutions, or categories differ?

steps.title: Comparative insight
steps.prompt: What can be learned from the comparison without collapsing important differences?

definition.name: Ritual Analysis
definition.summary: Analyze ritual as patterned action by examining sequence, participants, space, objects, symbols, authority, embodiment, and social effects.

steps.title: Ritual event
steps.prompt: Define the ritual, ceremony, observance, or repeated practice being studied.

steps.title: Sequence and roles
steps.prompt: Map major actions, transitions, participants, specialists, audiences, and role changes.

steps.title: Space and materiality
steps.prompt: How do place, objects, dress, sound, gesture, food, images, or technologies participate in the ritual?

steps.title: Meanings and interpretations
steps.prompt: How do participants and observers explain or experience what occurs?

steps.title: Social effects
steps.prompt: How might the ritual create identity, authority, memory, boundaries, solidarity, conflict, or transformation?

definition.name: Lived Religion Analysis
definition.summary: Study religion as practiced in everyday life rather than assuming official doctrine, institutions, or elite texts fully describe experience.

steps.title: People and setting
steps.prompt: Identify the people, households, networks, or local settings being studied.

steps.title: Everyday practice
steps.prompt: What do people actually do, say, display, avoid, improvise, or combine in ordinary life?

steps.title: Sources of authority
steps.prompt: Which texts, leaders, family traditions, media, memories, objects, or personal experiences carry authority?

steps.title: Variation and negotiation
steps.prompt: Where does lived practice differ from official teaching or vary across age, gender, class, place, or circumstance?

steps.title: Lived configuration
steps.prompt: How do people assemble religious meaning within the constraints and possibilities of everyday life?

definition.name: Social-Scientific Analysis of Religion
definition.summary: Examine religious behavior and institutions using social roles, networks, incentives, identity, authority, demography, and group dynamics.

steps.title: Phenomenon
steps.prompt: Define the religious behavior, institution, movement, community, or change to explain.

steps.title: Levels of analysis
steps.prompt: Separate individual, network, organizational, institutional, and societal mechanisms.
steps.placeholder: One level or mechanism per line

steps.title: Relevant variables
steps.prompt: Identify incentives, status, identity, resources, authority, social ties, demography, conflict, or other plausible factors.

steps.title: Alternative explanations
steps.prompt: What competing social mechanisms could generate the same observed pattern?

steps.title: Evidence and limits
steps.prompt: What evidence distinguishes the explanations, and what religious meanings would be lost by a purely external account?

definition.name: Material Religion Analysis
definition.summary: Analyze how objects, bodies, architecture, images, media, landscapes, and sensory practices participate in religious life and meaning.

steps.title: Material focus
steps.prompt: Identify the object, body practice, building, image, landscape, medium, relic, clothing, food, or other material form.

steps.title: Use and handling
steps.prompt: Who makes, owns, displays, touches, sees, hears, consumes, moves through, or restricts access to it?

steps.title: Sensory dimensions
steps.prompt: How do sight, sound, touch, smell, taste, posture, movement, or spatial arrangement matter?

steps.title: Social and sacred relations
steps.prompt: What authority, memory, identity, presence, absence, or boundary does the material form organize?

steps.title: Change over time
steps.prompt: How do shifts in medium, ownership, technology, location, or regulation alter its religious significance?

definition.name: Hermeneutic Circle
definition.summary: Iteratively interpret parts of a text or tradition through the whole and revise the understanding of the whole through increasingly precise readings of its parts.

steps.title: Initial whole
steps.prompt: State your provisional understanding of the work, tradition, argument, or practice as a whole.

steps.title: Difficult or revealing part
steps.prompt: Choose a passage, practice, symbol, or episode that tests that overall understanding.

steps.title: Fit and tension
steps.prompt: What does the part confirm, complicate, or contradict in the initial whole?

steps.title: Revised whole
steps.prompt: Revise the larger interpretation to account for the part without explaining away its difficulty.

steps.title: Next iteration
steps.prompt: Which additional part would most strongly test the revised interpretation?

definition.name: Myth and Symbol Analysis
definition.summary: Examine how narratives and symbols organize cosmology, identity, morality, social order, memory, and transformation within particular communities.

steps.title: Narrative or symbol
steps.prompt: Identify the mythic narrative, figure, image, place, object, or recurring symbolic complex.

steps.title: Narrative / symbolic structure
steps.prompt: What oppositions, transformations, archetypal roles, journeys, boundaries, or recurring relations organize it?

steps.title: Community contexts
steps.prompt: Who uses or interprets it, in what settings, and with what variations?

steps.title: Functions
steps.prompt: How might it orient identity, morality, authority, suffering, time, place, or collective memory?

steps.title: Interpretive limits
steps.prompt: Which meanings are supported by participants or evidence, and which are projections imposed by the analyst?

definition.name: Problem Restatement
definition.summary: Problem Restatement uses a Original problem → Embedded assumptions → Alternative restatements → What each frame reveals workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Original problem
steps.prompt: State the problem exactly as currently framed, including the decision, actor, scope, and time horizon.

steps.title: Embedded assumptions
steps.prompt: Identify assumptions, loaded terms, causal claims, and scope choices hidden in the wording.

steps.title: Alternative restatements
steps.prompt: Restate the problem from different actors, levels of analysis, time horizons, and causal perspectives.

steps.title: What each frame reveals
steps.prompt: For each restatement, identify evidence, alternatives, or collection needs that become more or less visible.

steps.title: Working formulation
steps.prompt: Choose the formulation that best supports the decision while preserving important uncertainty and explain why.

definition.name: Customer Checklist
definition.summary: Customer Checklist uses a Customer and decision → Need versus request → Scope and terms → Product requirements workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Customer and decision
steps.prompt: Identify the customer, decision, deadline, authorities, and consequences of being wrong.

steps.title: Need versus request
steps.prompt: Separate the customer's stated request from the underlying decision need, uncertainties, and constraints.

steps.title: Scope and terms
steps.prompt: Clarify actors, geography, time horizon, definitions, assumptions, and exclusions that bound the analysis.

steps.title: Product requirements
steps.prompt: Specify required depth, confidence language, sourcing, format, coordination, and delivery timing.

steps.title: Confirm understanding
steps.prompt: Restate the analytic task in decision-relevant terms and record unresolved questions or scope risks.

definition.name: Decomposition Tree
definition.summary: Decomposition Tree uses a Root problem → Primary branches → Subdivide → Coverage and overlap workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Root problem
steps.prompt: State the top-level problem or question as a single bounded node.

steps.title: Primary branches
steps.prompt: Break the root into collectively useful subproblems using one clear decomposition logic.

steps.title: Subdivide
steps.prompt: Continue decomposing until leaf questions are answerable with evidence or a defined analytic method.

steps.title: Coverage and overlap
steps.prompt: Check for missing branches, double counting, mixed levels, and dependencies that violate the tree structure.

steps.title: Prioritize leaves
steps.prompt: Identify which leaf questions are decision-critical, uncertain, time-sensitive, or prerequisite to other branches.

definition.name: Logic Tree
definition.summary: Logic Tree uses a Question → Branching rule → Build the tree → Logic test workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Question
steps.prompt: Define the decision or explanatory question the tree must resolve.

steps.title: Branching rule
steps.prompt: Choose a consistent logical split such as causes, options, conditions, or necessary components.

steps.title: Build the tree
steps.prompt: Decompose each branch into mutually intelligible subquestions while preserving the chosen logic.

steps.title: Logic test
steps.prompt: Check whether branches are exhaustive enough for the purpose, avoid hidden overlap, and expose assumptions at branch points.

steps.title: Analytic use
steps.prompt: Assign evidence, methods, owners, or judgments to terminal branches and identify where unresolved logic blocks the conclusion.

definition.name: Issue Tree
definition.summary: Issue Tree uses a Central issue → Issue branches → Subquestions → Evidence mapping workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Central issue
steps.prompt: Frame the central issue as a question whose answer would materially advance the decision.

steps.title: Issue branches
steps.prompt: Break it into the few major issues that jointly determine the answer.

steps.title: Subquestions
steps.prompt: Convert each branch into specific answerable questions and separate factual, causal, and evaluative questions.

steps.title: Evidence mapping
steps.prompt: Map available evidence and gaps to each terminal question so unsupported branches are visible.

steps.title: Synthesis path
steps.prompt: Define how answers to the branches will recombine into the top-level judgment and where dependencies or tradeoffs remain.

definition.name: MECE Decomposition
definition.summary: MECE Decomposition uses a Problem → Candidate dimensions → MECE partition → Exceptions and edge cases workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Problem
steps.prompt: State the problem and the purpose of decomposing it.

steps.title: Candidate dimensions
steps.prompt: Generate plausible ways to partition the problem by actor, stage, cause, geography, function, time, or another coherent dimension.

steps.title: MECE partition
steps.prompt: Choose a partition whose categories minimize overlap while covering the decision-relevant space.

steps.title: Exceptions and edge cases
steps.prompt: Test ambiguous cases, interactions, and omitted categories rather than forcing reality into a falsely clean partition.

steps.title: Apply the partition
steps.prompt: Use the categories to organize evidence or workstreams and record where non-MECE interactions must be handled explicitly.

definition.name: Question Decomposition
definition.summary: Question Decomposition uses a Original question → Clarify terms → Subquestions → Dependencies workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Original question
steps.prompt: State the question exactly and identify the decision or judgment it is intended to support.

steps.title: Clarify terms
steps.prompt: Define ambiguous terms, actors, units, time horizon, comparison class, and implied thresholds.

steps.title: Subquestions
steps.prompt: Break the question into factual, causal, comparative, forecasting, and evaluative subquestions as needed.

steps.title: Dependencies
steps.prompt: Identify which subquestions must be answered first and which can be analyzed independently or in parallel.

steps.title: Coverage check
steps.prompt: Confirm that answering the subquestions would actually resolve the original question and identify residual uncertainty.

definition.name: Assumption Surfacing
definition.summary: Assumption Surfacing uses a Judgment or plan → Surface assumptions → Evidence versus assumption → Criticality and uncertainty workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Judgment or plan
steps.prompt: State the conclusion, forecast, or plan whose assumptions need to be made explicit.

steps.title: Surface assumptions
steps.prompt: List factual, causal, behavioral, temporal, and boundary assumptions required for the reasoning to hold.

steps.title: Evidence versus assumption
steps.prompt: For each item, distinguish observed evidence, inference, convention, and unsupported assumption.

steps.title: Criticality and uncertainty
steps.prompt: Identify assumptions whose failure would most alter the judgment and those supported least securely.

steps.title: Tests and indicators
steps.prompt: Define evidence or signposts that would strengthen, weaken, or invalidate the most critical assumptions.

definition.name: Scope Boundary Matrix
definition.summary: Scope Boundary Matrix uses a Problem and purpose → Boundary dimensions → In / out / uncertain → Boundary effects workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Problem and purpose
steps.prompt: Define the analytic problem and why boundary choices matter to the result.

steps.title: Boundary dimensions
steps.prompt: List scope dimensions such as actors, geography, time, systems, populations, evidence types, and levels of analysis.

steps.title: In / out / uncertain
steps.prompt: For each dimension, record what is included, excluded, and intentionally left uncertain, with rationale.

steps.title: Boundary effects
steps.prompt: Test how plausible alternative boundaries would change evidence, causal explanations, stakeholders, or conclusions.

steps.title: Working boundary
steps.prompt: Adopt the narrowest defensible boundary for the task while documenting exclusions that could materially change the judgment.

definition.name: Stakeholder Question Matrix
definition.summary: Stakeholder Question Matrix uses a Stakeholders → Questions by stakeholder → Differences in perspective → Question gaps workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Stakeholders
steps.prompt: List the actors who decide, influence, implement, experience, or possess critical information about the issue.

steps.title: Questions by stakeholder
steps.prompt: For each stakeholder, identify the questions they need answered and the questions analysts need answered about them.

steps.title: Differences in perspective
steps.prompt: Compare incentives, information, definitions of success, and risk tolerances that make the questions diverge.

steps.title: Question gaps
steps.prompt: Identify decision-relevant questions with no clear owner, source, or analytic path and flag conflicting requirements.

steps.title: Priority question set
steps.prompt: Select the smallest cross-stakeholder question set that covers the decision without collapsing important disagreements.

definition.name: Key Intelligence Questions
definition.summary: Key Intelligence Questions uses a Decision context → Key intelligence questions → Priority and dependency → Information requirements workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Decision context
steps.prompt: What decision, warning problem, or uncertainty must the analysis support?

steps.title: Key intelligence questions
steps.prompt: Write the smallest set of answerable questions that would materially improve the decision.

steps.title: Priority and dependency
steps.prompt: Which questions are prerequisite, time-critical, or highest impact, and how do they depend on one another?

steps.title: Information requirements
steps.prompt: For each priority question, specify what information or observation would answer it.

steps.title: Coverage check
steps.prompt: What important decision uncertainty remains outside the question set?

definition.name: Intelligence Requirements Mapping
definition.summary: Intelligence Requirements Mapping uses a Decision and customer need → Priority requirements → Analytic questions → Information and source mapping workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Decision and customer need
steps.prompt: Define the decision, warning problem, or uncertainty the intelligence effort must support.

steps.title: Priority requirements
steps.prompt: Translate that need into bounded intelligence requirements and rank them by decision value and time sensitivity.

steps.title: Analytic questions
steps.prompt: Break each requirement into answerable questions while separating facts sought from judgments to be made.

steps.title: Information and source mapping
steps.prompt: Map each question to available evidence, candidate sources, collection disciplines, and known access limitations.

steps.title: Coverage and gaps
steps.prompt: Identify unanswered high-value questions, redundant collection, and requirements that should be revised because they are not observable or decision-relevant.

definition.name: Collection Gap Analysis
definition.summary: Collection Gap Analysis uses a Judgment or requirement → Known and supported → Material gaps → Gap impact workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Judgment or requirement
steps.prompt: State the judgment or intelligence requirement whose information base is being assessed.

steps.title: Known and supported
steps.prompt: List what is known, its source basis, and how directly it bears on the requirement.

steps.title: Material gaps
steps.prompt: List missing facts, inaccessible observations, stale reporting, and unresolved contradictions.

steps.title: Gap impact
steps.prompt: Which gaps could most change the judgment or confidence if resolved?

steps.title: Collection priorities
steps.prompt: Translate the highest-impact gaps into observable, feasible collection requirements.

definition.name: Problem Statement Canvas
definition.summary: Problem Statement Canvas uses a Situation → Problem gap → Affected actors and consequences → Knowns, assumptions, unknowns workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Situation
steps.prompt: Describe the observed situation and the decision context without embedding a preferred cause or solution.

steps.title: Problem gap
steps.prompt: State the difference between the current condition and the desired or acceptable condition, including scale and timing.

steps.title: Affected actors and consequences
steps.prompt: Identify who is affected, how, and what material consequences follow if the gap persists.

steps.title: Knowns, assumptions, unknowns
steps.prompt: Separate established facts from assumptions and the uncertainties that prevent a confident diagnosis.

steps.title: Working problem statement
steps.prompt: Write a concise, testable problem statement with scope, evidence basis, and explicit exclusions.

definition.name: Frame Analysis
definition.summary: Frame Analysis uses a Frame source → Frame elements → Foreground and background → Alternative frames workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Frame source
steps.prompt: Identify the statement, product, narrative, policy, or analytic formulation whose frame is being examined.

steps.title: Frame elements
steps.prompt: Identify problem definition, causal attribution, moral or evaluative language, actors, boundaries, metaphors, and implied remedies.

steps.title: Foreground and background
steps.prompt: What does the frame emphasize, normalize, exclude, or render difficult to see?

steps.title: Alternative frames
steps.prompt: Construct materially different frames from other actors, disciplines, scales, or causal assumptions.

steps.title: Analytic impact
steps.prompt: Assess how the chosen frame changes evidence selection, hypotheses, confidence, and policy or decision implications.

definition.name: Frame Shifting
definition.summary: Frame Shifting uses a Current frame → Shift dimensions → Generate shifted frames → Newly visible evidence and options workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Current frame
steps.prompt: State the current formulation and the assumptions or habitual categories it privileges.

steps.title: Shift dimensions
steps.prompt: Choose deliberate shifts in actor, scale, time horizon, geography, system boundary, causal direction, or objective.

steps.title: Generate shifted frames
steps.prompt: Reframe the issue along several selected dimensions without judging them immediately.

steps.title: Newly visible evidence and options
steps.prompt: For each shifted frame, identify explanations, stakeholders, evidence, risks, or actions that become visible.

steps.title: Frame portfolio
steps.prompt: Retain the frames that add distinct analytic value and note which conclusions depend heavily on one framing choice.

definition.name: Levels-of-Analysis Decomposition
definition.summary: Levels-of-Analysis Decomposition uses a Phenomenon → Levels → Mechanisms by level → Cross-level interactions workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Phenomenon
steps.prompt: Define the event, behavior, or outcome to explain and the time period of interest.

steps.title: Levels
steps.prompt: Separate plausible factors at individual, group, organizational, state, systemic, and environmental levels as appropriate.

steps.title: Mechanisms by level
steps.prompt: Explain how factors at each level could produce or constrain the observed outcome rather than merely naming variables.

steps.title: Cross-level interactions
steps.prompt: Identify mechanisms that connect levels, including feedback, delegation, institutions, incentives, and external constraints.

steps.title: Explanatory balance
steps.prompt: Judge which levels carry the most explanatory weight, what evidence would distinguish them, and where single-level explanations are inadequate.

definition.name: Actor-Interest Matrix
definition.summary: Actor-Interest Matrix uses a Actors → Interests and objectives → Influence and constraints → Alignment and conflict workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Actors
steps.prompt: Identify relevant actors at the appropriate level of aggregation and distinguish formal entities from internal factions where necessary.

steps.title: Interests and objectives
steps.prompt: For each actor, record desired outcomes, protected interests, fears, red lines, and time horizons.

steps.title: Influence and constraints
steps.prompt: Assess resources, authorities, dependencies, alliances, vulnerabilities, and constraints that shape each actor's choices.

steps.title: Alignment and conflict
steps.prompt: Compare where interests align, conflict, or are conditionally compatible and identify bargaining or escalation points.

steps.title: Analytic implications
steps.prompt: Use the matrix to derive likely coalitions, incentives, leverage points, and indicators that actor priorities are changing.

definition.name: Concept Mapping
definition.summary: Concept Mapping uses a Focus question → Key concepts → Labeled relationships → Hierarchy and cross-links workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Focus question
steps.prompt: Define the bounded question or domain the concept map is intended to clarify.

steps.title: Key concepts
steps.prompt: List the important entities, ideas, variables, categories, and processes without prematurely arranging them.

steps.title: Labeled relationships
steps.prompt: Connect concepts with explicit relationship labels so the map captures propositions rather than mere proximity.

steps.title: Hierarchy and cross-links
steps.prompt: Identify higher-order concepts, subordinate concepts, cross-links, feedbacks, and concepts that bridge otherwise separate clusters.

steps.title: Map review
steps.prompt: Check for missing concepts, ambiguous labels, circular definitions, and relationships that are asserted without evidence.

definition.name: Process Mapping
definition.summary: Process Mapping uses a Process scope → Process steps → Information and material flows → Exceptions and failure paths workflow to decompose ambiguous problems, expose scope choices, and turn broad questions into analyzable parts.

steps.title: Process scope
steps.prompt: Define the process start, end, customer or mission outcome, and level of detail.

steps.title: Process steps
steps.prompt: Map major activities, decisions, handoffs, inputs, outputs, and responsible actors in sequence.

steps.title: Information and material flows
steps.prompt: Record what information, data, authority, or material moves between steps and where queues or feedback occur.

steps.title: Exceptions and failure paths
steps.prompt: Identify rework, alternate paths, informal workarounds, bottlenecks, and conditions that cause the process to diverge from the nominal flow.

steps.title: Analytic insight
steps.prompt: Identify dependencies, control points, delays, vulnerabilities, and collection opportunities revealed by the mapped process.

definition.name: Source Reliability Assessment
definition.summary: Source Reliability Assessment uses a Source and access → Reliability → Motives and vulnerabilities → Independent corroboration workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Source and access
steps.prompt: Identify the source, its claimed access, reporting chain, and relevant track record.

steps.title: Reliability
steps.prompt: Assess whether the source has historically reported accurately and whether current access is direct, indirect, or uncertain.

steps.title: Motives and vulnerabilities
steps.prompt: What incentives, pressures, biases, deception risks, or misunderstandings could distort the reporting?

steps.title: Independent corroboration
steps.prompt: What genuinely independent evidence supports or contradicts the source?

steps.title: Assessment
steps.prompt: State a bounded reliability judgment and the caveats that matter most.

definition.name: Information Credibility Assessment
definition.summary: Information Credibility Assessment uses a Information item → Access and directness → Content credibility → Independent corroboration workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Information item
steps.prompt: State the reported information separately from the analyst's interpretation and identify its source chain.

steps.title: Access and directness
steps.prompt: Assess whether the information is firsthand, indirect, inferred, translated, summarized, or otherwise removed from the underlying event.

steps.title: Content credibility
steps.prompt: Evaluate internal consistency, specificity, plausibility, timing, and compatibility with independently established facts.

steps.title: Independent corroboration
steps.prompt: Identify genuinely independent support or contradiction and discount circular or derivative reporting.

steps.title: Credibility judgment
steps.prompt: State a bounded credibility assessment, the reasons for it, and what uncertainty or additional evidence matters most.

definition.name: Admiralty Code Evaluation
definition.summary: Admiralty Code Evaluation uses a Source reliability → Information credibility → Separate source from information → Corroboration and dependency workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Source reliability
steps.prompt: Assess the source's history, competence, access, and independence using the applicable reliability scale.

steps.title: Information credibility
steps.prompt: Assess how directly observed, plausible, corroborated, and internally consistent the reported information is.

steps.title: Separate source from information
steps.prompt: Keep source reliability and information credibility as distinct judgments; a reliable source can report weak information and vice versa.

steps.title: Corroboration and dependency
steps.prompt: Identify independent confirmation, contradiction, circular reporting, and common-source dependencies.

steps.title: Coded assessment
steps.prompt: Assign the code, explain the evidence for each dimension, and record uncertainty or reasons a code cannot be assigned.

definition.name: Source Validation Matrix
definition.summary: Source Validation Matrix uses a Claims and sources → Validation dimensions → Claim-source matrix → Dependencies and anomalies workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Claims and sources
steps.prompt: List the material claims and every source being used to support, qualify, or contradict them.

steps.title: Validation dimensions
steps.prompt: Assess each source for access, competence, track record, independence, motive, recency, and chain of reporting using consistent criteria.

steps.title: Claim-source matrix
steps.prompt: Map which sources directly support, indirectly support, contradict, or do not address each claim; distinguish source quality from information credibility.

steps.title: Dependencies and anomalies
steps.prompt: Identify common origins, circular reporting, unexplained inconsistencies, and sources whose apparent independence is doubtful.

steps.title: Validated support
steps.prompt: State which claims remain well supported, weakly supported, disputed, or unsupported and what validation work has highest value next.

definition.name: Corroboration Matrix
definition.summary: Corroboration Matrix uses a Claims → Source set → Claim-source matrix → Independence test workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Claims
steps.prompt: List the material claims that require corroboration.

steps.title: Source set
steps.prompt: List the sources or evidence streams and note likely dependencies among them.

steps.title: Claim-source matrix
steps.prompt: For each claim, record which independent sources support, contradict, or do not address it.

steps.title: Independence test
steps.prompt: Which apparent corroboration is actually circular, derivative, or based on a common origin?

steps.title: Corroboration result
steps.prompt: Which claims are robustly supported, singly sourced, disputed, or unsupported?

definition.name: Evidence Grading
definition.summary: Evidence Grading uses a Claim and decision relevance → Evidence items → Grade criteria → Body-of-evidence grade workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Claim and decision relevance
steps.prompt: State the claim and why the evidence quality matters to the judgment or decision.

steps.title: Evidence items
steps.prompt: List material evidence items with source, date, method, provenance, and directness.

steps.title: Grade criteria
steps.prompt: Assess reliability, validity, directness, independence, precision, recency, and risk of bias using a consistent scale.

steps.title: Body-of-evidence grade
steps.prompt: Integrate strengths and weaknesses across items rather than averaging mechanically.

steps.title: Confidence and limitations
steps.prompt: State the resulting evidence grade, major downgrade or upgrade reasons, and what evidence would most improve it.

definition.name: Evidence Provenance Mapping
definition.summary: Evidence Provenance Mapping uses a Claims and evidence → Origins → Transformations → Dependencies and breaks workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Claims and evidence
steps.prompt: List the material claims and the evidence items being used to support or challenge them.

steps.title: Origins
steps.prompt: Trace each evidence item to its earliest recoverable source, collection event, dataset, document, or observation.

steps.title: Transformations
steps.prompt: Record copying, translation, extraction, aggregation, filtering, analytic processing, and other transformations between origin and current use.

steps.title: Dependencies and breaks
steps.prompt: Identify shared origins, missing links, unverifiable steps, and transformations that could introduce error or false corroboration.

steps.title: Analytic impact
steps.prompt: Reassess which claims remain well-supported after provenance dependencies and uncertainties are made explicit.

definition.name: Chain-of-Custody Analysis
definition.summary: Chain-of-Custody Analysis uses a Evidence item → Custody timeline → Integrity controls → Gaps and anomalies workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Evidence item
steps.prompt: Identify the physical, digital, documentary, or data item whose handling history matters.

steps.title: Custody timeline
steps.prompt: Record each transfer, custodian, system, location, timestamp, and handling event in sequence.

steps.title: Integrity controls
steps.prompt: Assess authentication, hashes, seals, access controls, logging, storage conditions, and other controls relevant to the item.

steps.title: Gaps and anomalies
steps.prompt: Identify undocumented intervals, inconsistent timestamps, unauthorized access, format changes, or other integrity concerns.

steps.title: Usability assessment
steps.prompt: State what the custody record supports, what remains uncertain, and how any break affects evidentiary weight rather than treating custody as all-or-nothing.

definition.name: Source Independence Check
definition.summary: Source Independence Check uses a Candidate sources → Provenance paths → Dependency links → Independent clusters workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Candidate sources
steps.prompt: List the sources or evidence streams being treated as separate support.

steps.title: Provenance paths
steps.prompt: Trace ownership, collection, publication, funding, citations, intermediaries, and likely upstream origins.

steps.title: Dependency links
steps.prompt: Mark direct copying, shared datasets, common informants, coordinated messaging, or common institutional processes.

steps.title: Independent clusters
steps.prompt: Collapse dependent sources into common-origin clusters and identify genuinely independent lines of evidence.

steps.title: Analytic impact
steps.prompt: Reassess corroboration and confidence using the independent clusters rather than the raw source count.

definition.name: Circular Reporting Check
definition.summary: Circular Reporting Check uses a Claim under review → Reporting chain → Independent origins → Amplification effects workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Claim under review
steps.prompt: State the claim that appears to have multiple sources of support.

steps.title: Reporting chain
steps.prompt: Trace each citation, report, retelling, translation, and intermediary back toward its earliest recoverable origin.

steps.title: Independent origins
steps.prompt: Group reports that ultimately derive from the same source, event, dataset, or unattributed assertion.

steps.title: Amplification effects
steps.prompt: Identify repetition, laundering, or institutional cross-citation that creates false apparent corroboration.

steps.title: Reassess support
steps.prompt: Recalculate how many genuinely independent evidence streams remain and revise confidence accordingly.

definition.name: Missing Evidence Analysis
definition.summary: Missing Evidence Analysis uses a Hypothesis or judgment → Expected evidence → Observed absences → Alternative explanations for absence workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Hypothesis or judgment
steps.prompt: State the proposition whose expected evidence is being examined.

steps.title: Expected evidence
steps.prompt: If the proposition were true, what observable evidence should normally exist?

steps.title: Observed absences
steps.prompt: Which expected observations are missing, delayed, inaccessible, or ambiguous?

steps.title: Alternative explanations for absence
steps.prompt: Could denial, concealment, collection gaps, timing, low base rates, or a wrong hypothesis explain the absence?

steps.title: Update
steps.prompt: How should the missing evidence change confidence, and what observation would be most diagnostic next?

definition.name: Negative Evidence Analysis
definition.summary: Negative Evidence Analysis uses a Claim or hypothesis → Expected observations → Observability and collection → Reasons for absence workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Claim or hypothesis
steps.prompt: State the proposition for which an absence of expected evidence may be informative.

steps.title: Expected observations
steps.prompt: Identify what should normally be observable if the proposition is true, including timing and collection conditions.

steps.title: Observability and collection
steps.prompt: Assess whether existing collection had a realistic opportunity to detect each expected observation.

steps.title: Reasons for absence
steps.prompt: Test concealment, delay, rarity, collection failure, definitional error, and rival hypotheses as explanations for the absence.

steps.title: Evidentiary weight
steps.prompt: Judge how much the absence should change confidence and specify future observations that would make it more diagnostic.

definition.name: Competing Source Reconciliation
definition.summary: Competing Source Reconciliation uses a Conflicting reports → Source and provenance comparison → Definition and scope check → Reconciliation hypotheses workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Conflicting reports
steps.prompt: State the material disagreement among sources without prematurely choosing a winner.

steps.title: Source and provenance comparison
steps.prompt: Compare access, timing, independence, incentives, transformations, and reliability histories for each source.

steps.title: Definition and scope check
steps.prompt: Test whether apparent conflict results from different time windows, terminology, populations, measurement methods, or levels of aggregation.

steps.title: Reconciliation hypotheses
steps.prompt: Generate explanations that could make the reports jointly true, partly true, sequentially true, or genuinely incompatible.

steps.title: Reconciled assessment
steps.prompt: State the best-supported interpretation, preserve unresolved differences, and identify evidence that would resolve the remaining conflict.

definition.name: Translation Ambiguity Review
definition.summary: Translation Ambiguity Review uses a Source passage → Ambiguous terms → Alternative translations → Analytic impact workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Source passage
steps.prompt: Preserve the original-language passage, available translations, speaker or author, date, and surrounding context.

steps.title: Ambiguous terms
steps.prompt: Identify words, idioms, grammar, honorifics, technical terms, ellipsis, or cultural references that permit materially different readings.

steps.title: Alternative translations
steps.prompt: Record defensible translation alternatives and explain what linguistic or contextual evidence favors each one.

steps.title: Analytic impact
steps.prompt: For each ambiguity, determine whether competing translations change facts, intent, tone, confidence, attribution, or the resulting judgment.

steps.title: Handling decision
steps.prompt: Choose the safest rendering, preserve unresolved ambiguity explicitly, and identify where native-speaker or specialist review is required.

definition.name: Data Lineage Analysis
definition.summary: Data Lineage Analysis uses a Analytic product or dataset → Data origins → Transformations → Lineage risks workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Analytic product or dataset
steps.prompt: Identify the estimate, chart, model input, or claim whose data lineage must be understood.

steps.title: Data origins
steps.prompt: Trace observations to original collection systems, providers, surveys, sensors, records, or datasets and record ownership and timing.

steps.title: Transformations
steps.prompt: Map cleaning, filtering, joins, imputation, aggregation, recoding, model-derived fields, and manual edits applied before analytic use.

steps.title: Lineage risks
steps.prompt: Identify undocumented steps, schema changes, duplicated records, inherited bias, unit changes, stale extracts, or transformations that could alter meaning.

steps.title: Fitness for use
steps.prompt: State which downstream conclusions are supported by the lineage, which are fragile, and what provenance or validation gaps must be resolved.

definition.name: Collection Bias Audit
definition.summary: Collection Bias Audit uses a Analytic question → Collection architecture → Likely blind spots → Effect on judgments workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Analytic question
steps.prompt: State what the collection is being used to infer and the target population, activity, or environment the inference is meant to represent.

steps.title: Collection architecture
steps.prompt: Describe sensors, sources, platforms, tasking, access, reporting incentives, geographic coverage, language coverage, and time windows.

steps.title: Likely blind spots
steps.prompt: Identify systematic overcoverage and undercoverage caused by access, survivorship, visibility, security behavior, prioritization, reporting thresholds, or institutional incentives.

steps.title: Effect on judgments
steps.prompt: Test how each bias could distort frequency, trend, actor importance, apparent absence, correlation, or confidence in the current assessment.

steps.title: Mitigation and caveats
steps.prompt: Identify alternative collection, weighting, comparison groups, explicit caveats, and indicators that would reveal whether the bias is materially affecting conclusions.

definition.name: Sampling Bias Check
definition.summary: Sampling Bias Check uses a Target population → Observed sample → Representativeness check → Bias sensitivity workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Target population
steps.prompt: Define the population or event universe the analysis intends to characterize.

steps.title: Observed sample
steps.prompt: Describe how cases entered the sample, inclusion and exclusion rules, missing cases, response behavior, and any convenience or survivorship mechanisms.

steps.title: Representativeness check
steps.prompt: Compare the sample with known population characteristics or plausible missing strata and identify dimensions on which representation may fail.

steps.title: Bias sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test how conclusions would change if underrepresented or missing groups differed materially from observed cases.

steps.title: Generalization limit
steps.prompt: State what population the sample can defensibly represent, what it cannot, and what additional sampling or weighting would reduce uncertainty.

definition.name: Recency and Relevance Audit
definition.summary: Recency and Relevance Audit uses a Judgment under review → Evidence inventory → Staleness and context drift → Reweight evidence workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Judgment under review
steps.prompt: State the analytic judgment and the time, geography, actors, and conditions to which it is meant to apply.

steps.title: Evidence inventory
steps.prompt: List the evidence carrying material weight and record date, observation period, context, and direct relevance to the current question.

steps.title: Staleness and context drift
steps.prompt: Identify evidence whose value may have decayed because actors, incentives, technology, policy, geography, definitions, or operating conditions changed.

steps.title: Reweight evidence
steps.prompt: Distinguish old but structurally informative evidence from obsolete evidence and adjust analytic weight explicitly rather than discarding by age alone.

steps.title: Refresh priorities
steps.prompt: Identify which stale or weakly relevant evidence most needs replacement and what current observation would materially improve confidence.

definition.name: Confidence Calibration Worksheet
definition.summary: Confidence Calibration Worksheet uses a Judgment and stated confidence → Basis of confidence → Calibration evidence → Confidence challenge workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Judgment and stated confidence
steps.prompt: Record the current judgment, probability language or numeric probability, confidence level, and forecast horizon.

steps.title: Basis of confidence
steps.prompt: Separate evidence quality, evidence quantity, source independence, model or argument strength, agreement among analysts, and stability of assumptions.

steps.title: Calibration evidence
steps.prompt: Compare similar past judgments or forecasts with outcomes where available and note systematic overconfidence, underconfidence, or domain-specific error.

steps.title: Confidence challenge
steps.prompt: Ask what evidence, assumption failure, alternative hypothesis, or collection limitation would make the current confidence too high or too low.

steps.title: Calibrated statement
steps.prompt: Revise the confidence statement so its strength matches the evidence base, unresolved alternatives, and known calibration performance; record what would trigger an update.

definition.name: Evidence Triangulation
definition.summary: Evidence Triangulation uses a Analytic question → Evidence streams → Independence check → Convergence and divergence workflow to assess evidence quality, provenance, corroboration, independence, gaps, and collection effects.

steps.title: Analytic question
steps.prompt: Define the claim or uncertainty to be assessed and why independent lines of evidence are needed.

steps.title: Evidence streams
steps.prompt: Identify evidence from different sources, methods, sensors, datasets, observers, or theoretical perspectives.

steps.title: Independence check
steps.prompt: Determine which streams are genuinely independent and which share origins, methods, assumptions, or institutional incentives.

steps.title: Convergence and divergence
steps.prompt: Compare where streams converge, contradict, or answer different parts of the question and assess whether differences are informative.

steps.title: Triangulated judgment
steps.prompt: State what remains supported across independent streams, what depends on one method or source, and what further evidence has highest value.

definition.name: Hypothesis Mapping
definition.summary: Hypothesis Mapping uses a Question → Hypothesis set → Map structure → Overlap and nesting workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Question
steps.prompt: Define the event, behavior, or condition to explain without embedding a preferred answer.

steps.title: Hypothesis set
steps.prompt: Generate distinct explanations and separate alternatives that rely on materially different mechanisms.

steps.title: Map structure
steps.prompt: For each hypothesis, map assumptions, causal links, predicted observations, and incompatible observations.

steps.title: Overlap and nesting
steps.prompt: Identify hypotheses that are duplicates, subsets, combinations, or not truly mutually exclusive.

steps.title: Discriminating tests
steps.prompt: Prioritize evidence that would most sharply distinguish among the mapped explanations.

definition.name: Simple Hypothesis Testing
definition.summary: Simple Hypothesis Testing uses a Question → Competing hypotheses → Observable implications → Compare with evidence workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Question
steps.prompt: State the phenomenon to explain or proposition to test without embedding the preferred answer.

steps.title: Competing hypotheses
steps.prompt: List at least two plausible explanations, including a null or mundane explanation where appropriate.

steps.title: Observable implications
steps.prompt: For each hypothesis, state observations that would be expected, unexpected, or especially diagnostic.

steps.title: Compare with evidence
steps.prompt: Evaluate the observed evidence against the predictions, emphasizing inconsistencies and discriminating observations.

steps.title: Relative assessment
steps.prompt: Rank or bound the surviving hypotheses, state confidence, and identify the next evidence most likely to change the assessment.

definition.name: Quadrant Hypothesis Generation
definition.summary: Quadrant Hypothesis Generation uses a Problem to explain → Two generative dimensions → Generate by quadrant → Coverage and distinctness workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Problem to explain
steps.prompt: State the event or condition requiring explanation without embedding the favored hypothesis.

steps.title: Two generative dimensions
steps.prompt: Choose two independent dimensions that meaningfully divide the explanation space, such as intent versus capability or internal versus external cause.

steps.title: Generate by quadrant
steps.prompt: Create at least one plausible hypothesis in each quadrant, including combinations that initially seem less intuitive.

steps.title: Coverage and distinctness
steps.prompt: Merge duplicates, split hypotheses with different mechanisms, and check whether important explanations fall outside the chosen dimensions.

steps.title: Testable hypothesis set
steps.prompt: Retain a diverse set of hypotheses with distinct observable implications and identify the first discriminating evidence to seek.

definition.name: Deductive Test Matrix
definition.summary: Deductive Test Matrix uses a Hypotheses → Necessary predictions → Prediction matrix → Failed deductions workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Hypotheses
steps.prompt: List the competing hypotheses or propositions to be tested.

steps.title: Necessary predictions
steps.prompt: Deduce observations that should follow if each hypothesis is true, distinguishing necessary implications from merely compatible outcomes.

steps.title: Prediction matrix
steps.prompt: Compare actual observations with each prediction as present, absent, contradictory, unknown, or not observable.

steps.title: Failed deductions
steps.prompt: Identify hypotheses that require ad hoc exceptions, fail necessary predictions, or survive only because critical observations are unavailable.

steps.title: Deductive assessment
steps.prompt: Revise the hypothesis set and specify the highest-value observation that could produce a decisive deductive test.

definition.name: Inductive Pattern Assessment
definition.summary: Inductive Pattern Assessment uses a Observation set → Candidate pattern → Alternative pattern explanations → Exceptions and boundaries workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Observation set
steps.prompt: Define the observations, cases, or events from which a broader pattern is being inferred, including how they were selected.

steps.title: Candidate pattern
steps.prompt: Describe the recurring association, sequence, cluster, or regularity without converting it immediately into a causal claim.

steps.title: Alternative pattern explanations
steps.prompt: Test sampling effects, reporting bias, common causes, coincidence, changing definitions, and subgroup mixtures as explanations for the apparent pattern.

steps.title: Exceptions and boundaries
steps.prompt: Identify negative cases, outliers, boundary conditions, and contexts where the pattern weakens or reverses.

steps.title: Bounded induction
steps.prompt: State the narrowest generalization supported by the observations and what new cases would most strongly test whether it generalizes.

definition.name: Inference to the Best Explanation
definition.summary: Inference to the Best Explanation uses a Phenomenon → Candidate explanations → Explanatory virtues → Explanation matrix and rival survival workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Phenomenon
steps.prompt: Define the observations and anomalies that any adequate explanation must account for.

steps.title: Candidate explanations
steps.prompt: Generate serious alternatives based on distinct mechanisms and avoid treating the first plausible account as the comparison baseline.

steps.title: Explanatory virtues
steps.prompt: Compare explanatory scope, causal adequacy, coherence, simplicity, prior plausibility, independent support, and ability to explain anomalies without ad hoc rescue.

steps.title: Explanation matrix and rival survival
steps.prompt: Assess each candidate consistently against the explanatory criteria, record discriminating evidence, and identify observations that remain better explained by a rival rather than treating mere compatibility as support.

steps.title: Provisional best explanation
steps.prompt: Select the best current explanation provisionally, preserve viable rivals, state confidence, and identify evidence that could reverse the ranking.

definition.name: Argument Structure Analysis
definition.summary: Argument Structure Analysis uses a Main conclusion → Premises and evidence → Warrants and assumptions → Objections and defeaters workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Main conclusion
steps.prompt: State the exact conclusion or recommendation being advanced.

steps.title: Premises and evidence
steps.prompt: Identify explicit reasons, evidence, subclaims, and data supporting the conclusion.

steps.title: Warrants and assumptions
steps.prompt: Make explicit the inferential rules and assumptions connecting premises to claims.

steps.title: Objections and defeaters
steps.prompt: Map counterevidence, exceptions, alternative explanations, and premises whose failure would break the argument.

steps.title: Structural assessment
steps.prompt: Identify unsupported leaps, circularity, weak links, redundant support, and the minimum revisions needed for a defensible argument.

definition.name: Toulmin Argument Model
definition.summary: Toulmin Argument Model uses a Claim → Grounds → Warrant and backing → Qualifier and rebuttal workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Claim
steps.prompt: State the proposition being argued for with appropriate scope and qualifiers.

steps.title: Grounds
steps.prompt: List the facts, observations, or evidence offered in support.

steps.title: Warrant and backing
steps.prompt: State why the grounds justify the claim and what supports that inferential rule.

steps.title: Qualifier and rebuttal
steps.prompt: Specify the strength or conditions of the claim and the strongest recognized exceptions or rebuttals.

steps.title: Argument assessment
steps.prompt: Judge which Toulmin elements are strong, missing, or contested and revise the claim accordingly.

definition.name: Claim-Evidence-Reasoning Matrix
definition.summary: Claim-Evidence-Reasoning Matrix uses a Claims → Evidence → Reasoning and warrants → Alternative interpretations workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Claims
steps.prompt: List the major analytic claims at the level of precision actually intended.

steps.title: Evidence
steps.prompt: For each claim, list supporting, contradicting, and missing evidence with provenance and source-quality caveats.

steps.title: Reasoning and warrants
steps.prompt: State the inferential rule that connects each evidence item to the claim and expose assumptions required for that connection.

steps.title: Alternative interpretations
steps.prompt: Record rival explanations for the same evidence and evidence that would discriminate among interpretations.

steps.title: Argument audit
steps.prompt: Identify claims with weak evidence, weak warrants, excessive precision, or unresolved contradiction and revise them accordingly.

definition.name: Counterevidence Matrix
definition.summary: Counterevidence Matrix uses a Judgments or hypotheses → Counterevidence → Quality and diagnosticity → Possible responses workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Judgments or hypotheses
steps.prompt: List the conclusions or hypotheses to challenge.

steps.title: Counterevidence
steps.prompt: For each item, collect evidence that contradicts, weakens, or fails to fit it rather than only evidence that supports it.

steps.title: Quality and diagnosticity
steps.prompt: Assess source quality, independence, expectedness, and whether each counterevidence item truly discriminates among alternatives.

steps.title: Possible responses
steps.prompt: Distinguish legitimate explanations for counterevidence from ad hoc rationalization or moving the goalposts.

steps.title: Revision
steps.prompt: State which judgments survive, require qualification, lose confidence, or should be rejected after the counterevidence review.

definition.name: Discriminating Evidence Matrix
definition.summary: Discriminating Evidence Matrix uses a Hypotheses → Evidence → Diagnostic comparison → High-value evidence workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Hypotheses
steps.prompt: List the serious competing hypotheses.

steps.title: Evidence
steps.prompt: List evidence items that could differ in expectedness across the hypotheses.

steps.title: Diagnostic comparison
steps.prompt: For each evidence item, compare how expected it would be under each hypothesis; avoid counting merely compatible evidence as strongly diagnostic.

steps.title: High-value evidence
steps.prompt: Which items most sharply distinguish the hypotheses, and which are redundant or non-discriminating?

steps.title: Relative update
steps.prompt: Revise the relative standing of the hypotheses and identify the next most valuable discriminating evidence.

definition.name: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions Analysis
definition.summary: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions Analysis uses a Outcome or claim → Candidate conditions → Case comparison → Necessity and sufficiency tests workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Outcome or claim
steps.prompt: Define the outcome precisely enough that candidate conditions can be tested across positive and negative cases.

steps.title: Candidate conditions
steps.prompt: List factors proposed as necessary, sufficient, jointly sufficient, or enabling conditions.

steps.title: Case comparison
steps.prompt: For each condition, inspect cases where the outcome occurs and does not occur and record whether the condition is present, absent, or uncertain.

steps.title: Necessity and sufficiency tests
steps.prompt: Look for counterexamples: an outcome without a supposedly necessary condition or a condition present without a supposedly sufficient outcome.

steps.title: Conditional conclusion
steps.prompt: State which conditions remain necessary, sufficient, contributory, or unsupported and identify combinations or boundary conditions requiring further testing.

definition.name: Consistency Testing
definition.summary: Consistency Testing uses a Judgment or model → Consistency constraints → Cross-check → Resolve inconsistencies workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Judgment or model
steps.prompt: State the set of claims, assumptions, estimates, and causal statements that should fit together.

steps.title: Consistency constraints
steps.prompt: Identify logical, temporal, numerical, definitional, geographic, and behavioral relationships that the claims must satisfy.

steps.title: Cross-check
steps.prompt: Compare statements against one another and against source evidence to find contradictions, impossible combinations, double counting, or incompatible time sequences.

steps.title: Resolve inconsistencies
steps.prompt: Determine whether each inconsistency reflects error, scope mismatch, ambiguous terminology, uncertain evidence, or a genuine unresolved conflict.

steps.title: Coherent remainder
steps.prompt: Revise the analysis so remaining claims are mutually consistent and explicitly preserve unresolved contradictions that carry analytic significance.

definition.name: Coherence Testing
definition.summary: Coherence Testing uses a Explanation or narrative → Internal links → Whole-story fit → Coherent rivals workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Explanation or narrative
steps.prompt: State the proposed explanation, including causal sequence, actor motives, assumptions, and key supporting evidence.

steps.title: Internal links
steps.prompt: Examine whether each causal or inferential step follows from the prior one and whether important transitions rely on unstated assumptions.

steps.title: Whole-story fit
steps.prompt: Test whether the explanation accounts for the full observation set, including anomalies and inconvenient evidence, without excessive special pleading.

steps.title: Coherent rivals
steps.prompt: Compare at least one alternative explanation for equal internal coherence so a compelling story is not mistaken for a well-supported one.

steps.title: Coherence judgment
steps.prompt: State where the explanation is structurally strong, where it remains fragile, and what external evidence—not narrative smoothness—should decide among coherent rivals.

definition.name: Rival Explanation Matrix
definition.summary: Rival Explanation Matrix uses a Phenomenon → Rival explanations → Predicted observations → Evidence comparison workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Phenomenon
steps.prompt: Define what must be explained and the observation window.

steps.title: Rival explanations
steps.prompt: List plausible explanations that invoke meaningfully different causes or mechanisms.

steps.title: Predicted observations
steps.prompt: For each rival, state evidence that should be present, absent, or differently distributed if it were true.

steps.title: Evidence comparison
steps.prompt: Compare observed evidence across rivals, emphasizing inconsistencies and diagnostic differences rather than supportive counts.

steps.title: Residual uncertainty
steps.prompt: Identify surviving explanations, unresolved anomalies, and the next evidence most likely to separate them.

definition.name: Evidence Diagnosticity Ranking
definition.summary: Evidence Diagnosticity Ranking uses a Hypothesis set → Evidence items → Expectedness by hypothesis → Diagnosticity ranking workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Hypothesis set
steps.prompt: Define the serious competing hypotheses before ranking evidence.

steps.title: Evidence items
steps.prompt: List observations or arguments that bear on one or more hypotheses.

steps.title: Expectedness by hypothesis
steps.prompt: For each evidence item, compare how expected it would be if each hypothesis were true.

steps.title: Diagnosticity ranking
steps.prompt: Rank evidence by how sharply it changes relative support among hypotheses, discounting redundant or highly correlated items.

steps.title: Collection priority
steps.prompt: Identify missing evidence with the highest potential diagnostic value and specify what result would move the assessment.

definition.name: Hypothesis Sensitivity Analysis
definition.summary: Hypothesis Sensitivity Analysis uses a Baseline assessment → Critical evidence and assumptions → Plausible variants → Effect on ranking workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Baseline assessment
steps.prompt: State the current relative standing of the hypotheses and the evidence driving that assessment.

steps.title: Critical evidence and assumptions
steps.prompt: Identify the evidence items, source judgments, priors, thresholds, or assumptions with the greatest influence.

steps.title: Plausible variants
steps.prompt: Vary those inputs within defensible ranges, including removal of questionable evidence and alternative source-quality judgments.

steps.title: Effect on ranking
steps.prompt: Record which changes leave the ranking stable, narrow the gap, or reverse the preferred hypothesis.

steps.title: Robust conclusion
steps.prompt: State what survives the sensitivity test and which fragile inputs should drive collection, caveats, or lower confidence.

definition.name: Null Hypothesis Challenge
definition.summary: Null Hypothesis Challenge uses a Favored claim → Null or mundane alternative → Competing expectations → Challenge with evidence workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Favored claim
steps.prompt: State the substantive explanation, effect, or pattern currently receiving analytic weight.

steps.title: Null or mundane alternative
steps.prompt: Define a credible null explanation such as chance, base rates, routine process, measurement artifact, selection effect, or no meaningful change.

steps.title: Competing expectations
steps.prompt: Identify observations expected under both the favored claim and the null, emphasizing evidence that would differ between them.

steps.title: Challenge with evidence
steps.prompt: Re-examine the data for effect size, persistence, replication, negative cases, and whether the apparent signal exceeds ordinary variability.

steps.title: Update
steps.prompt: State whether the favored claim still adds explanatory value beyond the null and what observation would most strongly distinguish them next.

definition.name: Anomaly Resolution Matrix
definition.summary: Anomaly Resolution Matrix uses a Baseline model → Anomalies → Resolution candidates → Explanatory cost workflow to generate, map, compare, and stress-test explanations and the arguments that support them.

steps.title: Baseline model
steps.prompt: State the hypothesis, model, or judgment and the observations it explains well.

steps.title: Anomalies
steps.prompt: List observations that contradict, fall outside, or are unexpectedly difficult for the baseline to explain.

steps.title: Resolution candidates
steps.prompt: For each anomaly, compare data error, source problem, boundary condition, auxiliary mechanism, model revision, and rival hypothesis as possible resolutions.

steps.title: Explanatory cost
steps.prompt: Assess whether resolving an anomaly requires a modest justified refinement or repeated ad hoc exceptions that weaken the baseline.

steps.title: Model decision
steps.prompt: Classify anomalies as resolved, tolerable, collection-dependent, or model-threatening and state whether the baseline should be retained, revised, or replaced.

definition.name: Blue Team Review
definition.summary: Blue Team Review uses a Baseline judgment or plan → Likely challenges → Defend with evidence → Unanswered weaknesses workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Baseline judgment or plan
steps.prompt: State the assessment, plan, or product being defended and the evidence, assumptions, and objectives it depends on.

steps.title: Likely challenges
steps.prompt: List the strongest evidentiary, logical, operational, adversarial, and implementation challenges it is likely to face.

steps.title: Defend with evidence
steps.prompt: For each challenge, identify the strongest evidence, control, reasoning, or design feature that genuinely answers it rather than relying on assertion.

steps.title: Unanswered weaknesses
steps.prompt: Distinguish challenges that are resolved from those that expose real gaps, brittle assumptions, or missing safeguards.

steps.title: Strengthening actions
steps.prompt: Revise claims, controls, contingencies, evidence collection, or wording so the product survives legitimate challenge without concealing residual risk.

definition.name: Black Hat Review
definition.summary: Black Hat Review uses a Target decision or analysis → Critical concerns → Severity and plausibility → Mitigation test workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Target decision or analysis
steps.prompt: Define what is being reviewed and the conditions under which failure, harm, or invalidity would matter.

steps.title: Critical concerns
steps.prompt: Identify weaknesses, failure modes, adverse consequences, unsupported claims, hidden costs, and reasons the proposal or judgment may not work.

steps.title: Severity and plausibility
steps.prompt: Separate merely imaginable objections from concerns that are both consequential and supported by plausible mechanisms or evidence.

steps.title: Mitigation test
steps.prompt: For each serious concern, assess whether an existing control, redesign, caveat, or additional evidence can materially reduce it.

steps.title: Residual concern
steps.prompt: State which objections remain decision-relevant after mitigation and how they should change confidence, design, or go/no-go criteria.

definition.name: Murder Board
definition.summary: Murder Board uses a Product or argument → Critical claims → Adversarial questioning → Defend or concede workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Product or argument
steps.prompt: State the analytic product, recommendation, or briefing being challenged.

steps.title: Critical claims
steps.prompt: List the claims whose failure would most damage the product.

steps.title: Adversarial questioning
steps.prompt: Generate the hardest plausible questions about evidence, logic, assumptions, alternatives, precision, sourcing, and implications.

steps.title: Defend or concede
steps.prompt: Answer each challenge with evidence; distinguish claims that can be defended from those that require revision.

steps.title: Repair plan
steps.prompt: Revise weak claims, caveats, confidence, or sourcing before finalization.

definition.name: Red Cell Exercise
definition.summary: Red Cell Exercise uses a Target actor or system → Actor model → Independent red-cell moves → Interaction and adaptation workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Target actor or system
steps.prompt: Define the actor, organization, adversary, or competitive system whose perspective will be simulated.

steps.title: Actor model
steps.prompt: Specify objectives, constraints, information, doctrine, culture, incentives, capabilities, and perceived vulnerabilities using evidence rather than stereotype.

steps.title: Independent red-cell moves
steps.prompt: Generate plausible actions from the target's perspective without optimizing for the blue team's expectations.

steps.title: Interaction and adaptation
steps.prompt: Explore how the target could react to friendly actions, exploit assumptions, conceal intent, or change tactics after observing responses.

steps.title: Analytic insights
steps.prompt: Capture surprises, indicators, vulnerabilities, and assumptions exposed by the exercise while distinguishing simulation output from forecast.

definition.name: Alternative Interpretation Challenge
definition.summary: Alternative Interpretation Challenge uses a Shared evidence → Dominant interpretation → Alternative interpretations → Discriminating evidence workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Shared evidence
steps.prompt: List the observations or source material currently supporting the dominant interpretation without embedding that interpretation in the description.

steps.title: Dominant interpretation
steps.prompt: State the prevailing reading, its key assumptions, and the inferential steps connecting the evidence to it.

steps.title: Alternative interpretations
steps.prompt: Construct materially different interpretations that could account for the same evidence using different assumptions, actors, mechanisms, or contexts.

steps.title: Discriminating evidence
steps.prompt: Identify observations that would be expected under one interpretation but not the others and note evidence currently missing or ambiguous.

steps.title: Interpretive update
steps.prompt: State which interpretations survive, what remains genuinely ambiguous, and what should change in the wording or confidence of the dominant view.

definition.name: Cognitive Bias Audit
definition.summary: Cognitive Bias Audit uses a Judgment under review → Bias exposure → Observable signatures → Targeted countermeasures workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Judgment under review
steps.prompt: State the assessment, decision, forecast, or interpretation and document how it was produced.

steps.title: Bias exposure
steps.prompt: Check systematically for anchoring, confirmation, availability, recency, status quo, sunk-cost, framing, mirror imaging, overconfidence, attribution, motivated reasoning, and group effects.

steps.title: Observable signatures
steps.prompt: For each plausible bias, identify concrete features of the reasoning process, evidence selection, estimates, framing, or discussion that indicate exposure rather than merely naming the bias.

steps.title: Targeted countermeasures
steps.prompt: Apply an appropriate corrective such as independent estimation, base-rate review, reframing, contrary-evidence search, outside view, assumption reversal, or dissent capture.

steps.title: Reassess
steps.prompt: Record what changed after the countermeasures and which residual bias risks remain material enough to affect confidence or process design.

definition.name: Anchoring Challenge
definition.summary: Anchoring Challenge uses a Suspected anchor → Independent reconstruction → Plausible range → Anchor influence workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Suspected anchor
steps.prompt: Identify the first estimate, prior judgment, salient number, precedent, or framing that may be exerting disproportionate influence.

steps.title: Independent reconstruction
steps.prompt: Re-estimate or reframe the question without using the anchor, preferably from components, base rates, or an independent analyst.

steps.title: Plausible range
steps.prompt: Develop a defensible range from external evidence and alternative starting points before comparing it with the original anchor.

steps.title: Anchor influence
steps.prompt: Compare the independent result with the anchored result and identify which assumptions or adjustments explain the gap.

steps.title: De-anchored judgment
steps.prompt: State the revised estimate or judgment, why the anchor should or should not retain weight, and what future information would move the result.

definition.name: Confirmation Bias Challenge
definition.summary: Confirmation Bias Challenge uses a Favored hypothesis → Disconfirming search → Rival explanations → Symmetry check workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Favored hypothesis
steps.prompt: State the explanation or judgment currently receiving the most support and the evidence considered most persuasive.

steps.title: Disconfirming search
steps.prompt: Actively seek evidence, cases, sources, and observations that would be unlikely if the favored hypothesis were true.

steps.title: Rival explanations
steps.prompt: Generate credible alternatives and identify evidence currently interpreted one-sidedly that could also support them.

steps.title: Symmetry check
steps.prompt: Ask whether contradictory evidence is being discounted more readily than supportive evidence and whether source-quality standards are applied consistently.

steps.title: Bias-resistant update
