steps.prompt: Revise the judgment based on diagnostic evidence, preserve surviving alternatives, and identify collection designed to challenge rather than merely confirm the favorite.

definition.name: Availability Bias Challenge
definition.summary: Availability Bias Challenge uses a Salient examples → Reference population → Less visible cases → Frequency versus salience workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Salient examples
steps.prompt: Identify vivid, recent, repeated, emotionally striking, or easily recalled examples that may be shaping the judgment.

steps.title: Reference population
steps.prompt: Define the relevant denominator, time period, comparison class, and base-rate data needed to judge how representative those examples are.

steps.title: Less visible cases
steps.prompt: Search for quiet, routine, negative, unreported, or less memorable cases that the current mental sample may omit.

steps.title: Frequency versus salience
steps.prompt: Compare the apparent importance of the salient examples with their actual frequency, impact, and representativeness.

steps.title: Recalibrated judgment
steps.prompt: State what changes when the evidence is weighted by prevalence and diagnostic value rather than ease of recall.

definition.name: Mirror-Imaging Check
definition.summary: Mirror-Imaging Check uses a Judgment about another actor → Possible projections → Actor-grounded model → Non-mirrored alternatives workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Judgment about another actor
steps.prompt: State the assessment of the actor's likely motives, perceptions, or choices.

steps.title: Possible projections
steps.prompt: Identify places where the reasoning assumes the actor shares the analyst's values, risk tolerance, institutions, information, or definitions of rationality.

steps.title: Actor-grounded model
steps.prompt: Reconstruct objectives, constraints, history, doctrine, culture, incentives, and information from evidence specific to the actor.

steps.title: Non-mirrored alternatives
steps.prompt: Generate choices that could be rational within the actor's own frame even if they appear irrational or unattractive from ours.

steps.title: Observable tests
steps.prompt: Define behavior or evidence that would distinguish the projected model from actor-grounded alternatives.

definition.name: Groupthink Check
definition.summary: Groupthink Check uses a Group judgment → Groupthink conditions → Independent positions → Structured dissent workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Group judgment
steps.prompt: State the group conclusion, confidence, and process used to reach it.

steps.title: Groupthink conditions
steps.prompt: Check for premature unanimity, authority gradients, social pressure, self-censorship, illusion of consensus, isolated dissenters, and shared-source dependence.

steps.title: Independent positions
steps.prompt: Collect independent judgments or estimates before further discussion and record minority views without attribution pressure where practical.

steps.title: Structured dissent
steps.prompt: Assign or invite credible dissent, compare cruxes, and test whether the consensus survives exposure to the strongest alternative case.

steps.title: Post-challenge consensus
steps.prompt: State what agreement remains genuinely independent, what dissent persists, and whether process changes are needed before finalizing the judgment.

definition.name: Consensus Challenge
definition.summary: Consensus Challenge uses a Consensus judgment → Basis of agreement → Strongest challenge → Discriminating tests workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Consensus judgment
steps.prompt: State the prevailing judgment, its confidence, and whether agreement reflects independent analysis or shared assumptions and sources.

steps.title: Basis of agreement
steps.prompt: Identify common evidence, methods, definitions, incentives, and institutional dependencies that may make the consensus less independent than it appears.

steps.title: Strongest challenge
steps.prompt: Develop the strongest plausible alternative or boundary condition and identify evidence the consensus may underweight.

steps.title: Discriminating tests
steps.prompt: Define observations that would distinguish the consensus from the strongest alternative and assign responsibility for monitoring them.

steps.title: Consensus after challenge
steps.prompt: Record what remains robust, what dissent survives, and whether confidence or wording should change.

definition.name: Dissent Capture
definition.summary: Dissent Capture uses a Question and baseline → Dissenting judgments → Cruxes of disagreement → Evidence by view workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Question and baseline
steps.prompt: State the analytic question, prevailing judgment, and current confidence.

steps.title: Dissenting judgments
steps.prompt: Record materially different judgments in their strongest form, including minority confidence and scope rather than reducing them to objections.

steps.title: Cruxes of disagreement
steps.prompt: Identify the factual, causal, definitional, temporal, or probabilistic differences that actually drive the divergence.

steps.title: Evidence by view
steps.prompt: For each view, identify the evidence, assumptions, source-quality judgments, and reasoning that carry the most weight.

steps.title: Preserve and resolve
steps.prompt: State what evidence or event would move each view, what disagreement should be communicated to users, and when it should be revisited.

definition.name: Devil's Proof
definition.summary: Devil's Proof uses a Claim and burden → Search for counterexamples → Limits of proof → Narrow the proposition workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Claim and burden
steps.prompt: State the proposition being asserted and clarify what would count as adequate support, especially if it contains an absolute or negative claim.

steps.title: Search for counterexamples
steps.prompt: Look deliberately for a single credible observation, case, or mechanism that would defeat the universal or overbroad form of the claim.

steps.title: Limits of proof
steps.prompt: Identify whether the available evidence can actually establish absence or impossibility, or only failure to observe something under specific collection conditions.

steps.title: Narrow the proposition
steps.prompt: Replace an unprovable absolute with the strongest bounded claim supported by scope, time, observability, and evidence quality.

steps.title: Future test
steps.prompt: Define observations or collection conditions that would most strongly support or refute the narrowed proposition without pretending a negative can always be proved conclusively.

definition.name: Steelmanning
definition.summary: Steelmanning uses a Opposing position → Strongest version → Points of agreement → True cruxes workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Opposing position
steps.prompt: State the view being challenged in neutral language before evaluating it.

steps.title: Strongest version
steps.prompt: Reconstruct the position using its best evidence, most defensible assumptions, strongest causal logic, and most capable proponents rather than weak examples.

steps.title: Points of agreement
steps.prompt: Identify premises, facts, values, or uncertainties that the steelmanned view shares with the analyst's current position.

steps.title: True cruxes
steps.prompt: Isolate the smallest set of factual, causal, normative, or probabilistic differences that actually separate the two strongest positions.

steps.title: Update after steelman
steps.prompt: State what the stronger opposing case changes in the original judgment, confidence, caveats, or evidence priorities.

definition.name: Reversal Test
definition.summary: Reversal Test uses a Current position → Reverse the direction → Symmetry check → Substantive constraints workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Current position
steps.prompt: State the current policy, threshold, allocation, estimate, or directional preference and the reasons offered for maintaining it.

steps.title: Reverse the direction
steps.prompt: Imagine moving the relevant variable, policy, or judgment in the opposite direction and list the reasons that would be offered against that change.

steps.title: Symmetry check
steps.prompt: Ask whether the same reasons would also oppose moving from the reversed state back toward the current one; inconsistent reasoning may indicate status quo bias.

steps.title: Substantive constraints
steps.prompt: Separate genuine asymmetric costs, path dependence, thresholds, or irreversible effects from reasons that merely privilege the current state.

steps.title: Bias-adjusted conclusion
steps.prompt: State whether the current position remains justified after the reversal and what evidence would support a different reference point.

definition.name: Precommitment Review
definition.summary: Precommitment Review uses a Current judgment or plan → Precommit criteria → Alternative outcomes → Process guardrails workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Current judgment or plan
steps.prompt: State the assessment, forecast, or decision before new evidence or outcomes arrive.

steps.title: Precommit criteria
steps.prompt: Define in advance what observations, thresholds, failures, or successes would count as evidence for revision, escalation, continuation, or abandonment.

steps.title: Alternative outcomes
steps.prompt: Record plausible competing outcomes and how each would be interpreted before knowing which one occurs.

steps.title: Process guardrails
steps.prompt: Assign review timing, evidence ownership, documentation, and decision authority so criteria cannot be quietly rewritten after the fact.

steps.title: Future review record
steps.prompt: Specify how the later review will compare actual evidence with the precommitted criteria and how deviations from the original rules must be explained.

definition.name: Assumption Reversal
definition.summary: Assumption Reversal uses a Current judgment → Select assumptions → Reverse them → Rebuild the analysis workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Current judgment
steps.prompt: State the current conclusion, plan, or model and its most consequential assumptions.

steps.title: Select assumptions
steps.prompt: Identify assumptions that are both important and uncertain.

steps.title: Reverse them
steps.prompt: For each selected assumption, deliberately posit the opposite or a materially different state.

steps.title: Rebuild the analysis
steps.prompt: Trace how the reversed assumption changes causal logic, evidence interpretation, outcomes, risks, or actor behavior.

steps.title: Learning
steps.prompt: Identify hidden dependencies, contingency points, and indicators that would signal the reversed condition is becoming plausible.

definition.name: Surprise Analysis
definition.summary: Surprise Analysis uses a Baseline expectation → Plausible surprises → Pathways to surprise → Why we might miss it workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Baseline expectation
steps.prompt: State what the current assessment expects and the assumptions that make it unsurprising.

steps.title: Plausible surprises
steps.prompt: Generate developments that would materially violate expectations without requiring fantasy conditions.

steps.title: Pathways to surprise
steps.prompt: For each candidate, identify precursor conditions, triggers, actor decisions, or nonlinear mechanisms that could produce it.

steps.title: Why we might miss it
steps.prompt: Identify collection gaps, cognitive biases, institutional incentives, or model boundaries that could hide the pathway.

steps.title: Warning signposts
steps.prompt: Define early observations that should cause the surprise pathway to receive more weight.

definition.name: Propaganda Environment Analysis
definition.summary: Propaganda Environment Analysis uses a Information environment → Pre-propaganda and myths → Repetition and integration → Audience need and function workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Information environment
steps.prompt: Define the population, media system, institutions, social conditions, and decision context in which persuasion operates.

steps.title: Pre-propaganda and myths
steps.prompt: Identify preexisting myths, identities, grievances, aspirations, stereotypes, symbols, and accepted narratives that make messages intelligible and emotionally usable.

steps.title: Repetition and integration
steps.prompt: Map channel diversity, repetition, social reinforcement, institutional participation, and whether apparently independent messages share the same premises or system incentives.

steps.title: Audience need and function
steps.prompt: Assess what psychological or social needs the propaganda environment satisfies—orientation, belonging, justification, simplification, action, or relief from uncertainty.

steps.title: Environmental assessment
steps.prompt: State which conditions make influence durable, what counter-messaging alone is unlikely to change, and which environmental shifts would reduce susceptibility.

references.label: International Jacques Ellul Society — Propaganda overview

definition.name: Agitation–Integration Propaganda Analysis
definition.summary: Agitation–Integration Propaganda Analysis uses a Message set and actors → Agitation functions → Integration functions → Interaction and transition workflow to challenge prevailing judgments, cognitive habits, consensus pressure, influence environments, and unexamined assumptions.

steps.title: Message set and actors
steps.prompt: Define the message corpus, communicators, audiences, channels, time window, and political or organizational context.

steps.title: Agitation functions
steps.prompt: Identify messages that mobilize against an enemy or status quo through urgency, grievance, fear, rupture, sacrifice, or calls for exceptional action.

steps.title: Integration functions
steps.prompt: Identify messages that normalize an existing order through belonging, routine participation, legitimacy, conformity, identity, and reinforcement of accepted institutions.

steps.title: Interaction and transition
steps.prompt: Examine how agitation and integration reinforce one another, alternate over time, or move audiences from disruption into a new normalized order.

steps.title: Behavioral implications
steps.prompt: Identify observable participation, conformity, polarization, mobilization, or demobilization patterns that would support or weaken the classification.

references.label: International Jacques Ellul Society — Propaganda overview

definition.name: Environmental Scanning
definition.summary: Environmental Scanning uses a Scan scope → Source portfolio → Scan observations → Patterns and relevance workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Scan scope
steps.prompt: Define the decision area, horizon, geography, stakeholders, and domains to scan.

steps.title: Source portfolio
steps.prompt: Select diverse internal, external, peripheral, and contrarian sources rather than relying on familiar channels.

steps.title: Scan observations
steps.prompt: Capture developments, anomalies, weak signals, policy shifts, technologies, and social changes with source and date.

steps.title: Patterns and relevance
steps.prompt: Cluster related observations and assess novelty, momentum, uncertainty, and possible relevance to the focal issue.

steps.title: Watch list
steps.prompt: Prioritize developments for monitoring and define what additional evidence would justify escalation.

definition.name: Horizon Scanning
definition.summary: Horizon Scanning uses a Scan domain and horizon → Signals → Cluster and mature → Potential impact workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Scan domain and horizon
steps.prompt: Define the topic, geographic scope, stakeholders, and time horizon.

steps.title: Signals
steps.prompt: Collect weak signals, emerging issues, anomalies, innovations, policy changes, and peripheral developments.

steps.title: Cluster and mature
steps.prompt: Group related signals and distinguish isolated noise from reinforcing patterns.

steps.title: Potential impact
steps.prompt: Assess plausible direction, scale, timing, uncertainty, and affected actors for each important cluster.

steps.title: Watch list
steps.prompt: Select signals and indicators for continued monitoring, with explicit review triggers.

definition.name: STEEP Analysis
definition.summary: STEEP Analysis uses a Scope and horizon → STEEP scan → Drivers and interactions → Importance and uncertainty workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Scope and horizon
steps.prompt: Define the focal issue, geographic scope, stakeholders, and time horizon.

steps.title: STEEP scan
steps.prompt: Collect material social, technological, economic, environmental, and political developments without forcing equal weight across categories.

steps.title: Drivers and interactions
steps.prompt: Identify which developments act as drivers, constraints, or dependent effects and where categories interact.

steps.title: Importance and uncertainty
steps.prompt: Rank developments by potential impact, uncertainty, pace, and relevance to the focal issue.

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: Translate the strongest drivers into opportunities, risks, signposts, and questions for deeper analysis.

definition.name: PESTLE Analysis
definition.summary: PESTLE Analysis uses a Decision context → PESTLE factors → Impact pathways → Interactions and dependencies workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Decision context
steps.prompt: Define the organization, market, policy, or problem and the decision horizon.

steps.title: PESTLE factors
steps.prompt: Identify political, economic, social, technological, legal, and environmental factors with evidence and time direction.

steps.title: Impact pathways
steps.prompt: Explain how each important factor could affect objectives, actors, costs, constraints, or behavior rather than merely listing it.

steps.title: Interactions and dependencies
steps.prompt: Identify reinforcing, offsetting, or contingent relationships among factors.

steps.title: Priority external factors
steps.prompt: Select the factors that deserve monitoring or scenario treatment and define observable indicators.

definition.name: Trend Analysis
definition.summary: Trend Analysis uses a Trend variable → Historical pattern → Drivers → Continuation test workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Trend variable
steps.prompt: Define the measure, unit, population, geography, and time span.

steps.title: Historical pattern
steps.prompt: Inspect level, direction, rate of change, seasonality, cycles, volatility, and data breaks.

steps.title: Drivers
steps.prompt: Identify mechanisms or external factors plausibly producing the observed trend and distinguish them from coincident events.

steps.title: Continuation test
steps.prompt: Ask which drivers must persist for the trend to continue and what constraints or saturation points could alter it.

steps.title: Trend judgment
steps.prompt: State what can reasonably be extrapolated, where uncertainty expands, and which indicators would signal a break.

definition.name: Trend Extrapolation
definition.summary: Trend Extrapolation uses a Historical series → Trend form → Continuation assumptions → Projection range workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Historical series
steps.prompt: Define the variable, unit, population, time interval, and data-quality limits before extending the trend.

steps.title: Trend form
steps.prompt: Estimate the historical direction and rate, checking for nonlinearity, seasonality, saturation, and structural breaks.

steps.title: Continuation assumptions
steps.prompt: State which drivers, constraints, definitions, and measurement conditions must persist for extrapolation to remain meaningful.

steps.title: Projection range
steps.prompt: Extend the trend over an appropriate horizon with central, upper, and lower trajectories rather than a single point line.

steps.title: Break conditions
steps.prompt: Identify thresholds, shocks, feedbacks, or driver changes that would invalidate the extrapolation and define indicators to monitor.

definition.name: Trend Break Analysis
definition.summary: Trend Break Analysis uses a Established trend → Candidate break → Competing causes → Break tests workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Established trend
steps.prompt: Characterize the prior trend and the evidence that it was sufficiently stable to serve as a baseline.

steps.title: Candidate break
steps.prompt: Locate the point or interval where direction, level, variance, or relationship appears to change.

steps.title: Competing causes
steps.prompt: Generate structural, policy, behavioral, measurement, and random explanations for the apparent break.

steps.title: Break tests
steps.prompt: Check persistence, cross-series corroboration, measurement changes, and whether the new regime improves explanation or prediction.

steps.title: Regime assessment
steps.prompt: State whether a genuine break is likely and define evidence that would confirm reversal, persistence, or a temporary shock.

definition.name: Emerging Issue Analysis
definition.summary: Emerging Issue Analysis uses a Candidate issue → Evidence of emergence → Growth pathways → Potential impacts workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Candidate issue
steps.prompt: Define the emerging development and distinguish it from a mature trend, isolated event, or speculative possibility.

steps.title: Evidence of emergence
steps.prompt: Collect early observations across independent sources and assess recurrence, spread, novelty, and source quality.

steps.title: Growth pathways
steps.prompt: Identify mechanisms by which the issue could expand, diffuse, combine with other drivers, or fade.

steps.title: Potential impacts
steps.prompt: Assess who or what could be affected, over what time horizon, with attention to indirect and distributional effects.

steps.title: Monitoring status
steps.prompt: Classify the issue for dismissal, watch, investigation, or escalation and define evidence that would change the classification.

definition.name: Weak Signal Analysis
definition.summary: Weak Signal Analysis uses a Search domain → Candidate weak signals → Context and provenance → Amplification pathways workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Search domain
steps.prompt: Define where emerging change would matter and which peripheral sources or actors may reveal it early.

steps.title: Candidate weak signals
steps.prompt: Collect unusual, low-frequency, fragmented, or early observations without treating novelty alone as importance.

steps.title: Context and provenance
steps.prompt: Assess source quality, novelty, recurrence, related developments, and whether the signal is an artifact of collection or attention.

steps.title: Amplification pathways
steps.prompt: Ask what drivers, networks, technologies, policies, or feedbacks could make the signal grow in significance.

steps.title: Watch decision
steps.prompt: Classify signals for dismissal, continued monitoring, or escalation and define what additional observations would justify upgrading them.

definition.name: Wild Card Analysis
definition.summary: Wild Card Analysis uses a Wild card → Plausibility conditions → Consequence cascade → Preparedness gaps workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Wild card
steps.prompt: Define a low-probability, high-impact discontinuity clearly enough to analyze without treating it as a prediction.

steps.title: Plausibility conditions
steps.prompt: Identify the minimum enabling conditions, triggers, and precursor changes required for the event to become possible.

steps.title: Consequence cascade
steps.prompt: Trace first-, second-, and higher-order consequences across actors, systems, and time horizons.

steps.title: Preparedness gaps
steps.prompt: Identify assumptions, plans, capacities, or dependencies that would fail under the event and possible hedges.

steps.title: Precursor signposts
steps.prompt: Define observable developments that would increase or decrease the event's plausibility enough to warrant reassessment.

definition.name: Drivers of Change Analysis
definition.summary: Drivers of Change Analysis uses a Focal question → Candidate drivers → Mechanisms → Impact and uncertainty workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Focal question
steps.prompt: Define the system, decision, and time horizon whose change drivers are being examined.

steps.title: Candidate drivers
steps.prompt: List political, economic, social, technological, environmental, institutional, demographic, and actor-specific forces.

steps.title: Mechanisms
steps.prompt: Explain how each driver could alter behavior, constraints, incentives, resources, or system structure rather than merely naming it.

steps.title: Impact and uncertainty
steps.prompt: Rank drivers by potential impact, uncertainty, pace, persistence, and degree of influence or controllability.

steps.title: Interactions and signposts
steps.prompt: Identify reinforcing or offsetting driver interactions and indicators that a driver is strengthening, weakening, or changing direction.

definition.name: Megatrend Analysis
definition.summary: Megatrend Analysis uses a Megatrend candidate → Scale and reach → Counterforces and limits → Strategic implications workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Megatrend candidate
steps.prompt: Define the long-duration, broad-scope change and the evidence that it extends beyond a local or short-term trend.

steps.title: Scale and reach
steps.prompt: Assess geographic spread, affected sectors, duration, population reach, and underlying structural forces.

steps.title: Counterforces and limits
steps.prompt: Identify saturation, backlash, resource limits, institutional resistance, competing trends, and regional exceptions.

steps.title: Strategic implications
steps.prompt: Trace direct and indirect implications for the focal system while avoiding the assumption that broad trends affect all actors equally.

steps.title: Evolution indicators
steps.prompt: Define indicators of acceleration, deceleration, fragmentation, reversal, or transformation of the megatrend.

definition.name: Technology Scanning
definition.summary: Technology Scanning uses a Technology domain → Technology signals → Maturity and bottlenecks → Application pathways workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Technology domain
steps.prompt: Define the capabilities, applications, users, and horizon being scanned rather than searching for novelty in general.

steps.title: Technology signals
steps.prompt: Collect evidence from research, patents, standards, investment, prototypes, adoption, supply chains, and regulation.

steps.title: Maturity and bottlenecks
steps.prompt: Assess readiness, performance trajectory, cost, infrastructure, skills, dependencies, and barriers to scale.

steps.title: Application pathways
steps.prompt: Identify plausible use cases, substitutions, complements, second-order effects, and actor incentives for adoption.

steps.title: Watch indicators
steps.prompt: Prioritize technologies and define measurable indicators that would signal technical breakthrough, diffusion, constraint, or decline.

definition.name: Patent Landscaping
definition.summary: Patent Landscaping uses a Technology and search scope → Patent corpus → Landscape structure → Interpretation limits workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Technology and search scope
steps.prompt: Define the technical domain, jurisdictions, dates, classifications, keywords, assignees, and family rules.

steps.title: Patent corpus
steps.prompt: Build a reproducible corpus and normalize patent families, assignee names, legal status, and duplicate filings.

steps.title: Landscape structure
steps.prompt: Analyze activity over time, technology clusters, major assignees, inventors, citations, geography, and collaboration patterns.

steps.title: Interpretation limits
steps.prompt: Distinguish filing activity from technical quality, commercial value, freedom to operate, or real-world adoption.

steps.title: Strategic insight
steps.prompt: Identify crowded and sparse areas, emerging clusters, key actors, and follow-up questions for technical or legal review.

definition.name: Bibliometric Trend Analysis
definition.summary: Bibliometric Trend Analysis uses a Publication corpus → Trend measures → Field structure → Database and citation bias workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Publication corpus
steps.prompt: Define databases, fields, dates, document types, search logic, and deduplication rules.

steps.title: Trend measures
steps.prompt: Track publication volume, citation patterns, topics, authors, institutions, venues, and geographic participation with normalized measures where needed.

steps.title: Field structure
steps.prompt: Identify emerging and declining topics, collaboration patterns, citation communities, and shifts in disciplinary composition.

steps.title: Database and citation bias
steps.prompt: Assess coverage, language, field-age, citation-lag, self-citation, and indexing effects that could mimic a substantive trend.

steps.title: Trend interpretation
steps.prompt: State which changes are robust enough to support an emerging-field judgment and what additional evidence is required.

definition.name: Signal-to-Noise Review
definition.summary: Signal-to-Noise Review uses a Observation stream → Candidate signals → Noise mechanisms → Signal tests workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Observation stream
steps.prompt: Define the information stream, decision context, time horizon, and what would count as a meaningful signal.

steps.title: Candidate signals
steps.prompt: List observations that appear unusual, recurrent, or decision-relevant without filtering only for confirming evidence.

steps.title: Noise mechanisms
steps.prompt: Identify randomness, reporting incentives, duplication, measurement error, media amplification, seasonality, and collection artifacts.

steps.title: Signal tests
steps.prompt: Check persistence, independence, coherence with mechanisms, cross-source recurrence, and predictive or explanatory value.

steps.title: Disposition
steps.prompt: Classify candidates as noise, weak signal, established signal, or unresolved and specify monitoring thresholds.

definition.name: Leading Indicator Analysis
definition.summary: Leading Indicator Analysis uses a Target outcome → Candidate indicators → Lead relationship → Indicator set workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Target outcome
steps.prompt: Define the outcome to anticipate, including resolution criteria and relevant lead time.

steps.title: Candidate indicators
steps.prompt: Identify variables with plausible causal or behavioral links that may change before the outcome.

steps.title: Lead relationship
steps.prompt: Test historical lead time, stability, false positives, missed events, revisions, and whether the relationship survives regime changes.

steps.title: Indicator set
steps.prompt: Combine complementary indicators while avoiding redundant signals and document thresholds or probability updates.

steps.title: Monitoring rule
steps.prompt: Define cadence, trigger levels, escalation rules, and conditions under which an indicator should be retired or recalibrated.

definition.name: Lagging Indicator Analysis
definition.summary: Lagging Indicator Analysis uses a Process or outcome → Lagging measures → Validity and delay → Compare with expectations workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Process or outcome
steps.prompt: Define the condition whose realized performance or change needs confirmation.

steps.title: Lagging measures
steps.prompt: Identify outcome measures that reliably reflect what has already occurred, including reporting delay and revision behavior.

steps.title: Validity and delay
steps.prompt: Assess measurement validity, completeness, latency, seasonal effects, and whether later revisions materially change interpretation.

steps.title: Compare with expectations
steps.prompt: Use lagging measures to confirm, reject, or recalibrate earlier leading indicators, forecasts, or interventions.

steps.title: Learning loop
steps.prompt: Translate discrepancies into model updates, indicator redesign, or changes in monitoring thresholds.

definition.name: Early Warning Dashboard Design
definition.summary: Early Warning Dashboard Design uses a Warning objective → Indicator portfolio → Thresholds and states → Decision display workflow to detect emerging change, characterize trends, and distinguish durable signals from transient noise.

steps.title: Warning objective
steps.prompt: Define the event, deterioration, opportunity, or threshold the dashboard must detect and who must act on it.

steps.title: Indicator portfolio
steps.prompt: Select a small set of leading, confirmatory, contextual, and data-quality indicators with clear provenance.

steps.title: Thresholds and states
steps.prompt: Define normal, watch, warning, and critical states using historical evidence, expert judgment, or decision thresholds.

steps.title: Decision display
steps.prompt: Present trend, recency, uncertainty, source quality, and threshold status without hiding contradictory indicators behind a single score.

steps.title: Review and governance
steps.prompt: Assign owners, refresh cadence, escalation actions, false-alarm review, and periodic recalibration or retirement of indicators.

definition.name: Backcasting
definition.summary: Backcasting uses a Desired or assumed future → Necessary milestones → Pathways → Present requirements workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Desired or assumed future
steps.prompt: Define the future state clearly, including horizon and success conditions.

steps.title: Necessary milestones
steps.prompt: Work backward to identify conditions and milestones that would have to exist before the future state is reached.

steps.title: Pathways
steps.prompt: Connect milestones into plausible sequences and identify dependencies, bottlenecks, and branch points.

steps.title: Present requirements
steps.prompt: What would need to begin, stop, or change now for each pathway to remain feasible?

steps.title: Progress indicators
steps.prompt: Identify observable markers that would show movement toward or away from the pathway.

definition.name: Cone of Plausibility
definition.summary: Cone of Plausibility uses a Baseline → Drivers and constraints → Plausibility bounds → Branching developments workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Baseline
steps.prompt: State the current trajectory and time horizon without assuming it will continue unchanged.

steps.title: Drivers and constraints
steps.prompt: Identify forces that could widen, narrow, accelerate, or redirect the range of plausible futures.

steps.title: Plausibility bounds
steps.prompt: Define reasonable upper, lower, and discontinuous departures from the baseline; explain why they remain plausible.

steps.title: Branching developments
steps.prompt: Identify events or decisions that would move the system toward different portions of the cone.

steps.title: Monitor the cone
steps.prompt: What indicators would show the plausible range widening, narrowing, or shifting?

definition.name: Futures Wheel
definition.summary: Futures Wheel uses a Central change → First-order effects → Second-order effects → Higher-order cascades and interactions workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Central change
steps.prompt: State the event, trend, decision, innovation, or scenario change whose consequences are being explored.

steps.title: First-order effects
steps.prompt: List direct consequences across relevant domains without evaluating them too early.

steps.title: Second-order effects
steps.prompt: For each direct consequence, identify important follow-on effects, interactions, adaptations, and feedbacks.

steps.title: Higher-order cascades and interactions
steps.prompt: Trace selected branches to tertiary effects and identify where consequence chains reinforce, offset, intersect, or create shared bottlenecks.

steps.title: Priority implications
steps.prompt: Prioritize consequence chains by plausibility, impact, timing, reversibility, risk or opportunity, and monitoring value.

definition.name: Three Horizons
definition.summary: Three Horizons uses a Horizon 1 — prevailing system → Horizon 3 — emerging future → Horizon 2 — transition → Persistence and transition patterns workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Horizon 1 — prevailing system
steps.prompt: Describe the current dominant system, why it works, where it is degrading, and what should be preserved.

steps.title: Horizon 3 — emerging future
steps.prompt: Describe the desired or plausible future system and the conditions under which it could become dominant.

steps.title: Horizon 2 — transition
steps.prompt: Identify innovations, conflicts, hybrids, experiments, and power struggles that connect the present to possible futures.

steps.title: Persistence and transition patterns
steps.prompt: Separate innovations that reinforce Horizon 1 from those that enable Horizon 3 and identify contested transition points.

steps.title: Portfolio of actions
steps.prompt: Identify actions appropriate to maintaining what works now, accelerating transition, and preparing for the emerging future.

definition.name: Causal Layered Analysis
definition.summary: Causal Layered Analysis uses a Issue and horizon → Litany → Systemic causes → Worldviews and discourse workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Issue and horizon
steps.prompt: Define the issue and time horizon before moving between surface and deep explanatory layers.

steps.title: Litany
steps.prompt: Describe the visible quantitative trends, headlines, problems, and commonly accepted descriptions of the issue.

steps.title: Systemic causes
steps.prompt: Identify social, economic, political, technological, institutional, and ecological structures that generate the surface pattern.

steps.title: Worldviews and discourse
steps.prompt: Examine assumptions, ideologies, cultural frames, and ways of knowing that make the system appear natural or necessary.

steps.title: Myth, metaphor, and alternatives
steps.prompt: Identify deep narratives or metaphors, then construct alternative narratives and trace how they imply different systems and futures.

definition.name: 2x2 Scenario Matrix
definition.summary: 2x2 Scenario Matrix uses a Focal question → Critical uncertainties → Define axis endpoints → Four scenarios workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Focal question
steps.prompt: Define the strategic question, time horizon, and decision context.

steps.title: Critical uncertainties
steps.prompt: Identify drivers that are both highly consequential and genuinely uncertain, then choose two that are sufficiently independent.

steps.title: Define axis endpoints
steps.prompt: Describe meaningful, plausible extremes for each uncertainty without using simple good/bad labels.

steps.title: Four scenarios
steps.prompt: Develop each quadrant into an internally coherent world with causal logic, actor behavior, second-order effects, and tensions.

steps.title: Implications and signposts
steps.prompt: Compare vulnerabilities, opportunities, robust actions, and early indicators across the four scenarios.

definition.name: Branching Scenario Tree
definition.summary: Branching Scenario Tree uses a Starting state → Branch points → Conditional branches → Path coherence workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Starting state
steps.prompt: Define the present state, horizon, and focal decision or uncertainty.

steps.title: Branch points
steps.prompt: Identify consequential future decisions, events, thresholds, or uncertainties that can create materially different paths.

steps.title: Conditional branches
steps.prompt: For each branch point, define plausible alternatives and the conditions under which each path becomes available.

steps.title: Path coherence
steps.prompt: Trace complete paths through the tree, checking dependencies, timing, path dependence, and branches that later reconverge.

steps.title: Signposts and decisions
steps.prompt: Associate observable signposts and contingent decisions with major branches so the tree can support adaptive planning.

definition.name: Scenario Wind Tunneling
definition.summary: Scenario Wind Tunneling uses a Scenario set → Strategy or option → Performance by scenario → Adaptations and contingencies workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Scenario set
steps.prompt: Select a sufficiently distinct set of plausible scenarios and summarize the conditions that define each.

steps.title: Strategy or option
steps.prompt: State the policy, plan, investment, or decision being stress-tested.

steps.title: Performance by scenario
steps.prompt: Assess how the strategy performs in each scenario against explicit objectives and failure criteria.

steps.title: Adaptations and contingencies
steps.prompt: Identify modifications, hedges, triggers, and fallback actions that improve performance in weak scenarios.

steps.title: Robustness judgment
steps.prompt: Distinguish robust options from scenario-dependent bets and define indicators for when to adapt.

definition.name: Scenario Stress Testing
definition.summary: Scenario Stress Testing uses a Scenario set → Strategy or assumption → Test across scenarios → Fragility and robustness workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Scenario set
steps.prompt: Select scenarios that span materially different conditions and uncertainties rather than minor variants of one forecast.

steps.title: Strategy or assumption
steps.prompt: State the policy, plan, forecast, capability, or assumption being tested and its success criteria.

steps.title: Test across scenarios
steps.prompt: Assess performance, failure modes, bottlenecks, unintended effects, and dependencies under each scenario using consistent criteria.

steps.title: Fragility and robustness
steps.prompt: Identify conditions under which the object fails, degrades gracefully, or remains effective across scenarios.

steps.title: Adaptations
steps.prompt: Define hedges, redesigns, triggers, and contingent actions that improve robustness without optimizing for only one future.

definition.name: Scenario Discovery
definition.summary: Scenario Discovery uses a Decision model → Many futures → Outcome classification → Discover vulnerable regions workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Decision model
steps.prompt: Define uncertain inputs, candidate strategies, outcomes, and unacceptable performance thresholds.

steps.title: Many futures
steps.prompt: Generate or collect a broad ensemble of plausible input combinations rather than a small hand-picked scenario set.

steps.title: Outcome classification
steps.prompt: Evaluate strategies across the ensemble and classify futures by success, vulnerability, or other decision-relevant outcomes.

steps.title: Discover vulnerable regions
steps.prompt: Use interpretable clustering or rule-finding to identify combinations of uncertainties associated with failure or opportunity.

steps.title: Decision-relevant scenarios
steps.prompt: Translate discovered regions into understandable scenarios and validate that they capture important vulnerabilities without overstating probability.

definition.name: Scenario Archetypes
definition.summary: Scenario Archetypes uses a Focal question → Drivers and tensions → Archetype set → Contextualize workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Focal question
steps.prompt: Define the system, horizon, and decision that the archetype set must illuminate.

steps.title: Drivers and tensions
steps.prompt: Identify major structural drivers, uncertainties, and tensions from scanning and analysis.

steps.title: Archetype set
steps.prompt: Construct distinct futures using recognizable patterns such as continuity, constraint, collapse, transformation, or another justified typology.

steps.title: Contextualize
steps.prompt: Adapt each archetype to the specific domain with actors, causal mechanisms, institutions, resources, and plausible events.

steps.title: Implications and signposts
steps.prompt: Compare implications across archetypes and identify indicators that distinguish generic archetypal resemblance from the actual emerging future.

definition.name: Normative Scenario Planning
definition.summary: Normative Scenario Planning uses a Preferred future → Constraints and incompatibilities → Plausible pathways → Tradeoffs and excluded futures workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Preferred future
steps.prompt: Define the desired future state, values, horizon, and measurable conditions of success.

steps.title: Constraints and incompatibilities
steps.prompt: Identify physical, institutional, political, ethical, and resource constraints that the preferred future must respect.

steps.title: Plausible pathways
steps.prompt: Work backward and forward to construct multiple credible pathways from current conditions to the preferred state.

steps.title: Tradeoffs and excluded futures
steps.prompt: Identify who benefits, who bears costs, what values conflict, and which alternative desirable futures are being deprioritized.

steps.title: Near-term actions
steps.prompt: Define robust early actions, milestones, decision points, and indicators that show whether the normative pathway remains feasible.

definition.name: Transformative Scenario Planning
definition.summary: Transformative Scenario Planning uses a System and actors → Forces shaping change → Shared scenarios → Transformative reflection workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: System and actors
steps.prompt: Define the contested system, affected actors, power relationships, and reasons existing trajectories are unacceptable or unstable.

steps.title: Forces shaping change
steps.prompt: Map structural drivers, conflicts, constraints, and uncertainties with participation from actors who hold different perspectives.

steps.title: Shared scenarios
steps.prompt: Build plausible alternative futures that allow participants to see consequences of current choices and relationships without forcing consensus.

steps.title: Transformative reflection
steps.prompt: Identify assumptions, relationships, identities, and power structures that participants may need to reconsider for change to become possible.

steps.title: Action experiments
steps.prompt: Develop feasible collaborative experiments or commitments that can alter the system while maintaining learning across uncertain futures.

definition.name: Future History
definition.summary: Future History uses a Future endpoint → Historical milestones → Causal continuity → Alternative routes workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Future endpoint
steps.prompt: Select a clearly described future state and horizon without assuming it is inevitable.

steps.title: Historical milestones
steps.prompt: Working backward, identify decisions, events, innovations, crises, and institutional changes that would plausibly precede the endpoint.

steps.title: Causal continuity
steps.prompt: Connect milestones with mechanisms, actor incentives, constraints, and feedback so the history reads as a plausible sequence rather than a list.

steps.title: Alternative routes
steps.prompt: Identify points where different choices or shocks could have produced another future and preserve those branches.

steps.title: Present-day implications
steps.prompt: Extract near-term indicators, enabling conditions, and actions that would make the imagined history more or less plausible.

definition.name: Day-in-the-Life Scenario
definition.summary: Day-in-the-Life Scenario uses a Scenario world → Focal actor → Sequence of experience → System implications workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Scenario world
steps.prompt: Define the larger future conditions that constrain the day rather than inventing a persona in isolation.

steps.title: Focal actor
steps.prompt: Choose a representative or strategically important actor and document role, needs, resources, constraints, and environment.

steps.title: Sequence of experience
steps.prompt: Walk through a typical day, showing decisions, technologies, institutions, interactions, frictions, and workarounds in concrete sequence.

steps.title: System implications
steps.prompt: Identify what the lived experience reveals about infrastructure, incentives, inequalities, demand, behavior, and policy consequences.

steps.title: Scenario consistency
steps.prompt: Check that details follow from the scenario's drivers and do not smuggle in unsupported assumptions or present-day defaults.

definition.name: Robust Strategy Across Scenarios
definition.summary: Robust Strategy Across Scenarios uses a Candidate strategies → Scenario set → Performance matrix → Robustness and regret workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Candidate strategies
steps.prompt: Define the strategic options and the outcomes or constraints that determine acceptable performance.

steps.title: Scenario set
steps.prompt: Use a diverse scenario set that captures critical uncertainties and structural differences relevant to the decision.

steps.title: Performance matrix
steps.prompt: Assess each strategy against each scenario using consistent criteria, including failure thresholds and unintended consequences.

steps.title: Robustness and regret
steps.prompt: Identify strategies with acceptable performance across scenarios and expose options that depend heavily on one future.

steps.title: Adaptive portfolio
steps.prompt: Combine robust actions, hedges, staged commitments, and scenario-linked triggers into an adaptive strategy.

definition.name: Signpost-to-Scenario Mapping
definition.summary: Signpost-to-Scenario Mapping uses a Scenario set → Candidate signposts → Diagnosticity → Map and weight workflow to construct and compare plausible futures, pathways, signposts, and robust responses under uncertainty.

steps.title: Scenario set
steps.prompt: Define the scenarios and the causal conditions that make each distinct.

steps.title: Candidate signposts
steps.prompt: Identify observable events, trends, actor behaviors, thresholds, and absences expected under one or more scenarios.

steps.title: Diagnosticity
steps.prompt: Assess which signposts distinguish scenarios, which are common to several, and which could be misleading because of collection or timing effects.

steps.title: Map and weight
steps.prompt: Associate signposts with scenarios and record expected direction, timing, strength, source, and confidence.

steps.title: Update rules
steps.prompt: Define monitoring cadence and how accumulating signposts should shift scenario attention without prematurely declaring one scenario to be the forecast.

prerequisites: Defined scenarios or competing future states
Observable developments that would distinguish those futures
A monitoring cadence and ownership for indicators

definition.name: Real-Time Delphi
definition.summary: Real-Time Delphi uses a Forecast question → Panel and independence → Continuous rounds → Track convergence and dissent workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Forecast question
steps.prompt: Define the question, horizon, resolution criteria, and response format precisely.

steps.title: Panel and independence
steps.prompt: Select relevant and diverse experts, disclose conflicts, and preserve independent initial judgments.

steps.title: Continuous rounds
steps.prompt: Collect anonymous estimates and reasons, expose controlled feedback in near real time, and allow experts to revise without waiting for fixed rounds.

steps.title: Track convergence and dissent
steps.prompt: Monitor central tendency, dispersion, persistent disagreement, and argument changes rather than treating convergence as automatically correct.

steps.title: Closure and record
steps.prompt: Apply a stopping rule, preserve final distributions and dissent, and document the evidence or assumptions that drove revisions.

definition.name: Nominal Group Technique
definition.summary: Nominal Group Technique uses a Problem or decision → Silent generation → Round-robin collection → Clarification workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Problem or decision
steps.prompt: Define the question and the criterion by which ideas or priorities will be judged.

steps.title: Silent generation
steps.prompt: Have participants generate ideas independently before discussion to reduce production blocking and status effects.

steps.title: Round-robin collection
steps.prompt: Collect one idea at a time from each participant until all ideas are recorded without debate.

steps.title: Clarification
steps.prompt: Discuss items for understanding, merge only true duplicates, and preserve minority ideas without advocacy pressure.

steps.title: Independent ranking
steps.prompt: Have participants privately rank or score priorities, aggregate the results, and record residual disagreement.

definition.name: Expert Elicitation
definition.summary: Expert Elicitation uses a Target judgment → Expert selection → Training and evidence → Individual elicitation workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Target judgment
steps.prompt: Define the uncertain quantity or proposition, units, conditioning information, time point, and resolution meaning.

steps.title: Expert selection
steps.prompt: Select experts for relevant knowledge and diversity, manage conflicts, and document roles and selection rationale.

steps.title: Training and evidence
steps.prompt: Provide common evidence, definitions, uncertainty training, and practice questions while avoiding coaching toward consensus.

steps.title: Individual elicitation
steps.prompt: Elicit central estimates, bounds or distributions, reasons, and uncertainty independently using a structured protocol.

steps.title: Aggregate and document
steps.prompt: Combine judgments using a declared behavioral or mathematical rule, preserve dissent, and document the full elicitation process.

definition.name: Structured Expert Judgment
definition.summary: Structured Expert Judgment uses a Elicitation questions → Expert selection and independence → Individual elicitation → Aggregation workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Elicitation questions
steps.prompt: Define quantities or judgments precisely enough that experts are answering the same question.

steps.title: Expert selection and independence
steps.prompt: Document relevant expertise, diversity, conflicts, and steps taken to preserve independent judgment.

steps.title: Individual elicitation
steps.prompt: Collect estimates, uncertainty ranges, and reasoning independently before discussion.

steps.title: Aggregation
steps.prompt: Compare distributions, reasons, and calibration evidence; aggregate transparently rather than forcing consensus.

steps.title: Disagreement and update
steps.prompt: Record unresolved disagreement, its causes, and what new evidence would move the panel.

prerequisites: A plan for uncertainty capture and aggregation

definition.name: Cooke's Classical Model
definition.summary: Cooke's Classical Model uses a Target and seed questions → Expert quantiles → Calibration and information → Performance weights workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Target and seed questions
steps.prompt: Define target quantities and select calibration seed questions from the same expertise domain whose true values are known to the analyst but not the experts.

steps.title: Expert quantiles
steps.prompt: Elicit the same predefined quantiles for seed and target variables from each expert using consistent framing.

steps.title: Calibration and information
steps.prompt: Score each expert's statistical calibration on seeds and the informativeness of their distributions relative to the background range.

steps.title: Performance weights
steps.prompt: Compute declared performance-based weights, including any calibration cutoff or optimization rule, and compare with equal weighting.

steps.title: Combined distribution
steps.prompt: Pool target distributions using the selected weights and report sensitivity to seed choice, background range, and weighting rule.

definition.name: Probability Elicitation
definition.summary: Probability Elicitation uses a Event definition → Reference points → Initial probability → Calibration challenge workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Event definition
steps.prompt: Define the event, resolution criteria, time horizon, and information set so ambiguity is minimized.

steps.title: Reference points
steps.prompt: Consider relevant base rates, comparable cases, and decompositions before giving a probability.

steps.title: Initial probability
steps.prompt: State a numeric probability or distribution and record the key reasons behind it.

steps.title: Calibration challenge
steps.prompt: Test for overconfidence, anchoring, scope neglect, and whether alternative outcomes received enough probability mass.

steps.title: Uncertainty representation
steps.prompt: Record plausible bounds or quantiles and identify information most likely to move the estimate.

definition.name: Quantile Elicitation
definition.summary: Quantile Elicitation uses a Quantity and range → Median → Lower and upper quantiles → Coherence check workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Quantity and range
steps.prompt: Define the uncertain quantity, units, conditioning assumptions, and physically or logically possible range.

steps.title: Median
steps.prompt: Elicit the 50th percentile first or at an appropriate stage, asking for the value equally likely to be above or below.

steps.title: Lower and upper quantiles
steps.prompt: Elicit symmetric or protocol-specified tail quantiles and challenge whether the stated interval is unrealistically narrow.

steps.title: Coherence check
steps.prompt: Check ordering, bounds, interpretation of percentiles, and whether the implied distribution matches the expert's verbal beliefs.

steps.title: Review and record
steps.prompt: Allow revision after feedback on inconsistencies and document final quantiles plus the reasoning behind tail judgments.

definition.name: Calibration Training
definition.summary: Calibration Training uses a Forecast set → Probability bins → Calibration bias → Targeted practice workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Forecast set
steps.prompt: Assemble a sufficiently large set of resolved probabilistic judgments with clear resolution criteria.

steps.title: Probability bins
steps.prompt: Group forecasts into probability ranges and compare forecast probabilities with observed frequencies.

steps.title: Calibration bias
steps.prompt: Identify systematic overconfidence, underconfidence, extremizing, hedging, or category-specific errors.

steps.title: Targeted practice
steps.prompt: Create exercises that focus on weak probability ranges, base-rate use, decomposition, and updating behavior.

steps.title: Feedback loop
steps.prompt: Track calibration and discrimination over time and specify concrete habits to retain or change.

definition.name: Brier Score Review
definition.summary: Brier Score Review uses a Forecast set → Score outcomes → Calibration → Resolution and discrimination workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Forecast set
steps.prompt: List resolved probabilistic forecasts and their stated probabilities.

steps.title: Score outcomes
steps.prompt: Calculate squared probability errors for each forecast and the mean Brier score.

steps.title: Calibration
steps.prompt: Group forecasts by probability band and compare stated probabilities with observed frequencies.

steps.title: Resolution and discrimination
steps.prompt: Did forecasts meaningfully distinguish events that occurred from those that did not?

steps.title: Forecasting lessons
steps.prompt: Identify systematic overconfidence, underconfidence, base-rate neglect, or category-specific weaknesses to correct.

prerequisites: Original stated probabilities preserved before resolution

definition.name: Superforecasting Tournament
definition.summary: Superforecasting Tournament uses a Resolvable questions → Independent probabilities → Frequent updating → Proper scoring workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Resolvable questions
steps.prompt: Create clear, time-bounded questions with unambiguous resolution criteria and base-rate relevance.

steps.title: Independent probabilities
steps.prompt: Collect individual probabilistic forecasts with reasons and timestamps before discussion or aggregation.

steps.title: Frequent updating
steps.prompt: Encourage forecasters to update when evidence changes and preserve the full forecast trajectory rather than only final answers.

steps.title: Proper scoring
steps.prompt: Score resolved forecasts with a proper rule such as Brier score and compare calibration, discrimination, and update behavior.

steps.title: Selection and learning
steps.prompt: Use repeated performance, decomposition, feedback, and team practices to improve forecasting skill without overfitting to a small question set.

definition.name: Prediction Market Design
definition.summary: Prediction Market Design uses a Market question → Participation and incentives → Trading mechanism → Market quality workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Market question
steps.prompt: Translate the forecast into a contract with clear payoff, resolution source, deadline, and treatment of cancellation or ambiguity.

steps.title: Participation and incentives
steps.prompt: Define access, stake limits, incentives, information rules, and protections against manipulation or coercion.

steps.title: Trading mechanism
steps.prompt: Choose market maker, order book, auction, or other mechanism and specify liquidity and price interpretation.

steps.title: Market quality
steps.prompt: Monitor participation concentration, liquidity, manipulation, information cascades, and whether prices reflect genuine independent information.

steps.title: Resolution and evaluation
steps.prompt: Resolve transparently, score market forecasts against outcomes, and analyze when market prices added value over simpler aggregation.

definition.name: Wisdom-of-Crowds Aggregation
definition.summary: Wisdom-of-Crowds Aggregation uses a Common question → Preserve independence → Diversity and competence → Aggregation rule workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Common question
steps.prompt: Ensure all participants answer the same well-specified question with the same information cutoff.

steps.title: Preserve independence
steps.prompt: Collect judgments before group discussion and identify shared sources or coordination that reduce effective independence.

steps.title: Diversity and competence
steps.prompt: Assess whether the crowd contains relevant knowledge and genuinely different information rather than noise alone.

steps.title: Aggregation rule
steps.prompt: Use a transparent statistic or model such as median, mean, trimmed mean, or weighted average appropriate to the judgment type.

steps.title: Crowd audit
steps.prompt: Compare aggregate performance with individuals and benchmarks, checking correlation, herding, outliers, and domain-specific failure modes.

definition.name: Independent Estimate Aggregation
definition.summary: Independent Estimate Aggregation uses a Estimate task → Independent estimates → Dependency check → Combine estimates workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Estimate task
steps.prompt: Define the quantity, units, information set, and assumptions shared by all estimators.

steps.title: Independent estimates
steps.prompt: Obtain estimates and uncertainty from each analyst before exposing others' answers or rationales.

steps.title: Dependency check
steps.prompt: Identify common models, data, anchors, or organizational assumptions that make estimates less independent than they appear.

steps.title: Combine estimates
steps.prompt: Apply a declared aggregation rule and compare mean, median, trimmed, or performance-weighted results where appropriate.

steps.title: Review dispersion
steps.prompt: Investigate extreme disagreement as information, not merely noise, and document whether reconciliation changes the aggregate.

definition.name: Estimate-Talk-Estimate
definition.summary: Estimate-Talk-Estimate uses a First estimate → Reveal distribution → Focused discussion → Second independent estimate workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: First estimate
steps.prompt: Have participants make and record independent estimates, uncertainty, and key assumptions before any discussion.

steps.title: Reveal distribution
steps.prompt: Share the range and anonymized rationales so participants can see differences without status-driven advocacy.

steps.title: Focused discussion
steps.prompt: Discuss the evidence and crux assumptions causing dispersion rather than negotiating toward a midpoint.

steps.title: Second independent estimate
steps.prompt: Have participants privately re-estimate after discussion so updates remain individually accountable.

steps.title: Aggregate and learn
steps.prompt: Combine second-round estimates and record which arguments changed judgments and which disagreements persist.

definition.name: Wideband Delphi
definition.summary: Wideband Delphi uses a Question and criteria → Anonymous initial estimates → Facilitated discussion → Iterative re-estimation workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Question and criteria
steps.prompt: Define the estimate or decision problem, units, assumptions, and acceptance criteria.

steps.title: Anonymous initial estimates
steps.prompt: Collect independent estimates plus rationale before group interaction.

steps.title: Facilitated discussion
steps.prompt: Present the distribution and discuss major assumptions, evidence, and causes of divergence without forcing consensus.

steps.title: Iterative re-estimation
steps.prompt: Repeat anonymous estimates and structured feedback for a bounded number of rounds or until a stopping rule is met.

steps.title: Result and dissent
steps.prompt: Aggregate the final round, retain the range and dissenting rationales, and document what changed across rounds.

definition.name: Paired Comparison Elicitation
definition.summary: Paired Comparison Elicitation uses a Items → Pairwise judgments → Comparison coverage → Consistency and cycles workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Items
steps.prompt: Define the alternatives or attributes and the precise comparison criterion.

steps.title: Pairwise judgments
steps.prompt: Present pairs in a balanced order and ask which item better satisfies the criterion, optionally eliciting strength of preference.

steps.title: Comparison coverage
steps.prompt: Ensure enough pairs are judged to estimate an ordering while avoiding unnecessary respondent burden.

steps.title: Consistency and cycles
steps.prompt: Check transitivity, cycles, context effects, and inconsistent repeated pairs rather than silently forcing an order.

steps.title: Derive priorities
steps.prompt: Convert comparisons into a ranking or scale with a stated method and report uncertainty or unresolved ties.

definition.name: Rank-Order Elicitation
definition.summary: Rank-Order Elicitation uses a Candidate items → Ordering anchors → Independent rank order → Aggregate rankings workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Candidate items
steps.prompt: Define the items and the single criterion on which they must be ordered.

steps.title: Ordering anchors
steps.prompt: Clarify best, worst, ties, incomparability, and whether partial rankings are allowed before elicitation.

steps.title: Independent rank order
steps.prompt: Have experts rank items without seeing peers' rankings and capture reasons for adjacent distinctions.

steps.title: Aggregate rankings
steps.prompt: Use a transparent rank aggregation method and inspect disagreement, ties, and sensitivity to the chosen rule.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Separate ordinal priority from magnitude of difference and identify items needing richer scoring or additional evidence.

definition.name: Confidence Interval Elicitation
definition.summary: Confidence Interval Elicitation uses a Quantity → Central estimate → Interval bounds → Overconfidence challenge workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Quantity
steps.prompt: Define the uncertain quantity, units, reference class, and conditioning information.

steps.title: Central estimate
steps.prompt: Elicit a central or median estimate with reasoning before or between bound judgments according to the chosen protocol.

steps.title: Interval bounds
steps.prompt: Elicit bounds for a specified coverage probability and explicitly ask what outcomes would fall outside the interval.

steps.title: Overconfidence challenge
steps.prompt: Use counterexamples, base rates, decomposition, or equivalent-bin checks to test whether the interval is implausibly narrow.

steps.title: Final interval
steps.prompt: Record the final probability coverage, bounds, assumptions, and whether the interval is symmetric or skewed.

definition.name: Consensus Mapping
definition.summary: Consensus Mapping uses a Question → Individual positions → Position clusters → Consensus and cruxes workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Question
steps.prompt: Define the proposition, forecast, or decision on which agreement and disagreement will be mapped.

steps.title: Individual positions
steps.prompt: Collect independent judgments, confidence, key reasons, and definitions before discussing convergence.

steps.title: Position clusters
steps.prompt: Group genuinely similar positions and distinguish agreement on conclusion from agreement on evidence or reasoning.

steps.title: Consensus and cruxes
steps.prompt: Map points of agreement, partial agreement, factual disputes, value differences, and unresolved causal or probabilistic cruxes.

steps.title: Report structure
steps.prompt: Present the consensus area alongside material minority views and the evidence that could move each cluster.

definition.name: Disagreement Decomposition
definition.summary: Disagreement Decomposition uses a Observed disagreement → Decompose causes → Swap assumptions → Residual disagreement workflow to elicit, aggregate, calibrate, and diagnose expert forecasts and uncertain judgments.

steps.title: Observed disagreement
steps.prompt: State the differing judgments precisely, including probabilities, scope, timing, or recommended actions.

steps.title: Decompose causes
steps.prompt: Test whether disagreement comes from different data, source trust, definitions, models, causal assumptions, priors, values, or thresholds.

steps.title: Swap assumptions
steps.prompt: Ask how each analyst's conclusion would change if they adopted the other's key inputs or assumptions.

steps.title: Residual disagreement
steps.prompt: Separate disagreements that can be resolved with facts or clarification from deep model, value, or uncertainty differences.

steps.title: Resolution plan
steps.prompt: Identify the highest-value evidence, experiment, or decision rule for reducing disagreement while preserving unresolved dissent.

definition.name: Analytic Hierarchy Process
definition.summary: Analytic Hierarchy Process uses a Goal and hierarchy → Pairwise criteria comparisons → Alternative comparisons → Consistency check workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Goal and hierarchy
steps.prompt: Define the decision goal, criteria, subcriteria if needed, and alternatives.

steps.title: Pairwise criteria comparisons
steps.prompt: Compare criteria two at a time using a consistent preference scale and record the rationale.

steps.title: Alternative comparisons
steps.prompt: Compare alternatives pairwise under each criterion.

steps.title: Consistency check
steps.prompt: Review comparison consistency and revisit judgments that create strong contradictions.

steps.title: Priority synthesis
steps.prompt: Combine weights and alternative scores, then test whether modest judgment changes alter the ranking.

definition.name: Analytic Network Process
definition.summary: Analytic Network Process uses a Decision network → Pairwise comparisons → Supermatrix → Limit priorities workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Decision network
steps.prompt: Define the goal, criteria, subcriteria, alternatives, and feedback or dependence relationships that make a simple hierarchy inadequate.

steps.title: Pairwise comparisons
steps.prompt: Make pairwise judgments within and across dependent clusters using a consistent ratio scale and document the rationale.

steps.title: Supermatrix
steps.prompt: Assemble local priority vectors into the unweighted supermatrix, apply cluster weights, and form the weighted supermatrix.

steps.title: Limit priorities
steps.prompt: Raise or iterate the weighted supermatrix to convergence and extract limiting priorities for the alternatives.

steps.title: Consistency and sensitivity
steps.prompt: Check comparison consistency and test whether plausible changes in judgments or dependency structure alter the ranking.

definition.name: Weighted Sum Model
definition.summary: Weighted Sum Model uses a Decision matrix → Criterion weights → Normalize scores → Weighted totals workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Decision matrix
steps.prompt: Define alternatives, criteria, direction of preference, and commensurate or normalized criterion scores.

steps.title: Criterion weights
steps.prompt: Assign explicit nonnegative weights that reflect relative importance and sum to a common total.

steps.title: Normalize scores
steps.prompt: Transform criterion values to a comparable benefit scale when units differ, documenting the normalization rule.

steps.title: Weighted totals
steps.prompt: Multiply each normalized score by its criterion weight and sum across criteria for each alternative.

steps.title: Ranking sensitivity
steps.prompt: Inspect criterion contributions and test whether reasonable weight or normalization changes reverse the ranking.

definition.name: Weighted Product Model
definition.summary: Weighted Product Model uses a Decision matrix → Criterion exponents → Normalize or ratio-scale → Weighted products workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Decision matrix
steps.prompt: Define positive criterion values, alternatives, preference direction, and criteria requiring transformation before multiplication.
