steps.title: Criterion exponents
steps.prompt: Assign normalized importance weights and confirm that the multiplicative interpretation is appropriate.

steps.title: Normalize or ratio-scale
steps.prompt: Express performances on compatible positive ratio scales so multiplicative comparisons are meaningful.

steps.title: Weighted products
steps.prompt: Raise each criterion score to its weight, multiply across criteria, and derive relative preference values.

steps.title: Interpret and test
steps.prompt: Check dominance, zero or negative-value problems, scale sensitivity, and whether plausible weights alter the preferred alternative.

definition.name: TOPSIS
definition.summary: TOPSIS uses a Decision matrix → Normalize and weight → Ideal solutions → Distances workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Decision matrix
steps.prompt: Define alternatives, criteria, direction of preference, and measurement scales.

steps.title: Normalize and weight
steps.prompt: Normalize criterion values appropriately and apply explicit criterion weights.

steps.title: Ideal solutions
steps.prompt: Construct the positive ideal and negative ideal reference points across weighted criteria.

steps.title: Distances
steps.prompt: Calculate each alternative's distance from both ideals and the relative closeness score.

steps.title: Ranking and sensitivity
steps.prompt: Rank alternatives, inspect criterion contributions, and test whether plausible weight or normalization changes alter the result.

definition.name: ELECTRE
definition.summary: ELECTRE uses a Alternatives and criteria → Pairwise concordance → Discordance and veto → Outranking relation workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Alternatives and criteria
steps.prompt: Define alternatives, criteria, weights, preference direction, and any indifference, preference, or veto thresholds.

steps.title: Pairwise concordance
steps.prompt: For each pair of alternatives, assess the weighted evidence that one is at least as good as the other.

steps.title: Discordance and veto
steps.prompt: Identify criteria where poor performance strongly opposes or vetoes an outranking relation.

steps.title: Outranking relation
steps.prompt: Apply the selected ELECTRE variant's concordance and discordance rules to construct the outranking graph or ranking.

steps.title: Robustness
steps.prompt: Test sensitivity to thresholds, weights, incomparability, and the chosen ELECTRE variant before interpreting the result.

definition.name: PROMETHEE
definition.summary: PROMETHEE uses a Decision matrix → Pairwise preferences → Preference flows → PROMETHEE ranking workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Decision matrix
steps.prompt: Define alternatives, criteria, weights, preference direction, and criterion-specific preference functions.

steps.title: Pairwise preferences
steps.prompt: Convert pairwise performance differences into preference degrees using the selected functions and thresholds.

steps.title: Preference flows
steps.prompt: Calculate positive and negative outranking flows for each alternative and derive net flows where appropriate.

steps.title: PROMETHEE ranking
steps.prompt: Use partial or complete ranking consistent with the chosen PROMETHEE variant and identify incomparabilities if retained.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test how preference functions, thresholds, and weights affect flows and the final ranking.

definition.name: VIKOR
definition.summary: VIKOR uses a Decision matrix → Best and worst values → Utility and regret → Compromise index workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Decision matrix
steps.prompt: Define alternatives, criteria, weights, and benefit or cost direction for each criterion.

steps.title: Best and worst values
steps.prompt: Identify criterion-wise ideal and anti-ideal values and normalize regret from the ideal.

steps.title: Utility and regret
steps.prompt: Calculate each alternative's aggregate group utility measure and maximum individual-regret measure.

steps.title: Compromise index
steps.prompt: Combine utility and regret using the declared strategy weight and rank alternatives by the VIKOR index.

steps.title: Compromise conditions
steps.prompt: Check acceptable advantage and stability conditions and report a compromise set when a unique solution is not justified.

definition.name: SMART Decision Analysis
definition.summary: SMART Decision Analysis uses a Objectives and attributes → Value scores → Swing weights → Aggregate value workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Objectives and attributes
steps.prompt: Define a value tree of decision objectives and measurable attributes, avoiding double counting.

steps.title: Value scores
steps.prompt: Construct defensible single-attribute value scales and score each alternative's performance.

steps.title: Swing weights
steps.prompt: Weight attributes by the value of moving from their worst to best relevant levels, not by vague importance alone.

steps.title: Aggregate value
steps.prompt: Combine value scores and weights under the additive-independence assumptions of SMART.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test uncertain scores and weights, identify tradeoffs, and report where the additive model's assumptions are questionable.

definition.name: SMARTER
definition.summary: SMARTER uses a Objectives and attributes → Value scores → Rank importance → Rank-order centroid weights workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Objectives and attributes
steps.prompt: Define a nonredundant value tree and measurable attributes for comparing the alternatives.

steps.title: Value scores
steps.prompt: Convert performances to common value scales with explicit best, worst, and intermediate anchors.

steps.title: Rank importance
steps.prompt: Rank criteria by swing importance rather than eliciting precise numerical weights directly.

steps.title: Rank-order centroid weights
steps.prompt: Convert the criterion ranking into rank-order centroid weights and calculate aggregate alternative values.

steps.title: Robustness
steps.prompt: Test alternative plausible criterion orders and value scores to see whether the recommended option is stable.

definition.name: Swing Weighting
definition.summary: Swing Weighting uses a Criteria and ranges → Value of swings → Assign weights → Normalize workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Criteria and ranges
steps.prompt: Define decision criteria and the worst-to-best performance range that matters for each.

steps.title: Value of swings
steps.prompt: Imagine moving one criterion from worst to best while others remain worst; rank these swings by value.

steps.title: Assign weights
steps.prompt: Give the most valuable swing a reference weight and scale the remaining swings relative to it.

steps.title: Normalize
steps.prompt: Convert raw swing weights into normalized weights and verify that stakeholders understand their meaning.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test how plausible changes in ranges or swing judgments affect alternative rankings.

definition.name: Multi-Attribute Utility Theory
definition.summary: Multi-Attribute Utility Theory uses a Objectives → Single-attribute utilities → Tradeoff weights → Evaluate alternatives workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Objectives
steps.prompt: Define decision objectives and attributes so important values are represented without double counting.

steps.title: Single-attribute utilities
steps.prompt: Elicit utility functions that capture preference over performance levels and risk attitude where relevant.

steps.title: Tradeoff weights
steps.prompt: Elicit scaling constants or tradeoffs among attributes under the assumptions required for the chosen additive or multiplicative form.

steps.title: Evaluate alternatives
steps.prompt: Calculate expected utility for alternatives using explicit probabilities where outcomes are uncertain.

steps.title: Preference assumptions
steps.prompt: Check independence assumptions, risk sensitivity, and whether modest utility or probability changes alter the preferred option.

definition.name: Multi-Attribute Value Theory
definition.summary: Multi-Attribute Value Theory uses a Objectives → Value functions → Scaling constants → Aggregate values workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Objectives
steps.prompt: Define the decision objectives, value-relevant attributes, feasible alternatives, and stakeholder perspective.

steps.title: Value functions
steps.prompt: Construct single-attribute value functions that map each attribute's performance to relative value.

steps.title: Scaling constants
steps.prompt: Elicit tradeoff or swing weights consistent with the chosen additive or multiplicative value model.

steps.title: Aggregate values
steps.prompt: Calculate overall value for each alternative using the declared preference-independence assumptions.

steps.title: Preference sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test weights, value functions, omitted objectives, and independence assumptions before recommending an alternative.

definition.name: Kepner-Tregoe Decision Analysis
definition.summary: Kepner-Tregoe Decision Analysis uses a Decision statement and objectives → Screen musts → Score wants → Adverse consequences workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Decision statement and objectives
steps.prompt: State the decision, generate alternatives, and separate must-have requirements from weighted wants.

steps.title: Screen musts
steps.prompt: Reject alternatives that fail mandatory constraints using explicit pass/fail evidence.

steps.title: Score wants
steps.prompt: Weight desirable objectives and score surviving alternatives consistently against each one.

steps.title: Adverse consequences
steps.prompt: Identify material risks or negative consequences for leading alternatives and assess probability and seriousness.

steps.title: Balanced choice
steps.prompt: Select the alternative with the strongest objective performance after considering adverse consequences and sensitivity.

definition.name: Pugh Matrix
definition.summary: Pugh Matrix uses a Need and baseline → Concepts → Relative comparison → Synthesize concepts workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Need and baseline
steps.prompt: Define the design need, evaluation criteria, and a clear datum or reference concept.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.prompt: List the candidate concepts at a comparable level of maturity.

steps.title: Relative comparison
steps.prompt: Rate each concept as better, same, or worse than the datum for each criterion and document the rationale.

steps.title: Synthesize concepts
steps.prompt: Look for strong features that can be combined and weaknesses that suggest redesign rather than simply totaling marks.

steps.title: Iterate
steps.prompt: Select promising concepts, choose a new datum if useful, and repeat until tradeoffs and design directions are clear.

definition.name: QFD House of Quality
definition.summary: QFD House of Quality uses a Customer needs → Technical characteristics → Relationship matrix → Technical correlations workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Customer needs
steps.prompt: Capture and prioritize customer or stakeholder needs in their own terms, including evidence for importance.

steps.title: Technical characteristics
steps.prompt: Translate needs into measurable design or service characteristics under the team's control.

steps.title: Relationship matrix
steps.prompt: Rate how strongly each technical characteristic affects each need and document ambiguous relationships.

steps.title: Technical correlations
steps.prompt: Map reinforcing and conflicting relationships among technical characteristics and identify design tradeoffs.

steps.title: Priorities and targets
steps.prompt: Combine need importance, relationships, competitive benchmarks, and technical difficulty into prioritized engineering targets.

definition.name: MoSCoW Prioritization
definition.summary: MoSCoW Prioritization uses a Scope and timebox → Category rules → Classify requirements → Capacity check workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Scope and timebox
steps.prompt: Define the delivery scope, deadline, resource constraint, and minimum viable outcome before prioritizing requirements.

steps.title: Category rules
steps.prompt: Define operational rules for Must, Should, Could, and Won't-this-time so categories are not just synonyms for priority levels.

steps.title: Classify requirements
steps.prompt: Assign each requirement using consequence-of-omission and dependency reasoning, recording why it belongs in that category.

steps.title: Capacity check
steps.prompt: Verify that Must items fit the available capacity and demote items if everything has been labeled mandatory.

steps.title: Review dependencies
steps.prompt: Check cross-item dependencies, deferred items, and trigger conditions for reprioritization during the timebox.

definition.name: RICE Scoring
definition.summary: RICE Scoring uses a Candidate initiatives → Reach → Impact and confidence → Effort workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Candidate initiatives
steps.prompt: Define comparable initiatives and the horizon over which their impact and effort will be estimated.

steps.title: Reach
steps.prompt: Estimate how many users, cases, or units each initiative will affect within the chosen period and document the basis.

steps.title: Impact and confidence
steps.prompt: Assign impact using a consistent scale and confidence reflecting evidence quality for reach, impact, and effort estimates.

steps.title: Effort
steps.prompt: Estimate total person-time or another consistent resource measure including major hidden dependencies.

steps.title: RICE ranking
steps.prompt: Calculate reach × impact × confidence / effort, then review strategic dependencies and sensitivity rather than treating the score as automatic truth.

definition.name: WSJF Prioritization
definition.summary: WSJF Prioritization uses a Work items → Cost of delay → Job size → WSJF score workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Work items
steps.prompt: Define items at comparable granularity and the delivery system in which delay and job size matter.

steps.title: Cost of delay
steps.prompt: Estimate user or business value, time criticality, and risk reduction or opportunity enablement using a consistent relative scale.

steps.title: Job size
steps.prompt: Estimate relative duration or effort with the same reference scale across items.

steps.title: WSJF score
steps.prompt: Divide relative cost of delay by relative job size and rank the work items.

steps.title: Flow and dependency review
steps.prompt: Check dependencies, capacity, sequencing constraints, stale estimates, and whether score differences are meaningful enough to drive order.

definition.name: Pairwise Comparison Matrix
definition.summary: Pairwise Comparison Matrix uses a Items and criterion → Pairwise judgments → Reciprocal matrix → Derive priorities workflow to compare alternatives against explicit criteria, weights, priorities, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Items and criterion
steps.prompt: Define the alternatives or criteria and the single dimension on which each pair will be compared.

steps.title: Pairwise judgments
steps.prompt: Compare every required pair using a consistent ordinal or ratio scale and record the basis for each judgment.

steps.title: Reciprocal matrix
steps.prompt: Construct the comparison matrix, including reciprocal entries where the scale requires them.

steps.title: Derive priorities
steps.prompt: Calculate relative priorities using the declared method, such as normalized columns, eigenvector, or geometric mean.

steps.title: Consistency and sensitivity
steps.prompt: Check logical consistency or consistency ratio where applicable and test whether uncertain judgments affect the ordering.

definition.name: Expected Value Analysis
definition.summary: Expected Value Analysis uses a Options and outcomes → Probabilities → Outcome values → Expected values workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Options and outcomes
steps.prompt: List the available options and materially different outcomes for each.

steps.title: Probabilities
steps.prompt: Assign probabilities to uncertain outcomes using explicit evidence or assumptions; ensure mutually exclusive outcomes sum appropriately.

steps.title: Outcome values
steps.prompt: Estimate benefits, costs, or other commensurable values for each outcome and document perspective and units.

steps.title: Expected values
steps.prompt: Multiply outcome values by their probabilities and sum by option.

steps.title: Decision limits
steps.prompt: Compare options while noting risk tolerance, tail outcomes, non-monetized effects, and sensitivity to probability or value assumptions.

definition.name: Expected Utility Analysis
definition.summary: Expected Utility Analysis uses a Options and uncertain outcomes → Outcome probabilities → Utility function → Expected utility workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Options and uncertain outcomes
steps.prompt: Define feasible options and the materially different outcomes that can follow from each.

steps.title: Outcome probabilities
steps.prompt: Assign probabilities or distributions using explicit evidence and verify that mutually exclusive outcomes are exhaustive enough for the decision.

steps.title: Utility function
steps.prompt: Translate outcome consequences into utility that reflects the decision maker's preferences and risk attitude rather than using money or raw scores automatically.

steps.title: Expected utility
steps.prompt: Multiply each outcome utility by its probability and sum within each option.

steps.title: Preference and probability sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test whether the preferred option changes under plausible probability, utility, or risk-attitude assumptions.

definition.name: Minimax Decision Rule
definition.summary: Minimax Decision Rule uses a Options → Payoff matrix → Worst-case outcome → Minimax choice workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Options
steps.prompt: List feasible actions and the future states or adversary responses relevant to the decision.

steps.title: Payoff matrix
steps.prompt: Estimate the performance of each option in each state using a consistent objective.

steps.title: Worst-case outcome
steps.prompt: Identify the minimum payoff or maximum loss for each option.

steps.title: Minimax choice
steps.prompt: Choose the option whose worst-case outcome is best under the chosen payoff orientation.

steps.title: Applicability and sensitivity
steps.prompt: Assess whether extreme pessimism, payoff uncertainty, dominated options, or omitted states make the minimax rule misleading.

definition.name: Maximin Decision Rule
definition.summary: Maximin Decision Rule uses a Options → Payoff matrix → Minimum payoff → Maximin choice workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Options
steps.prompt: Define feasible options and the uncertain states of the world.

steps.title: Payoff matrix
steps.prompt: Record payoff or utility for every option-state combination using one consistent orientation.

steps.title: Minimum payoff
steps.prompt: Find the lowest payoff available to each option across all states.

steps.title: Maximin choice
steps.prompt: Select the option with the largest minimum payoff and record any ties.

steps.title: Conservatism check
steps.prompt: Test whether the rule is appropriate for the stakes and whether modest payoff changes or a broader state set change the recommendation.

definition.name: Minimax Regret
definition.summary: Minimax Regret uses a Options → Future states → Payoff matrix → Regret matrix workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Options
steps.prompt: List feasible decisions or strategies.

steps.title: Future states
steps.prompt: Define materially different states of the world without assigning probabilities if they are not defensible.

steps.title: Payoff matrix
steps.prompt: Estimate the payoff or performance of each option in each state using a consistent measure.

steps.title: Regret matrix
steps.prompt: For each state, calculate regret as the difference from the best-performing option in that state.

steps.title: Minimax-regret choice
steps.prompt: Identify each option's maximum regret, select the smallest maximum regret, and examine sensitivity to payoff assumptions.

definition.name: Laplace Criterion
definition.summary: Laplace Criterion uses a States without reliable probabilities → Payoff matrix → Equal-probability assumption → Average payoff workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: States without reliable probabilities
steps.prompt: Define mutually exclusive states of the world when no defensible probability differences are available.

steps.title: Payoff matrix
steps.prompt: Estimate option performance in each state on a consistent scale.

steps.title: Equal-probability assumption
steps.prompt: Assign equal probability to each state explicitly and verify that the state partition itself does not distort the weighting.

steps.title: Average payoff
steps.prompt: Calculate the arithmetic mean payoff for each option and rank the options.

steps.title: Partition sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test whether splitting or merging states, or obtaining even weak probability information, materially changes the result.

definition.name: Hurwicz Criterion
definition.summary: Hurwicz Criterion uses a Options and states → Best and worst outcomes → Optimism coefficient → Hurwicz score workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Options and states
steps.prompt: Define the payoff matrix for feasible options across uncertain future states.

steps.title: Best and worst outcomes
steps.prompt: Identify each option's maximum and minimum payoff.

steps.title: Optimism coefficient
steps.prompt: Choose and justify an optimism coefficient between 0 and 1 rather than selecting it to favor a preferred option.

steps.title: Hurwicz score
steps.prompt: Combine each option's best and worst payoff using the declared coefficient and rank the results.

steps.title: Optimism sensitivity
steps.prompt: Vary the coefficient across a reasonable range and identify where the preferred option switches.

definition.name: Dominance Analysis
definition.summary: Dominance Analysis uses a Alternatives and outcomes → Preference direction → Pairwise dominance → Remove dominated options workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Alternatives and outcomes
steps.prompt: Define alternatives and the criteria, states, or consequences on which dominance will be assessed.

steps.title: Preference direction
steps.prompt: Specify what better means for each dimension and normalize only where necessary.

steps.title: Pairwise dominance
steps.prompt: Identify alternatives that are at least as good on every relevant dimension and strictly better on at least one.

steps.title: Remove dominated options
steps.prompt: Eliminate strictly dominated alternatives and note weak or conditional dominance separately.

steps.title: Residual choice
steps.prompt: Analyze tradeoffs among nondominated options rather than forcing dominance where dimensions conflict.

definition.name: Stochastic Dominance
definition.summary: Stochastic Dominance uses a Outcome distributions → Cumulative distributions → Dominance order → Crossings and violations workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Outcome distributions
steps.prompt: Define the uncertain outcome distribution for each alternative on a common consequence scale.

steps.title: Cumulative distributions
steps.prompt: Compare cumulative distribution functions or equivalent integrals across the relevant outcome range.

steps.title: Dominance order
steps.prompt: Test first-order, second-order, or higher-order stochastic dominance according to the assumed class of utility functions.

steps.title: Crossings and violations
steps.prompt: Identify distribution crossings or regions where dominance fails instead of averaging away the conflict.

steps.title: Decision implications
steps.prompt: State which alternatives can be rejected under the chosen dominance order and what preference assumptions remain necessary among survivors.

definition.name: Sensitivity Analysis
definition.summary: Sensitivity Analysis uses a Result under review → Uncertain inputs → Plausible ranges → Vary systematically workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Result under review
steps.prompt: State the model result, ranking, estimate, or decision being tested.

steps.title: Uncertain inputs
steps.prompt: Identify assumptions and input values that could reasonably vary.

steps.title: Plausible ranges
steps.prompt: Set defensible alternative values or ranges rather than arbitrary extremes.

steps.title: Vary systematically
steps.prompt: Change one or more inputs and record how the result responds, including thresholds or reversals.

steps.title: Robustness conclusion
steps.prompt: Identify the inputs that dominate the result and the range over which the conclusion remains stable.

definition.name: Tornado Diagram Analysis
definition.summary: Tornado Diagram Analysis uses a Base-case result → Input ranges → One-way effects → Rank drivers workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Base-case result
steps.prompt: Define the model output and base-case assumptions.

steps.title: Input ranges
steps.prompt: Select influential uncertain inputs and defensible low/high values while holding other assumptions at baseline.

steps.title: One-way effects
steps.prompt: Recalculate the output at each input's low and high value and measure the resulting range.

steps.title: Rank drivers
steps.prompt: Order inputs by output impact to produce the tornado structure and identify nonlinear or asymmetric effects.

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.prompt: Use dominant drivers to prioritize better data, scenario analysis, or multi-way sensitivity where interactions matter.

definition.name: Threshold Analysis
definition.summary: Threshold Analysis uses a Decision and threshold → Decision relationship → Threshold value → Plausibility of crossing workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Decision and threshold
steps.prompt: Define the decision rule and the uncertain variable or performance measure that could change the preferred action.

steps.title: Decision relationship
steps.prompt: Specify how the variable affects costs, benefits, utility, risk, or another decision metric.

steps.title: Threshold value
steps.prompt: Solve for the value at which two options become equivalent or a requirement is just met.

steps.title: Plausibility of crossing
steps.prompt: Compare the threshold with current estimates, uncertainty ranges, historical evidence, and feasible intervention levels.

steps.title: Monitoring and action
steps.prompt: Define evidence or indicators that should trigger a decision update as the variable approaches the threshold.

definition.name: Break-Even Analysis
definition.summary: Break-Even Analysis uses a Alternatives and cost structure → Cost and benefit equations → Break-even point → Uncertainty and multiple drivers workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Alternatives and cost structure
steps.prompt: Define the alternatives, fixed costs, variable costs, revenues or benefits, and common unit of activity.

steps.title: Cost and benefit equations
steps.prompt: Express total cost or net value as a function of volume, time, price, or another key driver.

steps.title: Break-even point
steps.prompt: Solve for the activity level or variable value at which the alternatives have equal net outcome.

steps.title: Uncertainty and multiple drivers
steps.prompt: Test uncertain costs, capacity constraints, nonlinearities, and whether more than one variable moves together.

steps.title: Decision range
steps.prompt: State which alternative is preferred below and above the break-even point and whether the relevant range is realistically reachable.

definition.name: Monte Carlo Simulation Review
definition.summary: Monte Carlo Simulation Review uses a Simulation model → Input distributions → Simulation runs → Output distribution workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Simulation model
steps.prompt: Define outputs, uncertain inputs, dependencies, equations, and decision questions before running simulations.

steps.title: Input distributions
steps.prompt: Choose and justify probability distributions from data, expert judgment, or bounded assumptions, including correlations.

steps.title: Simulation runs
steps.prompt: Run enough trials to stabilize the decision-relevant output distribution and verify implementation against simple test cases.

steps.title: Output distribution
steps.prompt: Examine percentiles, tail probabilities, threshold exceedance, expected values, and drivers rather than reporting only an average.

steps.title: Sensitivity and validation
steps.prompt: Check convergence, distribution assumptions, correlation structure, model error, and whether simulation results change the decision.

definition.name: Probability Tree Analysis
definition.summary: Probability Tree Analysis uses a Initial decision or event → Conditional branches → Terminal consequences → Rollback calculation workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Initial decision or event
steps.prompt: Define the starting choice or uncertain event and the horizon of the tree.

steps.title: Conditional branches
steps.prompt: Add mutually exclusive branches for subsequent events and decisions, attaching conditional probabilities where defensible.

steps.title: Terminal consequences
steps.prompt: Assign costs, benefits, utility, or other consequences to terminal paths.

steps.title: Rollback calculation
steps.prompt: Multiply conditional probabilities along paths and work backward to compute expected values or utilities at chance nodes and optimal choices at decision nodes.

steps.title: Tree sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test probability, payoff, dependency, and missing-branch assumptions, especially where small changes switch the preferred path.

definition.name: Influence Diagramming
definition.summary: Influence Diagramming uses a Decision node → Chance variables → Value outcomes → Influence structure workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Decision node
steps.prompt: Define the decision or sequence of decisions to be supported.

steps.title: Chance variables
steps.prompt: List uncertain events or states that affect outcomes.

steps.title: Value outcomes
steps.prompt: Define the outcomes or objectives whose value matters.

steps.title: Influence structure
steps.prompt: Map informational, causal, and decision dependencies without implying causation where only information flow exists.

steps.title: Decision insight
steps.prompt: Identify pivotal uncertainties, information needs, and decisions whose timing or sequencing matters most.

definition.name: Real Options Analysis
definition.summary: Real Options Analysis uses a Investment and uncertainty → Embedded options → Evolution of uncertainty → Option value workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Investment and uncertainty
steps.prompt: Define the investment, irreversible commitments, uncertain drivers, and decision horizon.

steps.title: Embedded options
steps.prompt: Identify options to defer, stage, expand, contract, switch, abandon, or learn before committing further.

steps.title: Evolution of uncertainty
steps.prompt: Model how key uncertainties may resolve over time and what information becomes available at each decision point.

steps.title: Option value
steps.prompt: Compare flexible strategies with now-or-never commitment using an appropriate decision tree, lattice, simulation, or qualitative valuation.

steps.title: Exercise rules
steps.prompt: Define observable thresholds or conditions for exercising, preserving, or abandoning each option.

definition.name: Robust Decision Making
definition.summary: Robust Decision Making uses a Decision framework → Many plausible futures → Stress-test strategies → Vulnerability analysis workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Decision framework
steps.prompt: Define objectives, candidate strategies, uncertainties, and performance measures.

steps.title: Many plausible futures
steps.prompt: Generate a broad ensemble of plausible combinations of uncertain factors rather than relying on a single forecast.

steps.title: Stress-test strategies
steps.prompt: Evaluate strategy performance across the ensemble and identify failure regions or unacceptable regret.

steps.title: Vulnerability analysis
steps.prompt: Characterize the combinations of uncertainties that cause strategies to fail and assess their plausibility.

steps.title: Robust and adaptive strategy
steps.prompt: Choose strategies that perform acceptably across futures and define signposts and contingent adaptations for vulnerable regions.

definition.name: Info-Gap Decision Theory
definition.summary: Info-Gap Decision Theory uses a System model and uncertainty → Performance requirement → Nested uncertainty sets → Robustness function workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: System model and uncertainty
steps.prompt: Define the decision model and a nominal estimate for a deeply uncertain parameter or function without claiming a reliable probability distribution.

steps.title: Performance requirement
steps.prompt: Specify the minimum acceptable outcome or critical failure threshold.

steps.title: Nested uncertainty sets
steps.prompt: Define expanding horizons of departure from the nominal model that represent increasing uncertainty.

steps.title: Robustness function
steps.prompt: For each decision, find the greatest uncertainty horizon over which the performance requirement is guaranteed.

steps.title: Robustness and windfall
steps.prompt: Compare robustness with opportunity for unusually good outcomes and state how results depend on the uncertainty model and aspiration level.

definition.name: Portfolio Decision Analysis
definition.summary: Portfolio Decision Analysis uses a Candidate portfolio elements → Value, cost, and constraints → Interactions → Portfolio construction workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Candidate portfolio elements
steps.prompt: Define projects, assets, policies, or capabilities that compete for shared resources or jointly create value.

steps.title: Value, cost, and constraints
steps.prompt: Estimate each element's value contribution, resource demand, risk, timing, and mandatory or logical constraints.

steps.title: Interactions
steps.prompt: Identify synergies, cannibalization, dependencies, diversification effects, and correlated risks across elements.

steps.title: Portfolio construction
steps.prompt: Compare feasible combinations using the chosen optimization, efficient-frontier, or multicriteria approach rather than ranking items independently.

steps.title: Portfolio stress test
steps.prompt: Test budget changes, uncertain values, common shocks, sequencing constraints, and concentration risk before selecting the portfolio.

definition.name: Via Negativa Intervention Review
definition.summary: Via Negativa Intervention Review uses a Objective and current harms → Subtraction candidates → Removal asymmetry → Intervention harm check workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Objective and current harms
steps.prompt: Define the outcome sought and the concrete harms, friction, failure modes, or dependencies already present.

steps.title: Subtraction candidates
steps.prompt: List rules, features, handoffs, exposures, dependencies, incentives, or interventions that could be removed, simplified, or stopped before adding something new.

steps.title: Removal asymmetry
steps.prompt: For each subtraction, compare reversible loss of benefit with potential reduction in hidden downside, complexity, maintenance burden, and interaction effects.

steps.title: Intervention harm check
steps.prompt: Identify ways the proposed additive intervention could create new fragility, dependence, side effects, measurement gaming, or hard-to-reverse commitments.

steps.title: Minimum sufficient action
steps.prompt: Choose the smallest reversible set of removals or additions that addresses the objective, and define evidence required before escalating intervention.

definition.name: Serial Optionality Review
definition.summary: Serial Optionality Review uses a Goal under uncertainty → Commitments and exits → Low-cost trials → Ratchet and reset workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Goal under uncertainty
steps.prompt: Define the long-term objective while separating it from any single predetermined route for reaching it.

steps.title: Commitments and exits
steps.prompt: List current or proposed commitments, their cost of reversal, decision deadlines, exit paths, and information gained before the next commitment.

steps.title: Low-cost trials
steps.prompt: Identify small experiments, pilots, probes, or contracts that create information and upside while capping downside.

steps.title: Ratchet and reset
steps.prompt: Define conditions for expanding successful trials, abandoning failures, and resetting into new options without preserving sunk-cost commitments.

steps.title: Option-rich sequence
steps.prompt: Construct a staged path with frequent decision points and preserved exits rather than one long irreversible plan.

definition.name: Barbell Exposure Analysis
definition.summary: Barbell Exposure Analysis uses a Objective and ruin constraint → Protected core → Bounded-risk upside → Fragile middle workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Objective and ruin constraint
steps.prompt: Define the objective and the outcomes that are unacceptable because they threaten survival, mission continuity, solvency, or irreversible loss.

steps.title: Protected core
steps.prompt: Identify the portion of resources, capacity, commitments, or exposure that must remain highly robust, liquid, redundant, or otherwise protected from ruin.

steps.title: Bounded-risk upside
steps.prompt: Identify small exposures with capped downside and potentially large learning, opportunity, or payoff.

steps.title: Fragile middle
steps.prompt: Identify medium-risk commitments that look efficient in ordinary conditions but combine meaningful downside with limited upside, hidden leverage, or difficult exit.

steps.title: Allocation and triggers
steps.prompt: Set allocation limits and rebalancing triggers that protect the core while allowing repeated bounded experiments on the upside.

references.label: Taleb — Antifragility / barbell and optionality material

definition.name: OODA Decision-Cycle Analysis
definition.summary: OODA Decision-Cycle Analysis uses a Competitive decision environment → Observation quality → Orientation → Decision and tempo workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Competitive decision environment
steps.prompt: Define the actor, adversary or changing environment, objectives, time pressure, and the decision cycle being examined.

steps.title: Observation quality
steps.prompt: Assess what is sensed, missed, delayed, distorted, or overloaded and how collection latency affects the usable picture.

steps.title: Orientation
steps.prompt: Identify the prior experience, culture, doctrine, models, assumptions, unfolding circumstances, and synthesis processes shaping interpretation; treat orientation as the dominant filter rather than a mechanical step.

steps.title: Decision and tempo
steps.prompt: Examine how candidate actions are selected, how quickly assumptions can be revised, and whether decision tempo creates initiative or merely faster error.

steps.title: Action, feedback, and adaptation
steps.prompt: Trace how action changes the environment, what feedback returns, and whether the actor can cycle with greater adaptability, ambiguity, and irregularity than the competitor.

prerequisites: Observable feedback from the environment or adversary
A defined actor whose observation-orientation-decision-action cycle can be examined

references.label: Air University Press — Boyd, A Discourse on Winning and Losing

definition.name: Bounded Rationality / Satisficing Audit
definition.summary: Bounded Rationality / Satisficing Audit uses a Decision problem and bounds → Search process → Aspiration level → Stopping rule workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Decision problem and bounds
steps.prompt: Define the decision, available time, information, attention, computation, organizational rules, and other constraints on exhaustive optimization.

steps.title: Search process
steps.prompt: Map how alternatives are generated and screened, which heuristics guide search, which regions of the option space are never examined, and what order effects matter.

steps.title: Aspiration level
steps.prompt: State the thresholds that make an option good enough and identify whether those thresholds are explicit, inherited, politically set, or shifting with experience.

steps.title: Stopping rule
steps.prompt: Identify why search stops when it does and whether the first satisfactory option crowds out better but less immediately visible alternatives.

steps.title: Improve bounded choice
steps.prompt: Improve representation, search order, aspiration criteria, external memory, delegation, or staged review without pretending the decision-maker can optimize an immense problem space.

prerequisites: A concrete decision with real time or attention constraints
Known or inferable search and stopping behavior
A threshold for what counts as an acceptable option

references.label: Nobel Prize — Herbert Simon, Rational Decision-Making in Business Organizations

definition.name: Recognition-Primed Decision Audit
definition.summary: Recognition-Primed Decision Audit uses a Situation and expertise → Recognized pattern → Mental simulation → Modify or reject workflow to make choices explicit under uncertainty using utility, probability, robustness, sensitivity, optionality, bounded rationality, adaptive decision cycles, and asymmetric exposure.

steps.title: Situation and expertise
steps.prompt: Define the time-pressured decision, cues available, decision-maker experience, and whether the environment is familiar enough for pattern recognition to be credible.

steps.title: Recognized pattern
steps.prompt: Identify the situation prototype, salient cues, plausible goals, expectancies, and typical action that the decision-maker recognizes first.

steps.title: Mental simulation
steps.prompt: Mentally run the first plausible action forward, looking for points of failure, missing conditions, unintended effects, and mismatches with the current situation.

steps.title: Modify or reject
steps.prompt: If the action fails simulation, modify it or consider the next plausible action rather than generating an exhaustive option set by default.

steps.title: Recognition limits
steps.prompt: Check for misleading familiarity, weak feedback history, novel conditions, overlearned patterns, and cues that should trigger slower comparative analysis instead of recognition-primed action.

prerequisites: Enough situational detail to test recognized patterns through mental simulation

definition.name: Stock-and-Flow Mapping
definition.summary: Stock-and-Flow Mapping uses a System boundary → Stocks → Flows → Feedback and delays workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: System boundary
steps.prompt: Define the system and time horizon.

steps.title: Stocks
steps.prompt: Identify accumulations that persist over time, such as people, inventory, trust, capacity, or capital.

steps.title: Flows
steps.prompt: Identify rates that increase or decrease each stock and their governing conditions.

steps.title: Feedback and delays
steps.prompt: Connect stocks and flows through feedback loops and note important delays.

steps.title: Behavior implications
steps.prompt: What growth, depletion, overshoot, oscillation, or bottleneck behavior could the structure generate?

definition.name: System Archetype Analysis
definition.summary: System Archetype Analysis uses a Behavior pattern → Candidate archetypes → Underlying structure → Test the fit workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Behavior pattern
steps.prompt: Describe the recurring system behavior over time rather than a single event.

steps.title: Candidate archetypes
steps.prompt: Compare the pattern with archetypes such as limits to growth, fixes that fail, shifting the burden, escalation, or tragedy of the commons.

steps.title: Underlying structure
steps.prompt: Map the feedback loops, delays, resource constraints, and incentives that instantiate the candidate archetype in this case.

steps.title: Test the fit
steps.prompt: Look for evidence that distinguishes the archetype from alternative structures and identify where the analogy breaks.

steps.title: Archetype-informed intervention
steps.prompt: Select leverage points that address the structure rather than reinforcing the archetype's failure pattern.

definition.name: Iceberg Model
definition.summary: Iceberg Model uses a Events → Patterns over time → System structures → Mental models workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Events
steps.prompt: Describe the visible events or symptoms without treating them as the whole problem.

steps.title: Patterns over time
steps.prompt: Identify recurring trends, sequences, cycles, or conditions beneath the events.

steps.title: System structures
steps.prompt: Map rules, relationships, incentives, information flows, capacities, and feedbacks that generate the patterns.

steps.title: Mental models
steps.prompt: Identify beliefs, assumptions, goals, definitions of success, or paradigms that sustain the structures.

steps.title: Leverage
steps.prompt: Choose interventions at the deepest level that can realistically change the behavior while anticipating resistance and side effects.

definition.name: Leverage Points Analysis
definition.summary: Leverage Points Analysis uses a System structure → Candidate interventions → Leverage assessment → System resistance workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: System structure
steps.prompt: Describe the system, its goals, feedbacks, rules, information flows, and major parameters.

steps.title: Candidate interventions
steps.prompt: List possible interventions at different depths, from parameter changes to rules, goals, or paradigms.

steps.title: Leverage assessment
steps.prompt: For each intervention, estimate how strongly it could change system behavior and how difficult it would be to implement.

steps.title: System resistance
steps.prompt: How might feedback, adaptation, incentives, or delays neutralize or reverse the intervention?

steps.title: Priority leverage points
steps.prompt: Select interventions with high leverage and acceptable side effects, and specify what should be monitored.

definition.name: Reinforcing Loop Analysis
definition.summary: Reinforcing Loop Analysis uses a Amplifying behavior → Reinforcing loop → Gain and accelerants → Constraints and counterforces workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Amplifying behavior
steps.prompt: Define the growth, decline, escalation, contagion, or compounding pattern being examined.

steps.title: Reinforcing loop
steps.prompt: Map the circular chain in which changes feed back to amplify further change.

steps.title: Gain and accelerants
steps.prompt: Identify coefficients, thresholds, network effects, expectations, or resource flows that strengthen the reinforcing process.

steps.title: Constraints and counterforces
steps.prompt: Identify balancing loops, resource limits, saturation, delays, and external shocks that can slow or reverse amplification.

steps.title: Intervention implications
steps.prompt: Identify leverage points that damp harmful amplification or sustain beneficial reinforcement without triggering stronger counterforces.

definition.name: Balancing Loop Analysis
definition.summary: Balancing Loop Analysis uses a Target or equilibrium → Gap signal → Corrective response → Delays and overshoot workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Target or equilibrium
steps.prompt: Define the desired, expected, or constrained state around which the system appears to regulate.

steps.title: Gap signal
steps.prompt: Identify how the system senses deviation between current and target conditions.

steps.title: Corrective response
steps.prompt: Map actions or processes triggered by the gap and how they feed back to reduce deviation.

steps.title: Delays and overshoot
steps.prompt: Identify sensing, decision, implementation, and physical delays that can produce oscillation or instability.

steps.title: Limits and failure modes
steps.prompt: Assess capacity constraints, distorted signals, changing targets, and reinforcing loops that can defeat the balancing process.

definition.name: Delay Analysis
definition.summary: Delay Analysis uses a Process and outcome → Delay inventory → Behavioral effects → Observability workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Process and outcome
steps.prompt: Define the system process where effects arrive materially after causes.

steps.title: Delay inventory
steps.prompt: Identify information, perception, decision, implementation, transport, accumulation, and biological or technical delays.

steps.title: Behavioral effects
steps.prompt: Analyze how delays can create overshoot, oscillation, overreaction, underreaction, or false confidence.

steps.title: Observability
steps.prompt: Identify which state variables are observed late or indirectly and where decision-makers rely on stale indicators.

steps.title: Delay-aware action
steps.prompt: Adjust thresholds, buffers, pacing, or monitoring so interventions account for the lag between action and consequence.

definition.name: Limits to Growth Analysis
definition.summary: Limits to Growth Analysis uses a Growth engine → Limiting condition → Balancing response → Approaching-limit indicators workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Growth engine
steps.prompt: Identify the reinforcing process initially driving expansion or improvement.

steps.title: Limiting condition
steps.prompt: Identify the resource, capacity, demand, legitimacy, attention, infrastructure, or other constraint that becomes binding as growth proceeds.

steps.title: Balancing response
steps.prompt: Map how the limiting condition slows growth, increases costs, lowers quality, or creates compensating behavior.

steps.title: Approaching-limit indicators
steps.prompt: Identify observable signs that the constraint is tightening before growth visibly stalls.

steps.title: Constraint strategy
steps.prompt: Decide whether to expand the limiting capacity, reduce demand on it, change the growth mechanism, or accept a stable ceiling.

definition.name: Shifting the Burden Analysis
definition.summary: Shifting the Burden Analysis uses a Problem symptom → Symptomatic solution → Fundamental solution → Dependency loop workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Problem symptom
steps.prompt: Define the recurring symptom and why immediate relief is attractive.

steps.title: Symptomatic solution
steps.prompt: Identify the fast intervention that reduces the visible symptom without addressing its underlying cause.

steps.title: Fundamental solution
steps.prompt: Identify the slower capability, structural change, or root-cause intervention that would reduce dependence on the symptomatic response.

steps.title: Dependency loop
steps.prompt: Map how repeated use of the quick fix weakens incentives, resources, skills, or conditions needed for the fundamental solution.

steps.title: Rebalance action
steps.prompt: Protect short-term safety while investing in the fundamental solution and monitoring indicators of growing dependency.

definition.name: Fixes That Fail Analysis
definition.summary: Fixes That Fail Analysis uses a Problem and fix → Immediate benefit → Delayed side effect → Failure loop workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Problem and fix
steps.prompt: Define the problem, chosen intervention, and intended near-term effect.

steps.title: Immediate benefit
steps.prompt: Map the mechanism through which the fix initially improves the visible condition.

steps.title: Delayed side effect
steps.prompt: Identify secondary consequences that later worsen the original problem or create a new one.

steps.title: Failure loop
steps.prompt: Connect the worsening condition back to pressure for more of the same fix or stronger versions of it.

steps.title: Redesign
steps.prompt: Replace or constrain the failing fix, address the underlying structure, and define early indicators of the delayed adverse effect.

definition.name: Success to the Successful Analysis
definition.summary: Success to the Successful Analysis uses a Competing activities → Allocation rule → Self-reinforcing advantage → Structural distortion workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Competing activities
steps.prompt: Identify teams, products, strategies, regions, or programs competing for a shared limited resource.

steps.title: Allocation rule
steps.prompt: Describe how current performance influences future access to money, people, attention, data, or opportunity.

steps.title: Self-reinforcing advantage
steps.prompt: Map how resource gains improve performance and how resource losses reduce the rival's ability to recover.

steps.title: Structural distortion
steps.prompt: Assess whether observed performance reflects intrinsic merit, path dependence, measurement bias, or cumulative advantage.

steps.title: Allocation redesign
steps.prompt: Consider floors, experimentation budgets, rotation, normalization, or other mechanisms that preserve learning and prevent premature lock-in.

definition.name: Tragedy of the Commons Analysis
definition.summary: Tragedy of the Commons Analysis uses a Shared resource → Individual incentives → Depletion feedback → Governance conditions workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Shared resource
steps.prompt: Define the common resource, its regenerative or capacity limits, and the population drawing on it.

steps.title: Individual incentives
steps.prompt: Identify benefits to users from additional extraction or use and why costs are partly externalized.

steps.title: Depletion feedback
steps.prompt: Map how aggregate use degrades resource quality, capacity, access, or future returns.

steps.title: Governance conditions
steps.prompt: Assess visibility, boundaries, rules, monitoring, sanctions, trust, and collective-action capacity that affect restraint.

steps.title: Sustainable governance
steps.prompt: Identify rules, quotas, rights, pricing, monitoring, or cooperative arrangements that align individual incentives with resource sustainability.

definition.name: Escalation Archetype Analysis
definition.summary: Escalation Archetype Analysis uses a Competing actors → Relative-performance signal → Escalating responses → Escalation thresholds workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Competing actors
steps.prompt: Identify the parties whose actions are evaluated relative to one another.

steps.title: Relative-performance signal
steps.prompt: Define what each side interprets as advantage, inferiority, threat, or unacceptable gap.

steps.title: Escalating responses
steps.prompt: Map how one side's action increases pressure on the other to respond and how that response feeds back.

steps.title: Escalation thresholds
steps.prompt: Identify red lines, misperception, lags, status incentives, or commitment mechanisms that make de-escalation harder.

steps.title: De-escalation options
steps.prompt: Identify rule changes, common metrics, confidence-building measures, ceilings, or reframing that can break the comparative feedback loop.

definition.name: Growth and Underinvestment Analysis
definition.summary: Growth and Underinvestment Analysis uses a Demand or growth process → Capacity requirement → Performance erosion → Expectation adjustment workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Demand or growth process
steps.prompt: Define the reinforcing growth mechanism and the performance standard expected as demand increases.

steps.title: Capacity requirement
steps.prompt: Identify the infrastructure, staffing, skills, maintenance, or institutional capacity needed to sustain performance.

steps.title: Performance erosion
steps.prompt: Map how insufficient capacity creates delay, lower quality, congestion, or reliability loss.

steps.title: Expectation adjustment
steps.prompt: Identify whether deteriorating performance lowers demand, ambitions, service standards, or willingness to invest, concealing the need for capacity.

steps.title: Investment strategy
steps.prompt: Set leading capacity indicators and investment triggers that act before performance deterioration becomes self-confirming.

definition.name: System Dynamics Simulation Design
definition.summary: System Dynamics Simulation Design uses a Dynamic question → Model structure → Parameters and data → Behavior and structure validation workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Dynamic question
steps.prompt: Define the behavior over time the simulation must explain or explore and the decision it should support.

steps.title: Model structure
steps.prompt: Specify stocks, flows, auxiliary variables, feedback loops, delays, boundaries, and units consistent with the causal hypothesis.

steps.title: Parameters and data
steps.prompt: Estimate parameters from data, literature, or explicit assumptions and record uncertainty and dimensional consistency.

steps.title: Behavior and structure validation
steps.prompt: Test extreme conditions, historical reproduction, sensitivity, dimensional consistency, and whether structure—not curve fitting—explains the behavior.

steps.title: Policy experiments
steps.prompt: Compare interventions and scenarios, identify robust conclusions, and report where results are sensitive to uncertain structure or parameters.

definition.name: Agent-Based Model Framing
definition.summary: Agent-Based Model Framing uses a Emergent question → Agents and state → Behavior and interaction rules → Emergent outcomes workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Emergent question
steps.prompt: Define the macro pattern or policy question that may arise from heterogeneous interacting agents.

steps.title: Agents and state
steps.prompt: Define agent types, attributes, objectives, information, memory, and heterogeneity relevant to behavior.

steps.title: Behavior and interaction rules
steps.prompt: Specify decision rules, adaptation, network or spatial interactions, environment, and institutional constraints.

steps.title: Emergent outcomes
steps.prompt: Identify aggregate patterns to observe and explain how they could arise from local interaction rather than imposed equations.

steps.title: Validation and experiments
steps.prompt: Use stylized facts, micro-level evidence, sensitivity, multiple seeds, and alternative rules to assess whether conclusions are robust.

definition.name: Emergent Behavior Analysis
definition.summary: Emergent Behavior Analysis uses a Emergent pattern → Local rules and interactions → Enabling conditions → Alternative mechanisms workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Emergent pattern
steps.prompt: Define the macro-level pattern that is not trivially reducible to any single component's behavior.

steps.title: Local rules and interactions
steps.prompt: Identify component behaviors, information, constraints, and interaction mechanisms that could generate the pattern.

steps.title: Enabling conditions
steps.prompt: Identify density, connectivity, thresholds, heterogeneity, resource conditions, and feedback required for emergence.

steps.title: Alternative mechanisms
steps.prompt: Generate different micro-level mechanisms capable of producing similar aggregate patterns and identify discriminating observations.

steps.title: Intervention implications
steps.prompt: Assess whether acting on individual components, interaction rules, network structure, or boundary conditions is most likely to change the macro outcome.

definition.name: Path Dependence Analysis
definition.summary: Path Dependence Analysis uses a Current state → Critical junctures → Increasing returns and lock-in → Foreclosed alternatives workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Current state
steps.prompt: Define the institutional, technological, strategic, or behavioral state whose history appears to constrain present options.

steps.title: Critical junctures
steps.prompt: Identify early choices, shocks, accidents, standards, or commitments that created diverging possible paths.

steps.title: Increasing returns and lock-in
steps.prompt: Map learning, coordination, sunk costs, network effects, expectations, legal commitments, and complementary investments that reinforce the chosen path.

steps.title: Foreclosed alternatives
steps.prompt: Identify plausible alternatives that became more expensive, illegitimate, incompatible, or forgotten as the path matured.

steps.title: Path change
steps.prompt: Identify shocks, bridging technologies, compensation, coordinated switching, or policy interventions capable of overcoming lock-in.

definition.name: Tipping Point Analysis
definition.summary: Tipping Point Analysis uses a System and state → Forcing variables → Self-reinforcing feedback → Early warnings workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: System and state
steps.prompt: Define the system, current regime, important state variables, and potential alternate regime.

steps.title: Forcing variables
steps.prompt: Identify pressures or drivers that could move the system toward a threshold.

steps.title: Self-reinforcing feedback
steps.prompt: Identify mechanisms that could make change accelerate or become difficult to reverse once a threshold is crossed.

steps.title: Early warnings
steps.prompt: Look for slowing recovery, rising variance, autocorrelation, spatial pattern changes, behavioral precursors, or domain-specific indicators.

steps.title: Threshold uncertainty
steps.prompt: State plausible threshold ranges, reversibility limits, monitoring needs, and interventions that could increase resilience before crossing.

definition.name: Efficiency Imperative Audit
definition.summary: Efficiency Imperative Audit uses a System and stated purpose → Efficiency imperatives → Values displaced → Technical lock-in workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: System and stated purpose
steps.prompt: Define the institution, process, or decision and the substantive human or mission purpose it is supposed to serve.

steps.title: Efficiency imperatives
steps.prompt: Identify optimization metrics, procedural demands, throughput targets, automation pressures, or claims that a single most-efficient means is necessary.

steps.title: Values displaced
steps.prompt: Identify qualitative goods, local judgment, autonomy, redundancy, resilience, legitimacy, or human needs that the efficiency frame discounts or makes invisible.

steps.title: Technical lock-in
steps.prompt: Trace how infrastructure, expertise, standards, incentives, and prior investments make the efficient method increasingly difficult to refuse or reverse.

steps.title: Purpose-first alternatives
steps.prompt: Reassess the choice using the original purpose rather than efficiency as the terminal value; identify slower, redundant, plural, or reversible alternatives worth preserving.

references.label: International Jacques Ellul Society — Ellul and Technique

definition.name: Technological System Autonomy Analysis
definition.summary: Technological System Autonomy Analysis uses a Technical system boundary → Mutual dependencies → Self-reinforcing momentum → Constraint on choice workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Technical system boundary
steps.prompt: Define the linked technologies, procedures, institutions, experts, standards, and infrastructures shaping the issue.

steps.title: Mutual dependencies
steps.prompt: Map how one technical component creates requirements for others, including maintenance, measurement, security, scale, training, and coordination.

steps.title: Self-reinforcing momentum
steps.prompt: Identify feedbacks through which adoption generates new problems or dependencies that are answered by still more technique.

steps.title: Constraint on choice
steps.prompt: Distinguish nominal choices from options that remain practically feasible once interoperability, sunk costs, expertise, and institutional routines are considered.

steps.title: Leverage and escape
steps.prompt: Identify points where plural standards, manual fallback, decentralization, redundancy, or explicit non-efficiency values could restore meaningful choice.

references.label: International Jacques Ellul Society — Ellul and Technique

definition.name: Requisite Variety Analysis
definition.summary: Requisite Variety Analysis uses a Disturbance variety → Response variety → Information and channel capacity → Variety mismatch workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: Disturbance variety
steps.prompt: List materially different states, failures, adversary moves, demand patterns, exceptions, or environmental conditions the regulator must handle.

steps.title: Response variety
steps.prompt: Inventory the distinct actions, policies, controls, resources, authorities, and fallback modes actually available to the regulating system.

steps.title: Information and channel capacity
steps.prompt: Assess whether the regulator can distinguish the relevant disturbance states early and accurately enough to select among its responses.

steps.title: Variety mismatch
steps.prompt: Identify disturbances that collapse into the same response, responses that require unavailable information, and bottlenecks where the environment has more effective variety than the regulator.

steps.title: Amplify or attenuate variety
steps.prompt: Increase response repertoire, delegation, sensing, modularity, or learning—or reduce incoming variety through standardization, buffering, segmentation, or constraints—without hiding important differences.

references.label: W. Ross Ashby — An Introduction to Cybernetics

definition.name: Viable System Model Diagnosis
definition.summary: Viable System Model Diagnosis uses a System identity and recursion → Operations and coordination → Control and accountability → Intelligence and adaptation workflow to analyze feedback, accumulation, delays, nonlinear behavior, emergence, technical autonomy, regulation, and leverage in complex systems.

steps.title: System identity and recursion
steps.prompt: Define the viable system, its purpose, environment, and the operational units that must themselves remain viable at lower recursive levels.

steps.title: Operations and coordination
steps.prompt: Assess primary operations and the mechanisms that prevent oscillation, conflict, duplication, and destructive interference among them.

steps.title: Control and accountability
steps.prompt: Examine internal regulation, resource bargaining, audit, performance visibility, and whether central control overwhelms or under-supports operational autonomy.

steps.title: Intelligence and adaptation
steps.prompt: Assess how the system scans the external environment, models future change, learns, and balances present operational demands against adaptation.

steps.title: Policy and balance
steps.prompt: Examine identity, values, ultimate policy, and the balance among operations, internal control, and future intelligence; identify communication or variety failures threatening viability.

definition.name: Social Network Analysis
definition.summary: Social Network Analysis uses a Network question → Nodes and ties → Structural measures → Substantive interpretation workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Network question
steps.prompt: Define the behavior, influence, flow, cohesion, or vulnerability to explain.

steps.title: Nodes and ties
steps.prompt: Define node types, tie meaning, direction, weight, and time window before collecting relationships.

steps.title: Structural measures
steps.prompt: Assess relevant centrality, density, clustering, components, brokerage, or community structure.

steps.title: Substantive interpretation
steps.prompt: Explain what the network pattern means in the real system; do not equate high centrality automatically with importance.

steps.title: Boundary and data limits
steps.prompt: Identify missing nodes, uncertain ties, sampling effects, temporal changes, and alternative network definitions.

prerequisites: Relationship data with direction/weight/time decisions documented

definition.name: Link Analysis
definition.summary: Link Analysis uses a Analytic question → Entities → Typed links → Network patterns workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Analytic question
steps.prompt: Define what relationship, influence, coordination, dependency, or access pattern the network should help explain.

steps.title: Entities
steps.prompt: Define node types, inclusion rules, identifiers, and relevant attributes before drawing relationships.

steps.title: Typed links
steps.prompt: Add directed or undirected relationships with meaning, time, weight, source, and confidence rather than unlabeled connections.

steps.title: Network patterns
steps.prompt: Identify clusters, hubs, bridges, isolates, repeated motifs, and temporal changes while checking whether they reflect data collection boundaries.

steps.title: Analytic implications
steps.prompt: Generate bounded hypotheses and collection priorities without treating centrality or proximity as proof of intent or command.

definition.name: Ego Network Analysis
definition.summary: Ego Network Analysis uses a Focal node → Alters and ties → Local structure → Functional roles workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Focal node
steps.prompt: Define the person, organization, system, or entity whose immediate relational environment is being examined.

steps.title: Alters and ties
steps.prompt: Identify direct neighbors, tie types, direction, strength, duration, and relevant alter attributes.

steps.title: Local structure
steps.prompt: Assess density, redundancy, brokerage, isolates, factions, and whether alters are connected independently of the ego.

steps.title: Functional roles
steps.prompt: Identify suppliers, gatekeepers, advisers, conduits, competitors, dependencies, and other roles supported by evidence.

steps.title: Boundary and missing ties
steps.prompt: Assess hidden alters, sampling bias, multiplex relationships, and how conclusions change if the ego boundary is expanded.

definition.name: Centrality Analysis
definition.summary: Centrality Analysis uses a Network definition → Choose centrality → Calculate and compare → Contextual interpretation workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Network definition
steps.prompt: Define nodes, ties, direction, weights, and time window before selecting a centrality measure.

steps.title: Choose centrality
steps.prompt: Select degree, in/out-degree, closeness, betweenness, eigenvector, PageRank, or another measure based on the substantive question.

steps.title: Calculate and compare
steps.prompt: Compute the selected measures and compare rankings rather than treating one metric as universal importance.

steps.title: Contextual interpretation
steps.prompt: Explain what high or low values mean in this network and inspect whether results are driven by boundary choices or missing ties.

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: Identify candidate influencers, brokers, bottlenecks, vulnerabilities, or collection priorities and note where centrality should not be overinterpreted.

definition.name: Betweenness Centrality Review
definition.summary: Betweenness Centrality Review uses a Network definition → Betweenness calculation → Brokerage interpretation → Robustness workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Network definition
steps.prompt: Define nodes, ties, direction, weights, and what movement or paths mean substantively.

steps.title: Betweenness calculation
