steps.prompt: Calculate node or edge betweenness using a path definition appropriate to the domain and document normalization choices.

steps.title: Brokerage interpretation
steps.prompt: Identify nodes or links that lie on many relevant shortest paths and explain what control, exposure, or coordination role that could imply.

steps.title: Robustness
steps.prompt: Test sensitivity to missing edges, alternative weights, disconnected components, and plausible non-shortest-path behavior.

steps.title: Use and limits
steps.prompt: Translate results into hypotheses about brokerage or vulnerability while avoiding the assumption that high betweenness equals authority or importance.

definition.name: Community Detection
definition.summary: Community Detection uses a Network and purpose → Detection method → Detected communities → Substantive meaning workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Network and purpose
steps.prompt: Define the network and why grouping densely connected nodes would be analytically useful.

steps.title: Detection method
steps.prompt: Choose a method appropriate to weighted, directed, overlapping, or multilevel structure and document resolution parameters.

steps.title: Detected communities
steps.prompt: Identify clusters and inspect their internal cohesion, external connections, and stability across reasonable parameter choices.

steps.title: Substantive meaning
steps.prompt: Assess whether communities correspond to real organizations, roles, topics, geographies, or merely mathematical partitions.

steps.title: Boundaries and bridges
steps.prompt: Identify cross-community brokers, ambiguous memberships, and changes that could split or merge communities.

definition.name: Clique Analysis
definition.summary: Clique Analysis uses a Network and tie meaning → Maximal cliques → Overlap and membership → Substantive context workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Network and tie meaning
steps.prompt: Define the relation and why fully connected subgroups would be substantively meaningful.

steps.title: Maximal cliques
steps.prompt: Identify fully connected groups and distinguish maximal cliques from smaller subsets contained within them.

steps.title: Overlap and membership
steps.prompt: Assess nodes shared across cliques, isolated cliques, and whether overlap indicates brokerage, factions, or data artifacts.

steps.title: Substantive context
steps.prompt: Compare clique membership with organizations, geography, roles, time, or known affiliations to test whether the structure is meaningful.

steps.title: Limits
steps.prompt: Assess whether near-cliques, weighted ties, missing data, or temporal variation make exact clique structure too brittle for the analytic question.

definition.name: Broker and Gatekeeper Analysis
definition.summary: Broker and Gatekeeper Analysis uses a Flow or access → Candidate brokers → Brokerage and gatekeeping → Alternate routes workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Flow or access
steps.prompt: Define what information, resources, people, authority, or transactions move through the network.

steps.title: Candidate brokers
steps.prompt: Identify nodes connecting otherwise weakly connected groups, domains, locations, or stages of a process.

steps.title: Brokerage and gatekeeping
steps.prompt: Assess whether each candidate can actually control, filter, delay, translate, or redirect flows rather than merely occupy a structural position.

steps.title: Alternate routes
steps.prompt: Identify substitutes, redundancy, informal bypasses, and conditions under which the broker loses leverage.

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: Estimate vulnerability, influence, collection value, or intervention effects while preserving uncertainty about actual behavior.

definition.name: Two-Mode Network Analysis
definition.summary: Two-Mode Network Analysis uses a Two node modes → Incidence structure → Bipartite patterns → Optional projections workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Two node modes
steps.prompt: Define the two distinct entity sets—such as people-events, firms-projects, actors-locations—and the relation connecting them.

steps.title: Incidence structure
steps.prompt: Build the bipartite incidence matrix with time, weight, and provenance where relevant.

steps.title: Bipartite patterns
steps.prompt: Identify shared affiliations, specialization, concentration, bridges, and unusual co-participation without projecting away important information too early.

steps.title: Optional projections
steps.prompt: If projecting to one mode, specify the similarity or co-occurrence rule and check whether high-degree nodes create spurious ties.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Use the two-mode structure to generate hypotheses about affiliation, opportunity, exposure, or coordination while separating co-membership from direct interaction.

definition.name: Multiplex Network Analysis
definition.summary: Multiplex Network Analysis uses a Relationship layers → Layer structure → Cross-layer overlap → Layer coupling workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Relationship layers
steps.prompt: Define distinct tie types—such as communication, finance, command, kinship, trade, or technical dependency—and why they should remain separate.

steps.title: Layer structure
steps.prompt: Analyze density, centrality, communities, and reachability within each relationship layer.

steps.title: Cross-layer overlap
steps.prompt: Identify dyads and nodes whose relationships repeat, reinforce, conflict, or substitute across layers.

steps.title: Layer coupling
steps.prompt: Assess how activity or failure in one layer affects another and whether apparent centrality is robust across relationship types.

steps.title: Multiplex implications
steps.prompt: Identify resilient ties, hidden dependencies, role differentiation, and collection gaps that a collapsed single-layer graph would obscure.

definition.name: Temporal Network Analysis
definition.summary: Temporal Network Analysis uses a Time representation → Structural change → Time-varying measures → Events and mechanisms workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Time representation
steps.prompt: Define event time, snapshots, rolling windows, or intervals appropriate to the process being studied.

steps.title: Structural change
steps.prompt: Track additions, removals, persistence, activation, and tie-strength changes across time.

steps.title: Time-varying measures
steps.prompt: Compare centrality, communities, reachability, brokerage, or diffusion measures while accounting for changing network size.

steps.title: Events and mechanisms
steps.prompt: Relate structural changes to external events or internal dynamics without assuming temporal coincidence is causal.

steps.title: Emerging structure
steps.prompt: Identify persistent trends, transient bursts, precursors, and monitoring indicators for future network change.

definition.name: Diffusion Network Analysis
definition.summary: Diffusion Network Analysis uses a Diffusing process → Transmission opportunities → Observed or simulated cascades → Mechanism tests workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Diffusing process
steps.prompt: Define what spreads—information, behavior, disease, innovation, sentiment, or resources—and the observation window.

steps.title: Transmission opportunities
steps.prompt: Define ties through which diffusion is plausible and distinguish contact opportunity from actual transmission.

steps.title: Observed or simulated cascades
steps.prompt: Trace adoption or transmission sequences, timing, exposure, and repeated pathways across the network.

steps.title: Mechanism tests
steps.prompt: Compare contagion, homophily, shared external exposure, threshold effects, and influence mechanisms that can produce similar patterns.

steps.title: Intervention
steps.prompt: Identify high-leverage seeding, blocking, vaccination, communication, or monitoring strategies and test sensitivity to network uncertainty.

definition.name: Influence Network Mapping
definition.summary: Influence Network Mapping uses a Influence target → Influential actors → Influence relationships → Coalitions and countervailing influence workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Influence target
steps.prompt: Define the decision, belief, behavior, or allocation whose influence structure is being mapped.

steps.title: Influential actors
steps.prompt: Identify formal and informal actors with authority, expertise, resources, legitimacy, access, or persuasive reach.

steps.title: Influence relationships
steps.prompt: Map direction, domain, strength, mechanism, and evidence for influence rather than inferring it from contact alone.

steps.title: Coalitions and countervailing influence
steps.prompt: Identify reinforcing blocs, brokers, veto points, competing narratives, and actors whose influence depends on context.

steps.title: Change implications
steps.prompt: Identify leverage points, likely reactions, and indicators that influence relationships are shifting.

definition.name: Dependency Mapping
definition.summary: Dependency Mapping uses a Function or mission → Direct dependencies → Dependency chains → Criticality and substitutability workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Function or mission
steps.prompt: Define the service, capability, decision, or outcome whose dependencies matter.

steps.title: Direct dependencies
steps.prompt: Identify required people, systems, data, suppliers, facilities, authorities, infrastructure, and upstream services.

steps.title: Dependency chains
steps.prompt: Trace second- and higher-order dependencies, including shared utilities and hidden common providers.

steps.title: Criticality and substitutability
steps.prompt: Assess single points of failure, redundancy, switching time, inventory or buffer, and consequences of dependency loss.

steps.title: Resilience actions
steps.prompt: Prioritize diversification, redundancy, monitoring, contingency, and dependency reduction for the most critical chains.

definition.name: Supply Network Mapping
definition.summary: Supply Network Mapping uses a Supply scope → Suppliers and flows → Concentration and exposure → Disruption scenarios workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Supply scope
steps.prompt: Define the product, service, geography, tiers, and time horizon of the supply network.

steps.title: Suppliers and flows
steps.prompt: Map suppliers, subcontractors, logistics nodes, materials, information, ownership, and critical flows across tiers.

steps.title: Concentration and exposure
steps.prompt: Identify sole sources, geographic concentration, correlated suppliers, long lead times, constrained capacity, and shared infrastructure.

steps.title: Disruption scenarios
steps.prompt: Trace how supplier, transport, regulatory, cyber, environmental, or geopolitical disruptions propagate through the network.

steps.title: Resilience options
steps.prompt: Assess alternate sources, inventory, redesign, capacity reservation, visibility, and recovery plans against the highest-impact dependencies.

definition.name: Value Network Analysis
definition.summary: Value Network Analysis uses a Value proposition → Actors and exchanges → Roles and complementarity → Value creation and capture workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Value proposition
steps.prompt: Define what value is created, for whom, and what outcomes or exchanges sustain the network.

steps.title: Actors and exchanges
steps.prompt: Map participants and the tangible and intangible value exchanges among them, including information, trust, legitimacy, money, and services.

steps.title: Roles and complementarity
steps.prompt: Identify complements, bottlenecks, orchestrators, free riders, substitutes, and actors whose participation enables others.

steps.title: Value creation and capture
steps.prompt: Assess where value is produced, where it is captured, and where incentives are misaligned or exchanges are fragile.

steps.title: Network redesign
steps.prompt: Identify changes in roles, interfaces, incentives, or governance that could improve value creation without destabilizing critical participants.

definition.name: Stakeholder Network Mapping
definition.summary: Stakeholder Network Mapping uses a Issue and stakeholders → Stakeholder relationships → Network structure → Power and legitimacy workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Issue and stakeholders
steps.prompt: Define the policy, program, conflict, or decision and the stakeholders who affect or are affected by it.

steps.title: Stakeholder relationships
steps.prompt: Map collaboration, authority, dependency, conflict, information, funding, and representation ties with source and confidence.

steps.title: Network structure
steps.prompt: Identify coalitions, peripheral groups, brokers, veto players, and stakeholders who are structurally excluded despite being affected.

steps.title: Power and legitimacy
steps.prompt: Compare network position with formal authority, resources, legitimacy, urgency, and dependence rather than equating centrality with power.

steps.title: Engagement strategy
steps.prompt: Prioritize engagement, coalition building, consultation, or monitoring while anticipating network reactions and representation gaps.

definition.name: Relationship Strength Matrix
definition.summary: Relationship Strength Matrix uses a Entity pairs → Strength criteria → Consistent scoring → Pattern comparison workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Entity pairs
steps.prompt: Define the pairs of actors, systems, or organizations whose relationship strength must be compared.

steps.title: Strength criteria
steps.prompt: Choose dimensions such as frequency, duration, reciprocity, exclusivity, resource flow, trust, authority, dependence, or evidence confidence.

steps.title: Consistent scoring
steps.prompt: Rate relationships against explicit scales and preserve raw evidence and uncertainty behind each score.

steps.title: Pattern comparison
steps.prompt: Identify strong, weak, asymmetric, fragile, and rapidly changing relationships and check whether different criteria tell conflicting stories.

steps.title: Analytic use
steps.prompt: Use the matrix to prioritize validation, monitoring, or network modeling without collapsing distinct relationship types into one opaque number.

definition.name: Structural Hole Analysis
definition.summary: Structural Hole Analysis uses a Network and domain → Structural holes → Brokerage benefit → Brokerage cost and risk workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Network and domain
steps.prompt: Define the relation and why disconnected contacts or groups create potential brokerage value.

steps.title: Structural holes
steps.prompt: Identify nodes spanning contacts that are weakly connected to one another and distinguish genuine separation from missing data.

steps.title: Brokerage benefit
steps.prompt: Assess access to nonredundant information, control, coordination, innovation, or arbitrage that the bridging position could enable.

steps.title: Brokerage cost and risk
steps.prompt: Assess trust burdens, conflicting expectations, exposure, overload, and the possibility that contacts bypass the broker.

steps.title: Strategic implications
steps.prompt: Identify where brokerage is valuable, where closure is preferable, and how network change could create or eliminate the structural advantage.

definition.name: Network Resilience Analysis
definition.summary: Network Resilience Analysis uses a Network function → Critical structure → Disruption scenarios → Performance degradation workflow to analyze relational structure, influence, brokerage, clustering, diffusion, dependency, and network resilience.

steps.title: Network function
steps.prompt: Define what service, flow, connectivity, or mission the network must preserve.

steps.title: Critical structure
steps.prompt: Identify hubs, bridges, single points of failure, redundant paths, dependencies, and community bottlenecks.

steps.title: Disruption scenarios
steps.prompt: Test random failures, targeted removals, cascading dependency failures, and realistic adversary or hazard scenarios.

steps.title: Performance degradation
steps.prompt: Measure connectivity, flow, reachability, service level, or recovery as nodes and links fail.

steps.title: Resilience improvements
steps.prompt: Prioritize redundancy, diversification, hardening, spare capacity, reconfiguration, and recovery measures that reduce critical vulnerabilities.

definition.name: Preliminary Hazard Analysis
definition.summary: Preliminary Hazard Analysis uses a System and phase → Hazards → Causes and initiating conditions → Initial risk workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: System and phase
steps.prompt: Define the system, mission, lifecycle phase, operating environment, and boundaries.

steps.title: Hazards
steps.prompt: Identify hazardous states, energies, materials, interactions, or conditions before detailed design.

steps.title: Causes and initiating conditions
steps.prompt: List credible causes and enabling conditions for each hazard.

steps.title: Initial risk
steps.prompt: Assess severity and likelihood or exposure using the project's chosen risk criteria.

steps.title: Controls and follow-up
steps.prompt: Identify prevention, detection, mitigation, and analyses needed for the highest-priority hazards.

definition.name: Hazard Identification Study
definition.summary: Hazard Identification Study uses a System and operating context → Hazard inventory → Initiating conditions → Consequences and affected parties workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: System and operating context
steps.prompt: Define the system, lifecycle phase, intended functions, environment, interfaces, and boundaries.

steps.title: Hazard inventory
steps.prompt: Identify hazardous states, energies, materials, interactions, human factors, and environmental conditions without prematurely filtering by probability.

steps.title: Initiating conditions
steps.prompt: For each hazard, identify credible initiating events, enabling conditions, dependencies, and exposure pathways.

steps.title: Consequences and affected parties
steps.prompt: Describe plausible effects, escalation paths, and who or what could be harmed.

steps.title: Disposition
steps.prompt: Prioritize hazards for deeper analysis, define immediate controls where needed, and record information gaps.

definition.name: Hazard and Operability Study
definition.summary: Hazard and Operability Study uses a Node and design intent → Guide-word deviations → Causes and consequences → Safeguards and risk workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Node and design intent
steps.prompt: Define the process node, equipment, operation, design intent, operating envelope, interfaces, and current drawings or process description.

steps.title: Guide-word deviations
steps.prompt: Apply suitable guide words to process parameters or functions to generate credible deviations from design intent; record only meaningful combinations.

steps.title: Causes and consequences
steps.prompt: For each credible deviation, identify plausible causes, local and downstream consequences, escalation paths, and affected people or assets.

steps.title: Safeguards and risk
steps.prompt: Identify existing prevention, detection, mitigation, and recovery safeguards; assess independence, adequacy, and residual risk without treating safeguard count as proof of safety.

steps.title: Actions and closeout
steps.prompt: Record design changes, procedural actions, further analyses, owners, priorities, and evidence required to verify closeout.

prerequisites: A multidisciplinary team and agreed guide words/deviation logic

definition.name: What-If Hazard Review
definition.summary: What-If Hazard Review uses a Process or system → What-if questions → Consequences → Existing safeguards workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Process or system
steps.prompt: Define the activity, change, process, or design to review and the intended operating assumptions.

steps.title: What-if questions
steps.prompt: Generate structured what-if questions covering failures, deviations, incorrect actions, external events, timing errors, and unusual combinations.

steps.title: Consequences
steps.prompt: For each credible deviation, describe consequences, escalation, affected safeguards, and operational impact.

steps.title: Existing safeguards
steps.prompt: Identify controls that prevent, detect, mitigate, or recover from each scenario and assess their independence and reliability.

steps.title: Actions
steps.prompt: Record additional controls, design changes, tests, or analyses required for scenarios with unacceptable or uncertain risk.

definition.name: What-If/Checklist Analysis
definition.summary: What-If/Checklist Analysis uses a Scope and reference checklist → Checklist review → Beyond the checklist → Hazards and controls workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Scope and reference checklist
steps.prompt: Define the system or operation and select a checklist appropriate to its hazards, lifecycle phase, and operating environment.

steps.title: Checklist review
steps.prompt: Evaluate each checklist item explicitly and record evidence, applicability, deviations, and unresolved questions.

steps.title: Beyond the checklist
steps.prompt: Generate additional what-if scenarios for interfaces, novel conditions, human actions, dependencies, and changes not covered by the checklist.

steps.title: Hazards and controls
steps.prompt: For each material finding, identify consequences, existing safeguards, and residual uncertainty.

steps.title: Closeout
steps.prompt: Assign corrective actions, owners, validation criteria, and follow-up for checklist failures and novel scenarios.

definition.name: Layers of Protection Analysis
definition.summary: Layers of Protection Analysis uses a Accident scenario → Initiating frequency → Independent protection layers → Mitigated risk workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Accident scenario
steps.prompt: Define the initiating event, hazardous consequence, and process or operational context.

steps.title: Initiating frequency
steps.prompt: Estimate or bound the initiating-event frequency using defensible data and assumptions.

steps.title: Independent protection layers
steps.prompt: Identify safeguards that are effective, independent, auditable, and sufficiently specific to count as protection layers.

steps.title: Mitigated risk
steps.prompt: Apply layer failure probabilities consistently to estimate residual scenario frequency or risk.

steps.title: Risk gap
steps.prompt: Compare residual risk with tolerability criteria and identify where additional independent protection, redesign, or uncertainty reduction is needed.

definition.name: Safety Integrity Level Review
definition.summary: Safety Integrity Level Review uses a Safety function → Required risk reduction → SIL target and architecture → Verification and assumptions workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Safety function
steps.prompt: Define the hazardous event, required safety function, demand mode, process boundary, and tolerable risk target.

steps.title: Required risk reduction
steps.prompt: Estimate or justify the risk reduction required after accounting for non-instrumented protection layers and baseline risk.

steps.title: SIL target and architecture
steps.prompt: Determine the integrity target and assess sensor, logic, final-element architecture, diagnostics, independence, and common-cause vulnerabilities.

steps.title: Verification and assumptions
steps.prompt: Check failure rates, proof-test intervals, coverage, systematic capability, human dependencies, and lifecycle assumptions supporting the target.

steps.title: Lifecycle controls
steps.prompt: Define testing, maintenance, change control, bypass management, validation, and evidence needed to sustain integrity over time.

definition.name: Event Sequence Analysis
definition.summary: Event Sequence Analysis uses a Initiating event → Pivotal events → Event sequences → Likelihood and uncertainty workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Initiating event
steps.prompt: Define the triggering event and system state at the start of the sequence.

steps.title: Pivotal events
steps.prompt: Identify the successes, failures, decisions, barriers, and conditions that materially change the path toward different end states.

steps.title: Event sequences
steps.prompt: Trace credible sequences from the initiator through pivotal events to safe, degraded, and hazardous end states.

steps.title: Likelihood and uncertainty
steps.prompt: Estimate or bound branch likelihoods where defensible and record dependence, common-cause, and data uncertainty.

steps.title: Risk controls
steps.prompt: Identify which pivotal events dominate risk and where prevention, detection, mitigation, or recovery most effectively changes the sequence.

definition.name: Cause-Consequence Analysis
definition.summary: Cause-Consequence Analysis uses a Critical event → Cause side → Consequence side → Dependencies workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Critical event
steps.prompt: Define the central event whose causes and downstream consequences will be analyzed.

steps.title: Cause side
steps.prompt: Reason backward through necessary, sufficient, and combined conditions that could produce the event.

steps.title: Consequence side
steps.prompt: Reason forward through barrier success/failure, escalation, recovery, and alternative end states.

steps.title: Dependencies
steps.prompt: Identify shared causes, dependent barriers, common utilities, human actions, and environmental conditions linking both sides.

steps.title: Control priorities
steps.prompt: Select controls that reduce high-leverage causes or prevent severe consequence paths and define how their effectiveness will be verified.

definition.name: Barrier Analysis
definition.summary: Barrier Analysis uses a Hazard and target → Barriers → Barrier quality → Gaps and escalation factors workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Hazard and target
steps.prompt: Define the hazardous energy, condition, action, or information flow and the asset or population to protect.

steps.title: Barriers
steps.prompt: Identify physical, technical, procedural, organizational, and human barriers that prevent, detect, contain, or recover from the hazard.

steps.title: Barrier quality
steps.prompt: Assess independence, effectiveness, availability, detectability of failure, ownership, and susceptibility to common-cause degradation.

steps.title: Gaps and escalation factors
steps.prompt: Identify missing barriers, degraded controls, bypasses, latent conditions, and factors that can defeat multiple barriers.

steps.title: Barrier strategy
steps.prompt: Prioritize strengthening, adding, simplifying, or monitoring barriers and define evidence that each remains effective.

definition.name: Swiss Cheese Analysis
definition.summary: Swiss Cheese Analysis uses a Adverse event → Defense layers → Weaknesses in each layer → Alignment pathway workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Adverse event
steps.prompt: Define the adverse outcome and the organizational system in which it occurred or could occur.

steps.title: Defense layers
steps.prompt: Identify successive organizational, technical, procedural, supervisory, and frontline defenses intended to prevent the event.

steps.title: Weaknesses in each layer
steps.prompt: Identify active failures and latent conditions that create vulnerabilities within each defense layer.

steps.title: Alignment pathway
steps.prompt: Explain how weaknesses could align across layers to permit the adverse event without assuming a single root cause.

steps.title: System learning
steps.prompt: Identify changes that reduce simultaneous vulnerability across layers and improve detection of degrading defenses.

definition.name: Risk Matrix Analysis
definition.summary: Risk Matrix Analysis uses a Hazard and effect → Severity → Likelihood or exposure → Risk level workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Hazard and effect
steps.prompt: Define the hazard, affected operation, and specific credible effect being assessed.

steps.title: Severity
steps.prompt: Assign severity using the organization’s defined consequence categories and record the evidence and assumptions supporting the rating.

steps.title: Likelihood or exposure
steps.prompt: Assign likelihood using defined frequency/exposure criteria, relevant data, and uncertainty rather than intuition alone.

steps.title: Risk level
steps.prompt: Map severity and likelihood to the configured matrix and identify boundary cases, single-point failures, or conditions that warrant adjustment or additional analysis.

steps.title: Risk decision
steps.prompt: State required controls, acceptance authority, residual uncertainty, and why the matrix result is or is not sufficient for the decision.

definition.name: ALARP Assessment
definition.summary: ALARP Assessment uses a Risk and legal context → Further risk-reduction options → Cost and difficulty → Gross-disproportion test workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Risk and legal context
steps.prompt: Define the hazard, current risk estimate, affected parties, applicable obligations, and tolerability context.

steps.title: Further risk-reduction options
steps.prompt: Identify additional engineering, procedural, operational, and organizational controls that could reduce risk.

steps.title: Cost and difficulty
steps.prompt: Assess money, time, effort, operational burden, and adverse side effects of each additional control.

steps.title: Gross-disproportion test
steps.prompt: Determine whether the sacrifice is grossly disproportionate to the safety benefit, documenting uncertainty and avoiding simple cost-benefit equivalence.

steps.title: ALARP case
steps.prompt: Document implemented controls, rejected options and reasons, residual risk, assumptions, and triggers for reassessment.

definition.name: Resilience Engineering Review
definition.summary: Resilience Engineering Review uses a Critical function → Resilient capacities → Normal performance variability → Stress and adaptation workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Critical function
steps.prompt: Define the function, service, or mission that must be sustained under varying and disruptive conditions.

steps.title: Resilient capacities
steps.prompt: Assess the ability to anticipate, monitor, respond, and learn, including adaptive resources and decision authority.

steps.title: Normal performance variability
steps.prompt: Identify workload, resource, coordination, environmental, and timing variability that the system normally absorbs.

steps.title: Stress and adaptation
steps.prompt: Examine how buffers, tradeoffs, workarounds, and cross-level adaptations behave as demands exceed normal ranges.

steps.title: Resilience improvements
steps.prompt: Strengthen sensing, adaptive capacity, recovery, learning, and slack while watching for adaptations that create hidden risk elsewhere.

definition.name: Systems-Theoretic Process Analysis
definition.summary: Systems-Theoretic Process Analysis uses a Losses and hazards → Control structure → Unsafe control actions → Loss scenarios workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Losses and hazards
steps.prompt: Define unacceptable losses and system-level hazardous states.

steps.title: Control structure
steps.prompt: Model controllers, controlled processes, sensors, actuators, feedback, and responsibilities.

steps.title: Unsafe control actions
steps.prompt: For each control action, ask whether not providing, providing, mistiming, or sustaining it could create a hazard.

steps.title: Loss scenarios
steps.prompt: Explain how flawed process models, feedback, coordination, component behavior, or environment could produce each unsafe control action.

steps.title: Safety constraints
steps.prompt: Translate the scenarios into enforceable safety constraints and monitoring needs.

prerequisites: Control structure with controllers, feedback, and controlled processes

definition.name: AcciMap
definition.summary: AcciMap uses a Accident or loss → Socio-technical levels → Cross-level interactions → Control and feedback gaps workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Accident or loss
steps.prompt: Define the adverse event, affected system, and analysis boundary.

steps.title: Socio-technical levels
steps.prompt: Map relevant actors and decisions from equipment and operators through management, regulators, policy, and broader institutional context.

steps.title: Cross-level interactions
steps.prompt: Trace how decisions, constraints, information, resources, and feedback across levels contributed to the conditions for the event.

steps.title: Control and feedback gaps
steps.prompt: Identify missing, delayed, distorted, conflicting, or unenforced constraints and feedback across the system.

steps.title: System-level actions
steps.prompt: Prioritize interventions at multiple levels so recommendations do not collapse into frontline error correction alone.

definition.name: Functional Resonance Analysis Method
definition.summary: Functional Resonance Analysis Method uses a Functions → Performance variability → Functional couplings → Resonant combinations workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Functions
steps.prompt: Identify essential system functions and characterize input, output, preconditions, resources, controls, and time.

steps.title: Performance variability
steps.prompt: Describe normal variability in timing, precision, resources, workload, and conditions for each function.

steps.title: Functional couplings
steps.prompt: Map how variability in one function can propagate through shared inputs, resources, controls, or timing relationships.

steps.title: Resonant combinations
steps.prompt: Identify combinations of ordinary variability that could amplify into unexpected success or failure without any single component malfunction.

steps.title: Manage variability
steps.prompt: Strengthen dampening, monitoring, adaptive capacity, and system conditions that keep harmful resonance within tolerable bounds.

definition.name: Management Oversight and Risk Tree Analysis
definition.summary: Management Oversight and Risk Tree Analysis uses a Loss event → MORT branches → Evidence by branch → Management-system weaknesses workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Loss event
steps.prompt: Define the accident, incident, or unacceptable loss and its immediate context.

steps.title: MORT branches
steps.prompt: Examine specific control factors and management-system factors that could explain why hazards were inadequately controlled.

steps.title: Evidence by branch
steps.prompt: Record evidence supporting, contradicting, or leaving unresolved each relevant branch rather than checking boxes mechanically.

steps.title: Management-system weaknesses
steps.prompt: Identify policy, responsibility, analysis, change-control, supervision, maintenance, and feedback weaknesses that enabled lower-level failures.

steps.title: Corrective priorities
steps.prompt: Target verified management and control-system weaknesses and define how recurrence prevention will be demonstrated.

definition.name: Tripod Beta
definition.summary: Tripod Beta uses a Incident and barriers → Barrier failures → Preconditions → Underlying organizational factors workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Incident and barriers
steps.prompt: Define the incident, hazardous event, and barriers that should have prevented or mitigated it.

steps.title: Barrier failures
steps.prompt: Identify failed, missing, bypassed, or ineffective barriers and the immediate actions or conditions associated with each.

steps.title: Preconditions
steps.prompt: Identify local circumstances such as workload, competence, communication, procedures, equipment, or environment that made unsafe acts or barrier failures more likely.

steps.title: Underlying organizational factors
steps.prompt: Trace recurring preconditions to latent organizational weaknesses such as design, maintenance, planning, culture, supervision, or conflicting goals.

steps.title: System improvements
steps.prompt: Design actions that strengthen barriers and underlying organizational conditions rather than relying only on retraining or blame.

definition.name: Business Impact Analysis
definition.summary: Business Impact Analysis uses a Critical functions → Impact over time → Recovery objectives → Recovery dependencies workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Critical functions
steps.prompt: Identify business or mission functions, owners, customers, dependencies, and required outputs.

steps.title: Impact over time
steps.prompt: Assess operational, financial, legal, safety, reputational, and mission impacts as disruption duration increases.

steps.title: Recovery objectives
steps.prompt: Define maximum tolerable disruption, recovery time objectives, recovery point objectives, and minimum acceptable service levels where relevant.

steps.title: Recovery dependencies
steps.prompt: Map people, facilities, suppliers, technology, data, utilities, and upstream/downstream dependencies needed for recovery.

steps.title: Recovery priorities
steps.prompt: Prioritize functions and capabilities, identify gaps between objectives and current recovery capacity, and define remediation actions.

definition.name: Fragility / Antifragility Stress Test
definition.summary: Fragility / Antifragility Stress Test uses a Exposure and objective → Perturbation range → Nonlinear response → Tail and model-error sensitivity workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Exposure and objective
steps.prompt: Define the system, outcome, stressor, and performance measure; distinguish survival constraints from ordinary performance goals.

steps.title: Perturbation range
steps.prompt: Specify plausible changes in volatility, dispersion, load, error, demand, timing, or shock size without assuming a single forecast.

steps.title: Nonlinear response
steps.prompt: Assess whether harm accelerates with stress, remains roughly linear, or whether variability can create net benefit; identify thresholds and asymmetries.

steps.title: Tail and model-error sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test whether extreme observations or uncertainty about the model dominate the expected result and whether averaging conceals ruinous exposures.

steps.title: Reduce fragility
steps.prompt: Limit catastrophic downside, decentralize or cap exposures, add optionality or redundancy, and preserve small stressors that reveal weakness or create learning where appropriate.

references.label: Taleb & Douady — Mathematical Definition and Mapping of (Anti)Fragility

definition.name: Fat-Tail Exposure Audit
definition.summary: Fat-Tail Exposure Audit uses a Exposure variable → Tail-regime evidence → Aggregation and concentration → Model-error stress workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: Exposure variable
steps.prompt: Define the loss, delay, demand, conflict, error, or other quantity whose extreme behavior matters to the decision.

steps.title: Tail-regime evidence
steps.prompt: Examine whether extremes are bounded and well-behaved or whether scale, concentration, dependence, power-law behavior, or rare large observations make thin-tail assumptions doubtful.

steps.title: Aggregation and concentration
steps.prompt: Identify whether diversification assumptions fail because exposures share drivers, whether a few observations dominate totals, or whether aggregation preserves heavy tails.

steps.title: Model-error stress
steps.prompt: Compare decisions under substantially different tail assumptions and identify estimates—means, variances, confidence intervals, return periods—that become unstable or misleading.

steps.title: Tail-aware decision
steps.prompt: Set exposure caps, buffers, ruin constraints, monitoring triggers, or robust actions that do not depend on precise estimation of extreme-event probability.

references.label: Taleb — Incerto / Statistical Consequences of Fat Tails

definition.name: Interactive Complexity / Tight-Coupling Audit
definition.summary: Interactive Complexity / Tight-Coupling Audit uses a System and hazardous function → Interactive complexity → Coupling and slack → Control dilemma workflow to identify failure pathways, hazards, tail exposure, barrier weaknesses, accident mechanisms, interactive complexity, fragility, and resilience requirements.

steps.title: System and hazardous function
steps.prompt: Define the system, mission, hazardous energies or consequences, boundaries, and the functions whose failure could propagate.

steps.title: Interactive complexity
steps.prompt: Identify hidden, nonlinear, shared, feedback-rich, common-mode, proximity, or poorly understood interactions that can combine failures in unexpected ways.

steps.title: Coupling and slack
steps.prompt: Assess buffers, delays, substitutability, reversibility, sequence constraints, time to intervene, and whether disturbances propagate faster than diagnosis and recovery.

steps.title: Control dilemma
steps.prompt: Identify where complex interactions demand local improvisation while tight coupling simultaneously demands centralized coordination, creating incompatible control requirements.

steps.title: Structural risk response
steps.prompt: Reduce coupling, simplify interactions, add slack or isolation, redesign catastrophic potential, or explicitly recognize where procedural reliability cannot remove the structural accident risk.

prerequisites: Known interactions, dependencies, buffers, and timing constraints
A consequential failure or hazard to trace through the system

definition.name: DMAIC
definition.summary: DMAIC uses a Define → Measure → Analyze → Improve workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Define
steps.prompt: Define the customer or mission problem, scope, goal, stakeholders, and process boundary.

steps.title: Measure
steps.prompt: Establish operational definitions, baseline performance, and measurement reliability.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.prompt: Identify and verify root causes using data rather than selecting causes by intuition.

steps.title: Improve
steps.prompt: Design and test changes that address verified causes and assess side effects.

steps.title: Control
steps.prompt: Define controls, ownership, metrics, and response plans that sustain the improvement.

prerequisites: Baseline process data and an accountable process owner

definition.name: DMADV
definition.summary: DMADV uses a Define need → Measure needs → Analyze concepts → Design solution workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Define need
steps.prompt: Define the customer or mission need, scope, constraints, and success measures.

steps.title: Measure needs
steps.prompt: Translate needs into measurable critical-to-quality characteristics and baseline capability.

steps.title: Analyze concepts
steps.prompt: Compare design concepts against requirements, risks, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Design solution
steps.prompt: Develop the preferred design, interfaces, controls, and verification criteria.

steps.title: Verify
steps.prompt: Test the design against requirements and document residual gaps.

definition.name: A3 Problem Solving
definition.summary: A3 Problem Solving uses a Background and current condition → Target condition → Root-cause analysis → Countermeasures and plan workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Background and current condition
steps.prompt: State why the problem matters and depict the current condition with concrete evidence.

steps.title: Target condition
steps.prompt: Define the desired condition and measurable gap.

steps.title: Root-cause analysis
steps.prompt: Explain why the gap exists and distinguish verified causes from assumptions.

steps.title: Countermeasures and plan
steps.prompt: Select countermeasures linked to causes, owners, timing, and expected effects.

steps.title: Follow-up
steps.prompt: Compare actual results with expected results and capture remaining gaps and learning.

definition.name: Kaizen Event Analysis
definition.summary: Kaizen Event Analysis uses a Improvement scope → Current state → Causes → Rapid countermeasures workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Improvement scope
steps.prompt: Define the process, problem, team, and short event boundary.

steps.title: Current state
steps.prompt: Map work, delay, defects, handoffs, and waste using direct evidence.

steps.title: Causes
steps.prompt: Identify root causes and constraints rather than only symptoms.

steps.title: Rapid countermeasures
steps.prompt: Select and trial small changes with owners and expected effects.

steps.title: Sustainment
steps.prompt: Check results, standardize gains, and assign follow-up actions.

definition.name: Value Stream Mapping
definition.summary: Value Stream Mapping uses a Product or service family → Current-state map → Flow problems → Future-state design workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Product or service family
steps.prompt: Select a coherent value stream, customer need, start/end points, and demand context.

steps.title: Current-state map
steps.prompt: Map process steps, queues, inventories, information flows, cycle times, changeovers, uptime, and handoffs from demand backward.

steps.title: Flow problems
steps.prompt: Identify waiting, batching, rework, excess inventory, transport, overprocessing, unevenness, and constraints that interrupt value flow.

steps.title: Future-state design
steps.prompt: Design a more continuous pull-based flow with appropriate takt, pacemaker, supermarkets, leveling, and information signals.

steps.title: Transformation plan
steps.prompt: Prioritize changes, owners, measures, and review cadence that move the current state toward the future state.

definition.name: Process Capability Analysis
definition.summary: Process Capability Analysis uses a Critical characteristic → Stability first → Capability indices → Sources of variation workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Critical characteristic
steps.prompt: Define the measurable characteristic, specification limits, and process conditions.

steps.title: Stability first
steps.prompt: Check whether the process is statistically stable before interpreting capability.

steps.title: Capability indices
steps.prompt: Estimate suitable capability/performance indices and inspect distribution assumptions.

steps.title: Sources of variation
steps.prompt: Identify common and special causes that limit capability.

steps.title: Capability judgment
steps.prompt: State whether the process can meet requirements and what improvement is needed.

prerequisites: Representative measurement data with an adequate measurement system

definition.name: Control Chart Analysis
definition.summary: Control Chart Analysis uses a Measure and subgroup → Control limits → Signals → Investigate causes workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Measure and subgroup
steps.prompt: Define the metric, sampling cadence, subgroup logic, and chart type.

steps.title: Control limits
steps.prompt: Establish limits from stable baseline data rather than specification limits.

steps.title: Signals
steps.prompt: Identify points, runs, trends, shifts, or cycles that indicate special causes.

steps.title: Investigate causes
steps.prompt: Link signals to process conditions, changes, and plausible causes.

steps.title: Response plan
steps.prompt: Define actions for special causes and rules for recalculating limits.

prerequisites: A rational subgrouping or sampling plan
A chart type appropriate to the measurement scale

definition.name: Statistical Process Control
definition.summary: Statistical Process Control uses a Process and metric → Control chart → Special-cause signals → Cause response workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Process and metric
steps.prompt: Define the process, quality characteristic, rational subgrouping, sampling frequency, and measurement system.

steps.title: Control chart
steps.prompt: Select a chart appropriate to variable or attribute data and calculate center line and control limits from stable baseline data.

steps.title: Special-cause signals
steps.prompt: Interpret points beyond limits and nonrandom runs, shifts, trends, or cycles using a defined rule set.

steps.title: Cause response
steps.prompt: Investigate special causes without tampering with common-cause variation and document corrective actions.

steps.title: Stability before capability
steps.prompt: Only assess process capability against specifications after statistical stability is established; continue monitoring for regime changes.

definition.name: Measurement System Analysis
definition.summary: Measurement System Analysis uses a Measurement purpose → Measurement system → Error components → Adequacy workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Measurement purpose
steps.prompt: Define the characteristic, decision use, range, and required precision.

steps.title: Measurement system
steps.prompt: Map instruments, operators, methods, environment, software, and reference standards.

steps.title: Error components
steps.prompt: Assess bias, linearity, stability, repeatability, and reproducibility as relevant.

steps.title: Adequacy
steps.prompt: Compare measurement variation with process and tolerance variation.

steps.title: Improvement
steps.prompt: Correct dominant measurement errors and define revalidation.

definition.name: Gage R&R
definition.summary: Gage R&R uses a Study design → Repeated measurements → Variation components → Measurement adequacy workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Study design
steps.prompt: Choose parts, appraisers, trials, randomization, and crossed or nested design.

steps.title: Repeated measurements
steps.prompt: Collect blinded repeated measurements across representative parts.

steps.title: Variation components
steps.prompt: Separate repeatability, reproducibility, part-to-part, and interaction effects.

steps.title: Measurement adequacy
steps.prompt: Compare gage variation with total and tolerance variation using context-appropriate thresholds.

steps.title: Correct and repeat
steps.prompt: Identify instrument, method, fixture, or training changes and rerun the study.

definition.name: Design of Experiments
definition.summary: Design of Experiments uses a Experimental objective → Design structure → Execution controls → Effects and interactions workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Experimental objective
steps.prompt: Define the response, factors, ranges, nuisance variables, and decision the experiment must support.

steps.title: Design structure
steps.prompt: Choose factorial, fractional factorial, response-surface, blocking, randomization, replication, or other structure appropriate to the objective.

steps.title: Execution controls
steps.prompt: Randomize where feasible, preserve treatment fidelity, record deviations, and ensure measurement reliability.

steps.title: Effects and interactions
steps.prompt: Estimate factor effects, interactions, uncertainty, model adequacy, and practical significance rather than relying only on p-values.

steps.title: Confirmation and optimization
steps.prompt: Run confirmation trials or follow-up experiments at promising settings and state the region over which conclusions are supported.

definition.name: Taguchi Method
definition.summary: Taguchi Method uses a Quality objective → Experimental array → Run experiment → Robustness analysis workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Quality objective
steps.prompt: Define response variables, target behavior, factors, levels, and noise factors.

steps.title: Experimental array
steps.prompt: Select an orthogonal array or robust design covering the important factors efficiently.

steps.title: Run experiment
steps.prompt: Execute trials consistently and preserve noise conditions and replication logic.

steps.title: Robustness analysis
steps.prompt: Use signal-to-noise and factor effects to identify settings resistant to noise.

steps.title: Confirmation run
steps.prompt: Verify the predicted robust setting and quantify improvement.

definition.name: Poka-Yoke Analysis
definition.summary: Poka-Yoke Analysis uses a Error or defect → Error mechanism → Mistake-proofing concepts → Evaluate workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Error or defect
steps.prompt: Define the human or process error and the defect or harm it can create.

steps.title: Error mechanism
steps.prompt: Identify when, where, and why the error becomes possible.

steps.title: Mistake-proofing concepts
steps.prompt: Generate prevention, detection, constraint, sequencing, and forcing-function options.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.prompt: Prefer simple controls that act at the source and cannot be bypassed silently.

steps.title: Verify in use
steps.prompt: Test the control under realistic variation and monitor unintended workarounds.

definition.name: Standard Work Analysis
definition.summary: Standard Work Analysis uses a Work scope → Observed work → Standard sequence → Gap analysis workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Work scope
steps.prompt: Define the process boundary, demand, takt, and quality/safety requirements.

steps.title: Observed work
steps.prompt: Capture actual sequence, time, inventory, movement, and variation at the workplace.

steps.title: Standard sequence
steps.prompt: Define the best current sequence, expected time, and standard work-in-process.

steps.title: Gap analysis
steps.prompt: Compare actual work with the standard and distinguish bad standards from noncompliance.

steps.title: Maintain and improve
steps.prompt: Assign ownership, visual controls, training, and a method for updating the standard.

definition.name: Takt Time Analysis
definition.summary: Takt Time Analysis uses a Demand basis → Calculate takt → Compare cycle times → Balance work workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Demand basis
steps.prompt: Define customer demand, period, product mix, and available production time.

steps.title: Calculate takt
steps.prompt: Compute the required production rhythm using consistent units and realistic availability.

steps.title: Compare cycle times
steps.prompt: Compare station cycle times, changeovers, uptime, and variability with takt.

steps.title: Balance work
steps.prompt: Identify overload, underload, batching, and staffing or sequencing changes.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.prompt: Define triggers for demand changes, instability, or rebalance needs.

definition.name: Bottleneck Analysis
definition.summary: Bottleneck Analysis uses a System flow → Capacity by step → Identify constraint → Exploit and subordinate workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: System flow
steps.prompt: Define the process, demand, throughput unit, and major resources.

steps.title: Capacity by step
steps.prompt: Estimate effective capacity, utilization, queues, downtime, and variability at each constraint candidate.

steps.title: Identify constraint
steps.prompt: Determine which resource truly limits throughput under current conditions.

steps.title: Exploit and subordinate
steps.prompt: Protect the constraint and align upstream/downstream work to it.

steps.title: Elevate and recheck
steps.prompt: Increase constraint capacity if needed, then reassess because the bottleneck may move.

definition.name: Theory of Constraints
definition.summary: Theory of Constraints uses a System goal → Identify constraint → Exploit → Subordinate workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: System goal
steps.prompt: Define the system's goal and the throughput, inventory, operating expense, or mission measures that reflect it.

steps.title: Identify constraint
steps.prompt: Find the resource, policy, market, skill, or dependency that currently limits total system performance.

steps.title: Exploit
steps.prompt: Use the existing constraint as effectively as possible before adding capacity.

steps.title: Subordinate
steps.prompt: Align non-constraints and work release so they support rather than overload or starve the constraint.

steps.title: Elevate and repeat
steps.prompt: Add capacity or redesign where justified, then identify the next constraint and guard against inertia.

definition.name: Current Reality Tree
definition.summary: Current Reality Tree uses a Undesirable effects → Causal links → Core problem → Challenge logic workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Undesirable effects
steps.prompt: List observed problems and validate that they are real and meaningfully connected.

steps.title: Causal links
steps.prompt: Build sufficiency-based if-then links and expose assumptions in each connection.

steps.title: Core problem
steps.prompt: Identify the small set of root conditions generating many undesirable effects.

steps.title: Challenge logic
steps.prompt: Test alternative explanations, missing causes, circularity, and necessary-condition claims.

steps.title: Improvement focus
steps.prompt: Select root conditions whose change would remove the most downstream effects.

definition.name: Future Reality Tree
definition.summary: Future Reality Tree uses a Proposed change → Desired effects → Negative branches → Trim negatives workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Proposed change
steps.prompt: State the intervention or injection intended to resolve a core problem.

steps.title: Desired effects
steps.prompt: Map expected beneficial consequences using explicit causal links.

steps.title: Negative branches
steps.prompt: Search for harmful side effects, new constraints, and unintended reinforcing loops.

steps.title: Trim negatives
steps.prompt: Add preventive or compensating actions for credible negative branches.

steps.title: Implementation logic
steps.prompt: Define assumptions and indicators that would confirm or falsify the future-state logic.

definition.name: Evaporating Cloud
definition.summary: Evaporating Cloud uses a Conflict → Underlying needs → Assumptions → Challenge assumptions workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Conflict
steps.prompt: State the two incompatible actions or positions and the common objective they are meant to serve.

steps.title: Underlying needs
steps.prompt: Identify the need each side believes its action satisfies.

steps.title: Assumptions
steps.prompt: Expose assumptions linking each action to its need and creating the apparent incompatibility.

steps.title: Challenge assumptions
steps.prompt: Test which assumptions can be invalidated, reframed, or satisfied differently.

steps.title: Win-win injection
steps.prompt: Design an action that protects both legitimate needs and define how to test it.

definition.name: Goodhart–Campbell Metric Gaming Audit
definition.summary: Goodhart–Campbell Metric Gaming Audit uses a Underlying goal and proxy → Target pressure → Gaming and distortion pathways → Proxy-goal divergence workflow to find process causes, measure variation, detect metric distortion, improve flow, and design durable corrective action.

steps.title: Underlying goal and proxy
steps.prompt: State the substantive goal, the quantitative indicator used as its proxy, and the decisions, rewards, sanctions, rankings, or resources tied to that indicator.

steps.title: Target pressure
steps.prompt: Map how strongly actors are incentivized to improve the measured value and what discretion they have over classification, timing, denominator, case selection, reporting, or effort allocation.

steps.title: Gaming and distortion pathways
steps.prompt: Generate ways actors can improve the metric without improving—and possibly while damaging—the underlying goal, including teaching to the test, cream-skimming, reclassification, suppression, substitution, or data manipulation.

steps.title: Proxy-goal divergence
steps.prompt: Identify evidence that the metric is losing validity because behavior has adapted to measurement, and examine important outcomes displaced because they are unmeasured.

steps.title: Measurement safeguards
steps.prompt: Reduce single-metric stakes, rotate or triangulate indicators, add qualitative review and counter-metrics, audit manipulation channels, and keep the substantive objective distinct from the proxy.

prerequisites: One or more metrics used to judge or reward performance
Enough process knowledge to identify adaptation, gaming, classification, or displacement pathways

references.label: Campbell's Law in indicator design — PubMed

definition.name: Thematic Analysis
definition.summary: Thematic Analysis uses a Corpus and question → Initial coding → Candidate themes → Review and refine workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Corpus and question
steps.prompt: Define the dataset, analytic question, sampling logic, and unit of analysis.

steps.title: Initial coding
steps.prompt: Code meaningfully relevant features across the corpus while preserving context.

steps.title: Candidate themes
steps.prompt: Group codes into patterns of shared meaning organized around a central concept.

steps.title: Review and refine
steps.prompt: Test themes against coded extracts and the full dataset; split, merge, or discard weak themes.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Define and name each theme, show supporting and disconfirming evidence, and connect themes back to the analytic question.

definition.name: Reflexive Thematic Analysis
definition.summary: Reflexive Thematic Analysis uses a Analytic orientation → Familiarization and coding → Develop themes → Reflexive review workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Analytic orientation
steps.prompt: State the research question, theoretical orientation, researcher position, and whether coding is primarily inductive, deductive, semantic, or latent.

steps.title: Familiarization and coding
steps.prompt: Engage deeply with the dataset and produce flexible codes as interpretive tools rather than treating coding as objective measurement.

steps.title: Develop themes
steps.prompt: Construct patterns of shared meaning organized around central concepts, using researcher judgment rather than code frequency alone.

steps.title: Reflexive review
steps.prompt: Examine how assumptions, standpoint, theoretical commitments, and analytic decisions shaped theme construction.

steps.title: Analytic narrative
steps.prompt: Refine themes into a coherent interpretive account supported by data extracts, tensions, and clear boundaries between themes.

definition.name: Framework Analysis
definition.summary: Framework Analysis uses a Applied question → Analytic framework → Index and chart → Matrix comparison workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Applied question
steps.prompt: Define the policy, practice, or applied research questions and relevant cases or stakeholder groups.

steps.title: Analytic framework
steps.prompt: Develop an initial matrix of themes or issues from questions, prior knowledge, and emergent data; revise it as needed.

steps.title: Index and chart
steps.prompt: Index material consistently and summarize relevant data into case-by-theme cells while preserving links to source context.

steps.title: Matrix comparison
steps.prompt: Compare patterns within cases, across cases, and across themes; look for typologies, deviant cases, and explanatory relationships.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Develop conclusions that remain traceable to the matrix and original evidence, noting where the framework constrained what was visible.

definition.name: Qualitative Content Analysis
definition.summary: Qualitative Content Analysis uses a Analytic question → Coding frame → Systematic coding → Pattern comparison workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Analytic question
steps.prompt: Define the corpus, unit of analysis, and whether categories are inductive or deductive.

steps.title: Coding frame
steps.prompt: Develop categories with definitions, inclusion rules, and examples.

steps.title: Systematic coding
steps.prompt: Apply the frame consistently while preserving context and ambiguous cases.

steps.title: Pattern comparison
steps.prompt: Compare frequencies and meanings across cases or groups without reducing interpretation to counts.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Explain dominant and deviant patterns with traceable examples and limits.

definition.name: Grounded Theory Coding
definition.summary: Grounded Theory Coding uses a Phenomenon → Initial coding → Constant comparison → Theoretical coding workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Phenomenon
steps.prompt: Define the substantive area without imposing a finished theory.

steps.title: Initial coding
steps.prompt: Code actions and processes closely from the data.

steps.title: Constant comparison
steps.prompt: Compare incidents, codes, and cases continuously to refine categories.

steps.title: Theoretical coding
steps.prompt: Relate mature categories into an explanatory process or model.

steps.title: Saturation and memoing
steps.prompt: Document theoretical memos, negative cases, and where additional data stop adding conceptual value.

definition.name: Open Coding
definition.summary: Open Coding uses a Data segment → Open coding → Constant comparison → Category formation workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Data segment
steps.prompt: Define the corpus and coding unit.

steps.title: Open coding
steps.prompt: Break data into discrete concepts using close, descriptive or process-oriented labels.

steps.title: Constant comparison
steps.prompt: Compare incidents for similarities and differences.

steps.title: Category formation
steps.prompt: Group related codes while preserving variation.

steps.title: Analytic memos
steps.prompt: Record emerging questions, relationships, and sampling needs.

definition.name: Axial Coding
definition.summary: Axial Coding uses a Core categories → Conditions → Actions and interactions → Consequences workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Core categories
steps.prompt: Select categories developed from earlier coding.

steps.title: Conditions
steps.prompt: Identify causal, contextual, and intervening conditions around each category.

steps.title: Actions and interactions
steps.prompt: Map strategies or responses associated with the category.

steps.title: Consequences
steps.prompt: Trace outcomes and feedback from those actions.

steps.title: Relational model
steps.prompt: Integrate categories into a coherent explanatory structure and test it against cases.

definition.name: Selective Coding
definition.summary: Selective Coding uses a Core category → Relate categories → Validate relationships → Fill category gaps workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Core category
steps.prompt: Identify the category with greatest explanatory reach and analytic relevance.

steps.title: Relate categories
steps.prompt: Connect major categories systematically to the core category.

steps.title: Validate relationships
steps.prompt: Test proposed links against data, including negative cases.

steps.title: Fill category gaps
steps.prompt: Target underdeveloped relationships with additional coding or sampling.

steps.title: Integrate theory
steps.prompt: Produce a parsimonious theoretical account while retaining boundary conditions.

definition.name: Constant Comparative Method
definition.summary: Constant Comparative Method uses a Comparison units → Within-category comparison → Differentiate categories → Compare relations workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Comparison units
steps.prompt: Define incidents, cases, groups, or periods to compare.

steps.title: Within-category comparison
steps.prompt: Compare each new incident with prior coded incidents.

steps.title: Differentiate categories
steps.prompt: Split, merge, and refine categories based on meaningful variation.

steps.title: Compare relations
steps.prompt: Examine how categories co-vary across contexts and cases.

steps.title: Theoretical saturation
steps.prompt: State which categories are stable and where additional comparison is still needed.

definition.name: Narrative Analysis
definition.summary: Narrative Analysis uses a Narrative corpus → Narrative structure → Voice and perspective → Cross-narrative comparison workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Narrative corpus
steps.prompt: Define narrators, audience, setting, and the stories or episodes under study.

steps.title: Narrative structure
steps.prompt: Analyze sequence, turning points, plot, temporality, and positioning.

steps.title: Voice and perspective
steps.prompt: Examine identity, agency, omissions, and audience-oriented presentation.

steps.title: Cross-narrative comparison
steps.prompt: Compare recurring plots, contradictions, and contextual differences.

steps.title: Narrative interpretation
steps.prompt: Explain what the narratives accomplish socially or analytically without treating them as transparent fact reports.

definition.name: Conversation Analysis
definition.summary: Conversation Analysis uses a Interaction corpus → Sequential organization → Interactional detail → Case comparison workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Interaction corpus
steps.prompt: Define naturally occurring interaction and transcription conventions.

steps.title: Sequential organization
steps.prompt: Examine turn-taking, adjacency pairs, preference organization, and repair.

steps.title: Interactional detail
steps.prompt: Analyze timing, overlap, pauses, formulation, and embodied cues where available.

steps.title: Case comparison
steps.prompt: Compare deviant and recurrent interactional patterns.

steps.title: Interactional claim
steps.prompt: State how participants jointly produce meaning or action, grounded in sequence evidence.

definition.name: Critical Discourse Analysis
definition.summary: Critical Discourse Analysis uses a Social problem and discourse → Textual features → Discursive practice → Social practice and power workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Social problem and discourse
steps.prompt: Define the discourse, social issue, institutions, actors, and corpus without assuming the critical conclusion in advance.

steps.title: Textual features
steps.prompt: Analyze vocabulary, grammar, modality, agency, transitivity, presupposition, metaphor, intertextuality, and other relevant linguistic choices.

steps.title: Discursive practice
steps.prompt: Examine production, circulation, genre, audience, uptake, and relationships among texts and discourse communities.

steps.title: Social practice and power
steps.prompt: Relate discourse patterns to institutions, ideology, identity, inequality, or contestation while considering rival explanations.

steps.title: Critical interpretation
steps.prompt: State how discourse may reproduce or challenge social relations and ground claims in textual and contextual evidence rather than political assumption alone.

definition.name: Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis
definition.summary: Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis uses a Lived experience question → Idiographic reading → Experiential themes → Double hermeneutic workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Lived experience question
steps.prompt: Define the experience and relatively homogeneous participant group.

steps.title: Idiographic reading
steps.prompt: Analyze each case deeply before cross-case abstraction.

steps.title: Experiential themes
steps.prompt: Develop themes linking description with interpretation.

steps.title: Double hermeneutic
steps.prompt: Reflect on how participants make sense of experience and how the analyst interprets that sense-making.

steps.title: Cross-case synthesis
steps.prompt: Identify convergence and divergence without erasing individual cases.

definition.name: Phenomenological Reduction
definition.summary: Phenomenological Reduction uses a Phenomenon → Bracketing → Meaning units → Invariant structure workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Phenomenon
steps.prompt: Define the lived phenomenon to be described.

steps.title: Bracketing
steps.prompt: Identify and hold prior theoretical assumptions in suspension as far as practicable.

steps.title: Meaning units
steps.prompt: Describe experiential meaning units closely from accounts.

steps.title: Invariant structure
steps.prompt: Distinguish essential from incidental features through imaginative variation.

steps.title: Phenomenological description
steps.prompt: Synthesize the structure of experience and document interpretive limits.
