definition.name: Ethnographic Analysis
definition.summary: Ethnographic Analysis uses a Field setting → Field records → Cultural patterns → Situate behavior workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Field setting
steps.prompt: Define community, site, access, roles, and observation period.

steps.title: Field records
steps.prompt: Integrate observations, interviews, artifacts, and reflexive notes.

steps.title: Cultural patterns
steps.prompt: Identify routines, meanings, norms, roles, and contradictions across contexts.

steps.title: Situate behavior
steps.prompt: Explain patterns within local history, institutions, and power relations.

steps.title: Ethnographic account
steps.prompt: Develop a thick, evidence-grounded interpretation with positionality and limits.

definition.name: Domain Analysis
definition.summary: Domain Analysis uses a Cultural domain → Included terms → Semantic relations → Domain structure workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Cultural domain
steps.prompt: Define the semantic or cultural domain being investigated.

steps.title: Included terms
steps.prompt: Identify items participants treat as members of the domain.

steps.title: Semantic relations
steps.prompt: Specify relationships such as kinds-of, parts-of, causes, uses, or locations.

steps.title: Domain structure
steps.prompt: Organize cover terms, included terms, and semantic links.

steps.title: Cultural validation
steps.prompt: Check the structure against participant usage, exceptions, and contrasting cases.

definition.name: Taxonomic Analysis
definition.summary: Taxonomic Analysis uses a Selected domain → Contrast dimensions → Taxonomic structure → Test cases workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Selected domain
steps.prompt: Choose a domain with sufficiently developed included terms.

steps.title: Contrast dimensions
steps.prompt: Identify dimensions participants use to distinguish terms.

steps.title: Taxonomic structure
steps.prompt: Arrange terms hierarchically or relationally by those distinctions.

steps.title: Test cases
steps.prompt: Check ambiguous and boundary cases against the taxonomy.

steps.title: Interpretive meaning
steps.prompt: Explain what the taxonomy reveals about cultural organization and practice.

definition.name: Componential Analysis
definition.summary: Componential Analysis uses a Contrast set → Attributes → Feature matrix → Contrast patterns workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Contrast set
steps.prompt: Select related terms or categories within a cultural domain.

steps.title: Attributes
steps.prompt: Identify dimensions of contrast participants use.

steps.title: Feature matrix
steps.prompt: Map presence, absence, or values of attributes across terms.

steps.title: Contrast patterns
steps.prompt: Identify minimal contrasts, clusters, and exceptions.

steps.title: Cultural interpretation
steps.prompt: Explain what the contrast system reveals about meaning and decision rules.

definition.name: Template Analysis
definition.summary: Template Analysis uses a Analytic question → Initial template → Apply and revise → Theme hierarchy workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Analytic question
steps.prompt: Define the corpus and initial thematic focus.

steps.title: Initial template
steps.prompt: Create a provisional hierarchy of codes from theory and early data.

steps.title: Apply and revise
steps.prompt: Code cases and iteratively add, remove, merge, or reorder themes.

steps.title: Theme hierarchy
steps.prompt: Stabilize the template while preserving case-specific nuance.

steps.title: Cross-case interpretation
steps.prompt: Use the final template to compare patterns and exceptions transparently.

definition.name: Directed Content Analysis
definition.summary: Directed Content Analysis uses a Guiding theory → Directed codebook → Apply coding → Extend or challenge workflow to code, compare, interpret, and explain patterned meaning in interviews, documents, observations, and cases.

steps.title: Guiding theory
steps.prompt: Define the existing theory or prior framework that supplies initial categories.

steps.title: Directed codebook
steps.prompt: Operationalize categories and specify how uncodable material will be handled.

steps.title: Apply coding
steps.prompt: Code data systematically while marking evidence that does not fit the framework.

steps.title: Extend or challenge
steps.prompt: Use novel or contradictory material to refine, extend, or reject parts of the framework.

steps.title: Theory-informed conclusion
steps.prompt: State what was supported, modified, or newly discovered.

definition.name: Descriptive Statistics Review
definition.summary: Descriptive Statistics Review uses a Data scope → Core summaries → Distribution shape → Group comparison workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Data scope
steps.prompt: Define variables, units, population, sampling, missingness, and known data-quality issues.

steps.title: Core summaries
steps.prompt: Calculate appropriate center, spread, quantiles, counts, and rates by relevant groups.

steps.title: Distribution shape
steps.prompt: Inspect skew, tails, multimodality, zeros, and scale effects.

steps.title: Group comparison
steps.prompt: Compare summaries across meaningful groups or periods without implying significance or causation.

steps.title: Descriptive conclusion
steps.prompt: State what the data show directly and which patterns need inferential follow-up.

definition.name: Exploratory Data Analysis
definition.summary: Exploratory Data Analysis uses a Data and provenance → Univariate structure → Relationships → Anomalies and data issues workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Data and provenance
steps.prompt: Define variables, units, collection process, missingness, sampling, transformations, and known quality issues.

steps.title: Univariate structure
steps.prompt: Inspect distributions, center, spread, tails, zeros, outliers, and impossible or suspicious values.

steps.title: Relationships
steps.prompt: Explore bivariate and multivariate patterns with plots and summaries, preserving nonlinearities and subgroup structure.

steps.title: Anomalies and data issues
steps.prompt: Investigate missingness patterns, duplicates, coding errors, leverage points, regime changes, and artifacts before modeling.

steps.title: Next hypotheses
steps.prompt: Translate observed patterns into testable questions or model choices while clearly separating exploration from confirmatory inference.

definition.name: Distribution Analysis
definition.summary: Distribution Analysis uses a Variable and scale → Empirical distribution → Candidate distributions → Fit diagnostics workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Variable and scale
steps.prompt: Define the variable, support, censoring, and measurement process.

steps.title: Empirical distribution
steps.prompt: Inspect density, quantiles, tails, modes, skewness, and discreteness.

steps.title: Candidate distributions
steps.prompt: Compare plausible parametric or nonparametric representations.

steps.title: Fit diagnostics
steps.prompt: Assess graphical and numerical fit with attention to tail behavior and sample size.

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: State which distributional assumptions are defensible for downstream analysis.

definition.name: Outlier Analysis
definition.summary: Outlier Analysis uses a Data context → Candidate outliers → Verification → Influence assessment workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Data context
steps.prompt: Define variables, units, expected ranges, and whether unusual values could be substantively real.

steps.title: Candidate outliers
steps.prompt: Use robust univariate and multivariate diagnostics appropriate to the data.

steps.title: Verification
steps.prompt: Check transcription, measurement, timing, provenance, and leverage.

steps.title: Influence assessment
steps.prompt: Compare analyses with and without candidates and distinguish outliers from influential points.

steps.title: Disposition
steps.prompt: Retain, correct, exclude, or model separately with explicit rationale.

definition.name: Correlation Analysis
definition.summary: Correlation Analysis uses a Variables → Visual inspection → Correlation estimate → Uncertainty and dependence workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Variables
steps.prompt: Define variables, scales, sample, and whether the relationship is expected to be linear or monotonic.

steps.title: Visual inspection
steps.prompt: Plot the relationship and identify nonlinearities, subgroups, outliers, and range restriction.

steps.title: Correlation estimate
steps.prompt: Choose Pearson, Spearman, Kendall, or another measure suited to assumptions.

steps.title: Uncertainty and dependence
steps.prompt: Report intervals and account for repeated measures, clustering, or multiple comparisons.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Describe association strength and direction without causal overreach.

definition.name: Partial Correlation
definition.summary: Partial Correlation uses a Target relationship → Covariate rationale → Partial association → Diagnostics workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Target relationship
steps.prompt: Define the two focal variables and covariates to control.

steps.title: Covariate rationale
steps.prompt: Justify controls using substantive knowledge and avoid conditioning on mediators or colliders.

steps.title: Partial association
steps.prompt: Estimate residual or partial correlation with appropriate method.

steps.title: Diagnostics
steps.prompt: Check linearity, outliers, multicollinearity, and sensitivity to covariate choices.

steps.title: Conditional interpretation
steps.prompt: State the conditional association and why it may or may not have causal meaning.

definition.name: Regression Analysis
definition.summary: Regression Analysis uses a Estimand and variables → Model specification → Diagnostics → Estimates and uncertainty workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Estimand and variables
steps.prompt: Define the target relationship or prediction, outcome, predictors, population, and whether the goal is causal or associational.

steps.title: Model specification
steps.prompt: Choose functional form, transformations, interactions, and covariates based on theory and data structure rather than automated significance hunting.

steps.title: Diagnostics
steps.prompt: Check residual structure, heteroskedasticity, influential observations, multicollinearity, dependence, and model misspecification.

steps.title: Estimates and uncertainty
steps.prompt: Report coefficients or predictions with uncertainty, units, substantive magnitude, and any robust or clustered inference needed.

steps.title: Interpretation limits
steps.prompt: Assess extrapolation, omitted variables, measurement error, multiplicity, and why association should not be mislabeled causal.

definition.name: Logistic Regression
definition.summary: Logistic Regression uses a Binary outcome → Model specification → Fit model → Diagnostics workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Binary outcome
steps.prompt: Define outcome coding, predictors, population, and estimand.

steps.title: Model specification
steps.prompt: Choose functional forms, interactions, and covariates before significance hunting.

steps.title: Fit model
steps.prompt: Estimate log-odds effects and predicted probabilities with appropriate uncertainty.

steps.title: Diagnostics
steps.prompt: Check separation, calibration, discrimination, leverage, multicollinearity, and misspecification.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Report odds ratios or probability effects in substantive units and note causal limits.

definition.name: Multilevel Modeling
definition.summary: Multilevel Modeling uses a Data hierarchy → Fixed and random effects → Model estimation → Model checks workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Data hierarchy
steps.prompt: Define units, grouping levels, repeated measures, and substantive sources of dependence.

steps.title: Fixed and random effects
steps.prompt: Specify predictors and random intercepts/slopes consistent with the design.

steps.title: Model estimation
steps.prompt: Estimate variance components and effects with appropriate method.

steps.title: Model checks
steps.prompt: Assess residuals, shrinkage, influential groups, convergence, and sensitivity to random-effect structure.

steps.title: Cross-level interpretation
steps.prompt: Explain within- and between-group effects without conflating levels.

definition.name: Time-Series Analysis
definition.summary: Time-Series Analysis uses a Series definition → Temporal structure → Model and validation → Interventions and shocks workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Series definition
steps.prompt: Define frequency, time span, measurement process, missing periods, revisions, and the forecasting or explanatory goal.

steps.title: Temporal structure
steps.prompt: Inspect trend, seasonality, autocorrelation, cycles, structural breaks, variance changes, and calendar effects.

steps.title: Model and validation
steps.prompt: Select an appropriate statistical or state-space model and validate it using residual diagnostics and rolling or out-of-sample evaluation.

steps.title: Interventions and shocks
steps.prompt: Represent known interventions, anomalies, regime changes, and external regressors without allowing isolated shocks to distort persistent structure.

steps.title: Forecast and uncertainty
steps.prompt: Produce forecasts with intervals, benchmark against simple alternatives, and state how uncertainty grows with horizon and structural instability.

definition.name: Interrupted Time-Series Analysis
definition.summary: Interrupted Time-Series Analysis uses a Series and intervention → Pre-intervention structure → Interruption effects → Validity threats workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Series and intervention
steps.prompt: Define outcome frequency, intervention point, pre/post windows, and concurrent events.

steps.title: Pre-intervention structure
steps.prompt: Model trend, seasonality, autocorrelation, and baseline instability.

steps.title: Interruption effects
steps.prompt: Estimate immediate level and slope changes and, where relevant, lagged effects.

steps.title: Validity threats
steps.prompt: Check cointerventions, history, measurement changes, regression to the mean, and anticipation.

steps.title: Time-series conclusion
steps.prompt: State effect estimates and uncertainty with limits on causal attribution.

definition.name: Survival Analysis
definition.summary: Survival Analysis uses a Event and time origin → Survival description → Hazard model → Assumption checks workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Event and time origin
steps.prompt: Define event, censoring, competing events, entry time, and follow-up.

steps.title: Survival description
steps.prompt: Estimate survival or cumulative incidence and inspect group differences.

steps.title: Hazard model
steps.prompt: Choose Cox, parametric, or competing-risk models appropriate to the question.

steps.title: Assumption checks
steps.prompt: Assess proportional hazards, functional form, informative censoring, and time-varying effects.

steps.title: Time-to-event interpretation
steps.prompt: Report hazard or survival contrasts with absolute risks where useful.

definition.name: Cluster Analysis
definition.summary: Cluster Analysis uses a Objects and features → Clustering method → Cluster solution → Validation workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Objects and features
steps.prompt: Define cases, variables, scaling, distance metric, and missing-data handling.

steps.title: Clustering method
steps.prompt: Choose hierarchical, k-means, density-based, model-based, or another method suited to structure.

steps.title: Cluster solution
steps.prompt: Select number or granularity using stability and validity criteria, not one index alone.

steps.title: Validation
steps.prompt: Assess robustness to scaling, initialization, resampling, and feature choices.

steps.title: Cluster meaning
steps.prompt: Characterize clusters substantively and avoid treating algorithmic groups as natural kinds.

definition.name: Principal Component Analysis
definition.summary: Principal Component Analysis uses a Variable matrix → Component extraction → Retention → Loadings and scores workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Variable matrix
steps.prompt: Define variables, scaling, sample adequacy, and missing-data treatment.

steps.title: Component extraction
steps.prompt: Compute components from the covariance or correlation matrix as justified.

steps.title: Retention
steps.prompt: Use scree, parallel analysis, variance, and interpretability to select components.

steps.title: Loadings and scores
steps.prompt: Interpret loadings, communalities, and component scores with sign indeterminacy in mind.

steps.title: Use and limits
steps.prompt: State whether PCA is being used for compression, visualization, or preprocessing and preserve original-variable meaning.

definition.name: Factor Analysis
definition.summary: Factor Analysis uses a Latent construct question → Factorability → Factor extraction → Rotation and interpretation workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Latent construct question
steps.prompt: Define variables and hypothesized latent dimensions.

steps.title: Factorability
steps.prompt: Assess correlations, sample adequacy, and measurement properties.

steps.title: Factor extraction
steps.prompt: Choose exploratory or confirmatory methods and appropriate number of factors.

steps.title: Rotation and interpretation
steps.prompt: Use orthogonal or oblique rotation consistent with expected factor correlations.

steps.title: Model validation
steps.prompt: Assess fit, cross-loadings, reliability, invariance, and replication.

definition.name: Discriminant Analysis
definition.summary: Discriminant Analysis uses a Groups and predictors → Assumptions → Discriminant functions → Classification validation workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Groups and predictors
steps.prompt: Define group labels, predictor variables, and classification goal.

steps.title: Assumptions
steps.prompt: Assess multivariate normality, covariance structure, collinearity, and group size.

steps.title: Discriminant functions
steps.prompt: Estimate functions and group centroids or use quadratic forms where justified.

steps.title: Classification validation
steps.prompt: Use holdout or cross-validation and report confusion, sensitivity, and specificity.

steps.title: Discriminant interpretation
steps.prompt: Identify influential variables while noting instability and overlap among groups.

definition.name: Correspondence Analysis
definition.summary: Correspondence Analysis uses a Contingency table → Row and column profiles → Low-dimensional map → Contributions workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Contingency table
steps.prompt: Define rows, columns, counts, weighting, and structural zeros.

steps.title: Row and column profiles
steps.prompt: Compute marginal profiles and chi-square distances.

steps.title: Low-dimensional map
steps.prompt: Extract dimensions that represent the main deviations from independence.

steps.title: Contributions
steps.prompt: Identify categories driving each dimension and inspect rare-category leverage.

steps.title: Map interpretation
steps.prompt: Interpret proximities cautiously and relate dimensions back to the original table.

definition.name: Latent Class Analysis
definition.summary: Latent Class Analysis uses a Indicators and population → Class models → Class selection → Assumption checks workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Indicators and population
steps.prompt: Define categorical indicators, sample, and substantive latent-group question.

steps.title: Class models
steps.prompt: Fit candidate class counts with local-independence assumptions.

steps.title: Class selection
steps.prompt: Use information criteria, entropy, stability, and interpretability rather than fit alone.

steps.title: Assumption checks
steps.prompt: Assess local dependence, sparse patterns, label switching, and sensitivity to starts.

steps.title: Class interpretation
steps.prompt: Characterize probabilistic classes and avoid reifying them as observed categories.

definition.name: Change-Point Detection
definition.summary: Change-Point Detection uses a Series and objective → Baseline behavior → Detection method → Validation workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Series and objective
steps.prompt: Define the time series, candidate types of change, and detection horizon.

steps.title: Baseline behavior
steps.prompt: Characterize noise, seasonality, autocorrelation, and expected variation.

steps.title: Detection method
steps.prompt: Apply statistical or algorithmic methods suited to abrupt, gradual, mean, variance, or distributional change.

steps.title: Validation
steps.prompt: Assess false positives, minimum segment length, multiple changes, and sensitivity to tuning.

steps.title: Regime interpretation
steps.prompt: Relate detected changes to substantive events while preserving uncertainty about cause.

definition.name: Statistical Power Analysis
definition.summary: Statistical Power Analysis uses a Design and estimand → Effect assumptions → Power calculation → Sensitivity workflow to characterize data, estimate relationships, identify structure, detect change, and quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Design and estimand
steps.prompt: Define hypothesis, effect measure, sample structure, alpha, and planned analysis.

steps.title: Effect assumptions
steps.prompt: Specify minimally important or plausible effect sizes and nuisance parameters.

steps.title: Power calculation
steps.prompt: Estimate required sample size or detectable effect under the planned design.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Vary attrition, variance, prevalence, clustering, multiplicity, and model assumptions.

steps.title: Design decision
steps.prompt: State the sample or precision target and the consequences of underpowered alternatives.

definition.name: Causal Diagramming with DAGs
definition.summary: Causal Diagramming with DAGs uses a Causal question → Variables → Directed acyclic graph → Adjustment logic workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Causal question
steps.prompt: Specify the exposure, outcome, population, and causal contrast of interest.

steps.title: Variables
steps.prompt: List plausible causes of the exposure, outcome, and relevant common causes using substantive knowledge.

steps.title: Directed acyclic graph
steps.prompt: Draw causal arrows without conditioning on the observed data pattern; include unmeasured variables when conceptually important.

steps.title: Adjustment logic
steps.prompt: Identify backdoor paths, confounders to adjust for, mediators to avoid adjusting away, and colliders that should not be conditioned on.

steps.title: Identification and sensitivity
steps.prompt: State whether the effect is identifiable under the graph and which assumptions require sensitivity analysis or additional evidence.

definition.name: Backdoor Criterion Review
definition.summary: Backdoor Criterion Review uses a Causal effect → Candidate causal graph → Backdoor paths → Adjustment set workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Causal effect
steps.prompt: Define exposure, outcome, population, and causal contrast.

steps.title: Candidate causal graph
steps.prompt: Map plausible common causes, mediators, colliders, and descendants before choosing controls.

steps.title: Backdoor paths
steps.prompt: Identify noncausal paths entering the exposure through an incoming arrow and determine which remain open.

steps.title: Adjustment set
steps.prompt: Select a sufficient set that blocks relevant backdoor paths without conditioning on mediators or colliders.

steps.title: Identification assumptions
steps.prompt: State unmeasured-confounding, measurement, positivity, and model assumptions that remain after adjustment.

definition.name: Front-Door Criterion Review
definition.summary: Front-Door Criterion Review uses a Mediator structure → Criterion conditions → Evidence for assumptions → Identification plan workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Mediator structure
steps.prompt: Define exposure, mediator, outcome, and the mechanism that could support front-door identification.

steps.title: Criterion conditions
steps.prompt: Check whether the mediator intercepts the exposure effect, exposure-mediator confounding is controlled, and mediator-outcome backdoor paths are blocked.

steps.title: Evidence for assumptions
steps.prompt: Assess whether those structural assumptions are substantively defensible rather than merely statistically convenient.

steps.title: Identification plan
steps.prompt: Specify how exposure-to-mediator and mediator-to-outcome relationships would be estimated and combined.

steps.title: Failure modes
steps.prompt: Identify direct effects, hidden confounding, measurement error, or selection that would invalidate the design.

definition.name: Propensity Score Matching
definition.summary: Propensity Score Matching uses a Causal estimand → Pre-treatment covariates → Propensity model and overlap → Match and balance workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Causal estimand
steps.prompt: Define treatment, outcome, target population, timing, and the effect to estimate.

steps.title: Pre-treatment covariates
steps.prompt: Select variables that affect treatment assignment and outcome using causal knowledge; do not include post-treatment variables.

steps.title: Propensity model and overlap
steps.prompt: Estimate treatment propensity and inspect common support, positivity, and extreme scores before matching.

steps.title: Match and balance
steps.prompt: Choose matching rules, assess covariate balance after matching, and iterate without optimizing on the outcome.

steps.title: Effect and sensitivity
steps.prompt: Estimate the matched effect with appropriate uncertainty and assess residual confounding, hidden bias, and generalizability.

definition.name: Inverse Probability Weighting
definition.summary: Inverse Probability Weighting uses a Target estimand → Assignment model → Construct weights → Weighted balance workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Target estimand
steps.prompt: Define treatment or exposure, outcome, population, and the causal estimand to be weighted.

steps.title: Assignment model
steps.prompt: Estimate treatment or censoring probabilities using pre-exposure covariates that address exchangeability.

steps.title: Construct weights
steps.prompt: Calculate stabilized or unstabilized weights and inspect extreme values, overlap, and positivity.

steps.title: Weighted balance
steps.prompt: Check whether weighting balances covariates and whether a small number of observations dominate the pseudo-population.

steps.title: Effect and robustness
steps.prompt: Estimate the weighted effect and report sensitivity to truncation, model specification, and residual confounding.

definition.name: Difference-in-Differences
definition.summary: Difference-in-Differences uses a Groups and intervention → Pre-treatment trends → Difference in differences → Validity threats workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Groups and intervention
steps.prompt: Define treated and comparison groups, intervention timing, and outcome.

steps.title: Pre-treatment trends
steps.prompt: Examine whether groups followed sufficiently parallel trends before treatment and identify anticipatory effects.

steps.title: Difference in differences
steps.prompt: Compare outcome changes over time between groups using an appropriate specification.

steps.title: Validity threats
steps.prompt: Check concurrent shocks, compositional changes, spillovers, staggered treatment issues, and differential measurement.

steps.title: Causal interpretation
steps.prompt: State the estimated effect together with the assumptions and robustness checks required for a causal reading.

prerequisites: Pre-treatment outcome history sufficient to assess parallel trends

definition.name: Regression Discontinuity
definition.summary: Regression Discontinuity uses a Assignment rule → Local validity → Bandwidth and form → Discontinuity estimate workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Assignment rule
steps.prompt: Define the running variable, cutoff, treatment assignment mechanism, outcome, and whether the design is sharp or fuzzy.

steps.title: Local validity
steps.prompt: Assess whether units can precisely manipulate the running variable and whether other determinants change discontinuously at the cutoff.

steps.title: Bandwidth and form
steps.prompt: Choose bandwidth and local functional form transparently and test reasonable alternatives rather than high-order global polynomials.

steps.title: Discontinuity estimate
steps.prompt: Estimate the jump at the cutoff with appropriate uncertainty and graphical diagnostics.

steps.title: Local interpretation
steps.prompt: State the local causal effect, robustness checks, density and covariate continuity evidence, and limits on extrapolation away from the cutoff.

definition.name: Instrumental Variables
definition.summary: Instrumental Variables uses a Candidate instrument → Relevance → Independence and exclusion → IV estimand workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Candidate instrument
steps.prompt: Define the instrument, exposure, outcome, population, and causal effect of interest.

steps.title: Relevance
steps.prompt: Show that the instrument materially shifts the exposure in the target population.

steps.title: Independence and exclusion
steps.prompt: Assess whether the instrument is independent of outcome causes and affects the outcome only through the exposure.

steps.title: IV estimand
steps.prompt: Specify the estimation strategy and the population whose effect is identified, including monotonicity assumptions when relevant.

steps.title: Validity threats
steps.prompt: Test weak-instrument risk, direct pathways, selection, heterogeneous effects, and alternative explanations for the instrument-outcome association.

definition.name: Synthetic Control
definition.summary: Synthetic Control uses a Treated unit and intervention → Donor pool quality → Construct synthetic control → Post-treatment gap workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Treated unit and intervention
steps.prompt: Define the treated unit, intervention time, outcome, donor pool, and pre-intervention predictors.

steps.title: Donor pool quality
steps.prompt: Exclude donors affected by the intervention or structurally inappropriate and document why remaining units are plausible comparators.

steps.title: Construct synthetic control
steps.prompt: Choose donor weights to reproduce pre-intervention outcomes and relevant predictors and inspect pre-treatment fit.

steps.title: Post-treatment gap
steps.prompt: Compare treated and synthetic trajectories after intervention and characterize effect size and persistence.

steps.title: Inference and robustness
steps.prompt: Use placebo-in-space or time tests, donor sensitivity, and alternative specifications to judge whether the observed gap is unusual and robust.

definition.name: Matching Analysis
definition.summary: Matching Analysis uses a Causal comparison → Pre-treatment covariates → Matching design → Balance and overlap workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Causal comparison
steps.prompt: Define treated and comparison conditions, outcome, target population, and estimand.

steps.title: Pre-treatment covariates
steps.prompt: Select confounders measured before treatment and avoid matching on post-treatment variables or colliders.

steps.title: Matching design
steps.prompt: Choose distance, propensity, caliper, exact, or other matching rules and define replacement and ratio choices.

steps.title: Balance and overlap
steps.prompt: Evaluate covariate balance, common support, discarded cases, and sensitivity to alternate matching specifications.

steps.title: Matched effect
steps.prompt: Estimate the effect in the matched sample and state limits from residual confounding, representativeness, and matching uncertainty.

definition.name: Natural Experiment Analysis
definition.summary: Natural Experiment Analysis uses a Exogenous variation → Assignment mechanism → Alternative pathways → Identification design workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Exogenous variation
steps.prompt: Identify the event, rule, boundary, timing, or process that creates plausibly exogenous exposure variation.

steps.title: Assignment mechanism
steps.prompt: Explain why units on different sides of the variation should be comparable apart from exposure.

steps.title: Alternative pathways
steps.prompt: Test anticipation, sorting, concurrent shocks, spillovers, differential measurement, and selective attrition.

steps.title: Identification design
steps.prompt: Choose the comparison strategy appropriate to the natural experiment and specify falsification or placebo tests.

steps.title: Causal inference
steps.prompt: State the effect, population to which it applies, and the assumptions required to interpret the result causally.

definition.name: Randomized Controlled Trial Design
definition.summary: Randomized Controlled Trial Design uses a Trial question → Randomization → Outcomes and protocol → Sample size and power workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Trial question
steps.prompt: Define population, intervention, comparator, outcomes, estimand, and follow-up horizon.

steps.title: Randomization
steps.prompt: Specify assignment unit, allocation method, concealment, stratification or blocking, and contamination risks.

steps.title: Outcomes and protocol
steps.prompt: Predefine primary and secondary outcomes, measurement schedule, adherence, missing-data handling, and analysis population.

steps.title: Sample size and power
steps.prompt: Set effect size assumptions, variance, attrition, clustering, and error rates needed for a defensible sample size.

steps.title: Analysis and integrity
steps.prompt: Specify intention-to-treat or other estimands, protocol deviations, stopping rules, multiplicity, and transparent reporting.

definition.name: A/B Test Design
definition.summary: A/B Test Design uses a Decision and metric → Randomization unit → Sample and duration → Analysis plan workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Decision and metric
steps.prompt: Define the product or policy decision, treatment contrast, primary metric, guardrails, and decision threshold.

steps.title: Randomization unit
steps.prompt: Choose user, session, cluster, or other assignment unit and address interference, repeated exposure, and contamination.

steps.title: Sample and duration
steps.prompt: Estimate required sample size and runtime from baseline rates, minimum detectable effect, variance, traffic, and novelty or seasonality concerns.

steps.title: Analysis plan
steps.prompt: Predefine exclusions, metric transformations, multiplicity handling, sequential looks, and segment analyses before inspecting outcomes.

steps.title: Decision rule
steps.prompt: Interpret statistical and practical significance together and record rollout, rollback, or further-test conditions.

definition.name: Factorial Experiment Design
definition.summary: Factorial Experiment Design uses a Factors and levels → Factorial structure → Execution controls → Main and interaction effects workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Factors and levels
steps.prompt: Define experimental factors, levels, outcomes, constraints, and interactions that matter.

steps.title: Factorial structure
steps.prompt: Choose full or fractional factorial structure and document aliasing, blocking, randomization, and replication.

steps.title: Execution controls
steps.prompt: Standardize treatment delivery, measurement, and assignment while tracking deviations and missing runs.

steps.title: Main and interaction effects
steps.prompt: Estimate main effects and interactions without interpreting a main effect in isolation when strong interactions exist.

steps.title: Design insight
steps.prompt: Use effect patterns to identify promising combinations, nonlinearities requiring follow-up, and settings robust to noise.

definition.name: Quasi-Experimental Design
definition.summary: Quasi-Experimental Design uses a Causal question → Identification strategy → Design assumptions → Validity threats workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Causal question
steps.prompt: Define the intervention or exposure, outcome, target population, and counterfactual of interest.

steps.title: Identification strategy
steps.prompt: Choose a credible nonrandom design such as interrupted time series, regression discontinuity, matched comparison, synthetic control, or difference-in-differences.

steps.title: Design assumptions
steps.prompt: State the assumptions that create comparability and identify observable implications that can be tested.

steps.title: Validity threats
steps.prompt: Assess selection, history, maturation, regression to the mean, spillovers, measurement changes, and model dependence.

steps.title: Robustness and inference
steps.prompt: Apply placebo, falsification, sensitivity, or alternate-specification checks and bound the causal conclusion accordingly.

definition.name: Mediation Analysis
definition.summary: Mediation Analysis uses a Mediation model → Path assumptions → Effect decomposition → Mediator assumptions workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Mediation model
steps.prompt: Define exposure, proposed mediator, outcome, timing, and the causal mechanism being tested.

steps.title: Path assumptions
steps.prompt: Identify exposure-mediator, mediator-outcome, and direct pathways plus confounders of each relationship.

steps.title: Effect decomposition
steps.prompt: Estimate total, direct, and indirect effects using an approach appropriate to scale and interaction structure.

steps.title: Mediator assumptions
steps.prompt: Assess mediator-outcome confounding, post-treatment confounding, measurement error, and sensitivity to alternate mediator definitions.

steps.title: Mechanism inference
steps.prompt: State what the mediation results do and do not establish about mechanism, especially when temporal or causal assumptions are weak.

definition.name: Moderation Analysis
definition.summary: Moderation Analysis uses a Effect of interest → Interaction specification → Data support → Conditional effects workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Effect of interest
steps.prompt: Define the relationship or treatment effect and the variable hypothesized to modify it.

steps.title: Interaction specification
steps.prompt: Specify the interaction on a meaningful scale and distinguish effect modification from confounding or subgroup description.

steps.title: Data support
steps.prompt: Check sample size, overlap, distribution of the moderator, functional form, and whether categories were chosen post hoc.

steps.title: Conditional effects
steps.prompt: Estimate and visualize effects across substantively meaningful moderator values with uncertainty.

steps.title: Heterogeneity judgment
steps.prompt: Assess robustness, multiplicity, plausibility, and whether observed heterogeneity warrants different decisions or further study.

definition.name: Mechanism Mapping
definition.summary: Mechanism Mapping uses a Causal claim → Mechanism sequence → Evidence by link → Rival mechanisms workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Causal claim
steps.prompt: State the cause, outcome, context, and proposed mechanism that connects them.

steps.title: Mechanism sequence
steps.prompt: Decompose the mechanism into entities, activities, state changes, and intermediate links in temporal or logical order.

steps.title: Evidence by link
steps.prompt: Attach supporting, contradicting, and missing evidence to each mechanism link and record provenance.

steps.title: Rival mechanisms
steps.prompt: Identify alternate pathways, shortcuts, feedbacks, and common causes that could produce similar observations.

steps.title: Mechanism tests
steps.prompt: Define observations or interventions that would discriminate among mechanisms and identify the weakest link in the current chain.

definition.name: Process Tracing
definition.summary: Process Tracing uses a Causal claim → Mechanism steps → Within-case evidence → Evidence tests workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Causal claim
steps.prompt: State the proposed mechanism linking cause to outcome in this case.

steps.title: Mechanism steps
steps.prompt: Break the mechanism into a sequence of actors, actions, states, and observable implications.

steps.title: Within-case evidence
steps.prompt: Collect evidence for each mechanism step and assess its provenance and independence.

steps.title: Evidence tests
steps.prompt: Classify important observations by how necessary or sufficient they are for the hypothesis and compare rival mechanisms.

steps.title: Causal inference
steps.prompt: State which mechanism steps are supported, where the chain remains weak, and which rival explanations survive.

definition.name: Contribution Analysis
definition.summary: Contribution Analysis uses a Theory of change → Contribution evidence → Alternative explanations → Contribution story workflow to distinguish causal effects and mechanisms from association, confounding, selection, and rival explanations.

steps.title: Theory of change
steps.prompt: Define the intervention, expected causal pathway, contextual conditions, and outcomes.

steps.title: Contribution evidence
steps.prompt: Assemble evidence for implementation, intermediate results, final outcomes, and each causal link in the theory.

steps.title: Alternative explanations
steps.prompt: Identify other programs, external events, selection effects, secular trends, and contextual factors that could explain the results.

steps.title: Contribution story
steps.prompt: Assess whether the observed pattern is consistent with the theory and stronger than plausible alternative explanations without claiming attribution beyond the design.

steps.title: Strengthen the inference
steps.prompt: Identify additional evidence, comparisons, process observations, or tests that would most improve the contribution claim.

definition.name: Systematic Review
definition.summary: Systematic Review uses a Review question → Search strategy → Screen and select → Critical appraisal and extraction workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Review question
steps.prompt: Define the review question, population or domain, concepts, outcomes, and eligibility criteria.

steps.title: Search strategy
steps.prompt: Specify databases or sources, search terms, dates, languages, grey literature, and supplementary searching.

steps.title: Screen and select
steps.prompt: Apply inclusion and exclusion criteria consistently and record reasons for exclusion.

steps.title: Critical appraisal and extraction
steps.prompt: Assess risk of bias or study quality and extract results using a predefined structure.

steps.title: Synthesis
steps.prompt: Integrate findings using an appropriate qualitative or quantitative synthesis and report heterogeneity, uncertainty, and evidence gaps.

definition.name: Scoping Review
definition.summary: Scoping Review uses a Review scope → Search coverage → Eligibility and charting → Evidence map workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Review scope
steps.prompt: Define the broad question, concepts, populations, contexts, and intended map of the field.

steps.title: Search coverage
steps.prompt: Design a transparent broad search across relevant databases, grey literature, and supplementary sources.

steps.title: Eligibility and charting
steps.prompt: Apply inclusion criteria and chart study characteristics consistently.

steps.title: Evidence map
steps.prompt: Describe concepts, methods, populations, and concentrations or gaps without overstating effect strength.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: State what the field contains, where uncertainty remains, and what synthesis or research should follow.

definition.name: Rapid Review
definition.summary: Rapid Review uses a Decision need → Streamlining choices → Focused search → Rapid synthesis workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Decision need
steps.prompt: Define the time-critical decision and the minimum evidence question needed.

steps.title: Streamlining choices
steps.prompt: Document deliberate shortcuts in searching, screening, appraisal, or synthesis and their likely bias.

steps.title: Focused search
steps.prompt: Search the highest-yield sources transparently within the time constraint.

steps.title: Rapid synthesis
steps.prompt: Summarize findings and quality with clear separation of evidence from inference.

steps.title: Decision caveats
steps.prompt: State what may have been missed and how the shortcuts constrain confidence.

definition.name: Umbrella Review
definition.summary: Umbrella Review uses a Review-of-reviews question → Review set → Review quality → Cross-review comparison workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Review-of-reviews question
steps.prompt: Define interventions, exposures, outcomes, populations, and eligible review types.

steps.title: Review set
steps.prompt: Identify relevant systematic reviews and assess overlap among their primary studies.

steps.title: Review quality
steps.prompt: Appraise methodological quality, recency, and certainty of each review.

steps.title: Cross-review comparison
steps.prompt: Compare conclusions, heterogeneity, discordance, and duplicate evidence.

steps.title: Overview conclusion
steps.prompt: Summarize the strongest conclusions and unresolved conflicts without double counting evidence.

definition.name: Meta-Analysis
definition.summary: Meta-Analysis uses a Effect question → Study effects → Pooling model → Heterogeneity and bias workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Effect question
steps.prompt: Define the effect or association, eligibility criteria, and compatible outcome metric.

steps.title: Study effects
steps.prompt: Extract or compute comparable effect estimates and uncertainties from eligible studies.

steps.title: Pooling model
steps.prompt: Choose and justify fixed- or random-effects assumptions and estimate the pooled effect.

steps.title: Heterogeneity and bias
steps.prompt: Assess between-study heterogeneity, influential studies, reporting bias, and meaningful moderators.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Report pooled magnitude, uncertainty, heterogeneity, evidence quality, and limits on generalization.

prerequisites: Eligible studies from a systematic evidence set

definition.name: Network Meta-Analysis
definition.summary: Network Meta-Analysis uses a Treatment network → Transitivity and consistency → Network model → Inconsistency diagnostics workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Treatment network
steps.prompt: Define interventions, comparators, outcomes, and the connected evidence network.

steps.title: Transitivity and consistency
steps.prompt: Assess whether effect modifiers are sufficiently comparable and direct/indirect evidence can be combined.

steps.title: Network model
steps.prompt: Estimate relative effects across the network using an appropriate fixed or random effects model.

steps.title: Inconsistency diagnostics
steps.prompt: Check local and global inconsistency, heterogeneity, and influential studies.

steps.title: Interpretation and ranking
steps.prompt: Report relative effects and ranking uncertainty without treating rank order as certainty.

definition.name: Meta-Regression
definition.summary: Meta-Regression uses a Moderator question → Effect and moderator data → Meta-regression model → Robustness checks workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Moderator question
steps.prompt: Define the study-level effect and candidate moderators before analysis.

steps.title: Effect and moderator data
steps.prompt: Extract comparable effect estimates, uncertainty, and moderator variables.

steps.title: Meta-regression model
steps.prompt: Estimate moderator relationships with appropriate weighting and random-effects structure.

steps.title: Robustness checks
steps.prompt: Assess leverage, collinearity, multiplicity, residual heterogeneity, and sparse categories.

steps.title: Ecological limits
steps.prompt: Interpret moderators cautiously and distinguish study-level association from individual-level causation.

definition.name: Evidence Mapping
definition.summary: Evidence Mapping uses a Evidence domain → Search and screen → Evidence coding → Map the landscape workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Evidence domain
steps.prompt: Define the field, intervention, population, outcome, geography, and study-type dimensions the map should cover.

steps.title: Search and screen
steps.prompt: Use a transparent search and eligibility process broad enough to characterize the evidence landscape.

steps.title: Evidence coding
steps.prompt: Code included studies consistently by topic, design, population, intervention, outcome, quality marker, or other mapping dimensions.

steps.title: Map the landscape
steps.prompt: Visualize or tabulate concentrations, sparse areas, redundancies, and intersections without conflating volume with evidence strength.

steps.title: Research gaps and next steps
steps.prompt: Distinguish true evidence gaps from poorly studied but low-priority questions and identify where synthesis or new primary research is most useful.

definition.name: Evidence Gap Map
definition.summary: Evidence Gap Map uses a Evidence framework → Systematic search → Structured coding → Gap map workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Evidence framework
steps.prompt: Define intervention/exposure and outcome dimensions plus study-design eligibility.

steps.title: Systematic search
steps.prompt: Search and screen transparently enough to characterize the evidence landscape.

steps.title: Structured coding
steps.prompt: Code studies by framework cells, design, population, geography, and quality markers.

steps.title: Gap map
steps.prompt: Display evidence concentrations and sparse cells without equating study count with evidence strength.

steps.title: Gap interpretation
steps.prompt: Identify decision-relevant gaps, redundant research areas, and priorities for synthesis or new studies.

definition.name: Best Evidence Synthesis
definition.summary: Best Evidence Synthesis uses a Synthesis question → Evidence hierarchy → Consistent findings → Contradictions workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Synthesis question
steps.prompt: Define the substantive question and criteria for evidentiary relevance.

steps.title: Evidence hierarchy
steps.prompt: Assess methodological quality and relevance rather than treating all studies equally.

steps.title: Consistent findings
steps.prompt: Identify patterns among the strongest studies and reasons lower-quality evidence diverges.

steps.title: Contradictions
steps.prompt: Examine robust contrary findings and plausible methodological explanations.

steps.title: Weighted conclusion
steps.prompt: State the conclusion driven by the best evidence and where uncertainty still matters.

definition.name: Realist Review
definition.summary: Realist Review uses a Review question → Initial program theories → Theory-driven search → Configure evidence workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Review question
steps.prompt: Frame the intervention or phenomenon in terms of what works, for whom, in what circumstances, how, and why.

steps.title: Initial program theories
steps.prompt: Develop candidate context–mechanism–outcome configurations from prior theory, stakeholder knowledge, and exploratory literature.

steps.title: Theory-driven search
steps.prompt: Search iteratively for evidence that can test, refine, refute, or extend the candidate program theories rather than pursuing exhaustiveness alone.

steps.title: Configure evidence
steps.prompt: Compare cases to determine how contexts activate or suppress mechanisms and produce different outcomes.

steps.title: Refined theory
steps.prompt: Produce a more precise middle-range explanation of how outcomes arise, where it applies, and what uncertainty or rival theories remain.

definition.name: Meta-Ethnography
definition.summary: Meta-Ethnography uses a Interpretive focus → First- and second-order concepts → Reciprocal and refutational translation → Line-of-argument synthesis workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Interpretive focus
steps.prompt: Define the phenomenon and qualitative studies to be synthesized.

steps.title: First- and second-order concepts
steps.prompt: Extract participant meanings and authors' interpretations from each study.

steps.title: Reciprocal and refutational translation
steps.prompt: Compare how concepts translate across studies, including contradictions.

steps.title: Line-of-argument synthesis
steps.prompt: Build a higher-order interpretation that explains relations among studies.

steps.title: Reflexive limits
steps.prompt: Document how selection and interpretation shaped the synthesis.

definition.name: Qualitative Evidence Synthesis
definition.summary: Qualitative Evidence Synthesis uses a Synthesis question → Study selection and appraisal → Cross-study coding → Synthesis themes workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Synthesis question
steps.prompt: Define the experience, implementation, acceptability, or contextual question.

steps.title: Study selection and appraisal
steps.prompt: Identify relevant qualitative studies and assess methodological limitations.

steps.title: Cross-study coding
steps.prompt: Code findings across studies while preserving context and provenance.

steps.title: Synthesis themes
steps.prompt: Develop descriptive and analytic themes, including disconfirming cases.

steps.title: Confidence in findings
steps.prompt: State confidence in each synthesized finding and the contexts in which it applies.

definition.name: Critical Interpretive Synthesis
definition.summary: Critical Interpretive Synthesis uses a Problematic literature → Theoretical sampling → Critical reading → Synthetic constructs workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Problematic literature
steps.prompt: Define the contested concept or body of literature requiring critical reinterpretation.

steps.title: Theoretical sampling
steps.prompt: Iteratively select literature for conceptual contribution rather than exhaustiveness alone.

steps.title: Critical reading
steps.prompt: Interrogate assumptions, categories, methods, and contradictions across sources.

steps.title: Synthetic constructs
steps.prompt: Develop new concepts that explain or reorganize the literature.

steps.title: Synthesizing argument
steps.prompt: Present the higher-order argument and where alternative interpretations remain viable.

definition.name: Narrative Synthesis
definition.summary: Narrative Synthesis uses a Review question → Organize evidence → Explore relationships → Assess robustness workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Review question
steps.prompt: Define the intervention, phenomenon, outcomes, and study differences relevant to synthesis.

steps.title: Organize evidence
steps.prompt: Group studies by design, intervention, population, mechanism, or another justified structure.

steps.title: Explore relationships
steps.prompt: Compare direction, magnitude, context, and study quality to explain patterns and heterogeneity.

steps.title: Assess robustness
steps.prompt: Test whether conclusions depend on weak studies, selective reporting, or arbitrary grouping.

steps.title: Narrative conclusion
steps.prompt: Produce a transparent narrative linking evidence to conclusions without vote counting.

definition.name: Bibliometric Analysis
definition.summary: Bibliometric Analysis uses a Bibliographic corpus → Bibliometric measures → Bibliometric networks → Coverage bias workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Bibliographic corpus
steps.prompt: Define databases, query, period, fields, and deduplication rules.

steps.title: Bibliometric measures
steps.prompt: Analyze output, citations, authors, institutions, journals, and normalized impact where appropriate.

steps.title: Bibliometric networks
steps.prompt: Construct coauthorship, citation, co-citation, or keyword networks suited to the question.

steps.title: Coverage bias
steps.prompt: Assess database, language, field-age, and citation-lag biases.

steps.title: Field structure
steps.prompt: Interpret growth, influence, collaboration, and intellectual structure without equating citation with quality.

definition.name: Co-Citation Analysis
definition.summary: Co-Citation Analysis uses a Citation corpus → Co-citation matrix → Cluster structure → Temporal change workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Citation corpus
steps.prompt: Define the source set and citation window.

steps.title: Co-citation matrix
steps.prompt: Count how often pairs of works, authors, or journals are cited together.

steps.title: Cluster structure
steps.prompt: Identify communities and central references using explicit thresholds or normalization.

steps.title: Temporal change
steps.prompt: Compare how co-citation structure evolves as the field changes.

steps.title: Intellectual interpretation
steps.prompt: Interpret clusters substantively and check whether data coverage distorts apparent schools of thought.

definition.name: Co-Word Analysis
definition.summary: Co-Word Analysis uses a Text and keyword corpus → Co-occurrence matrix → Concept clusters → Theme evolution workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Text and keyword corpus
steps.prompt: Define documents, fields, preprocessing, and term normalization.

steps.title: Co-occurrence matrix
steps.prompt: Measure term co-occurrence using a consistent unit and normalization.

steps.title: Concept clusters
steps.prompt: Identify thematic clusters and bridges among concepts.

steps.title: Theme evolution
steps.prompt: Track emergence, decline, and recombination of themes over time.

steps.title: Semantic validation
steps.prompt: Inspect source texts to verify that statistical proximity reflects meaningful conceptual association.

definition.name: Citation Network Analysis
definition.summary: Citation Network Analysis uses a Citation network → Network structure → Intellectual lineage → Citation anomalies workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Citation network
steps.prompt: Define nodes, directed citation edges, time window, and document types.

steps.title: Network structure
steps.prompt: Assess components, paths, centrality, communities, and citation flows.

steps.title: Intellectual lineage
steps.prompt: Trace influential chains and branching schools while accounting for age and field effects.

steps.title: Citation anomalies
steps.prompt: Inspect self-citation, review-article dominance, missing records, and retracted or disputed sources.

steps.title: Network interpretation
steps.prompt: State what the citation structure suggests and what it cannot establish about quality or truth.

definition.name: Snowball Search Strategy
definition.summary: Snowball Search Strategy uses a Seed set → Backward chaining → Forward chaining → Iterative saturation workflow to systematically locate, compare, synthesize, map, and evaluate bodies of research and evidence.

steps.title: Seed set
steps.prompt: Select high-relevance seed studies with transparent inclusion rationale.

steps.title: Backward chaining
steps.prompt: Review reference lists to identify earlier relevant evidence.

steps.title: Forward chaining
steps.prompt: Use citation indexes to identify later studies citing the seeds.

steps.title: Iterative saturation
steps.prompt: Repeat chaining from newly included high-value studies until marginal yield becomes low.

steps.title: Audit trail
steps.prompt: Record seed choices, databases, iterations, inclusions, and biases introduced by citation-network dependence.

definition.name: Empathy Mapping
definition.summary: Empathy Mapping uses a User and context → Evidence base → Says, thinks, does, feels → Tensions and contradictions workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: User and context
steps.prompt: Define the user or stakeholder segment and the specific situation being understood.

steps.title: Evidence base
steps.prompt: Ground the map in interviews, observation, service data, or other user evidence rather than invented personas.

steps.title: Says, thinks, does, feels
steps.prompt: Organize observed or carefully inferred statements, beliefs, behaviors, emotions, pains, and gains while marking inference separately from direct evidence.

steps.title: Tensions and contradictions
steps.prompt: Identify gaps between what users say and do, conflicting needs, workarounds, and contextual constraints.

steps.title: Design insights
steps.prompt: Translate patterns into needs, questions, or opportunity areas without jumping directly to a preferred solution.

definition.name: Persona Analysis
definition.summary: Persona Analysis uses a Evidence base → Behavioral patterns → Persona → Needs and tensions workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Evidence base
steps.prompt: Define the research sources and population used to construct personas.

steps.title: Behavioral patterns
steps.prompt: Identify recurring goals, behaviors, constraints, contexts, and motivations.

steps.title: Persona
steps.prompt: Construct an evidence-grounded archetype without inventing unsupported demographics.

steps.title: Needs and tensions
steps.prompt: Map jobs, pain points, workarounds, and decision criteria.

steps.title: Design implications
steps.prompt: Translate persona evidence into testable design requirements and flag uncertainty.

definition.name: Jobs-to-be-Done Analysis
definition.summary: Jobs-to-be-Done Analysis uses a Situation and progress → Core job → Forces of change → Desired outcomes workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Situation and progress
steps.prompt: Describe the circumstance in which a person seeks progress rather than starting from a product feature.

steps.title: Core job
steps.prompt: State what the person is trying to accomplish, including functional, emotional, and social dimensions.

steps.title: Forces of change
steps.prompt: Identify push from the current situation, pull of a new solution, habits of the present, and anxieties about change.

steps.title: Desired outcomes
steps.prompt: Translate the job into observable outcomes customers use to judge success.

steps.title: Opportunity
steps.prompt: Identify underserved outcomes or moments where current solutions force costly workarounds.

definition.name: Contextual Inquiry
definition.summary: Contextual Inquiry uses a Work context → Observe in context → Contextual probing → Work model workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Work context
steps.prompt: Define the activity, participants, environment, and research question.

steps.title: Observe in context
steps.prompt: Watch real work while preserving sequence, tools, interruptions, and environmental constraints.

steps.title: Contextual probing
steps.prompt: Ask participants to explain choices and tacit practices during or immediately after action.

steps.title: Work model
steps.prompt: Capture flows, artifacts, breakdowns, roles, and workarounds.

steps.title: Design insight
steps.prompt: Separate observed behavior from interpretation and derive opportunities grounded in context.

definition.name: Diary Study Analysis
definition.summary: Diary Study Analysis uses a Diary study → Entry preparation → Within-person patterns → Across-person comparison workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Diary study
steps.prompt: Define participants, period, prompts, event triggers, and expected reporting burden.

steps.title: Entry preparation
steps.prompt: Normalize timestamps, context, missingness, and participant-specific baselines.

steps.title: Within-person patterns
steps.prompt: Identify recurring behaviors, emotions, events, and temporal sequences.

steps.title: Across-person comparison
steps.prompt: Compare patterns while preserving meaningful differences and reporting bias.

steps.title: Design implications
steps.prompt: Translate longitudinal evidence into needs, moments, and hypotheses for further testing.

definition.name: Critical Incident Technique
definition.summary: Critical Incident Technique uses a Activity and outcome → Critical incidents → Behavioral coding → Critical patterns workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Activity and outcome
steps.prompt: Define the behavior domain and what counts as unusually effective or ineffective performance.

steps.title: Critical incidents
steps.prompt: Collect concrete episodes with context, actions, consequences, and participant perspective.

steps.title: Behavioral coding
steps.prompt: Code incident features and actions rather than vague attitudes.

steps.title: Critical patterns
steps.prompt: Identify behaviors or conditions repeatedly associated with success or failure.

steps.title: Application
steps.prompt: Translate patterns into requirements, training, controls, or design hypotheses.

definition.name: Service Blueprinting
definition.summary: Service Blueprinting uses a Customer journey → Frontstage interactions → Backstage and support → Failure and handoff points workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Customer journey
steps.prompt: Define the service, user segment, trigger, end state, and major customer actions.

steps.title: Frontstage interactions
steps.prompt: Map visible touchpoints, channels, employees, interfaces, and physical evidence encountered by the customer.

steps.title: Backstage and support
steps.prompt: Map invisible activities, systems, policies, teams, suppliers, and dependencies enabling each frontstage step.

steps.title: Failure and handoff points
steps.prompt: Identify waits, rework, ambiguity, ownership gaps, bottlenecks, fragile dependencies, and recovery moments across the blueprint.

steps.title: Redesign priorities
steps.prompt: Select changes that improve customer outcomes and operational feasibility and define measures for validating the redesign.

definition.name: Customer Journey Mapping
definition.summary: Customer Journey Mapping uses a Journey scope → Stages and actions → Experience layer → Breakdowns and transitions workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Journey scope
steps.prompt: Define user, goal, start/end points, channels, and scenario.

steps.title: Stages and actions
steps.prompt: Map stages, actions, touchpoints, actors, and artifacts.

steps.title: Experience layer
steps.prompt: Record expectations, emotions, effort, pain points, and unmet needs with evidence.

steps.title: Breakdowns and transitions
steps.prompt: Identify handoff failures, delays, duplication, and moments of truth.

steps.title: Opportunities
steps.prompt: Prioritize changes by user value, operational feasibility, and evidence strength.

definition.name: Experience Mapping
definition.summary: Experience Mapping uses a Experience domain → Phases → Experience forces → Cross-channel patterns workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Experience domain
steps.prompt: Define the broad experience across products, services, or contexts.

steps.title: Phases
steps.prompt: Map major phases, goals, behaviors, environments, and actors.

steps.title: Experience forces
steps.prompt: Capture motivations, emotions, constraints, social influences, and information needs.

steps.title: Cross-channel patterns
steps.prompt: Identify persistent problems and opportunities that exceed any single touchpoint.

steps.title: Strategic implications
steps.prompt: Define experience principles and opportunity areas that can guide multiple solutions.

definition.name: Story Mapping
definition.summary: Story Mapping uses a User goal → Activity backbone → Tasks and stories → Release slices workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: User goal
steps.prompt: Define the user outcome or end-to-end activity being mapped.

steps.title: Activity backbone
steps.prompt: Arrange major user activities in narrative sequence.

steps.title: Tasks and stories
steps.prompt: Break activities into user tasks and candidate stories at useful granularity.

steps.title: Release slices
steps.prompt: Create horizontal slices that deliver coherent outcomes, not arbitrary feature batches.

steps.title: Gap review
steps.prompt: Identify missing steps, dependencies, risks, and learning needed before sequencing work.

definition.name: Opportunity Solution Tree
definition.summary: Opportunity Solution Tree uses a Desired outcome → Opportunity space → Solution branches → Assumption tests workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Desired outcome
steps.prompt: Define a measurable product, mission, or user outcome.

steps.title: Opportunity space
steps.prompt: Derive user needs, problems, and desires from evidence and structure them without jumping to solutions.

steps.title: Solution branches
steps.prompt: Generate multiple solution approaches for promising opportunities.

steps.title: Assumption tests
steps.prompt: Identify critical assumptions and small experiments for each solution branch.

steps.title: Update tree
steps.prompt: Use evidence to prune, split, reprioritize, or add opportunities and solutions.

definition.name: How-Might-We Framing
definition.summary: How-Might-We Framing uses a Observed need → HMW question → Range check → Alternative frames workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Observed need
steps.prompt: Start from a specific evidence-backed user problem, tension, or opportunity.

steps.title: HMW question
steps.prompt: Write an open but bounded how-might-we question that avoids embedding a preferred solution.

steps.title: Range check
steps.prompt: Test whether the frame is neither so narrow it predetermines an answer nor so broad it loses the user need.

steps.title: Alternative frames
steps.prompt: Generate frames that shift actor, context, constraint, or desired effect.

steps.title: Select frame
steps.prompt: Choose frames likely to produce diverse, relevant concepts and record assumptions.

definition.name: SCAMPER
definition.summary: SCAMPER uses a Object or process → SCAMPER prompts → Idea capture → Screen ideas workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Object or process
steps.prompt: Define what is being redesigned and the outcome to improve.

steps.title: SCAMPER prompts
steps.prompt: Apply substitute, combine, adapt, modify, put-to-another-use, eliminate, and reverse/rearrange prompts systematically.

steps.title: Idea capture
steps.prompt: Generate concrete variants without evaluating too early.

steps.title: Screen ideas
steps.prompt: Assess novelty, user value, feasibility, side effects, and compatibility with constraints.

steps.title: Test candidates
steps.prompt: Select concepts for prototyping or evidence gathering.

definition.name: TRIZ
definition.summary: TRIZ uses a Problem and contradiction → Ideal final result → Available resources → Inventive principles workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Problem and contradiction
steps.prompt: State the engineering or system problem as a contradiction: improving one property worsens another, or a property must have opposing states.

steps.title: Ideal final result
steps.prompt: Describe the desired function with minimal cost, harm, complexity, or added resources.

steps.title: Available resources
steps.prompt: List existing materials, fields, time, space, information, and system functions that could be reused.

steps.title: Inventive principles
steps.prompt: Use relevant contradiction patterns or inventive principles to generate solution concepts rather than compromise immediately.

steps.title: Evaluate concepts
steps.prompt: Compare concepts against the contradiction, ideality, secondary effects, and implementation constraints.

definition.name: Six Thinking Hats
definition.summary: Six Thinking Hats uses a Decision or problem → White hat → Red/black/yellow hats → Green hat workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Decision or problem
steps.prompt: Define the focal question and participants.

steps.title: White hat
steps.prompt: Separate known information, missing data, and disputed facts.

steps.title: Red/black/yellow hats
steps.prompt: Capture intuition, risks/cautions, and benefits/value without forcing them into one argument.

steps.title: Green hat
steps.prompt: Generate alternatives, provocations, and modifications.

steps.title: Blue hat synthesis
steps.prompt: Summarize the process, unresolved tensions, next evidence, and decision without treating hats as evidence quality.

definition.name: Design Studio
definition.summary: Design Studio uses a Design challenge → Independent sketching → Share and critique → Converge workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Design challenge
steps.prompt: Define users, scenario, constraints, and success criteria.

steps.title: Independent sketching
steps.prompt: Have participants generate multiple concrete concepts before discussion.

steps.title: Share and critique
steps.prompt: Present concepts, ask clarifying questions, and critique against evidence and criteria rather than status.

steps.title: Converge
steps.prompt: Combine promising elements into stronger concepts while preserving materially different alternatives.

steps.title: Prototype plan
