steps.prompt: Select concepts and assumptions for prototyping and user testing.

definition.name: Crazy Eights
definition.summary: Crazy Eights uses a Focus question → Constraints → Eight variations → Review workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Focus question
steps.prompt: Define a specific user problem or design opportunity.

steps.title: Constraints
steps.prompt: Set the eight-frame format, short timebox, and evidence or requirements that must be respected.

steps.title: Eight variations
steps.prompt: Generate eight visibly different concepts or variations rather than polishing one idea.

steps.title: Review
steps.prompt: Identify distinct mechanisms, repeated assumptions, and surprising directions.

steps.title: Advance concepts
steps.prompt: Choose several candidates for elaboration or testing, not simply the prettiest sketch.

definition.name: Concept Screening
definition.summary: Concept Screening uses a Concept set → Screening criteria → Coarse rating → Review eliminations workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Concept set
steps.prompt: Define comparable concepts and minimum requirements.

steps.title: Screening criteria
steps.prompt: Choose a small set of critical criteria and a reference concept or threshold.

steps.title: Coarse rating
steps.prompt: Rate each concept consistently as better, same, worse, pass/fail, or another simple scheme.

steps.title: Review eliminations
steps.prompt: Check whether weak evidence, correlated criteria, or premature constraints caused rejection.

steps.title: Screen result
steps.prompt: Advance, combine, or discard concepts with reasons and learning needs.

definition.name: Concept Scoring
definition.summary: Concept Scoring uses a Concepts → Weighted criteria → Score concepts → Sensitivity workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Concepts
steps.prompt: Define the surviving concepts at comparable maturity.

steps.title: Weighted criteria
steps.prompt: Define measurable criteria, scales, and weights tied to user and system requirements.

steps.title: Score concepts
steps.prompt: Score each concept with evidence and record uncertainty rather than false precision.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test plausible weight and score changes for ranking reversals.

steps.title: Decision
steps.prompt: Select, combine, or retest concepts based on robust performance and evidence gaps.

definition.name: Kano Analysis
definition.summary: Kano Analysis uses a Attributes → Functional/dysfunctional responses → Kano classification → Segment and uncertainty workflow to understand user needs, reframe opportunities, generate concepts, and compare design alternatives.

steps.title: Attributes
steps.prompt: Define candidate product/service attributes in user-understandable terms.

steps.title: Functional/dysfunctional responses
steps.prompt: Collect paired reactions to presence and absence of each attribute.

steps.title: Kano classification
steps.prompt: Classify must-be, performance, attractive, indifferent, reverse, or questionable responses.

steps.title: Segment and uncertainty
steps.prompt: Inspect differences across user segments, sample size, and time because categories can migrate.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.prompt: Combine Kano class with strategic value, cost, and evidence to guide—not dictate—roadmap choices.

definition.name: PASTA Threat Modeling
definition.summary: PASTA Threat Modeling uses a Business and security objectives → Technical scope and decomposition → Threat and attack analysis → Risk analysis workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Business and security objectives
steps.prompt: Define assets, business impact, security objectives, and scope.

steps.title: Technical scope and decomposition
steps.prompt: Map application components, data flows, trust boundaries, dependencies, and attack surface.

steps.title: Threat and attack analysis
steps.prompt: Identify credible threat actors, objectives, attack paths, and relevant weaknesses.

steps.title: Risk analysis
steps.prompt: Estimate attack likelihood or feasibility and impact using explicit criteria rather than threat count alone.

steps.title: Controls and residual risk
steps.prompt: Map preventive, detective, and recovery controls to priority attack paths and record residual risk.

definition.name: LINDDUN Privacy Threat Modeling
definition.summary: LINDDUN Privacy Threat Modeling uses a System and privacy scope → Data-flow model → Interaction-by-interaction threats → Risk and affected parties workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: System and privacy scope
steps.prompt: Define the system, personal-data processing, actors, trust boundaries, and privacy objectives.

steps.title: Data-flow model
steps.prompt: Model external entities, processes, data stores, data flows, and relevant trust boundaries before eliciting threats.

steps.title: Interaction-by-interaction threats
steps.prompt: For each sending, transfer, and receiving interaction, examine linking, identifying, non-repudiation, detecting, disclosure, unawareness/unintervenability, and non-compliance threats.

steps.title: Risk and affected parties
steps.prompt: Assess impact, exploitability, scale, affected data subjects, and uncertainty for each material privacy threat.

steps.title: Mitigations and traceability
steps.prompt: Link mitigations to specific threats and interactions, record residual privacy risk, and preserve traceability to the model.

definition.name: Attack Surface Analysis
definition.summary: Attack Surface Analysis uses a System and assets → Exposed attack surface → Likely attack paths → Change and drift workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: System and assets
steps.prompt: Define assets, entry points, trust boundaries, identities, interfaces, data stores, and exposed dependencies.

steps.title: Exposed attack surface
steps.prompt: Inventory reachable services, APIs, protocols, user inputs, credentials, administrative paths, physical interfaces, and supply-chain dependencies.

steps.title: Likely attack paths
steps.prompt: Connect exposures to assets through required access, privileges, weaknesses, and trust transitions.

steps.title: Change and drift
steps.prompt: Identify new exposure created by configuration changes, integrations, privileges, remote access, cloud resources, or abandoned components.

steps.title: Reduction priorities
steps.prompt: Prioritize removal, isolation, hardening, monitoring, and privilege reduction based on reachable impact and attacker effort.

definition.name: Abuse Case Analysis
definition.summary: Abuse Case Analysis uses a Asset and legitimate use → Abuse goals → Abuse scenarios → Current controls workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Asset and legitimate use
steps.prompt: State the system function, actor goal, and normal use that could be abused.

steps.title: Abuse goals
steps.prompt: Generate harmful goals that misuse intended features, permissions, workflows, or business logic rather than requiring software exploitation.

steps.title: Abuse scenarios
steps.prompt: Describe actor, preconditions, sequence, target, impact, and observable behavior for each high-value abuse case.

steps.title: Current controls
steps.prompt: Identify preventive, detective, rate-limiting, authorization, policy, and recovery controls relevant to each scenario.

steps.title: Control gaps and tests
steps.prompt: Identify unmitigated abuse paths, monitoring gaps, and concrete tests or requirements to reduce them.

definition.name: Misuse Case Analysis
definition.summary: Misuse Case Analysis uses a Use cases and actors → Misuser goals → Misuse-use relationships → Security requirements workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Use cases and actors
steps.prompt: Identify important legitimate use cases, actors, assets, and trust assumptions.

steps.title: Misuser goals
steps.prompt: Define malicious or inappropriate goals that oppose, subvert, or parasitize the legitimate use cases.

steps.title: Misuse-use relationships
steps.prompt: Map which misuse cases threaten, include, or exploit which legitimate use cases and under what preconditions.

steps.title: Security requirements
steps.prompt: Derive prevention, detection, authorization, resilience, and audit requirements from the mapped misuse relationships.

steps.title: Validation
steps.prompt: Test whether the derived requirements actually block or reveal the high-priority misuse cases without breaking essential use.

definition.name: Threat Actor Profiling
definition.summary: Threat Actor Profiling uses a Actor identity and scope → Intent and objectives → Capabilities and resources → Behavioral pattern workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Actor identity and scope
steps.prompt: Define the actor or actor set and distinguish confirmed identity, aliases, suspected links, and attribution uncertainty.

steps.title: Intent and objectives
steps.prompt: Assess strategic and operational objectives, target preferences, incentives, and constraints using observed behavior rather than stereotype.

steps.title: Capabilities and resources
steps.prompt: Assess access, skills, tooling, infrastructure, logistics, partnerships, and operational maturity with evidence and confidence.

steps.title: Behavioral pattern
steps.prompt: Map recurring TTPs, timing, targeting, risk tolerance, adaptation, and operational security while separating reusable techniques from actor-unique signatures.

steps.title: Likely future behavior
steps.prompt: Identify plausible next actions, target shifts, capability growth, and indicators that would strengthen or weaken the profile.

definition.name: TTP Mapping
definition.summary: TTP Mapping uses a Observed behavior → Tactic-technique-procedure map → Evidence provenance → Behavioral pattern workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Observed behavior
steps.prompt: Extract concrete adversary behaviors, tools, access patterns, procedures, and artifacts from evidence before applying labels.

steps.title: Tactic-technique-procedure map
steps.prompt: Map observations to tactics, techniques, procedures, and sub-techniques at the most specific level justified by evidence.

steps.title: Evidence provenance
steps.prompt: Preserve source, timestamp, confidence, and ambiguity for every mapped behavior and avoid upgrading inference to observation.

steps.title: Behavioral pattern
steps.prompt: Identify recurring combinations, sequencing, preferences, and deviations that characterize the activity beyond single indicators.

steps.title: Analytic use
steps.prompt: Derive detection gaps, adjacent behaviors, collection priorities, and attribution-relevant similarities while preserving uncertainty.

definition.name: Kill Chain Analysis
definition.summary: Kill Chain Analysis uses a Adversary objective → Attack stages → Stage dependencies → Control coverage workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Adversary objective
steps.prompt: Define the campaign or intrusion objective and the defended environment.

steps.title: Attack stages
steps.prompt: Map observed or hypothesized activity across reconnaissance, preparation, access, execution, persistence, command/control, and actions on objectives using the chosen kill-chain model.

steps.title: Stage dependencies
steps.prompt: Identify prerequisites, transitions, and alternative paths; do not force every incident into a perfectly linear sequence.

steps.title: Control coverage
steps.prompt: Map preventive, detective, and response controls to stages and identify where one missed stage leaves downstream opportunities.

steps.title: Disruption priorities
steps.prompt: Select the earliest and most reliable points to deny, detect, degrade, or contain the campaign and define evidence needed to confirm disruption.

definition.name: Diamond Model Analysis
definition.summary: Diamond Model Analysis uses a Intrusion event → Four vertices → Relationships → Analytic pivots workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Intrusion event
steps.prompt: Define the bounded malicious event or activity being analyzed.

steps.title: Four vertices
steps.prompt: Identify adversary, capability, infrastructure, and victim evidence, preserving uncertainty and source provenance.

steps.title: Relationships
steps.prompt: Analyze how the vertices interact and what additional relationships, direction, or dependencies are implied.

steps.title: Analytic pivots
steps.prompt: Pivot from known vertices to discover related events, infrastructure, capabilities, victims, or adversary behavior.

steps.title: Activity thread
steps.prompt: Connect related events cautiously into activity threads and distinguish observation from attribution.

definition.name: MITRE ATT&CK Mapping
definition.summary: MITRE ATT&CK Mapping uses a Observed activity → Observed behaviors → Technique mapping → Coverage gaps workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Observed activity
steps.prompt: Define the incident, campaign, or actor behavior and the evidence window.

steps.title: Observed behaviors
steps.prompt: Extract concrete adversary actions before assigning ATT&CK labels.

steps.title: Technique mapping
steps.prompt: Map each supported behavior to the most specific applicable ATT&CK technique or sub-technique and preserve evidence links.

steps.title: Coverage gaps
steps.prompt: Distinguish unobserved behavior from behavior that was not detectable with available telemetry.

steps.title: Detection and mitigation implications
steps.prompt: Use the mapping to identify detection coverage, control gaps, collection priorities, and likely adjacent behaviors.

definition.name: Cyber Kill Chain Mapping
definition.summary: Cyber Kill Chain Mapping uses a Campaign scope → Cyber kill-chain phases → Alternative paths → Detection and prevention workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Campaign scope
steps.prompt: Define the intrusion set, victims, time window, and evidence boundary.

steps.title: Cyber kill-chain phases
steps.prompt: Map evidence to reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, and actions on objectives, preserving gaps.

steps.title: Alternative paths
steps.prompt: Record skipped, repeated, parallel, outsourced, or cloud-native paths that do not fit a strict linear progression.

steps.title: Detection and prevention
steps.prompt: Map controls, telemetry, and opportunities to interrupt each phase and distinguish missing telemetry from absent behavior.

steps.title: Campaign lessons
steps.prompt: Identify recurring weak points, high-value choke points, and phase transitions that deserve future collection or hardening.

definition.name: Indicator of Compromise Analysis
definition.summary: Indicator of Compromise Analysis uses a Indicator and context → Indicator quality → Corroboration → Scope and prevalence workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Indicator and context
steps.prompt: Define the observable, its source, time window, system context, and why it was considered suspicious.

steps.title: Indicator quality
steps.prompt: Assess specificity, stability, false-positive rate, adversary control, age, and whether the indicator is merely correlated with malicious activity.

steps.title: Corroboration
steps.prompt: Correlate the indicator with independent logs, behaviors, assets, identities, and timeline evidence rather than treating a match as proof.

steps.title: Scope and prevalence
steps.prompt: Determine where else the indicator appears, whether occurrence is benign, and what related infrastructure or activity may be discoverable.

steps.title: Disposition
steps.prompt: Classify as high-confidence, contextual, weak, obsolete, or false positive and define detection, blocking, hunting, and expiration rules.

definition.name: Timeline Forensics
definition.summary: Timeline Forensics uses a Evidence scope → Normalize time → Event timeline → Sequence and causality workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Evidence scope
steps.prompt: Define systems, accounts, clocks, sources, and the incident window.

steps.title: Normalize time
steps.prompt: Convert timestamps to a common reference, record timezone and clock skew, and preserve original timestamps.

steps.title: Event timeline
steps.prompt: Order relevant events with source provenance and confidence, including gaps and contradictory timestamps.

steps.title: Sequence and causality
steps.prompt: Separate temporal adjacency from causal dependence and identify candidate chains, parallel activity, and impossible sequences.

steps.title: Findings and gaps
steps.prompt: State supported sequences, uncertain intervals, and the evidence most likely to resolve remaining ambiguity.

definition.name: Artifact Correlation
definition.summary: Artifact Correlation uses a Artifact set → Correlation keys → Cross-artifact relationships → Correlated pattern workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Artifact set
steps.prompt: List relevant files, hashes, logs, registry entries, memory artifacts, network data, identities, and metadata with provenance.

steps.title: Correlation keys
steps.prompt: Identify stable join points such as timestamps, hosts, users, process IDs, paths, hashes, domains, IPs, session IDs, or transaction IDs.

steps.title: Cross-artifact relationships
steps.prompt: Link artifacts only where keys and timing support the relationship, and record alternative explanations for ambiguous matches.

steps.title: Correlated pattern
steps.prompt: Identify sequences, repeated infrastructure, shared tooling, persistence, privilege transitions, or victim overlap emerging across artifact types.

steps.title: Confidence and next collection
steps.prompt: Assess which relationships are strong, circumstantial, or unresolved and identify the highest-value missing artifact.

definition.name: Event Correlation
definition.summary: Event Correlation uses a Event streams → Correlation logic → Candidate incidents → Validate correlations workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Event streams
steps.prompt: Define log sources, schemas, clocks, retention, and the analytic time window.

steps.title: Correlation logic
steps.prompt: Define time, entity, sequence, threshold, or causal rules used to associate events and document why they should co-occur.

steps.title: Candidate incidents
steps.prompt: Group events into candidate incidents while preserving unmatched events and avoiding over-aggregation from noisy identifiers.

steps.title: Validate correlations
steps.prompt: Check source independence, timestamp quality, duplicate reporting, benign workflows, and whether the correlated pattern has a plausible mechanism.

steps.title: Incident-level output
steps.prompt: Produce bounded incident hypotheses with confidence, supporting events, contradictory evidence, and collection needs.

definition.name: Root Cause Security Analysis
definition.summary: Root Cause Security Analysis uses a Security failure → Contributing causes → Verify mechanisms → Systemic conditions workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Security failure
steps.prompt: Define the observed compromise, control failure, or exposure without embedding a preferred cause.

steps.title: Contributing causes
steps.prompt: Separate triggering events, technical weaknesses, identity and access failures, process gaps, organizational conditions, and external dependencies.

steps.title: Verify mechanisms
steps.prompt: For each candidate cause, identify evidence that demonstrates how it enabled or failed to prevent the incident.

steps.title: Systemic conditions
steps.prompt: Identify incentives, ownership gaps, monitoring limitations, architectural debt, or recurring conditions that make recurrence likely.

steps.title: Corrective actions
steps.prompt: Link corrective actions to verified causes and define tests showing the fixes remove or contain the causal pathway.

definition.name: Incident Reconstruction
definition.summary: Incident Reconstruction uses a Incident boundary → Normalized timeline → Causal sequence → Alternative reconstructions workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Incident boundary
steps.prompt: Define the systems, identities, assets, and time window under investigation.

steps.title: Normalized timeline
steps.prompt: Order events from independent logs and artifacts using normalized time and record clock uncertainty.

steps.title: Causal sequence
steps.prompt: Distinguish temporal adjacency from causal dependency and connect events only when evidence supports the link.

steps.title: Alternative reconstructions
steps.prompt: Identify gaps, ambiguous artifacts, anti-forensics, and plausible alternative sequences.

steps.title: Findings
steps.prompt: State the best-supported reconstruction, confidence by segment, unresolved gaps, and evidence needed next.

definition.name: Hypothesis-Driven Investigation
definition.summary: Hypothesis-Driven Investigation uses a Investigative question → Competing hypotheses → Observable implications → Targeted collection workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Investigative question
steps.prompt: Define the bounded question and avoid embedding the suspected answer.

steps.title: Competing hypotheses
steps.prompt: Generate plausible malicious, benign, procedural, and data-quality explanations before collecting only confirmatory evidence.

steps.title: Observable implications
steps.prompt: State what should be observed under each hypothesis and which observations would discriminate among them.

steps.title: Targeted collection
steps.prompt: Prioritize logs, artifacts, interviews, queries, or experiments with the highest expected diagnostic value.

steps.title: Update and closure
steps.prompt: Revise relative support as evidence arrives, preserve unresolved alternatives, and define closure criteria.

definition.name: Link Charting
definition.summary: Link Charting uses a Entities → Relationships → Structural patterns → Validate important links workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Entities
steps.prompt: Define people, accounts, devices, organizations, locations, infrastructure, or artifacts included in the chart.

steps.title: Relationships
steps.prompt: Add typed, directed relationships with source, time, confidence, and meaning rather than unlabeled lines.

steps.title: Structural patterns
steps.prompt: Identify clusters, brokers, shared resources, temporal changes, isolated nodes, and suspiciously dense or sparse regions.

steps.title: Validate important links
steps.prompt: Check whether central or surprising links reflect independent evidence, duplicated reporting, common infrastructure, or coincidental identifiers.

steps.title: Investigative implications
steps.prompt: Generate bounded hypotheses, collection priorities, and candidate pivots without treating visual proximity as proof of association.

definition.name: Pattern-of-Life Analysis
definition.summary: Pattern-of-Life Analysis uses a Subject and baseline → Recurring patterns → Deviations → Context and alternatives workflow to structure adversary, incident, evidence, timeline, behavior, and defensive analysis without assuming a single threat pathway.

steps.title: Subject and baseline
steps.prompt: Define the actor, system, place, or activity and the observation period used to establish normal behavior.

steps.title: Recurring patterns
steps.prompt: Identify repeated timing, locations, associations, sequences, volumes, or routines without treating correlation as intent.

steps.title: Deviations
steps.prompt: Identify material departures from baseline and assess whether they exceed normal variability.

steps.title: Context and alternatives
steps.prompt: Test benign, operational, seasonal, data-quality, and adversarial explanations for each deviation.

steps.title: Indicators and limits
steps.prompt: State what the pattern can support, what it cannot establish, and which future observations would be most informative.

definition.name: Regulatory Impact Assessment
definition.summary: Regulatory Impact Assessment uses a Policy problem → Options → Impacts → Compare options workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Policy problem
steps.prompt: Define the problem, baseline, affected groups, and why government action is being considered.

steps.title: Options
steps.prompt: Specify realistic regulatory and non-regulatory options, including a do-nothing baseline.

steps.title: Impacts
steps.prompt: Identify economic, social, environmental, rights, administrative, and distributional effects for each option.

steps.title: Compare options
steps.prompt: Compare benefits, costs, risks, uncertainty, implementation burden, and coherence using explicit criteria.

steps.title: Implementation and review
steps.prompt: Specify preferred option, residual uncertainty, monitoring indicators, and conditions for ex-post review.

definition.name: Cost-Benefit Analysis
definition.summary: Cost-Benefit Analysis uses a Scope and perspective → Identify effects → Value and timing → Uncertainty and sensitivity workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Scope and perspective
steps.prompt: Define the decision, affected population, time horizon, counterfactual, and whose costs and benefits count.

steps.title: Identify effects
steps.prompt: List material benefits, costs, transfers, externalities, and distributional effects without double counting.

steps.title: Value and timing
steps.prompt: Monetize effects where defensible, discount future values consistently, and preserve non-monetized effects explicitly.

steps.title: Uncertainty and sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test key assumptions, ranges, discounting, and scenarios that could change net benefits.

steps.title: Net assessment
steps.prompt: Report net present value or benefit-cost ratio together with distributional effects, unquantified impacts, and limitations.

definition.name: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis
definition.summary: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis uses a Outcome and comparator → Costs → Effects → Incremental comparison workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Outcome and comparator
steps.prompt: Define the policy objective, target population, comparator, and outcome metric.

steps.title: Costs
steps.prompt: Estimate incremental resource costs consistently across options.

steps.title: Effects
steps.prompt: Estimate outcome changes using a common effectiveness unit and uncertainty ranges.

steps.title: Incremental comparison
steps.prompt: Compare incremental cost-effectiveness and identify dominated options.

steps.title: Decision and uncertainty
steps.prompt: State the preferred option, thresholds, sensitivity, and non-quantified effects.

definition.name: Distributional Impact Analysis
definition.summary: Distributional Impact Analysis uses a Affected groups → Impact channels → Distribution of effects → Equity interpretation workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Affected groups
steps.prompt: Define relevant income, geography, demographic, sectoral, or vulnerability groups.

steps.title: Impact channels
steps.prompt: Trace how costs, benefits, risks, and access changes reach each group.

steps.title: Distribution of effects
steps.prompt: Estimate direction, scale, timing, and uncertainty by group.

steps.title: Equity interpretation
steps.prompt: Identify regressivity, concentration, protected interests, and tradeoffs.

steps.title: Mitigation
steps.prompt: Assess design changes or compensations that reduce unjustified burdens.

definition.name: Policy Options Appraisal
definition.summary: Policy Options Appraisal uses a Policy problem → Genuine options → Evidence and assumptions → Structured comparison workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Policy problem
steps.prompt: Define the problem, baseline, objectives, constraints, and decision criteria.

steps.title: Genuine options
steps.prompt: Develop materially different interventions including a credible status quo.

steps.title: Evidence and assumptions
steps.prompt: Assess effectiveness, cost, risk, implementation, and behavioral assumptions for each option.

steps.title: Structured comparison
steps.prompt: Compare options consistently and test sensitivity to contested judgments.

steps.title: Recommendation
steps.prompt: Recommend, reject, or sequence options with caveats and monitoring needs.

definition.name: Logic Model
definition.summary: Logic Model uses a Context and need → Inputs and activities → Outputs → Outcome chain workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Context and need
steps.prompt: Define the problem, population, resources, and external conditions.

steps.title: Inputs and activities
steps.prompt: Specify resources and actions within program control.

steps.title: Outputs
steps.prompt: Define direct products or services delivered.

steps.title: Outcome chain
steps.prompt: Link short-, medium-, and long-term outcomes with explicit causal assumptions.

steps.title: Indicators and assumptions
steps.prompt: Define indicators, external factors, and evidence needed to test the model.

definition.name: Theory of Change
definition.summary: Theory of Change uses a Long-term outcome → Preconditions → Mechanisms and assumptions → Context and alternatives workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Long-term outcome
steps.prompt: Define the desired change and target population or system.

steps.title: Preconditions
steps.prompt: Work backward to identify necessary intermediate outcomes and actor changes.

steps.title: Mechanisms and assumptions
steps.prompt: Explain why activities should produce each transition and what assumptions must hold.

steps.title: Context and alternatives
steps.prompt: Identify enabling conditions, competing explanations, and unintended pathways.

steps.title: Evidence and learning
steps.prompt: Attach indicators and evidence to causal links and specify how the theory will be revised.

definition.name: Stakeholder Consultation Analysis
definition.summary: Stakeholder Consultation Analysis uses a Consultation purpose → Stakeholder coverage → Views and evidence → Interpretation workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Consultation purpose
steps.prompt: Define the decision, questions, and whose knowledge or interests are relevant.

steps.title: Stakeholder coverage
steps.prompt: Assess who participated, who was absent, and how recruitment shaped the evidence.

steps.title: Views and evidence
steps.prompt: Code positions, reasons, experience, factual claims, and proposed alternatives.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Distinguish frequency from representativeness or evidentiary strength and preserve minority views.

steps.title: Policy response
steps.prompt: Record which inputs changed the analysis, which did not, and why.

definition.name: Implementation Feasibility Analysis
definition.summary: Implementation Feasibility Analysis uses a Policy or program → Delivery capacity → Actor feasibility → Implementation risks workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Policy or program
steps.prompt: Define the proposed intervention and required outcomes.

steps.title: Delivery capacity
steps.prompt: Assess legal authority, staffing, funding, technology, supply chains, and administrative capability.

steps.title: Actor feasibility
steps.prompt: Assess incentives, compliance, coordination, political support, and likely resistance.

steps.title: Implementation risks
steps.prompt: Identify sequencing, timing, dependencies, failure modes, and transition costs.

steps.title: Feasibility judgment
steps.prompt: State conditions for successful implementation, adaptations, pilots, and go/no-go triggers.

definition.name: Policy Coherence Analysis
definition.summary: Policy Coherence Analysis uses a Policy set → Interactions → Vertical and horizontal coherence → Tradeoffs workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Policy set
steps.prompt: Define the policies, objectives, jurisdictions, and time horizons to compare.

steps.title: Interactions
steps.prompt: Map reinforcing, neutral, duplicative, and conflicting policy mechanisms.

steps.title: Vertical and horizontal coherence
steps.prompt: Check alignment across sectors, agencies, government levels, and international commitments.

steps.title: Tradeoffs
steps.prompt: Identify incompatible objectives, displaced harms, and sequencing problems.

steps.title: Resolution
steps.prompt: Recommend alignment, governance, or monitoring changes while preserving legitimate policy differences.

definition.name: Skin-in-the-Game Incentive Audit
definition.summary: Skin-in-the-Game Incentive Audit uses a Decision and actors → Upside and downside map → Exposure asymmetries → Knowledge and accountability workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Decision and actors
steps.prompt: Identify who recommends, decides, implements, benefits, bears downside, and can exit from the decision.

steps.title: Upside and downside map
steps.prompt: Map material, reputational, career, political, legal, and operational consequences for each actor under success and failure.

steps.title: Exposure asymmetries
steps.prompt: Identify actors able to capture upside while transferring tail losses, uncertainty, cleanup, or long-term consequences to others.

steps.title: Knowledge and accountability
steps.prompt: Assess whether those with superior information bear consequences for concealment, poor forecasts, unsafe recommendations, or repeated error.

steps.title: Realign exposure
steps.prompt: Propose decision rights, warranties, clawbacks, staged authority, independent review, disclosure, or other mechanisms that better align influence with consequences.

definition.name: Commons Governance Design Audit
definition.summary: Commons Governance Design Audit uses a Resource and boundaries → Rules and local fit → Participation, monitoring, and sanctions → Conflict and rights workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Resource and boundaries
steps.prompt: Define the common-pool resource or shared capability, its users, legitimate rights, spatial or functional boundaries, and the appropriation problem.

steps.title: Rules and local fit
steps.prompt: Assess whether use and contribution rules fit local conditions and whether costs, benefits, and obligations are proportionate.

steps.title: Participation, monitoring, and sanctions
steps.prompt: Check whether affected users can help modify rules, whether users and resource conditions are monitored, and whether sanctions are graduated rather than all-or-nothing.

steps.title: Conflict and rights
steps.prompt: Assess access to low-cost conflict resolution and whether higher authorities recognize users' rights to organize rather than routinely overriding local rules.

steps.title: Nesting and durability
steps.prompt: For larger systems, examine nested governance layers, cross-scale coordination, and which missing design principles most threaten long-term institutional durability.

definition.name: Polycentric Governance Analysis
definition.summary: Polycentric Governance Analysis uses a Governance problem → Decision centers → Coordination and competition → Scale fit and feedback workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Governance problem
steps.prompt: Define the public problem, geography, affected populations, externalities, and functions that require collective action.

steps.title: Decision centers
steps.prompt: Map overlapping public, private, community, professional, and informal centers with meaningful autonomy over parts of the problem.

steps.title: Coordination and competition
steps.prompt: Identify cooperation, rivalry, redundancy, mutual adjustment, information sharing, appeals, and gaps among centers.

steps.title: Scale fit and feedback
steps.prompt: Assess which functions are handled at scales matching the problem and whether local experimentation can inform higher-level coordination without eliminating diversity.

steps.title: Governance resilience
steps.prompt: Identify single points of institutional failure, beneficial redundancy, accountability problems, and changes that improve adaptation while preserving effective local autonomy.

definition.name: Legibility / Local-Knowledge Audit
definition.summary: Legibility / Local-Knowledge Audit uses a Administrative scheme → Legibility simplifications → Implementation power → Practical knowledge workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Administrative scheme
steps.prompt: Define the policy, plan, model, classification, standard, map, metric, or redesign intended to make a complex population or system easier to see and manage.

steps.title: Legibility simplifications
steps.prompt: Identify what local variation, informal practice, tacit knowledge, ecological interdependence, exceptional cases, or competing values are removed by the administrative representation.

steps.title: Implementation power
steps.prompt: Assess how strongly the simplified scheme can be imposed, how reversible it is, and whether affected people have meaningful capacity to resist, adapt, or correct it.

steps.title: Practical knowledge
steps.prompt: Identify local, experiential, situated, or improvisational knowledge required for the system to work that is absent from the formal model.

steps.title: Legibility-safe redesign
steps.prompt: Preserve feedback from local actors, plural representations, reversibility, experimentation, exceptions, and adaptive discretion rather than forcing reality to conform to the simplified map.

prerequisites: A policy, model, classification, or administrative scheme
Access to both formal representations and local practice
Affected actors able to identify tacit knowledge, exceptions, or workarounds

references.label: Yale University Press — James C. Scott, Seeing Like a State

definition.name: Exit–Voice–Loyalty Analysis
definition.summary: Exit–Voice–Loyalty Analysis uses a Decline or dissatisfaction → Exit options → Voice channels → Loyalty effects workflow to compare policy options, impacts, implementation constraints, incentive alignment, governance structure, administrative simplification, institutional feedback, distributional effects, and theories of change.

steps.title: Decline or dissatisfaction
steps.prompt: Define the deterioration in quality, performance, legitimacy, service, or relationship that prompts actors to respond.

steps.title: Exit options
steps.prompt: Identify who can leave, switch, disengage, migrate, defect, or withhold participation; assess costs, barriers, substitutes, and who lacks meaningful exit.

steps.title: Voice channels
steps.prompt: Identify formal and informal mechanisms for complaint, protest, correction, participation, bargaining, or internal reform and assess their credibility and responsiveness.

steps.title: Loyalty effects
steps.prompt: Assess how loyalty, identity, sunk relationships, duty, or expected improvement delay exit, strengthen voice, or instead suppress warning and prolong decline.

steps.title: System dynamics and intervention
steps.prompt: Examine whether exit deprives the system of its strongest correctives, whether voice is heard before actors leave, and which institutional changes improve feedback without trapping participants.

prerequisites: A deteriorating organization, service, relationship, or institution
Observable or plausible exit, complaint, reform, and loyalty behaviors

references.label: Harvard / Google Books — Hirschman, Exit, Voice, and Loyalty

definition.name: Supply-Demand Analysis
definition.summary: Supply-Demand Analysis uses a Market definition → Demand and supply drivers → Market adjustment → Elasticity and incidence workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Market definition
steps.prompt: Define the good or service, geography, time period, substitutes, and relevant buyer and seller groups.

steps.title: Demand and supply drivers
steps.prompt: Identify determinants that shift demand or supply separately from movements along a curve.

steps.title: Market adjustment
steps.prompt: Assess how price and quantity respond to changes, including short-run versus long-run adjustment and capacity constraints.

steps.title: Elasticity and incidence
steps.prompt: Consider responsiveness of buyers and sellers and how elasticity shapes quantity response, revenue, and burden incidence.

steps.title: Market complications
steps.prompt: Check market power, externalities, price controls, search costs, information problems, rationing, and other reasons the simple competitive model may mislead.

definition.name: Elasticity Analysis
definition.summary: Elasticity Analysis uses a Variables and market → Estimate elasticity → Conditions → Interpretation workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Variables and market
steps.prompt: Define the quantity, price or driver, population, period, and market boundary.

steps.title: Estimate elasticity
steps.prompt: Estimate percentage responsiveness using an appropriate arc, point, or model-based method.

steps.title: Conditions
steps.prompt: Check range, time horizon, substitutes, income effects, and structural breaks.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Classify responsiveness and explain what behavior the estimate implies.

steps.title: Decision use
steps.prompt: Assess pricing, demand, tax, or policy implications with uncertainty.

definition.name: Marginal Analysis
definition.summary: Marginal Analysis uses a Incremental decision → Marginal benefit → Marginal cost → Compare at the margin workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Incremental decision
steps.prompt: Define the unit of additional action, output, input, or investment being considered.

steps.title: Marginal benefit
steps.prompt: Estimate the additional benefit from one more unit at the relevant scale.

steps.title: Marginal cost
steps.prompt: Estimate additional opportunity, resource, and external costs.

steps.title: Compare at the margin
steps.prompt: Identify where marginal benefit and cost cross or where constraints bind.

steps.title: Decision
steps.prompt: State the efficient stopping or adjustment rule and sensitivity.

definition.name: Opportunity Cost Analysis
definition.summary: Opportunity Cost Analysis uses a Choice → Foregone alternatives → Foregone value → Hidden costs workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Choice
steps.prompt: Define the scarce resource and decision that excludes alternatives.

steps.title: Foregone alternatives
steps.prompt: Identify realistic next-best uses rather than every conceivable option.

steps.title: Foregone value
steps.prompt: Estimate the value of the best displaced alternative, including timing and risk.

steps.title: Hidden costs
steps.prompt: Identify non-cash, capacity, delay, lock-in, and option-value losses.

steps.title: Net choice
steps.prompt: Compare the chosen use against its opportunity cost and record uncertainty.

definition.name: Welfare Analysis
definition.summary: Welfare Analysis uses a Change and baseline → Surplus changes → Externalities and distortions → Distribution workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Change and baseline
steps.prompt: Define the intervention, market, affected groups, and counterfactual.

steps.title: Surplus changes
steps.prompt: Estimate consumer, producer, government, and other relevant surplus changes.

steps.title: Externalities and distortions
steps.prompt: Include external costs/benefits, taxes, market power, and non-market effects.

steps.title: Distribution
steps.prompt: Identify who gains, loses, and whether transfers are being double-counted as net welfare.

steps.title: Welfare judgment
steps.prompt: State efficiency and distributional implications with assumptions and limits.

definition.name: Market Structure Analysis
definition.summary: Market Structure Analysis uses a Relevant market → Structure → Conduct → Performance workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Relevant market
steps.prompt: Define products, geography, customers, substitutes, and time horizon.

steps.title: Structure
steps.prompt: Assess concentration, entry barriers, differentiation, vertical relationships, and buyer power.

steps.title: Conduct
steps.prompt: Examine pricing, capacity, innovation, coordination, and strategic behavior.

steps.title: Performance
steps.prompt: Assess margins, quality, output, innovation, and consumer outcomes without inferring causality from concentration alone.

steps.title: Competitive outlook
steps.prompt: Identify likely structural changes and indicators of competitive harm or improvement.

definition.name: Game-Theoretic Payoff Matrix
definition.summary: Game-Theoretic Payoff Matrix uses a Players and strategies → Payoffs → Best responses and equilibria → Assumptions and dynamics workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Players and strategies
steps.prompt: Define players, feasible strategies, timing, and information.

steps.title: Payoffs
steps.prompt: Specify ordinal or cardinal payoffs including strategic and non-monetary objectives.

steps.title: Best responses and equilibria
steps.prompt: Identify dominant strategies, best responses, and candidate equilibria.

steps.title: Assumptions and dynamics
steps.prompt: Test sensitivity to repeated play, commitment, incomplete information, and coalition possibilities.

steps.title: Strategic implications
steps.prompt: Identify leverage, deterrence, bargaining, and signaling implications.

definition.name: Input-Output Analysis
definition.summary: Input-Output Analysis uses a System boundary → Technical coefficients → Demand or supply shock → Direct and indirect effects workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: System boundary
steps.prompt: Define sectors, geography, year, price basis, and transaction table.

steps.title: Technical coefficients
steps.prompt: Derive input requirements and check fixed-coefficient assumptions.

steps.title: Demand or supply shock
steps.prompt: Specify the exogenous change and affected sectors.

steps.title: Direct and indirect effects
steps.prompt: Estimate output, value-added, labor, or other multiplier effects while avoiding unsupported induced effects.

steps.title: Interpretation limits
steps.prompt: Assess imports, capacity constraints, substitution, prices, and temporal limits.

definition.name: Comparative Statics
definition.summary: Comparative Statics uses a Equilibrium model → Parameter change → Directional effects → Conditions workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Equilibrium model
steps.prompt: Define endogenous variables, exogenous parameters, constraints, and baseline equilibrium.

steps.title: Parameter change
steps.prompt: Specify the exogenous change to analyze.

steps.title: Directional effects
steps.prompt: Derive how equilibrium variables change and identify ambiguous signs.

steps.title: Conditions
steps.prompt: State assumptions needed for the result and thresholds where it may reverse.

steps.title: Economic interpretation
steps.prompt: Translate the comparative result into behavior, welfare, or policy implications.

definition.name: Economic Scenario Analysis
definition.summary: Economic Scenario Analysis uses a Economic baseline → Scenario shocks → Transmission channels → Scenario paths workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Economic baseline
steps.prompt: Define horizon, key variables, institutions, and baseline trajectory.

steps.title: Scenario shocks
steps.prompt: Specify coherent macro, market, policy, technology, or geopolitical shocks.

steps.title: Transmission channels
steps.prompt: Trace effects through demand, supply, prices, finance, trade, labor, and expectations.

steps.title: Scenario paths
steps.prompt: Develop internally consistent paths for key indicators and sectoral effects.

steps.title: Implications
steps.prompt: Compare vulnerabilities, opportunities, leading indicators, and robust actions across scenarios.

definition.name: Strategic Commitment Analysis
definition.summary: Strategic Commitment Analysis uses a Strategic interaction → Commitment device → Credibility → Opponent response workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Strategic interaction
steps.prompt: Define the actors, objectives, alternatives, sequence of moves, information, and what each side believes the other can still choose.

steps.title: Commitment device
steps.prompt: Identify actions that remove, worsen, delegate, automate, publicize, or otherwise constrain the actor's own future options.

steps.title: Credibility
steps.prompt: Assess whether the constraint is observable, costly to reverse, institutionally enforced, or otherwise believable to the other actor.

steps.title: Opponent response
steps.prompt: Model how the commitment changes the other side's incentives, bargaining position, coordination problem, and escalation or accommodation choices.

steps.title: Commitment risk
steps.prompt: Identify bluff failure, accidental escalation, loss of flexibility, domestic audience costs, and conditions under which preserving options is strategically superior.

references.label: Nobel Prize — Schelling on commitment and conflict

definition.name: Focal-Point Coordination Analysis
definition.summary: Focal-Point Coordination Analysis uses a Coordination problem → Candidate focal points → Shared expectations → Competing focal points workflow to analyze incentives, strategic interaction, coordination, tradeoffs, market structure, responses to change, and economy-wide relationships.

steps.title: Coordination problem
steps.prompt: Define the situation in which actors benefit from converging on the same action or interpretation but cannot fully communicate or enforce agreement.

steps.title: Candidate focal points
steps.prompt: List salient defaults, precedents, boundaries, symbols, round numbers, conventions, institutions, or culturally prominent solutions.

steps.title: Shared expectations
steps.prompt: Assess what each actor expects others to notice and what they expect others to expect in turn.

steps.title: Competing focal points
steps.prompt: Identify rival conventions or frames, actor-specific salience, asymmetric information, and signals that could shift coordination.

steps.title: Coordination assessment
steps.prompt: Judge which focal point is most likely to organize behavior, how robust that judgment is, and what observable choices would reveal convergence.

references.label: Nobel Prize — Schelling and strategic coordination

definition.name: Hot Spot Analysis
definition.summary: Hot Spot Analysis uses a Events and geography → Expected spatial pattern → Hot-spot method → Significance and stability workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Events and geography
steps.prompt: Define the event type, study area, observation period, coordinate quality, and spatial unit or distance assumptions.

steps.title: Expected spatial pattern
steps.prompt: Establish the appropriate population-at-risk or background distribution so density is not mistaken for excess risk.

steps.title: Hot-spot method
steps.prompt: Apply a suitable local clustering or intensity method and state neighborhood, bandwidth, or spatial-weight choices.

steps.title: Significance and stability
steps.prompt: Assess statistical significance or robustness and test sensitivity to scale, edge effects, and multiple comparisons.

steps.title: Spatial interpretation
steps.prompt: Explain what clusters may indicate while separating spatial association from causal explanation.

definition.name: Kernel Density Estimation
definition.summary: Kernel Density Estimation uses a Events and extent → Kernel and bandwidth → Density surface → Baseline comparison workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Events and extent
steps.prompt: Define event type, study area, time window, coordinate quality, and population-at-risk context.

steps.title: Kernel and bandwidth
steps.prompt: Choose kernel, bandwidth, cell size, and edge treatment with substantive justification.

steps.title: Density surface
steps.prompt: Generate the density estimate and inspect sensitivity to bandwidth and resolution.

steps.title: Baseline comparison
steps.prompt: Compare density with exposure or opportunity where raw event concentration could mislead.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Identify robust concentration patterns without treating smoothed density as causal risk.

definition.name: Spatial Autocorrelation Analysis
definition.summary: Spatial Autocorrelation Analysis uses a Variable and units → Spatial weights → Global pattern → Local structure workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Variable and units
steps.prompt: Define the measured variable, spatial units, time period, and data quality.

steps.title: Spatial weights
steps.prompt: Specify contiguity, distance, k-nearest-neighbor, or other neighborhood logic.

steps.title: Global pattern
steps.prompt: Assess whether similar or dissimilar values cluster overall.

steps.title: Local structure
steps.prompt: Inspect local clusters and spatial outliers where relevant, accounting for multiple testing.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Test sensitivity to scale, boundaries, weights, and spatial nonstationarity.

definition.name: Moran's I Analysis
definition.summary: Moran's I Analysis uses a Variable and geography → Weight matrix → Moran's I → Significance and diagnostics workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Variable and geography
steps.prompt: Define the variable, areal units, transformations, and study extent.

steps.title: Weight matrix
steps.prompt: Construct and justify spatial weights and row standardization.

steps.title: Moran's I
steps.prompt: Calculate the statistic and compare it with an appropriate randomization or analytical expectation.

steps.title: Significance and diagnostics
steps.prompt: Assess permutation significance and inspect influential units or nonstationarity.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Explain whether the pattern indicates positive, negative, or negligible autocorrelation and its limits.

definition.name: Getis-Ord Gi* Analysis
definition.summary: Getis-Ord Gi* Analysis uses a Measure and units → Neighborhood definition → Local Gi* → Statistical control workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Measure and units
steps.prompt: Define the attribute, spatial units, time window, and any rate standardization.

steps.title: Neighborhood definition
steps.prompt: Choose distance or contiguity parameters that reflect the process being studied.

steps.title: Local Gi*
steps.prompt: Calculate local hot- and cold-spot statistics for each unit.

steps.title: Statistical control
steps.prompt: Assess z-scores or permutation results and control for multiple comparisons where appropriate.

steps.title: Hot-spot interpretation
steps.prompt: Identify stable clusters and test sensitivity to scale and neighborhood choices.

definition.name: Viewshed Analysis
definition.summary: Viewshed Analysis uses a Observer and target → Surface assumptions → Line-of-sight computation → Sensitivity workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Observer and target
steps.prompt: Define observer locations/heights, targets, terrain model, and visibility question.

steps.title: Surface assumptions
steps.prompt: Check DEM resolution, curvature, vegetation/buildings, and vertical accuracy.

steps.title: Line-of-sight computation
steps.prompt: Calculate visible and hidden areas under stated parameters.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Vary heights, surface assumptions, and terrain resolution to identify fragile results.

steps.title: Operational implications
steps.prompt: Translate visibility into observation, concealment, communications, or siting implications without overstating certainty.

definition.name: Least-Cost Path Analysis
definition.summary: Least-Cost Path Analysis uses a Origins and destinations → Cost surface → Least-cost paths → Alternative paths workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Origins and destinations
steps.prompt: Define start/end points, movement mode, and what 'cost' represents.

steps.title: Cost surface
steps.prompt: Construct traversability or friction values from terrain, infrastructure, risk, rules, and barriers.

steps.title: Least-cost paths
steps.prompt: Compute candidate routes and cumulative costs.

steps.title: Alternative paths
steps.prompt: Inspect near-optimal routes and sensitivity to weights, resolution, and barriers.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Use paths as constrained hypotheses about movement rather than predictions of actual behavior.

definition.name: Spatial Network Analysis
definition.summary: Spatial Network Analysis uses a Network definition → Network measures → Calculate structure → Disruption scenarios workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Network definition
steps.prompt: Define nodes, links, direction, impedance, restrictions, and geographic accuracy.

steps.title: Network measures
steps.prompt: Select shortest path, accessibility, centrality, service area, flow, or resilience measures appropriate to the question.

steps.title: Calculate structure
steps.prompt: Analyze routes, connectivity, bottlenecks, and reachability.

steps.title: Disruption scenarios
steps.prompt: Test closures, capacity loss, alternative origins, or demand shifts.

steps.title: Operational meaning
steps.prompt: Explain what network structure implies while distinguishing topology from real-world capacity and behavior.

definition.name: Site Suitability Analysis
definition.summary: Site Suitability Analysis uses a Siting objective → Criteria layers → Standardize and weight → Suitability model workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Siting objective
steps.prompt: Define the facility/activity, constraints, stakeholders, and success criteria.

steps.title: Criteria layers
steps.prompt: Select exclusion and suitability factors with defensible units, thresholds, and provenance.

steps.title: Standardize and weight
steps.prompt: Transform criteria to comparable scales and justify weights or dominance rules.

steps.title: Suitability model
steps.prompt: Combine layers, identify feasible areas, and preserve hard constraints.

steps.title: Sensitivity and validation
steps.prompt: Test alternative weights/thresholds and compare candidate sites with ground truth or expert review.

definition.name: Spatial Change Detection
definition.summary: Spatial Change Detection uses a Comparable datasets → Alignment and normalization → Detect change → Validate workflow to analyze spatial concentration, proximity, accessibility, terrain, network structure, and change across geography.

steps.title: Comparable datasets
steps.prompt: Define dates, sensors/sources, coordinate systems, resolution, and classification schemes.

steps.title: Alignment and normalization
steps.prompt: Correct registration, scale, illumination, classification, and seasonal differences that could mimic change.

steps.title: Detect change
steps.prompt: Apply a suitable pixel-, object-, feature-, or classification-based comparison.

steps.title: Validate
steps.prompt: Estimate false change and missed change using reference data or manual review.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Separate genuine spatial change from measurement artifacts and identify causal hypotheses requiring further evidence.

definition.name: IRAC Analysis
definition.summary: IRAC Analysis uses a Issue → Rule → Application → Counterarguments workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: Issue
steps.prompt: Frame the precise legal issue as a question tied to material facts.

steps.title: Rule
steps.prompt: State the governing rule, elements, exceptions, standards, and controlling authority.

steps.title: Application
steps.prompt: Apply each relevant rule element to the facts using analogies, distinctions, counterarguments, and evidentiary limits.

steps.title: Counterarguments
steps.prompt: Present the strongest competing interpretation or application and explain what facts or authorities support it.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.prompt: Give a bounded conclusion proportionate to the authority and factual uncertainty.

definition.name: CREAC Analysis
definition.summary: CREAC Analysis uses a Conclusion preview → Rule → Rule explanation → Application workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: Conclusion preview
steps.prompt: State the likely answer to the legal issue in bounded terms.

steps.title: Rule
steps.prompt: State controlling authority, elements, standards, and exceptions.

steps.title: Rule explanation
steps.prompt: Explain how relevant authorities interpret and apply the rule.

steps.title: Application
steps.prompt: Apply the rule to material facts with analogies, distinctions, and counterarguments.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.prompt: Restate the supported conclusion and unresolved factual or legal uncertainty.

definition.name: Statutory Interpretation Analysis
definition.summary: Statutory Interpretation Analysis uses a Operative text → Textual meaning → Whole-statute context → Interpretive authority workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: Operative text
steps.prompt: Identify the exact statutory language, provision structure, definitions, cross-references, amendments, and relevant jurisdiction.

steps.title: Textual meaning
steps.prompt: Analyze ordinary or technical meaning, grammar, syntax, canons, and the provision's immediate textual context.

steps.title: Whole-statute context
steps.prompt: Examine statutory scheme, related provisions, exceptions, purpose clauses, and consequences of competing readings.

steps.title: Interpretive authority
steps.prompt: Assess binding precedent, applicable interpretive doctrine, legislative history where permitted, and administrative interpretations.

steps.title: Competing constructions
steps.prompt: Present the strongest competing readings, their doctrinal support and consequences, and the interpretation best supported under the governing legal method.

definition.name: Precedent Synthesis
definition.summary: Precedent Synthesis uses a Legal issue → Relevant precedents → Comparison dimensions → Synthesize rule workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: Legal issue
steps.prompt: Define the precise issue and jurisdictional hierarchy.

steps.title: Relevant precedents
steps.prompt: Collect controlling and persuasive cases with holdings, facts, and procedural posture.

steps.title: Comparison dimensions
steps.prompt: Identify legally meaningful similarities, distinctions, exceptions, and doctrinal trends.

steps.title: Synthesize rule
steps.prompt: Derive the best-supported rule or pattern without flattening conflicting cases.

steps.title: Current implication
steps.prompt: Explain how the synthesized precedent bears on the present facts and where uncertainty remains.

definition.name: Analogical Legal Reasoning
definition.summary: Analogical Legal Reasoning uses a Target case → Source cases → Material similarities → Material distinctions workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: Target case
steps.prompt: State the current facts and legal issue.

steps.title: Source cases
steps.prompt: Select precedents with potentially relevant factual and doctrinal features.

steps.title: Material similarities
steps.prompt: Identify similarities that matter under the governing rule, not merely surface resemblance.

steps.title: Material distinctions
steps.prompt: Identify differences that could justify a different result.

steps.title: Analogical judgment
steps.prompt: Assess which analogy is strongest and what competing analogy a reasonable opponent would use.

definition.name: Rule Synthesis
definition.summary: Rule Synthesis uses a Authority set → Rule propositions → Reconcile authorities → Synthesized rule workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: Authority set
steps.prompt: Identify statutes, regulations, cases, and other sources relevant to the issue.

steps.title: Rule propositions
steps.prompt: Extract explicit tests, elements, exceptions, standards, and burden rules.

steps.title: Reconcile authorities
steps.prompt: Resolve hierarchy, chronology, jurisdiction, and apparent doctrinal conflicts.

steps.title: Synthesized rule
steps.prompt: Write a coherent rule that captures controlling principles and recognized exceptions.

steps.title: Limits
steps.prompt: Record unresolved splits, fact dependence, and authorities that resist synthesis.

definition.name: Elements Analysis
definition.summary: Elements Analysis uses a Claim or offense → Elements → Facts by element → Element strength workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: Claim or offense
steps.prompt: Identify the cause of action, offense, defense, or legal test.

steps.title: Elements
steps.prompt: List every required element, subelement, burden, and applicable definition.

steps.title: Facts by element
steps.prompt: Map supporting, contradicting, and missing facts to each element.

steps.title: Element strength
steps.prompt: Assess whether each element is satisfied, contested, or evidentially weak.

steps.title: Whole-claim conclusion
steps.prompt: State whether failure or uncertainty on any required element changes the overall result.

definition.name: Proportionality Analysis
definition.summary: Proportionality Analysis uses a State action or restriction → Suitability → Necessity → Balancing workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: State action or restriction
steps.prompt: Define the challenged measure, objective, affected right or interest, and legal framework.

steps.title: Suitability
steps.prompt: Assess whether the measure can rationally advance the legitimate objective.

steps.title: Necessity
steps.prompt: Assess whether a less restrictive but similarly effective alternative exists.

steps.title: Balancing
steps.prompt: Compare the importance of the objective with the severity of rights or interest burdens.

steps.title: Proportionality judgment
steps.prompt: State the conclusion and factual assumptions that drive it.

definition.name: Balancing Test Analysis
definition.summary: Balancing Test Analysis uses a Balancing framework → Facts by factor → Relative weight → Competing balance workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: Balancing framework
steps.prompt: Identify the governing factors, their legal source, and any threshold or presumptions.

steps.title: Facts by factor
steps.prompt: Map record facts and uncertainty to each factor.

steps.title: Relative weight
steps.prompt: Assess which factors carry more legal significance and why.

steps.title: Competing balance
steps.prompt: Construct the strongest plausible balancing argument for the opposite result.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.prompt: State the likely balance and what factual change could alter it.

definition.name: Legal Issue Spotting
definition.summary: Legal Issue Spotting uses a Fact pattern → Actors and relationships → Potential issues → Prioritize workflow to structure legal issues, synthesize authority, interpret rules, compare precedent, and test application to facts.

steps.title: Fact pattern
steps.prompt: Summarize legally material facts without prematurely choosing doctrines.

steps.title: Actors and relationships
steps.prompt: Identify parties, duties, transactions, harms, authorities, and procedural posture.

steps.title: Potential issues
steps.prompt: Generate plausible claims, defenses, jurisdictional, evidentiary, procedural, and remedy issues.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.prompt: Rank issues by legal significance, factual support, deadlines, and outcome leverage.

steps.title: Research questions
steps.prompt: Translate unresolved issues into precise authority and fact questions.

definition.name: Linear Programming
definition.summary: Linear Programming uses a Objective function → Decision variables → Constraints → Solve and inspect workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: Objective function
steps.prompt: Define the quantity to maximize or minimize and its coefficients.

steps.title: Decision variables
steps.prompt: Define controllable variables, units, bounds, and non-negativity assumptions.

steps.title: Constraints
steps.prompt: Translate resource, capacity, balance, policy, or demand limits into linear constraints.

steps.title: Solve and inspect
steps.prompt: Find the optimal feasible solution and inspect binding constraints, slack, and shadow values where available.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test how coefficient or resource changes alter the solution and identify assumptions that make the optimum fragile.

definition.name: Integer Programming
definition.summary: Integer Programming uses a Objective → Integer decisions → Constraints → Solve and inspect workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: Objective
steps.prompt: Define the quantity to optimize and the decision horizon.

steps.title: Integer decisions
steps.prompt: Define binary or integer variables and what each represents.

steps.title: Constraints
steps.prompt: Encode logical, capacity, resource, sequencing, and policy constraints.

steps.title: Solve and inspect
steps.prompt: Find feasible and optimal or near-optimal solutions and inspect binding constraints.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test coefficient, bound, and integrality assumptions and identify fragile decisions.

definition.name: Goal Programming
definition.summary: Goal Programming uses a Goals → Priority structure → Deviation model → Solve compromise workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: Goals
steps.prompt: Define multiple goals, target levels, and units.

steps.title: Priority structure
steps.prompt: Assign lexicographic priorities or defensible weights and define acceptable deviations.

steps.title: Deviation model
steps.prompt: Create decision variables, constraints, and positive/negative deviation variables.

steps.title: Solve compromise
steps.prompt: Minimize prioritized deviations and inspect which goals remain unmet.

steps.title: Tradeoff review
steps.prompt: Test alternative priorities or targets and explain the resulting tradeoffs.

definition.name: Queueing Analysis
definition.summary: Queueing Analysis uses a Queueing system → Arrival and service rates → Queue model → Performance measures workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: Queueing system
steps.prompt: Define arrivals, service mechanism, number of servers, queue discipline, capacity, and customer classes.

steps.title: Arrival and service rates
steps.prompt: Estimate arrival and service distributions and check stationarity, dependence, balking, reneging, or priority behavior.

steps.title: Queue model
steps.prompt: Choose an appropriate analytical or simulation model and verify its assumptions against the real system.

steps.title: Performance measures
steps.prompt: Estimate utilization, expected queue length, waiting time, probability of delay, throughput, and service-level measures.

steps.title: Capacity decisions
steps.prompt: Test staffing, routing, prioritization, pooling, or demand-management changes and identify the utilization levels at which delay becomes operationally unacceptable.

definition.name: Discrete-Event Simulation
definition.summary: Discrete-Event Simulation uses a System boundary → Input distributions → Event logic → Simulation experiments workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: System boundary
steps.prompt: Define entities, resources, queues, events, routing, and performance measures.

steps.title: Input distributions
steps.prompt: Estimate arrival, service, failure, and routing distributions with data-quality caveats.

steps.title: Event logic
steps.prompt: Specify state transitions, priorities, schedules, and resource rules.

steps.title: Simulation experiments
steps.prompt: Run replications, warm-up, scenarios, and sensitivity tests with uncertainty intervals.

steps.title: Validation
