steps.prompt: Compare simulated behavior with real or expected system behavior before drawing conclusions.

definition.name: Markov Chain Analysis
definition.summary: Markov Chain Analysis uses a States → Transition probabilities → State evolution → Sensitivity workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: States
steps.prompt: Define mutually interpretable system states and time step.

steps.title: Transition probabilities
steps.prompt: Estimate or elicit transition probabilities and check row consistency and stationarity assumptions.

steps.title: State evolution
steps.prompt: Compute multi-step distributions, absorbing behavior, or steady state as relevant.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test alternate transition matrices and structural breaks.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Translate probabilities into operational implications without implying memoryless dynamics where unsupported.

definition.name: Dynamic Programming
definition.summary: Dynamic Programming uses a State definition → Actions and transitions → Bellman recursion → Solve policy workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: State definition
steps.prompt: Define the state variables that summarize all information needed for future decisions.

steps.title: Actions and transitions
steps.prompt: Define feasible actions, state transitions, rewards/costs, and horizon.

steps.title: Bellman recursion
steps.prompt: Formulate the stagewise value relation and terminal conditions.

steps.title: Solve policy
steps.prompt: Compute an optimal policy by backward induction or suitable approximation.

steps.title: Robustness
steps.prompt: Test horizon, transition, reward, and state-space assumptions.

definition.name: Transportation Model
definition.summary: Transportation Model uses a Origins and destinations → Supply-demand balance → Transportation model → Solve allocation workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: Origins and destinations
steps.prompt: Define supply nodes, demand nodes, shipment units, and route costs.

steps.title: Supply-demand balance
steps.prompt: Check totals, add dummy nodes if appropriate, and preserve prohibited routes.

steps.title: Transportation model
steps.prompt: Formulate shipment variables, conservation constraints, and objective.

steps.title: Solve allocation
steps.prompt: Find a minimum-cost feasible shipping plan and inspect capacity or route bottlenecks.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test cost, supply, demand, and route-disruption changes.

definition.name: Assignment Model
definition.summary: Assignment Model uses a Agents and tasks → Assignment matrix → Optimal assignment → Interpretation workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: Agents and tasks
steps.prompt: Define the entities to assign, tasks, eligibility, and performance/cost metric.

steps.title: Assignment matrix
steps.prompt: Construct one-to-one or capacity-adjusted costs/benefits and prohibited matches.

steps.title: Optimal assignment
steps.prompt: Solve for the best feasible matching under assignment constraints.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Inspect high-cost pairings, unused capacity, and ties rather than treating the optimum as self-explanatory.

steps.title: Sensitivity
steps.prompt: Test score uncertainty, new constraints, and reassignments.

definition.name: Inventory Model
definition.summary: Inventory Model uses a Inventory system → Cost structure → Policy parameters → Demand and lead-time uncertainty workflow to optimize constrained choices, model queues and stochastic systems, and compare operational policies.

steps.title: Inventory system
steps.prompt: Define item, demand process, replenishment lead time, review policy, and service objective.

steps.title: Cost structure
steps.prompt: Estimate ordering/setup, holding, shortage, obsolescence, and stockout costs.

steps.title: Policy parameters
steps.prompt: Calculate or simulate order quantity, reorder point, safety stock, or base-stock levels.

steps.title: Demand and lead-time uncertainty
steps.prompt: Test variability, seasonality, disruptions, and service-level tradeoffs.

steps.title: Operating policy
steps.prompt: Define replenishment rules, exception triggers, and recalibration cadence.

definition.name: Rhetorical Criticism
definition.summary: Rhetorical Criticism uses a Rhetorical artifact → Rhetorical situation → Rhetorical strategies → Functions and effects workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Rhetorical artifact
steps.prompt: Define the speech, text, image, performance, or communication event and its context.

steps.title: Rhetorical situation
steps.prompt: Identify rhetor, audiences, exigence, constraints, genre, and relevant historical conditions.

steps.title: Rhetorical strategies
steps.prompt: Analyze appeals, framing, arrangement, style, tropes, identification, omissions, and audience positioning.

steps.title: Functions and effects
steps.prompt: Explain what the rhetoric invites audiences to believe, feel, value, or do and how form supports that work.

steps.title: Interpretive claim
steps.prompt: State an evidence-grounded claim about how the artifact functions rhetorically, including plausible alternative readings.

definition.name: Genre Criticism
definition.summary: Genre Criticism uses a Artifact and genre claim → Genre conventions → Fit and deviation → Genre function workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Artifact and genre claim
steps.prompt: Define the artifact, proposed genre, audience, and communicative setting.

steps.title: Genre conventions
steps.prompt: Identify recurring structural, stylistic, rhetorical, and thematic conventions expected of the genre.

steps.title: Fit and deviation
steps.prompt: Compare the artifact with conventions, noting conformity, hybridization, parody, or deliberate deviation.

steps.title: Genre function
steps.prompt: Explain how genre expectations shape interpretation, credibility, audience response, or social action.

steps.title: Alternative classification
steps.prompt: Test plausible alternative genre classifications and state what each would change.

definition.name: Stylistic Analysis
definition.summary: Stylistic Analysis uses a Text and comparison basis → Linguistic features → Patterning → Interpretive effects workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Text and comparison basis
steps.prompt: Define the text, passage, authorial corpus, or comparison set.

steps.title: Linguistic features
steps.prompt: Identify salient lexical, syntactic, phonological, graphological, and figurative features.

steps.title: Patterning
steps.prompt: Distinguish systematic style from isolated examples and compare frequencies or distributions where useful.

steps.title: Interpretive effects
steps.prompt: Explain how stylistic choices shape tone, viewpoint, emphasis, pacing, characterization, or persuasion.

steps.title: Attribution limits
steps.prompt: Separate stylistic description from claims about intention, authorship, or effect that require additional evidence.

definition.name: Corpus Linguistics Analysis
definition.summary: Corpus Linguistics Analysis uses a Corpus question → Corpus design → Corpus measures → Quantitative-to-text inspection workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Corpus question
steps.prompt: Define the linguistic question, target population of texts, and appropriate comparison corpus.

steps.title: Corpus design
steps.prompt: Specify inclusion, sampling, metadata, preprocessing, tokenization, and representativeness constraints.

steps.title: Corpus measures
steps.prompt: Select frequencies, dispersion, keyness, collocation, n-grams, concordance, or grammatical measures appropriate to the question.

steps.title: Quantitative-to-text inspection
steps.prompt: Trace aggregate patterns back to concordance lines and source contexts to avoid decontextualized inference.

steps.title: Interpretation and limits
steps.prompt: State the linguistic finding with corpus, annotation, multiple-testing, and generalization limits.

definition.name: Concordance Analysis
definition.summary: Concordance Analysis uses a Target form → Concordance lines → Context patterns → Variation and exceptions workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Target form
steps.prompt: Define the word, lemma, phrase, construction, or annotation to inspect.

steps.title: Concordance lines
steps.prompt: Generate context windows and sample or sort them transparently.

steps.title: Context patterns
steps.prompt: Identify recurrent semantic, grammatical, positional, and discourse patterns across lines.

steps.title: Variation and exceptions
steps.prompt: Inspect unusual or contradictory contexts rather than reporting only dominant patterns.

steps.title: Usage claim
steps.prompt: Summarize what the concordance supports about use, meaning, stance, or patterning and what remains uncertain.

definition.name: Collocation Analysis
definition.summary: Collocation Analysis uses a Node and corpus → Candidate collocates → Dispersion and stability → Concordance validation workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Node and corpus
steps.prompt: Define the node word or construction, corpus, span, and linguistic unit.

steps.title: Candidate collocates
steps.prompt: Calculate co-occurrence counts and an appropriate association measure while retaining raw frequency.

steps.title: Dispersion and stability
steps.prompt: Check whether associations are widespread or driven by a few documents, speakers, periods, or genres.

steps.title: Concordance validation
steps.prompt: Inspect concordance contexts to distinguish meaningful association from grammatical or sampling artifacts.

steps.title: Collocational meaning
steps.prompt: Interpret semantic preference, prosody, phraseology, or discourse association with methodological caveats.

definition.name: Keyword Analysis
definition.summary: Keyword Analysis uses a Target and reference corpora → Frequency basis → Keyness test → Contextual validation workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Target and reference corpora
steps.prompt: Define comparable target and reference corpora and the substantive contrast they represent.

steps.title: Frequency basis
steps.prompt: Normalize frequencies and document tokenization, lemmatization, and filtering choices.

steps.title: Keyness test
steps.prompt: Use an appropriate effect-size or significance measure to identify unusually frequent or infrequent items.

steps.title: Contextual validation
steps.prompt: Inspect dispersion and concordances so keyness is not mistaken for thematic importance automatically.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.prompt: Group robust keywords into defensible lexical or discourse patterns and state corpus-comparability limits.

definition.name: Semantic Field Analysis
definition.summary: Semantic Field Analysis uses a Conceptual domain → Field members → Semantic relations → Distribution in context workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Conceptual domain
steps.prompt: Define the domain or concept whose lexical organization is being examined.

steps.title: Field members
steps.prompt: Identify lexical items and expressions participating in the field, including oppositions, hierarchies, overlaps, and boundary cases.

steps.title: Semantic relations
steps.prompt: Map synonymy, antonymy, hyponymy, meronymy, association, metaphorical extension, and evaluative loading where relevant.

steps.title: Distribution in context
steps.prompt: Examine how field members distribute across speakers, genres, periods, or rhetorical positions.

steps.title: Conceptual pattern
steps.prompt: Explain how the field structures distinctions and values without assuming a fixed universal lexicon.

definition.name: Metaphor Analysis
definition.summary: Metaphor Analysis uses a Corpus and question → Metaphorical expressions → Source-target patterns → Discursive function workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Corpus and question
steps.prompt: Define the text set and analytic purpose for identifying metaphorical language.

steps.title: Metaphorical expressions
steps.prompt: Identify expressions whose contextual meaning contrasts with but can be understood through a more basic or concrete sense.

steps.title: Source-target patterns
steps.prompt: Group expressions into recurring source-target mappings without forcing isolated figures into broad schemas.

steps.title: Discursive function
steps.prompt: Assess how metaphors frame causality, agency, evaluation, emotion, identity, or policy possibilities.

steps.title: Competing readings
steps.prompt: Test literal, conventionalized, ironic, metonymic, or alternative metaphor readings and report uncertainty.

definition.name: Conceptual Metaphor Analysis
definition.summary: Conceptual Metaphor Analysis uses a Target concept → Linguistic evidence → Cross-domain mapping → Entailments and constraints workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Target concept
steps.prompt: Define the abstract target domain and corpus or community in which it is expressed.

steps.title: Linguistic evidence
steps.prompt: Collect multiple metaphorical expressions with context rather than inferring a conceptual metaphor from one phrase.

steps.title: Cross-domain mapping
steps.prompt: Specify source-domain structure and systematic correspondences projected onto the target.

steps.title: Entailments and constraints
steps.prompt: Trace which inferences the mapping licenses, highlights, hides, or conflicts with.

steps.title: Conceptual claim
steps.prompt: Assess conventionality, competing mappings, cultural specificity, and evidential strength of the proposed conceptual metaphor.

definition.name: Speech Act Analysis
definition.summary: Speech Act Analysis uses a Utterances and setting → Illocutionary force → Felicity conditions → Indirectness and implication workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Utterances and setting
steps.prompt: Define the utterances, participants, institutional setting, and sequential context.

steps.title: Illocutionary force
steps.prompt: Classify relevant acts such as asserting, requesting, promising, warning, declaring, or expressing, using contextual evidence.

steps.title: Felicity conditions
steps.prompt: Assess authority, sincerity, uptake, preparatory conditions, and conventional procedures required for the act to function.

steps.title: Indirectness and implication
steps.prompt: Identify indirect speech acts, politeness strategies, ambiguity, and mismatches between form and force.

steps.title: Interactional effect
steps.prompt: Explain how the acts alter commitments, relationships, permissions, obligations, or subsequent interaction.

definition.name: Pragmatic Analysis
definition.summary: Pragmatic Analysis uses a Exchange and context → Encoded content → Pragmatic inference → Alternative interpretations workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Exchange and context
steps.prompt: Define the communicative exchange, participants, shared knowledge, and relevant situational context.

steps.title: Encoded content
steps.prompt: Separate conventional semantic content from context-dependent interpretation.

steps.title: Pragmatic inference
steps.prompt: Analyze implicature, presupposition, deixis, reference, relevance, politeness, and common-ground reasoning as applicable.

steps.title: Alternative interpretations
steps.prompt: Test plausible interpretations against linguistic form, context, speaker goals, and subsequent uptake.

steps.title: Pragmatic conclusion
steps.prompt: State the best-supported contextual meaning and the assumptions on which it depends.

definition.name: Conversation Repair Analysis
definition.summary: Conversation Repair Analysis uses a Trouble sequence → Repair initiation → Repair outcome → Interactional organization workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Trouble sequence
steps.prompt: Identify the talk segment, participants, and point where speaking, hearing, or understanding becomes problematic.

steps.title: Repair initiation
steps.prompt: Classify who initiates repair, where it occurs, and what linguistic form signals the trouble.

steps.title: Repair outcome
steps.prompt: Trace self- or other-repair, replacement, clarification, abandonment, or failure and its sequential placement.

steps.title: Interactional organization
steps.prompt: Assess preference for self-repair, delay, face management, authority, or institutional constraints.

steps.title: Analytic implication
steps.prompt: Explain what repair reveals about understanding, norms, identities, expertise, or interactional organization.

definition.name: Narrative Positioning Analysis
definition.summary: Narrative Positioning Analysis uses a Narrative event → Story-world positioning → Interactional positioning → Cultural positioning workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Narrative event
steps.prompt: Define the story, telling context, narrator, audiences, and relevant interactional setting.

steps.title: Story-world positioning
steps.prompt: Analyze how characters are positioned relative to agency, blame, morality, power, and available identities within the narrated events.

steps.title: Interactional positioning
steps.prompt: Analyze how the teller positions self and listeners in the present telling through stance, alignment, and claims to identity.

steps.title: Cultural positioning
steps.prompt: Identify broader master narratives, categories, or social discourses the telling reproduces or resists.

steps.title: Positioning claim
steps.prompt: Synthesize how the levels of positioning construct identity while preserving contradictions and alternative readings.

definition.name: Framing Analysis
definition.summary: Framing Analysis uses a Issue and corpus → Frame devices → Frame packages → Frame competition workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Issue and corpus
steps.prompt: Define the issue, communicators, audiences, media or text corpus, and time period.

steps.title: Frame devices
steps.prompt: Identify problem definitions, causal attributions, moral evaluations, remedies, metaphors, exemplars, labels, omissions, and visual cues.

steps.title: Frame packages
steps.prompt: Group recurring devices into coherent interpretive frames and distinguish frames from isolated topics or sentiments.

steps.title: Frame competition
steps.prompt: Compare which actors advance, contest, combine, or suppress frames and how prominence changes across contexts.

steps.title: Interpretive implications
steps.prompt: Explain how frames make some interpretations and actions salient while backgrounding others, without assuming audience effects absent evidence.

definition.name: Critical Media Analysis
definition.summary: Critical Media Analysis uses a Media corpus and context → Representation → Power and production → Silences and alternatives workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Media corpus and context
steps.prompt: Define outlets, platforms, genres, ownership or institutional context, audience, and period.

steps.title: Representation
steps.prompt: Analyze selection, sourcing, visibility, categorization, language, imagery, and narrative organization.

steps.title: Power and production
steps.prompt: Examine institutional routines, ownership, political economy, platform incentives, access, and whose voices gain authority.

steps.title: Silences and alternatives
steps.prompt: Identify exclusions, naturalized assumptions, counter-discourses, and plausible alternative constructions.

steps.title: Critical interpretation
steps.prompt: Connect textual patterns to structures of power carefully, distinguishing demonstrated mechanisms from broader contextual hypotheses.

definition.name: Visual Rhetoric Analysis
definition.summary: Visual Rhetoric Analysis uses a Visual artifact → Visual composition → Rhetorical appeals → Circulation and convention workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Visual artifact
steps.prompt: Define the image, graphic, interface, spatial display, or multimodal artifact and its circulation context.

steps.title: Visual composition
steps.prompt: Analyze salience, framing, gaze, perspective, color, typography, spatial hierarchy, symbolism, and sequencing as relevant.

steps.title: Rhetorical appeals
steps.prompt: Identify credibility, emotion, identification, analogy, evidence claims, and audience positioning achieved visually.

steps.title: Circulation and convention
steps.prompt: Relate the visual to genre conventions, platform constraints, accompanying text, historical imagery, and intended or actual audiences.

steps.title: Rhetorical claim
steps.prompt: Explain how visual form supports persuasion or meaning while considering alternative readings and accessibility limitations.

definition.name: Multimodal Discourse Analysis
definition.summary: Multimodal Discourse Analysis uses a Multimodal artifact → Mode-specific resources → Intermodal relations → Social meaning workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Multimodal artifact
steps.prompt: Define the artifact, communicative event, modes present, producers, audiences, and context.

steps.title: Mode-specific resources
steps.prompt: Analyze language, image, sound, gesture, layout, movement, typography, and other modes using appropriate descriptive categories.

steps.title: Intermodal relations
steps.prompt: Examine reinforcement, elaboration, contradiction, sequencing, anchoring, substitution, and division of communicative labor across modes.

steps.title: Social meaning
steps.prompt: Relate modal choices to genre, identity, authority, ideology, platform affordances, and interactional goals.

steps.title: Multimodal interpretation
steps.prompt: State how the modes jointly produce meaning, preserving tensions that would disappear if reduced to text alone.

definition.name: Semiotic Analysis
definition.summary: Semiotic Analysis uses a Sign system → Sign relations → Codes and conventions → Higher-order meanings workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Sign system
steps.prompt: Define the artifact or practice, relevant sign vehicles, codes, community, and context.

steps.title: Sign relations
steps.prompt: Analyze iconic, indexical, symbolic, denotative, connotative, syntagmatic, and paradigmatic relations where applicable.

steps.title: Codes and conventions
steps.prompt: Identify cultural codes and conventions that make the signs interpretable to particular communities.

steps.title: Higher-order meanings
steps.prompt: Examine how combinations of signs naturalize identities, values, classifications, or broader cultural narratives.

steps.title: Interpretive limits
steps.prompt: Compare alternative code systems, audiences, and contexts rather than treating a semiotic reading as universally fixed.

definition.name: Interdiscursivity Analysis
definition.summary: Interdiscursivity Analysis uses a Text and setting → Constituent discourses → Relations among discourses → Social change workflow to analyze language, rhetoric, discourse, symbols, genre, media form, and patterned textual choices.

steps.title: Text and setting
steps.prompt: Define the text or discourse event and its institutional, historical, and interactional setting.

steps.title: Constituent discourses
steps.prompt: Identify recognizable genres, registers, styles, professional discourses, or ideological vocabularies combined in the text.

steps.title: Relations among discourses
steps.prompt: Analyze quotation, recontextualization, hybridization, colonization, tension, hierarchy, and boundary crossing.

steps.title: Social change
steps.prompt: Assess whether the mixture reproduces established orders of discourse or signals institutional, identity, or ideological change.

steps.title: Interdiscursive interpretation
steps.prompt: State the best-supported account of how discourse mixing functions and what contextual evidence supports it.

definition.name: Historical Method
definition.summary: Historical Method uses a Historical question → Source base → Source criticism → Context and sequence workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Historical question
steps.prompt: Define the event, process, actor, period, and historical claim to be investigated.

steps.title: Source base
steps.prompt: Identify primary and secondary sources, provenance, survival bias, and relevant archives or material evidence.

steps.title: Source criticism
steps.prompt: Assess authorship, purpose, audience, chronology, transmission, reliability, and corroboration for key evidence.

steps.title: Context and sequence
steps.prompt: Reconstruct chronology, institutions, constraints, contingencies, and plausible causal mechanisms without presentism.

steps.title: Historical argument
steps.prompt: State the best-supported interpretation, competing explanations, evidentiary gaps, and limits on generalization.

definition.name: Internal Criticism
definition.summary: Internal Criticism uses a Source content → Knowledge and competence → Candor and bias → Internal coherence workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Source content
steps.prompt: Define the source passage or testimony and the factual or interpretive claims it contains.

steps.title: Knowledge and competence
steps.prompt: Assess whether the author or witness could know the reported information, including access, expertise, memory, and temporal distance.

steps.title: Candor and bias
steps.prompt: Examine incentives, rhetoric, exaggeration, omission, inconsistency, prejudice, and intended audience.

steps.title: Internal coherence
steps.prompt: Test chronology, factual consistency, terminology, anachronism, and contradictions within the source.

steps.title: Credibility judgment
steps.prompt: Determine which claims are credible, doubtful, symbolic, or unusable and why.

definition.name: External Criticism
definition.summary: External Criticism uses a Source object → Origin and dating → Integrity and transmission → External comparison workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Source object
steps.prompt: Identify the physical or transmitted source whose authenticity and provenance are being tested.

steps.title: Origin and dating
steps.prompt: Examine material, script, language, metadata, archival history, ownership, and dating evidence.

steps.title: Integrity and transmission
steps.prompt: Assess whether the source is original, copied, interpolated, edited, forged, damaged, or reconstructed.

steps.title: External comparison
steps.prompt: Compare with authenticated exemplars, contemporaneous records, technical analyses, and known historical constraints.

steps.title: Authenticity status
steps.prompt: State the source's likely authenticity, provenance, integrity, and unresolved authentication questions.

definition.name: Contextualization
definition.summary: Contextualization uses a Object of interpretation → Relevant contexts → Actor horizons → Context-evidence links workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Object of interpretation
steps.prompt: Define the text, action, institution, event, or belief to be situated historically.

steps.title: Relevant contexts
steps.prompt: Identify political, economic, social, intellectual, linguistic, religious, technological, and local settings that materially bear on interpretation.

steps.title: Actor horizons
steps.prompt: Reconstruct categories, expectations, constraints, interests, and available knowledge from the actors' own historical horizon.

steps.title: Context-evidence links
steps.prompt: Show specifically how contextual evidence changes interpretation rather than listing background facts.

steps.title: Contextual limits
steps.prompt: Distinguish contextual explanation from determinism and note competing contexts or surviving ambiguity.

definition.name: Comparative Historical Analysis
definition.summary: Comparative Historical Analysis uses a Cases and outcome → Comparability → Within- and cross-case patterns → Alternative explanations workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Cases and outcome
steps.prompt: Define the cases, time periods, outcome or process, and rationale for comparison.

steps.title: Comparability
steps.prompt: Assess scope conditions, case selection, measurement equivalence, and whether apparent similarities mask different institutions or sequences.

steps.title: Within- and cross-case patterns
steps.prompt: Compare timing, mechanisms, necessary or sufficient conditions, path dependence, and divergent outcomes.

steps.title: Alternative explanations
steps.prompt: Test rival causal accounts, selection effects, diffusion, common shocks, and equifinality.

steps.title: Comparative inference
steps.prompt: State what the comparison supports about mechanisms or conditions and what cannot be generalized beyond the cases.

definition.name: Prosopography
definition.summary: Prosopography uses a Collective population → Biographical attributes → Record linkage → Collective patterns workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Collective population
steps.prompt: Define the historical group, membership criteria, period, geography, and research question.

steps.title: Biographical attributes
steps.prompt: Specify comparable variables such as origin, education, office, kinship, patronage, wealth, affiliation, career, and mobility.

steps.title: Record linkage
steps.prompt: Reconcile names, identities, missing data, duplicate persons, uncertain dates, and uneven source survival.

steps.title: Collective patterns
steps.prompt: Analyze distributions, career paths, networks, factions, recruitment, social origins, and change over time.

steps.title: Group inference
steps.prompt: Explain what collective biography reveals while avoiding inference from documented elites to undocumented populations.

definition.name: Genealogical Analysis
definition.summary: Genealogical Analysis uses a Concept or practice → Discontinuities and episodes → Power-knowledge relations → Lines of descent workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Concept or practice
steps.prompt: Define the category, practice, identity, institution, or truth claim whose historical emergence is being traced.

steps.title: Discontinuities and episodes
steps.prompt: Identify shifts, ruptures, forgotten alternatives, conflicts, and contingent events rather than assuming linear development.

steps.title: Power-knowledge relations
steps.prompt: Examine institutions, classifications, expertise, discipline, incentives, and practices that make particular meanings or subjects possible.

steps.title: Lines of descent
steps.prompt: Trace heterogeneous antecedents and recombinations without seeking a single origin or inevitable endpoint.

steps.title: Critical implication
steps.prompt: Show how the genealogy denaturalizes present arrangements while distinguishing documented history from theoretical interpretation.

definition.name: Microhistory
definition.summary: Microhistory uses a Small-scale case → Dense evidence → Exceptional clues → Move across scales workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Small-scale case
steps.prompt: Define the person, event, locality, trial, object, or episode selected for intensive investigation and explain why it is analytically revealing.

steps.title: Dense evidence
steps.prompt: Assemble granular records and reconstruct actors, relationships, language, routines, anomalies, and uncertainties at close range.

steps.title: Exceptional clues
steps.prompt: Use unusual details or discrepancies to expose wider structures, norms, strategies, or categories while testing alternative explanations.

steps.title: Move across scales
steps.prompt: Relate the micro-case to regional, institutional, cultural, or macro-historical processes without treating it as statistically representative.

steps.title: Microhistorical claim
steps.prompt: State what the case illuminates about broader history and the limits imposed by exceptional evidence or survival bias.

definition.name: Oral History Analysis
definition.summary: Oral History Analysis uses a Interview corpus → Memory and narration → Corroboration → Subjective meaning workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Interview corpus
steps.prompt: Define narrators, interview circumstances, research question, recording practices, consent, and relevant life-history context.

steps.title: Memory and narration
steps.prompt: Analyze retrospective reconstruction, chronology, silence, repetition, emotion, genre, interviewer effects, and later knowledge.

steps.title: Corroboration
steps.prompt: Compare oral accounts with contemporaneous records and other testimony without treating documentary sources as automatically superior.

steps.title: Subjective meaning
steps.prompt: Interpret how narrators understand identity, experience, causality, community, and change, including contradictions across tellings.

steps.title: Historical use
steps.prompt: Separate evidence about events from evidence about memory and meaning, and state ethical and representativeness limits.

definition.name: Tradition-Historical Analysis
definition.summary: Tradition-Historical Analysis uses a Tradition unit → Earlier forms → Social settings → Development and reuse workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Tradition unit
steps.prompt: Define the saying, motif, narrative, law, ritual, creed, or thematic unit whose development is being investigated.

steps.title: Earlier forms
steps.prompt: Identify probable earlier formulations, oral or written forms, variants, and recurring traditional elements.

steps.title: Social settings
steps.prompt: Assess communities, institutions, rituals, controversies, or pedagogical settings in which the tradition may have functioned.

steps.title: Development and reuse
steps.prompt: Trace adaptation, expansion, combination, reinterpretation, and theological or ideological reshaping across stages.

steps.title: Reconstruction limits
steps.prompt: Distinguish textually supported development from hypothetical prehistory and note where sequence or setting remains uncertain.

definition.name: Canonical Criticism
definition.summary: Canonical Criticism uses a Canonical context → Placement and neighbors → Intra-canonical relationships → Canonical function workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Canonical context
steps.prompt: Identify the canon, community, ordering, and final-form context in which the text is being interpreted.

steps.title: Placement and neighbors
steps.prompt: Examine how position, grouping, superscriptions, framing, and neighboring texts shape interpretation.

steps.title: Intra-canonical relationships
steps.prompt: Trace quotation, echo, reinterpretation, thematic development, and tensions across the canon.

steps.title: Canonical function
steps.prompt: Ask how the received form functions for the interpreting community without erasing historical layers or diversity.

steps.title: Limits
steps.prompt: Distinguish canonical interpretation from claims about original composition, historical events, or universal meaning.

definition.name: Sociological Criticism
definition.summary: Sociological Criticism uses a Text and social world → Social structure → Social location → Social function workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Text and social world
steps.prompt: Define the text or tradition and the social setting or community whose relations are being analyzed.

steps.title: Social structure
steps.prompt: Identify status, class, institutions, roles, networks, authority, norms, conflict, exchange, and group boundaries relevant to the text.

steps.title: Social location
steps.prompt: Assess the likely positions and interests of producers, implied audiences, represented groups, and excluded actors.

steps.title: Social function
steps.prompt: Analyze how the text legitimates, contests, negotiates, or imagines social arrangements and collective identity.

steps.title: Sociological limits
steps.prompt: Separate evidence about textual representation from claims about actual historical social structures unless independently supported.

definition.name: Anthropological Criticism
definition.summary: Anthropological Criticism uses a Cultural practice or text → Emic categories → Analytic comparison → Cultural function workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Cultural practice or text
steps.prompt: Define the ritual, symbol, narrative, institution, exchange, kinship pattern, or worldview under study.

steps.title: Emic categories
steps.prompt: Identify local classifications, values, roles, cosmologies, purity systems, reciprocity, honor, or other culturally salient categories.

steps.title: Analytic comparison
steps.prompt: Use anthropological models or cross-cultural comparison cautiously, specifying similarities, differences, and historical distance.

steps.title: Cultural function
steps.prompt: Assess how practices organize meaning, identity, social relations, boundaries, conflict, or adaptation.

steps.title: Translation limits
steps.prompt: Avoid treating reconstructed cultures as static wholes and distinguish indigenous categories from analyst-imposed models.

definition.name: Feminist Hermeneutics
definition.summary: Feminist Hermeneutics uses a Text and interpretive problem → Gendered positions → Silences and asymmetries → Resistance and recovery workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Text and interpretive problem
steps.prompt: Define the text, tradition, practice, or doctrine and the gendered question being examined.

steps.title: Gendered positions
steps.prompt: Analyze representation, agency, voice, embodiment, labor, authority, kinship, sexuality, and access to institutions across differently situated actors.

steps.title: Silences and asymmetries
steps.prompt: Identify exclusions, androcentric assumptions, interpretive traditions, and whose experience is normalized or marginalized.

steps.title: Resistance and recovery
steps.prompt: Examine counter-readings, resistant voices, alternative practices, and historical possibilities without romanticizing them.

steps.title: Interpretive judgment
steps.prompt: State the gender-conscious interpretation, intersectional qualifications, evidentiary basis, and ethical implications.

definition.name: Postcolonial Hermeneutics
definition.summary: Postcolonial Hermeneutics uses a Text and colonial location → Colonial power relations → Subaltern and hybrid voices → Colonial afterlives workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Text and colonial location
steps.prompt: Define the text, tradition, interpretation, or institution and its relation to empire, colonialism, mission, migration, or decolonization.

steps.title: Colonial power relations
steps.prompt: Analyze representation, race, civilization discourse, land, language, knowledge, conversion, extraction, governance, and center-periphery relations.

steps.title: Subaltern and hybrid voices
steps.prompt: Identify silenced actors, mimicry, hybridity, resistance, translation, appropriation, and diasporic or indigenous perspectives.

steps.title: Colonial afterlives
steps.prompt: Trace how inherited categories and interpretive habits persist or are contested in later institutions and readings.

steps.title: Postcolonial interpretation
steps.prompt: State the interpretation while distinguishing textual evidence, historical context, and theoretical critique.

definition.name: Liberationist Interpretation
definition.summary: Liberationist Interpretation uses a Context of oppression → Textual engagement → Praxis and social analysis → Ideology critique workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Context of oppression
steps.prompt: Define the community, concrete conditions, structures of domination, and practical concerns from which interpretation proceeds.

steps.title: Textual engagement
steps.prompt: Analyze themes of suffering, liberation, justice, covenant, community, power, and agency using close textual evidence.

steps.title: Praxis and social analysis
steps.prompt: Relate interpretation to institutions, material conditions, collective action, and consequences rather than remaining purely abstract.

steps.title: Ideology critique
steps.prompt: Identify readings that legitimate domination as well as tensions or resources for emancipatory interpretation.

steps.title: Normative discernment
steps.prompt: State the proposed liberative reading, affected groups, ethical stakes, and risks of projecting present agendas onto historical texts.

definition.name: Comparative Theology
definition.summary: Comparative Theology uses a Comparative theological question → Deep engagement → Comparative return → Difference and asymmetry workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Comparative theological question
steps.prompt: Define the theological question, traditions, texts, practices, or concepts to be studied and the interpreter's standpoint.

steps.title: Deep engagement
steps.prompt: Interpret the comparison tradition on its own terms with adequate linguistic, historical, doctrinal, and practice context.

steps.title: Comparative return
steps.prompt: Bring insights back to the home tradition or original theological problem, identifying genuine challenge, resonance, or reframing.

steps.title: Difference and asymmetry
steps.prompt: Preserve irreducible differences, internal diversity, power asymmetries, and non-equivalent categories rather than forcing synthesis.

steps.title: Constructive conclusion
steps.prompt: State what theological learning or revision emerges and what the comparison does not warrant.

definition.name: Phenomenology of Religion
definition.summary: Phenomenology of Religion uses a Religious phenomenon → Descriptive bracketing → Experienced structures → Comparative variation workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Religious phenomenon
steps.prompt: Define the ritual, experience, symbol, myth, sacred space, practice, or community being described.

steps.title: Descriptive bracketing
steps.prompt: Temporarily suspend judgments about truth, falsity, pathology, or reduction to external causes in order to describe how the phenomenon appears to participants.

steps.title: Experienced structures
steps.prompt: Identify intentionality, sacred/profane distinctions, temporality, embodiment, affect, community, transcendence, and meaning as they are manifested.

steps.title: Comparative variation
steps.prompt: Compare manifestations across cases while preserving historical and cultural specificity.

steps.title: Reflexive limits
steps.prompt: State the descriptive insight and the limits of bracketing, access to experience, and claims of universal religious essence.

definition.name: Cognitive Science of Religion Analysis
definition.summary: Cognitive Science of Religion Analysis uses a Target phenomenon → Candidate cognitive mechanisms → Observable predictions → Competing levels of explanation workflow to analyze traditions, texts, practices, historical development, comparison, and interpretation with explicit evidentiary controls.

steps.title: Target phenomenon
steps.prompt: Define the religious belief, ritual, transmission pattern, agency attribution, memory effect, or group behavior to explain.

steps.title: Candidate cognitive mechanisms
steps.prompt: Identify mechanisms such as agency detection, theory of mind, minimally counterintuitive concepts, memory biases, ritual learning, costly signaling, or coalition psychology.

steps.title: Observable predictions
steps.prompt: Translate each proposed mechanism into behavioral, developmental, experimental, demographic, or cross-cultural predictions.

steps.title: Competing levels of explanation
steps.prompt: Compare cognitive explanations with historical, institutional, ecological, economic, and theological accounts rather than treating levels as mutually exclusive.

steps.title: Explanatory judgment
steps.prompt: State which mechanisms are supported, what evidence would discriminate alternatives, and limits on evolutionary or universal claims.
